# Unit combat drawn by the server (epic 0042)

The knowledge file for epic 0042's combat part: what the server must do when it owns each fight's clock (route S,
decision D210 of 2026-11-20), the premises measured live, and later the contract and the build. Sections 0-2 are ticket
4771's (the premises); section 3 is ticket 4775's (the choreography core as built, merged in by lead-0042 on 2026-11-20 from 4775's own file of the same name); later sections belong to the tickets that build route S.

Written 2026-11-20 by w3-0042 (account B, branch `w3-4771`). Marks: `[L]` seen live in this ticket's runs (named), `[C]`
read in the EXE's machine code (the analysis copy of `research/06-tooling-and-workflows/reverse-engineering-setup.md`;
addresses only, no code, D83) or in this repository, `[I]` inferred. Every picture is DIAGNOSTIC (D112) and stays
outside git (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w3/`).

Scope change during the ticket (lead-0042, 02:14, decision D210, route S): P2 (alignment of the EXE's effects) and P3
(depth of the EXE's effects over server units) were dropped; S1 (what the EXE still shows and plays with Combat and
Projectile off) and S2 (the repeating melee sound) were added. P1, P4, P5 and P7 stayed.

## 0. In short

**For route S (the server owns the fight's clock; the EXE's Combat and Projectile off):**

- **S1, what the EXE still does with Combat and Projectile off** (arm s0, old build 4390913) `[L]`:

    after the order for the killed warrior) follow in the next frames. So the flags, which UnitFlagManager hides on Run
    and shows on End (0321's reading), hide for one or two frames only: Q9 of `combat-choreography.md` 10 answered `[L]`
    (that row is not this ticket's to edit). Two attacks in a row on one defender stay serial: the second Run comes after
    the first End.
  - **No combat sound and no death sound.** The EXE's audio session has only the selection click (peak 0.17-0.20 at
    +0.5 s, the unit's selection sound, there too when an order failed) and the ambient level (up to 0.024) for every
    fight, ranged and melee, the kill included, Quick Combat off and on (three s0 launches); with Combat on (u0, u1) the
    same fights sound from about +1.5 s to the fight's end (peaks 0.19-0.50) and then stop. Measured with the audio
    session's peak meter (`tools/harness/audio.py meter_run`, every 0.1 s), not by ear.
  - **The camera still moves to the target** (the DLL's `lookAt`, as 0316 saw it): r3's s0 pictures show the view

    the EXE shows the damage number (+1.0 to +2.2 s) and fades the figures above the new damage state, plays NO death
    clip, death sound or hit effect (the killed unit is removed 0.23-0.26 s after the order), and the attacker's figures
    stand on the defender's plot by +0.43-0.74 s with no walk seen. The bullet below is kept as 4771 wrote it.
  - (4771, superseded by the line above) **Not determined from the pictures:** whether the EXE still shows damage numbers, a death animation or a hit
    particle with Combat off. In every launch the defenders stood under the server's fog clouds (the Lua visibility
    change does not reach the server's cloud layer `[I]`), and most burst frames are PrintWindow frames without the EXE's
    interface or flat grey (E9). This is for 4799 (S-C) to measure, on a plot the player has really seen.
- **S2, the repeating melee sound:** not reproduced. Eight melee fights with Combat on (Quick Combat off and on; u0 in r1,
  r2, r3 and u1 in r1), 20 s of quiet after each: the EXE's session peak stayed at or below 0.0205 after the fight's end,
  the same ambient level as with Combat off (s0: up to 0.0241), while fight sounds reach 0.19-0.50. No repeat `[L]`.
  What was not tried is in section 2.4.
- **P1 holds** `[L, u1]`: the server's unit scene shows the defender's new damage 0.133-0.166 s after the order (7
  fights; the order's own `RunCombatSim` came at 0.124-0.159 s) and removes a killed defender 0.265 s after it, while the
  EXE's `EndCombatSim` comes 4.21-4.76 s after the order (8.85 s for the second of two fights in a row, whose damage the
  server showed at 0.262 s). Times are the dump files' write times (one per drawn frame whose unit scene changed), so
  they are at most a frame late. So under route S every DLL-side event of a fighter is in the server long before
  any picture of the fight would end: the server's own visual queue (C2) must hold them; nothing waits on the EXE.
- **P4, stock's fight length with Combat on** (the reference for the server's own clock) `[L, u0 and u1]`:
  `RunCombatSim` 0.086-0.194 s after the order was sent (20 fights; includes the Lua channel's call); `EndCombatSim`
  4.033-4.866 s after `RunCombatSim` for one archer's volley on a warrior (16 fights), 4.534-4.767 s for a warrior's
  melee on a warrior (4 fights); `SerialEventUnitSetDamage` one frame (0.032-0.037 s, 24 ends) after `EndCombatSim`. Two
  attacks in a row on one defender: the second `RunCombatSim` comes 0.033-0.034 s after the first `EndCombatSim` (4
  pairs; Q3 of 0321 `[L]`: per unit the picture runs a fight behind), its fight 3.900-4.199 s. Quick Combat on: no
  `RunCombatSim` / `EndCombatSim` at all; the damage events 0.087-0.159 s after the order (8 fights). Every value is
  computed by `server/evidence/0042/4771/p4_4771.py` from the recorded Lua clock (`p4-all.txt`); Tiny, frame cap 30.
- **P5, death count: not measured.** The defenders stood under the server's fog clouds or at a barbarian camp in every
  usable picture, and figure counts from PrintWindow frames at this zoom are not reliable (falling figures are visible
  3.7 s into a Combat-on volley, r3 u0 scene 3, but not countable). The pose tap or RenderDoc of 0321's Q6 remains the
  method.
- **P7, the EXE's combat randomness** `[C, partial]`: the victory roll (5.3 of `combat-choreography.md`, "random(100)
  > 25") draws from a generator object kept inside the combat simulation's object, not from the C runtime's shared
  `rand()`. The generator is the MSVC linear congruential step (multiplier 0x343FD, increment 0x269EC3) with its own
  state word and call counter, and a bounded draw by rejection with a power-of-two mask. Where its state is seeded
  (per fight, per process, from what) was not found in the time box. So reproducing the EXE's victory poses exactly needs
  that seed and every draw before it in the same object; until the seed is found, route S's choreography uses its own
  random source and is accepted by statistics (sheet 8 item 4), which route S does not need anyway.

**What this means for route S** `[I]`: the server can start each fight at the DLL's combat record (it arrives first,
P1), play it for about the stock length (P4: 4-5 s for one volley or melee exchange on Tiny, Quick Combat off; 0 s with
Quick Combat on) and apply the held damage, death and moves at its own end. The EXE adds nothing to a fight in route S
except what S1 lists, so effects and sounds are the server's to add or to leave out.

### 2.2 The scene (each arm)

A Lua listener in the InGame state stamps `os.clock()` on `RunCombatSim`, `EndCombatSim`, `SerialEventUnitSetDamage`,
`SerialEventUnitDestroyedInCombat`, `SerialEventUnitDestroyed` and `SerialEventCitySetDamage` (0456's method, 12.1 of
`combat-choreography.md`); `os.clock()` is tied to the wall clock by a read between two `time.time()` readings at the
start and the end (offset spread 35-60 ms over 200 s). Music and ambience knobs at 0 for the session (not saved), SFX
and speech at 1; the EXE's audio session peak sampled every 0.1 s. Units asleep, auto unit cycle off, Quick Combat off
by `Network.SendGameOptions` and read back. The plots within 9 of the capital made visible; popups closed (D114). Then,
with the camera on each pair (`UI.LookAt`, 3 wheel ticks in) and a picture before, a burst of pictures every 0.3 s
during, and a picture after:

| Scene | Attack | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | two human archers on one barbarian warrior, the two orders sent 0.1 s apart | P4 two in a row, P1 |
| 2-4 | a human archer on a barbarian warrior whose damage was set to 0, 35, 65 first (scene 4 kills) | P5, P1, P4 |
| 5 | a human warrior on a barbarian warrior (melee), then 20 s of quiet | S2, P4 |
| 6 | Quick Combat on: a melee attack, then 20 s of quiet | S1, S2 |
| 7 | Quick Combat on: a ranged attack | S1 |

Orders as `WorldView.lua` gives them: `UI.SelectUnit`, then `Game.SelectionListGameNetMessage(GAMEMESSAGE_PUSH_MISSION,
MISSION_RANGE_ATTACK or MISSION_MOVE_TO, x, y, 0, false, false)`. For range 2 the plot between the archer and the target
has no feature and no hill (line of sight).

### 2.4 S2: what was tried, and what was not

Tried (r1-r3, eight fights): a human warrior's melee on a full-health barbarian warrior with Combat on, Quick Combat off
and on (u0 in r1, r2, r3; u1 in r1), on Tiny turn 18 in the human's turn, then 20 s of quiet with the camera on the fight: no sound above the
ambient level after the fight's end. Not tried: a melee that kills and advances; AI-turn melee (the barrier of 12.3);
other unit types (spearmen, horsemen, a city attack); a melee while the camera is moved away; long sessions; the new
build 26577625.

### 2.5 P7: the static look

Read 2026-11-20 02:24-02:40 with llvm-objdump 19 on the analysis copy (addresses only). The victory test of the figure-end
function (0x7556C0, `combat-choreography.md` 5.3) calls a bounded-random routine (0x750AD0) on a generator at offset +8
of its own object (the combat object, which also holds the participants at +0x2B84 and up); the routine steps the state
with the MSVC constants (multiplier 0x343FD, increment 0x269EC3), counts its calls at +4, reduces by an optional modulus
at +0xC and rejects draws above a power-of-two mask. Only one other call site of that routine exists (0x4BE9F9, guarded by
the global next to the Particle system's, read as a sound or effect variant pick `[I]`). The same LCG step is inlined at
about twenty other places of the EXE. The writer of the generator's state at +8 was not found within the time box.

Written 2026-11-20 02:08-03:50 EST by W2 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w2-4775`. Marks: `[C]` checked by this
worker in this repository's code or tests (each names the check), `[C 0321]` a rule as `combat-choreography.md` (0321)
reads it from the EXE's code (not re-checked here: D83, the description is the only source), `[L 0557]` the recorded
live data of ticket 0557 (`tools/harness/evidence/0557/batch-s-stock1.json`, stock route, 2026-11-18), `[I]` this
section's reading where 0321 leaves the rule open. Offline only: no game instance, no EXE address, nothing from the EXE

### What it is

`render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h`, `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`, `combat_tables.cpp`; the controller's
entry in `controller.h` / `controller.cpp`. One visualised combat in, a schedule out, route independent (route S, D210:
the server's fight clock 4782 takes `CombatResult::end`; the entry has no pacing rule of its own).

- **Input** (`CombatInput`): the server's `SrvFeed::CombatRecord` fields (`unit-server-scene.md` 2.3, 11): seq, kind
  (25 unit, 28 city), the flag bits as the record has them, plot, attacker and defender (owner, unit or city, final
  damage, max hit points), nuclear level, damage members. Per unit side `CombatUnitFigures`: the members in member
  order (count, domain, `EnableActions` words, rush, LastToDie, weapons, victory) and the figures standing at the start.
- **Output** (`CombatResult`): per figure the state sequence (`FigureStep`: time, state, the code requested, target
  figure, approach intent 1 run / 2 run charge; the motion is 4776's), the hits (`CombatHit`: landing and trigger time,
  striker, code, the trigger's id in the member's trigger file, target, Death / OwedHit / Spent), the controller events
  in time order (`TimedEvent`: `action run / combat_ready / charge / attack / attack_charge / attack_city / bombard /
  bombard_defend / idle / victory` and `kill`, each with its figure set), notes (MissingClip, NoHitTrigger, Naval), the
  per-side outcome, and `end` (every figure finished) or the limit. `combatFrames` cuts the events into timeline frames.
- **Timing source** (`CombatClips`): per member and code the clip's duration and its hit moments: the code's Action
  triggers, or, when it has none, its Transfer triggers plus the weapon's flight. The controller's
  `combatClips(duration)` reads them from the member's ec bindings and trigger files; a clip the art step did not find
  is `found = false` with 4770's `missing in install:` text.
- **Refusals** (`CombatCode`): QuickCombat (bit 8 with bit 10), NotVisualised, BadInput (each field named), NoFigures,
  UnknownKind. (Corrected 2026-11-20 by 4777, section 8: CityAttacker, AirCombat, Nuclear and AreaMembers are played
  since 4777, no longer refused; naval units have their own rule. Replaced: "and 4777's cases: CityAttacker, AirCombat
  (an air member, a bombing run or an air sweep), Nuclear, AreaMembers (any damage member, the garrison bystander
  included). Naval units play the general rule with a note.")
- **Deterministic**: one xoshiro256** seeded from (scene seed, attacker, seq, defender); the draws are target ties and
  the victory rolls, in a fixed order [C: `deterministic_for_a_seed`, two runs byte-equal, another seed differs].

### The rules as built

| Rule | Source | As built |
|---|---|---|
| Who can attack | [C 0321] 5.1 | a member with none of Attack, AttackSurfaceToAir, AttackCharge, AttackCity, Bombard plays 1280 and never strikes |
| Deaths per side | [C 0321] 13.4 | standing - `units::livingFigures(total, final damage, max HP)` (the 0x4B4B80 rule); a killed unit loses every figure |
| Which figures die | lead-0042 #7555 | `DeathPick::LastFirst` (default): the last standing figures by index, as `unit-formations.md` 7 and the placement draw 0..m-1. **Named difference:** 0321 13.4 kills the figure hit; here a hit aimed elsewhere kills a doomed figure, shown by the re-layout, until 4776 (`DeathPick::Targeted` keeps the EXE's reading) |
| Protected survivor | [C 0321] 13.4 | one survivor (LastToDie first) is skipped by every chooser; [I] taken when it is the only figure left: 0557 n1 / n2 (one-figure ships) ended in 3.0 / 3.7 s, not at the limit [L 0557] |
| Owed hits | [C 0321] 13.4 | the defender owes one; the attacker owes one when it has no planned death, the defender has a ranged member, retaliates, and the attacker's weapon is not one-shot |
| Strikes | [I] | a figure strikes only while the opponent's needs (deaths left + owed hits) exceed the strikes under way: 0321 5.1's wave counts are the participant's planned deaths, deaths done, hits in flight and hits owed, read as that limit. `max_in_flight` caps it further (a knob, off). Stock's rule as read since (18.14 S1, [C]): a ranged figure strikes while the opponent's planned deaths exceed those played plus the figures under projectiles in flight, or while it owes a hit (no cap then); the core's limit is the same or tighter, and the difference does not lengthen a fight |
| Approach | [I] 0321 5.5; [C] 18.44 | **Corrected 2026-11-25 (0743, 18.44) [C]:** with positions an attacking land melee figure of a non-rush member runs (1120 / 1400) at the nearest candidate figure and stops within the two members' `AttackRadius` (8 + 8 = 16 units) of the nearest standing opponent figure, as stock's target step and melee chooser (`CombatParams::melee_reach`); rush members, ships and aircraft as before. *Was:* an attacking melee figure runs (1400) for `approach` s (1.0, a placeholder until 4776's distances; since 4776 to `MoveRadius` of its target); a rush member with RunCharge charges (1120). Ranged figures and defenders do not approach; a melee defender strikes only at engaged attackers. *Corrected 2026-11-21 (4737, 10.10) [C]: stock run-charges (state 0xC, 1120) every attacking melee figure out of `MoveRadius` reach, rush or not (the Tiny archer ran with 1400: ranged attackers not covered); the code still has the rush test (proposal P2 (a))* |
| Combat ready | [C 0321] 5.3 + [I] | 1600 on first entering Ready / Wait; the first strike waits for the 1600 clip's length ("5 -> 10 when its animation is done"), after a run also for the run stop (1440); no second 1600 request while the figure is combat ready; found necessary offline, below |
| Attack code | [C 0321] 5.2, [I] choice | city target: 1180 for a ranged attacker, else 1160; ranged attacker or a defender with a projectile weapon: 1180; 1140 right after a 1120 charge when AttackCharge is enabled; else 1100 |
| After a charge | [I] | with AttackCharge: straight into 1140; without (VP's horseman, knight): Ready (1600) first, found offline below |
| Hit | [C 0321] 4.2 / 6.4 | at the clip's Action trigger; a Transfer (projectile, thrown torch) lands after the weapon's flight |
| A missing clip | 4770 | the strike never plays and never lands; the combat holds to the limit, like the EXE's unplayable 1130 of 0321 13.5 [C: `a_missing_attack_clip_holds_the_combat_to_the_limit`] |
| Dying | [C 0321] 5.3 | 1200; removed after the 1200 clip or 3.0 s, whichever first |
| End | [C 0321] 13.4, 5.3 | every figure is held while either side has deaths left, an owed hit, or a projectile in flight; then each ends: victory (1800) when its last request was 1600 or 1000, its member takes 1800, it is not air, and `random(100) > 25` (74 of 100) [C: `a_kill_takes_every_figure_and_victory_is_drawn_about_three_in_four`, 1,200 draws within the 99.9 % interval of 0.74]; else Done with 1000 |
| Victory's count test | [I] | 0321's "its side's count at +0x34 is not above +0x2B84" read as "the opponent unit is killed" (`VictoryRule::OpponentKilled`; `Always` for comparison) |
| Limit | [C 0321] 4.2 | 12 s (`limit`; 20 s is `limit_air`, air is 4777's). At the limit dying figures are removed and every other figure ends with 1000, no victory [I] |
| City target | [I] + [L 0557] | the city is a participant without figures and owes one hit. **Correction found here:** the literal hold (the attacker's planned deaths need a striker the city does not have) ran to 12 s on 0557 c1 / c2, whose recorded Run -> End were 2.97 s and 3.50 s; so the striking side's planned deaths fall at its first hit on the city |

### 4.1 What it is

`server/src/units/srv_units_fights.{h,cpp}`: `srvunits::FightClock`, independent of the renderer (it includes
`feed/srv_feed.h` only) and of the seam files. The caller (4774's wiring in `srv_units_anim`, agreed with lead-0042)
adds each drained `SrvFeed::CombatRecord` with its members in the DLL's order, calls `frame(F, dt, figures, out)` once
per server frame, and passes the `OwnerEnd` records to the trigger stream (4795) and the proxy's hold (4773). The
choreography is behind `FightPlayer` (start / advance / end): the 4775 core, stepped live (4.3).

| Rule | Source | As built |
|---|---|---|
| No fight | [C 0321] 4.1, 7 | Quick Combat (bit 8 with bit 10) or the visualise flag clear: nothing queued, no OwnerEnd (no hold to drop) |
| Order | [C 0321] 2.1, 3.4 | fights start in the records' seq order; `add()` refuses a seq that does not increase, or a kind other than 25 / 28 |
| Per-unit wait | [C 0321] 3.2 | a fight waits while an earlier fight, playing or waiting, names one of its units (owner and id) or its city; the plot words of the EXE's header are not in the record and are not compared [I] |
| Barrier | [C 0321] 3.3 | `kCombatGameRead` set and `kCombatActiveTurn` clear (the human watches the AI turn), or `nuclearLevel > 0`: the fight waits for every earlier fight and every later fight waits for it. The EXE also tests that the active player is human and alive; that is not in the record [I: taken as true] |
| Start | [L 4771 P4], [L 0477] | at the earliest in the frame after the frame that ended the fight it waited for (4771: "the second fight on the same defender starts one frame after the first ends", 4 pairs; 0477: Run 0.03 s after End) |
| End | 4775, [C 0321] 4.2, 13.2 | the player's (the choreography's) own end, else the limit: 12 s, 20 s when the plan names an air figure. No pacing or catch-up rule of the server's own (note 3.2: the EXE waits on the hold) |
| Refusal | D118 | a fight the player refuses (since 4777, section 8: bad input, a unit side without figures, an unknown kind; corrected 2026-11-20, was "4777's cases: `AirCombat`, `CityAttacker`, `Nuclear`, `AreaMembers`") ends in its start frame with OwnerEnd `Refused` and the core's text, counted; the caller logs it LOUD |
| OwnerEnd per fight | note 1.3, 1.5 item 2 | owner = `CombatRecord::returned` (the EXE's event id of the `RunCombatSim` record, the DLL's parent id) when `kCombatReturnedKnown`; else 0 with the seq, counted `ownerUnknown` |
| OwnerEnd per clip instance | note 1.5 item 2 | for the figures of a playing fight's units: when a figure's clip instance (`FigureProgram::instance`, a new id at each state entry with a graph) changes or the figure vanishes, OwnerEnd `ClipEnded` with player, unit, figure, instance. At the fight's own end its figures' open instances are covered by the fight's OwnerEnd and get no record of their own [I] |
| Unit gone, reset | [C 0321] 4.2 ("if a model is gone, the simulation ends") | `unitGone(owner, unit)` ends every fight naming it, queued ones included (OwnerEnd `Gone`); `reset()` ends all (`Reset`), so every hold the proxy took is dropped |

machine code (a read-only headless Ghidra 12.1.4 pass on a scratch copy of the analysis project of
`research/06-tooling-and-workflows/reverse-engineering-setup.md`, old build, PE time stamp 0x546CD0A8; addresses and
behaviour only, the decompiler text stays outside git, D83) or checked in this repository's code and tests (each names
the check); `[L 0557]` 0557's recorded stock fights; `[I]` this section's reading. Offline only: no game instance.

### 5.1 How the EXE moves a figure in a fight (static read, 2026-11-20 05:28-06:00 EST) `[C]`

Starts from `combat-choreography.md` 11, which listed the simulation's per-frame passes (0x6C8FD0, 0x5EFC50, 0x6902C0,
0x613940, 0x51F3B0) as not covered.

- **M1 The member's motion record.** Each figure points at its member's combat record (figure + 0x5C), the row of
  `ArtDefine_UnitMemberCombats` as the database reader 0x4B8BF0 stores it from + 0x150 of the member's object. Offsets
  in that record and the default the reader puts in for a NULL or non-positive value: + 0x00 `MoveRadius` (3.5), + 0x04
  `ShortMoveRadius` (0; readers fall back to `MoveRadius`, 0x598950), + 0x08 `ChargeRadius` (9.0), + 0x0C `AttackRadius`
  (8.0), + 0x10 `RangedAttackRadius` (default `AttackRadius` x 3), + 0x14 `MoveRate` (0.78125), + 0x18 `ShortMoveRate`
  (0; falls back to `MoveRate`, 0x67CF40), + 0x1C / + 0x20 `TurnRateMin` / `Max` (0.5 / 1.0, max raised to min),
  + 0x24 / + 0x28 `TurnFacingRateMin` / `Max` (15 / 20), + 0x2C / + 0x30 roll (0.25 / 0.5), + 0x34 / + 0x38 pitch
  (1.0 / 1.5), + 0x3C `LOSRadiusScale`, + 0x40 `TargetRadius` (3.0), + 0x44 `TargetHeight` (0); bytes + 0x48
  `HasShortRangedAttack`, + 0x49 `HasLongRangedAttack`, + 0x4A `HasLeftRightAttack`, + 0x4B `HasStationaryMelee`,
  + 0x4C `HasStationaryRangedAttack`, + 0x4D `HasIndependentWeaponFacing`, + 0x4E `HasCollisionAttack`, + 0x50
  `HasOpponentTracking`; + 0x54 `ReformBeforeCombat` (an int); + 0x5C `AttackAltitude` (90), + 0x60
  `AltitudeDecelerationDistance`. The named ones are read by name in 0x4B8BF0; the unnamed bytes + 0x4F, + 0x51, + 0x52
  were not matched to a column. In VP's database most rows leave these NULL (`MoveRate` set in 11 of 364 rows,
  `ShortMoveRadius` in 149, `MoveRadius` in 7), so the defaults are what most figures use.
- **M2 Speed.** The move step (0x61D7D0) advances a figure straight towards its waypoint by frame time x 64.0 (the
  float at 0x9E0AA8, the plot spacing) x `MoveRate`, or x `ShortMoveRate` while its action is 1450 (shuffle). So the
  default run is **50 world units per second** (0.78125 x 64) and the default shuffle the same; VP's 0.35 shuffle rate
  is 22.4 units per second. The move ends when the waypoint is within `MoveRadius` (flag 0x400), or, in the charge
  state, when the figure has passed its target line (a dot product with the participant's direction at + 0x2B78).
- **M3 Which figures move.** The simulation has a phase (+ 0xC1500) and a fight type (+ 0xC14FC, set by 0x41F5F0 from
  the participants' flags); 0x7635E0 maps (type, phase) to the next phase, taken when every figure of the side being
  waited for is in state 3. Phase 1 (0x493300): a participant whose flag + 0x2D3C is set lays its formation out again
  facing its opponent (0x5ACA80 -> 0x4A3560) and its figures move there (state 0xD, then 3 on arrival); the others go
  to 3 at once. Phase 2: both sides turn (0x5BB190, state 0xF, 3 when turned). Phase 3, the fight: the attacker's
  figures go into the charge state 0xC, which moves each towards its target's position (0x6902C0 case 0xC with
  0x5C61F0: the target figure's current position, or the target participant's slot table at + 0x2B8C), and the
  defender into 3, 5 or 0xE by the fight type. ~~Melee attackers with a projectile weapon (riflemen, tanks) move as
  well.~~ *Corrected 2026-11-22 (W51, 4745, 18.15 [C]): phase 3 exists only in fight type 2 (an attacker with no
  `HasShortRangedAttack` member); an attacker with such a member (riflemen, GWI, tanks) fights in type 1 or 4, whose
  phase 5 has its figures strike from where they stand. Phase 2 turns only `HasLeftRightAttack` members (ships), a
  quarter turn. The layout of 0x4A3560 and the defender's states per type are in 18.15; the layout's centre is still
  open.*
- **M4 Run or shuffle.** When a figure gets a new waypoint, 0x6902C0 picks 1450 (shuffle) if the waypoint is within
  `ShortMoveRadius` of it, else 1400 (run); without a 1450 clip it sets flag 0x1000.
- **M5 Turning.** 0x4ACAD0 turns a figure's heading (figure + 0x4C) towards the wanted one by (`TurnRateMin` +
  (`TurnRateMax` - `TurnRateMin`) x a fraction) x 2 pi x frame time: 0.5 to 1.0 turns per second by default.
- **M6 For `combat-choreography.md`'s owner:** its 5.3 reads "the weapon record has the byte at + 0x4E set" as a one-shot
  weapon. The pointer at figure + 0x5C is the member's combat record (M1), whose + 0x4E is `HasCollisionAttack` (3
  rows in VP: collision attackers); 0x41F5F0 also picks fight type 5 or 6 by it. The one-shot reading stands in effect,
  the record named there is the member's, not the weapon's `[C]` (not edited here: not this ticket's file).
- **Not read in the time box:** what sets + 0x2D3C (read as `ReformBeforeCombat` on a member `[I]`), the layout
  0x4A3560 makes for the reform, the turn amount of phase 2, the return to the unit's formation after the fight (0x5192A0
  hands each participant's position and facing to its model; what the model then plays was not read), and the
  defender's phase-3 states per fight type.

### 5.2 As built

- **The core times the approach by distance** (`combat.h` additive: `CombatMotion` on each member from the table with
  M1's defaults, `CombatUnitFigures::x, y` and the centre, `FigureMove` in `CombatResult::moves`). With positions given,
  every attacking figure of a melee attack (M3, projectile weapons included) moves straight at its target figure's
  position (a city: its centre) and stops `MoveRadius` short (a city: `CombatParams::city_reach`, 32 units `[I]`), at
  `MoveRate` x 64 units per second, or as a shuffle (1450) at `ShortMoveRate` x 64 when the target is within
  `ShortMoveRadius` (M2, M4). A figure already within reach does not move. A figure whose target died before its strike
  moves again to its next target. Without positions the core keeps 4775's 1.0 s approach and its melee-weapon rule, so
  today's callers are unchanged. Found offline and fixed in the core: a figure that re-targeted before its next strike
  kept its old "landed" mark, so releasing the new reservation did nothing and the fight held to 12 s (0557 h1 with
  positions); the reservation now clears the mark.
- **`c5r/unitanim/motion.h`**: `combatPositions` (each standing figure in its slot of the unit's placement, all n
  figures laid out, so a unit whose damage leaves fewer living by the 0x4B4B80 rule still has a position per figure the
  controller holds standing: 0557 w2); `FightMotion` (each figure's world position and heading over the fight: on a move
  straight at constant speed facing its way; standing, facing its target figure, else the opponent's centre; dying
  figures stay where they fell; after the fight's end every survivor walks back at its `MoveRate` x 64 into the slot its
  rank takes in the unit's placement after the damage: rank i of the survivors in figure order to the i-th placed
  figure, which is the reform of `unit-formations.md` 7; since 2026-11-22 (4742, 18.18) the core walks the survivors home
  inside the fight by default and this after-end walk closes only what is left); `FightPlacement`, a `units::PlacementSource` that wraps the
  module's placement and moves the figures of a unit in a fight by those offsets, in the unit's own frame, through
  `placement.h`'s new `applyFigureOffsets` (the agreed hunk, lead-0042 #7815: one function appended, nothing existing
  changed; heights sampled again at the new spot with the figure's `ZOffset` kept).
- **Scene and reflection:** the renderer places each unit once per frame (`UnitRenderer::prepare`, the one
  `UnitPlan::placement`), and the server draws the reflection and the scene pass from the same plan
  (`srv_units_scene.cpp` `drawPass` on `m_plans[c]` for both), so a placement source's offsets reach both passes; the
  shadow-mask pass too. A unit with no fight set is placed exactly as by the inner source (test
  `fight_placement_no_fight_no_change`).
- **The 4981 seam:** the extras' root override is applied before `prepare` (`UnitInput::has_root`), so the inner
  placement already stands on it and the fight's offsets come after it in the unit's own frame, as agreed (#7520,
  `extras-units.md` 4981.1 item 2); a unit held in a fight gets no extra's override (item 3), so `ApplyUnitXforms` does
  not turn it.
- **Not wired here:** the server sets `FightPlacement` with `UnitRenderer::setPlacementSource`, builds one
  `FightMotion` per fight from `CombatRun::result()` with `combatPositions` of both units, and hands each fighting unit
  its fight's clock until `offsets` returns false after the end (the return walk). That is the server's adapter of 4782 /
  4774 (`server/src/units/`, not this ticket's touches).

## 6. The per-unit hold and the fight player (4774)

Written 2026-11-20 06:00-08:30 EST by W11 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w11-4774`, route S (the owner's D210; the
Architect's note 3.1; breakdown 11.1 and 12). Marks as in sections 3-4: `[C]` checked by this worker in code or tests
(each names the check), `[C 0321]` a rule as `combat-choreography.md` reads it, `[L x]` recorded live by ticket x, `[I]`
this section's reading. Offline only; no game instance, no EXE address.

### 6.1 What it is

- **The hold** (`server/src/units/srv_units_queue.{h,cpp}`, `UnitHold`): the ops of kinds 12 moved, 13 teleported, 14
  destroyed, 15 died in combat, 16 damage, 30 rebased and the EXE's arrival of a walk (mode exe, `AnimFeed::arrive`) of a
  unit that a pending or playing fight names wait in that unit's queue, each owned by the latest fight that named the unit
  when it came. At a fight's end (any `FightEnd`) the front run of each of its units' queues whose owners have all ended
  comes back, and `AnimFeed` sorts what came back by the DLL's seq (an arrive carries the seq of the event taken before it).
  So what came between fight A and fight B on one unit comes back at A's end, before B starts (0321 3.4 [C 0321]); other
  kinds (fortify, visibility, work, embark, ...) and other units pass [C: `fight_hold`, `fight_two_on_one_unit`,
  `TestTwoFightsOneUnit`]. A combat with Quick Combat on or not visualised makes no fight (4782's clock), so it holds
  nothing and everything passes at once [C: `fight_quick_combat`].
- **The drawn state** (`HoldView`): the feed's unit table is final at once (the combat, the damage, the death and the move
  usually come in one drain, 4771 P1 [L 4771]), and `UnitsCore::buildList` draws plot, damage (the figure count) and
  presence from it. So a held unit is drawn from its view: the unit as it was listed in the last drawn frame before its
  hold began (plot, root, facing, damage, flags, seed, type, art row, the wrap copies it was in), plus the ops of the same
  frame that passed before the combat, plus the ops that come back at a fight's end (damage, place, move to the path's last
  plot, death). A held unit whose removal waits stays listed in the copies it was last listed in, with its player row
  [C: `fight_hold`, `TestView`]. The view is applied in `AnimRunner::fillFigures` (the host and unitfeed call it for copies
  0, 1, 2 after `apply`), so no hunk in `srv_units_core.*` draws it. Mode exe: a held unit keeps its view's root, and a kind 12 that passed before its combat or came back does not
  move its view (the core's walk places the unit: it stands at the plot it left until its positions come, `test_unitfeed.py
  ::test_positions_option`); the
  kind-6 position records still go into the core as they come and are seen once the hold ends (the drawn unit then stands
  at the newest one) [I: under 4773's hold the EXE's `Moved` and its positions come after the drop anyway, note 3.1].
- **The fights** (`AnimFeed`, `srv_units_anim.cpp`): `take()` keeps each combat record (25 / 28) with its damage members in
  the DLL's order; `close()` calls `fightsFrame` once per drawn frame, before the frame's ops are mapped: (1) the clock's
  `frame(seq, dt)` (fights added in earlier frames start, so the controller has applied their units' creates; playing ones
  advance), the player's events appended to this timeline frame (so the `.c5anim` records them and `unitanim play`
  replays them), (2) the fights' ends give their ops back, (3) this frame's ops through the hold in seq order: a combat adds
  its fight (and freezes its units' views), a waiting op of a held unit waits, a load (kind 32) ends every fight with
  OwnerEnd `Reset` and drops the held ops, a removal that passes a broken hold ends that unit's fights (`unitGone`).
- **The FightPlayer adapter** (`ControllerFightPlayer` in `srv_units_anim.cpp`, owned by `AnimRunner`): `start` maps the
  record to the 4775 core's `CombatInput` (the flag bits are the same; a unit side's maximum HP from the controller's
  unit input, a city's 100 [I: not in the record]), takes each unit side's figures from the controller (`combatFigures`),
  the clip timings from the controller's art (`combatClips`, durations read once per clip with the runner's loader) and
  starts a `CombatRun` with `ControllerFeedback`; a refusal (the core's code and text, or the controller's: a unit not
  held, the combat tables unreadable) ends the fight in its start frame. `advance` steps the run by the frame's dt;
  `end` drops it and reports a fight that reached the limit (with both sides' planned and played deaths and owed hits) and
  the core's notes (a missing clip, no hit trigger). The air flag of the plan: a member whose domain is Air.
- **The runner** (`AnimRunner::apply`): sets the scene's 'held in a fight' field (`UnitsCore::setHeldInFight`, 4981's seam,
  agreed with lead-0455 #7522) for every unit a fight names and clears it after; adds those units to the controller's drawn
  set, so a fighter the cull or the fog leaves out still steps (otherwise its attack clip never plays and the live core
  holds the fight to its limit, 4.3); logs the feed's LOUD texts through `UnitsCore::note(AnimFailed, ...)` (the first 20,
  then every 100th) [I: a status of its own would need a `srv_units_core.h` line; AnimFailed is the controller's family].
- **The ends** (`FightEndRecord`: the OwnerEnd, the frame id and frame seq it closed in, the ops it gave back) are kept for
  the trigger stream (4795) and the proxy's hold (4773: OwnerEnd(event id = `CombatRecord::returned`), lead-0042 #7862);
  nothing sends them yet. unitfeed writes them to `fights.tsv` (the file form: seq, event_id, owner_known, why, elapsed_s,
  exe_frame, frame_seq, released, text) and prints a `fights` and a `hold` line.
- **Limits** (named, counted, LOUD): a unit queue over 256 ops or all queues over 8192: that unit's queue comes back at once
  in order, and it passes everything until its fights end ("broken") [C: `fight_overflow`, `TestOverflowUnit`,
  `TestOverflowTotal`]. An end for a fight that held nothing changes nothing (counted `endsUnknown`) [C: `TestUnknownEnd`].

**Seam hunks** (lead-0042 #7867, agreed with lead-0455 #7864; one line each): **H1** `srv_units_core.cpp`
`UnitsCore::onBatch`, the combat branch after `m_c.combatNotes++;`: `if(m_anim) m_anim->take(e, b);` (combat records reach
`srv_units_anim` in the DLL's order; before 4774 they reached only the seed allocator). **H2** `srv_units_scene.cpp`, the
host's controller open beside `m_animFeed.setBuilds(r->builds());`: `m_animFeed.setRunner(r.get());`. No
`srv_units_core.h` hunk: `setHeldInFight` / `heldInFight` existed (4981). `srv_units_fights.cpp` now builds inside
test_scene_units.exe and unitfeed.exe (the units glob; clang-cl /W3 /WX and MSVC ASan) with no change. **Link break
fixed on the way:** since 0598 `srv_render_scene.cpp` calls the model module (`srvmodels::FrameEye`,
`server/src/render/landmarks/`), which `build_units_tests.py` and `build_unitfeed.py` do not compile, so neither links
on the team branch after stage 2c (`lld-link: undefined symbol srvmodels::FrameEye`). The MC's ruling #7945: the fix is
account A's on main (FrameEye and its partner inline in `srv_models_scene.h`, no builder change); 4774's runs here used a
local, uncommitted copy of both builders with the `landmarks/` and `cities/` globs of `build_server.render_sources`.

### 6.4 Where 4772 and 4774 meet (the merge; 4724 item 0)

Written 2026-11-20 08:30-09:10 EST by W18 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w18-4724` from lead-0042's merge 20b677385
(team branch dbff56d2a + `w11-4774` 666dd8e77; the conflicts with 4772 in `srv_units_anim.{h,cpp}` and
`test_scene_units.cpp` resolved as unions). Offline only.

- **The merge as resolved builds and passes** [C: runs of 2026-11-20 08:27-08:36 EST, workstation]: `render/build.py --test
  -R c5r_unitanim` 24 of 24; unitfeed and test_scene_units link (with an untracked local double of `srvmodels::FrameEye`,
  0598's link break, 6.1); test_scene_units 63 of 63 plain (58 + 4772's 5); `run_units_queue_test.py --asan` 8542 passed,
  0 failed, ASan PASS.
- **Held unit vs walk facing: correct as merged** [C: code read, `merge_walk_held_fight`]. `AnimRunner::fillFigures`
  applies the walk facings first and the held units' views over them, and `HoldView::remember` stores the list after both,
  so a unit a fight names is drawn with its frozen view's facing, never a walk facing; a view is taken from the list as
  drawn (a walking unit is frozen with its walk facing of that frame). The fight's own events are Action and Kill only
  (`combat.cpp`), so `WalkFacings::follow` never sees them.
- **Fix 1, a walk's turns while the unit is held** [C: `merge_walk_held_fight`]. As merged, a walk open when a fight began
  (the move passed before the combat, mode exe) went on sampling the EXE's positions and gave `turn` events during the fight,
  while its arrive waited in the hold: the turns came out among the fight's events, ahead of the ops the hold gives back.
  Now `AnimFeed::walkHeadings` skips a unit that `UnitHold::named` names (no sample, no turn); at the hold's end the step
  from the sample before the hold to the newest position gives one turn to the newest heading, after the ops given back
  in that frame (`damage:2001,turn:1001`). The controller takes `turn` as no request (`unit-controller.md` 14.1), so the
  change is to the timeline and the drawn facing's bookkeeping only.
- **Fix 2, a given-back arrive deferred into the next fight** [C: `merge_released_arrive`]. 4755's rule defers an arrive
  whose unit's move is in the same frame. When the hold gives back a move and its arrive together (both held by fight A),
  the deferred arrive went through the hold again in the next frame, where fight B on the same unit (queued behind A) now
  holds it: the walk stayed open through B. Now an arrive the hold gave back (`Op::released`) is not deferred: the EXE's
  arrival had already happened, so move and arrive come in A's end frame and the walk is closed before B starts.
- **Open, for 4773 / 4724's live runs** [I]: a fight that begins while its attacker's walk is open in mode exe freezes the
  attacker where it was last drawn (mid-walk or on the plot it left), and the EXE's arrival of that walk waits in the hold
  until the fight ends, although in the EXE's own queue that arrival comes before `RunCombatSim`. Whether the fight should
  instead wait for the walk's arrival is a FightClock start rule (4782), not changed here; 6.3's "cannot happen" for an open
  walk at the hold's start is corrected to "can happen in mode exe: the DLL's move and attack come in one drain or a few
  frames apart, the EXE's walk takes longer".

### 6.5 The figure motion wired in the server (4724)

Written 2026-11-20 09:00-10:00 EST by W18 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w18-4724`. Offline only (no game instance). This
closes 5.2's "Not wired here" and 6.3's third item. `[C]` = checked in this branch's code or tests, `[I]` = this section's
reading.

- **Where it sits.** `AnimRunner` (`srv_units_anim.{h,cpp}`) owns the drawing renderer's placement source:
  `MotionPlacement` -> 4776's `FightPlacement` -> the module's own placement (`makeModulePlacement` of the same install, the
  same code the renderer would use without a source). With no fight set a unit is placed exactly as before
  (`fight_placement_no_fight_no_change`, 5.3) [C].
- **Host hunks** (lead-0042 with lead-0455, #8027; two lines in `srv_units_scene.cpp`, nothing else there): **H3**
  `UnitsHost::openDraw`, after `setPoseSource`: `m_draw->setPlacementSource(m_anim ? m_anim->fightPlacement(m_env->gf,
  m_env->install) : nullptr)`. **H4** `UnitsHost::beginFrame`, before `animFrame`: `m_anim->setGrid(grid)`. With
  ServerUnits off there is no unit host; with the controller off (`render_units_anim=0`) `m_anim` is null and both lines do
  nothing (the module's own placement, as before) [C: code; `anim_off`, `anim_unavailable` pass].
- **(b) The grid and the formation table: both.** The formation table is read by the runner from the install
  (`FormationTable::load(files, installRoot)`, the module's rule: the loose 24-entry `UnitFormations.xml` first), because
  `FightPlacement` needs an inner module placement anyway and `makeModulePlacement` takes the same two inputs, which H3
  hands over. The grid comes by H4 because the fight starts inside `animFrame` (the feed's close), before the frame's
  `prepare`: a grid pointer kept from the previous frame's placement requests could outlive a re-bake of the scene's grid.
  When either is missing (`fightPlacement` returns null with `motionWhy()`, or no grid) the fight runs without positions:
  the core's fixed 1.0 s approach and no motion, counted `noPositions`, as before 4724 [C: `motion_no_grid`].
- **Start positions** (`ControllerFightPlayer::positions`): each unit side through `combatPositions` on this frame's grid,
  with the unit's placement input as `MotionPlacement` last saw it (kept only for units a fight names: the frozen view's

## 7. The trigger stream's contract (4721)

Written 2026-11-20 06:52-07:50 EST by W13 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w13-4721`, route S (decision D210; the
Architect's note `research/07-architecture-decisions/architect-2026-11-20-route-s-combat.md` 1.3-1.6, with the MC's
correction of 1.6 from 4799). Stage 1 of 4795: the contract that 4722 (the server's emitter), 4723 (the shell's sound
executor) and 4793 (effect routes) build on. Marks: `[C]` checked by this worker in code or tests (each names the check),
`[I]` this section's design choice or reading. Offline only; no game instance, no EXE address, no game name in git.

### 7.1 What it is

- `shell/common/vp_trigger.h` (new; path agreed with lead-0590, thread 0590 #7888, the MC's republish v12 #7886): the
  record, the name table, the shared section's layout, the rules R1-R8 in its head comment, and small inline helpers for
  both sides (`VPTrigInit`, `VPTrigAddName`, `VPTrigWrite`, `VPTrigStop` for the server; `VPTrigReadNext`,
  `VPTrigPublishReader`, `VPTrigNameAt` for the shell; `VPTrigPlayedFor`, `VPTrigIsFightEnd`). It holds no EXE address,
  no symbol of `exebuild/symbols/*.tsv`, no `vp_exe_*.h` include and no game name (lead-0590's conditions, D83, D202);
  it includes only `<stdint.h>`, `<stddef.h>`, `<string.h>` and `<intrin.h>`. `vp_frame.h`, `shell_shared.h`,
  `exe_camera.h` and `shell/build.cmd` are untouched.
- `render/include/c5r/unitanim/trigger_log.h`, `render/src/unitanim/trigger_log.cpp` (new): the offline trigger log
  (D137): the text form, its parser, the server's writer, and `checkTriggerRecord`, the contract's checks of one record.
- Tests: `render/tests/unitanim/test_trigger_record.cpp` (the header alone, self-contained, also built as an x86
  program), `test_trigger_log.cpp` (the log), `vp_trigger_vc9_probe.cpp` (a compile-only probe for the proxy's
  environment, not a ctest). No build file changed: `render/src/unitanim/` and `render/tests/unitanim/` are globbed, and
  `c5render` already has `shell/common` on its public include path (`render/src/landmarks/CMakeLists.txt`).

### 7.2 The record [C: static_asserts in the header; the same offsets measured at run time on x64 and x86]

128 bytes, alignment 8, `#pragma pack(push, 8)`, no implicit padding, identical for the x64 server and the x86 shell.

| Offset | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `uint64 seq` | the record's number in its generation, from 1; the slot's seqlock (R4) |
| 8 | `int64 frameId` | F: the frame whose insertion executes it (vp_frame.h's frame id) |
| 16 | `uint16 version` | `VPTRIG_VERSION` (1) |
| 18 | `uint8 kind` | 1 SoundStart, 2 SoundStop, 3 EffectStart, 4 EffectMove, 5 EffectStop, 6 OwnerEnd |
| 19 | `uint8 reason` | OwnerEnd: 0 Natural, 1 Limit, 2 Refused, 3 Gone, 4 Reset, 5 ClipEnded (= `FightEnd` of section 4.1, number for number); 0 otherwise |
| 20 | `uint32 flags` | 0x1 loop, 0x2 follows its owner (Start records only), 0x4 played (OwnerEnd only) |
| 24 | `uint32 owner` | the fight's id = `CombatRecord::returned` (the EXE's event id of the `RunCombatSim` record, the DLL's parent id); 0 = not known |
| 28 | `uint32 fightSeq` | the combat record's seq (names the fight when owner is 0); 0 = no fight |
| 32, 36, 40 | `int32 player, unit, figure` | the figure's unit and the figure (member order); figure -1 = the unit or the fight itself |
| 44 | `uint32 handle` | the server's handle of a sound or effect (from 1, unique per generation); 0 = none (OwnerEnd) |
| 48 | `uint64 instance` | the clip instance that fired it (`FigureProgram::instance`, section 4.3); 0 = the fight itself |
| 56 | `uint32 name` | name table index of the audio script or effect (0 = none) |
| 60 | `uint32 file` | name table index of the trigger file (for the log; 0 = none) |
| 64 | `float pos[3]` | world position x, y, z, z up (HexToWorld's order; the 3D play's `&pos`, `exe-audio.md` 2 step 4) |
| 76 | `float scale` | effects: scale (EffectStart > 0); 0 for sound and OwnerEnd |
| 80 | `float orient[4]` | effects: orientation quaternion x, y, z, w; 0 for sound and OwnerEnd |
| 96 | `float vel[3]` | effects: velocity, world units per second; 0 for sound and OwnerEnd |
| 108, 112 | `int32 ec, trigger` | the trigger's identity: its clip's ec and its trigger id in the file (-1 none) |
| 116 | `float clipTime` | the trigger's time in its clip (s) |
| 120 | `float late` | how late against frame F's time (s, >= 0); the server drops one-shots over 0.1 s (note 1.5 item 1) |
| 124 | `uint32 reserved0` | 0 |

The name table: 4,096 entries of 128 bytes (`uint32 kind`: 1 sound3d, 2 effect, 3 triggerfile; `uint32 length`; 120
bytes of NUL-terminated text, at most 119 characters), index 0 unused. Sizes against the install (read at run time
from the Steam install's files, 2026-11-20, nothing copied) [C]: the longest `ScriptID` of the 17,960 rows of the
`*3DScripts.xml` files is 64 characters; the longest trigger `event` attribute in the loose `.ftsxml` files 41 and their
file names 43 (only 7 loose `.ftsxml` files; the 673 of `exe-audio.md` 0 are inside the packs, not measured here). A
name that does not fit is refused and counted (`namesRefused`), never cut.

What the shell needs for the EXE's 3D play (`exe-audio.md` 2, 4.3, 8) is in the record or one lookup away: the script
index from `name` (the shell resolves each name once per generation through `ICvEngineUtility1::GetAudioTagIndex`,
`AUDIOTAG_3DSCRIPT`, which the proxy already carries), the world point from `pos`; the returned `FSound` pointer is kept
by the shell under (`handle`, the owner fields) for SoundStop, the owner's end and the watchdogs. The record carries no
loop argument for the play (a loop is the script's own property, `exe-audio.md` 4.2): the loop flag tells the shell
which sounds it must stop at the owner's end.

### 7.3 Ring beside the frame ring, not a wire record [I, argued]

The records live in a second shared section, `<base>.Trig` (`VPTRIG_SECTION_BYTES` = 1,048,832 bytes: a 128-byte
server block, a 128-byte reader block, the name table at 256, a ring of 4,096 records at 524,544), created-or-opened by
both sides like `<base>.Frame`. Why not the frame section itself: it is 4,096 bytes with 2,048 used and its header is
not to be touched (lead-0590's condition); a ring of 4,096 records does not fit there anyway. Why not a wire record (a
server -> proxy runtime method of `proxy/include/vp_wire.h`):

1. **Frame alignment by construction.** The shell executes a record at the insertion of its frame (note 1.4). In the
   section, R1 makes it visible before that frame's slot is READY, so the insertion that waits for frame F already has
   F's records. A message on the IPC arrives on the proxy's channel thread with no order against the frame ring: the
   proxy would need its own queue keyed by frame and a rule for records that arrive after their frame was shown.
2. **The executor reads where it already is.** The insertion (vp_frame.h step 3) runs on the EXE's main thread, the
   thread the audio entries need (`exe-audio.md` 8: "main thread only"); it maps sections by the same `<base>` name.
   No thread hop, no lock, no allocation on the frame path.
3. **No traffic when nothing happens**, and none per record: the server writes memory; the shell reads at its own
   frame. The IPC stays the DLL's channel.
4. **The OwnerEnd for the proxy's hold** (4773) is in the same stream: the executor calls
   `OwnerEnd(owner, played)` (R8) from the record, in frame order with the sounds it ends.

Costs: one more named section (1 MB), and the shell's watchdogs must cover a broken stream (they do anyway: note 1.5
item 3; the hold's own watchdog, 4773).

### 7.4 The rules (the header's R1-R8, in short)

R1 records in seq order, frame ids never decreasing, all of frame F written before F's slot is READY. R2 at the
insertion of frame G the shell executes every unread record with frameId <= G, in order, and keeps the first later one.
R3 the server never blocks: with a reader attached (and of the same generation) and fewer than 256 free records it drops
everything but OwnerEnd (counted `droppedFull`); a reader that finds records overwritten jumps and counts them
(`lostTotal`), and its watchdogs end what they would have ended. R4 a slot's `seq` is 0 while written and the record's
seq after; the reader copies only when it reads the expected seq before and after (64-bit loads by
`_InterlockedCompareExchange64` on x86). R5 names are published before the first record that names them; index 0 = no
name. R6 a new generation at each server init; the reader then ends every owner with Reset and drops its name cache; an
orderly stop (magic 0) reads the same way. R7 Start records name an owner (fight, or player and unit); OwnerEnd with
figure -1 and instance 0 ends a fight, with a figure and an instance (ClipEnded) a clip instance; loops of an ended owner
stop, one-shots ring out. R8 a fight OwnerEnd with owner != 0 goes to `proxy_combat_hold`'s `OwnerEnd(eventId = owner,
played)` (4773's form, #7862): played is set for Natural and Limit, clear for Refused, Gone and Reset; owner 0 is
counted, never passed on. ClipEnded carries played set and never reaches the hold. *Added 2026-11-20 (ticket 4783):
R9 route S arms as one: the server asks in its block's reserved words (`routeSAsk`, `routeSTaken`), the shell answers in
the reader block's (`routeSGen`, `routeSState`, `routeSParts`, `routeSBuild`), and the server writes no record of a
generation whose answer is not ARMED; section 16.1.*

Memory order: no `<atomic>` (the proxy builds against the VC9 headers, which have none, `proxy/build_proxy.py`); the
helpers put a compiler barrier between the volatile accesses, which on x86 and x64 (stores not reordered with stores,
loads not with loads) gives the release and acquire order the rules need; no rule needs store -> load order [I, the
two-thread test below is the check].

### 7.5 The offline trigger log (D137)

Text, one line per name and per record (`trigger_log.h` has the grammar):

```
# c5r trigger log 1
N 1 sound3d <script id>
N 2 triggerfile <trigger file name>
R v=1 seq=1 F=345 kind=SoundStart reason=- flags=loop owner=11259375 fseq=7 player=1 unit=8193 figure=2 handle=17 inst=55 name=1 file=2 pos=1.5,-2.25,0.100000001 scale=0 orient=0,0,0,0 vel=0,0,0 ec=1100 trig=3 t=0.400000006 late=0.0166666675
R v=1 seq=9 F=400 kind=OwnerEnd reason=Limit flags=played owner=11259375 fseq=7 player=1 unit=8193 figure=-1 handle=0 inst=0 name=0 file=0 pos=0,0,0 scale=0 orient=0,0,0,0 vel=0,0,0 ec=0 trig=-1 t=0 late=0
```

Keys are written in a fixed order and read in any order, each exactly once; floats with 9 significant digits (exact
for a float); kinds, reasons and flags by name (an unknown flag bit as `0x..`). The reader (`parseTriggerLog`,
`readTriggerLog`) refuses a log whose header or version is wrong, a name out of order or a record naming an index not
declared before it (R5), a record that fails `checkTriggerRecord`, and a seq or frame id that goes back (R1).
`TriggerLogWriter` refuses the same before writing anything. Logs carry names from the player's install: they stay
outside git (D83).

`checkTriggerRecord` is the contract as code: version, kind, frame id >= 0, known flags, reserved 0, finite floats,
late >= 0, loop / follows on Start records only, OwnerEnd's played = `VPTrigPlayedFor(reason)`, OwnerEnd with no handle
or name, a fight OwnerEnd naming a fight with figure -1 and instance 0, a ClipEnded naming player, unit, figure and
instance, every other kind with a handle, Starts with a name and an owner, no name outside Starts, orientation / scale /
velocity only on effects, EffectStart scale > 0.

### 7.8 Not verified, open

  records over its seconds; the name count of a long game is not measured. Both are header constants under one version.

  says they cover lost records.

  kind is kept for explicit stops of the server's own (an owner's end stops loops without it).

## 8. Special cases (4777)

Written 2026-11-20 07:14-09:30 EST by W14 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w14-4777`. Marks as in section 3: `[C]`
checked by this worker in this repository's code or tests (each names the check), `[C 0321]` a rule as
`combat-choreography.md` reads it from the EXE's code, `[C DLL]` read in the DLL's source (the x64 fork's
`CvUnitCombat.cpp`), `[D]` read in the database copy of 4872 (VP 5.4.x), `[L x]` recorded live by ticket x, `[I]` this
section's reading. Offline only: no game instance, no EXE address, nothing from the EXE or the game's files in git.

### 8.1 What is built

The core (`combat.h`, `combat.cpp`, `combat_tables.cpp`) no longer refuses the four cases 4782's clock listed
(`CityAttacker`, `AirCombat`, `Nuclear`, `AreaMembers`): it plays them. The `CombatCode` values stay for the callers'
texts. The participants are a list, as in 0321 4.1: attacker 0, defender 1, the interceptor 2 when named, then each
damage member. A participant without figures (a city, the nuke's plot, a member whose figures the caller does not give)
takes part as a centre only.

| Case | Rule as built | Source |
|---|---|---|
| A city attacks | The city has no figures. Its volley leaves the city's centre `city_strike_at` (0.5 s) after the start, one shot per open need of the defender (its planned deaths and its owed hit), `city_stagger` (0.1 s) apart, each landing `city_flight` (0.6 s) after it leaves. The defender, which does not retaliate against a ranged strike, bombard-defends (1280). | [I] every time; 0321 5.5 for the figureless city; no recording exists |
| A city defends | 4775's rule (the attacker's planned deaths fall at its first hit on the city), now with the city's centre as the origin and the caller's `city_effect` / `city_sound`. | 4775 [I], 4777 |
| Air limit | 20 s when a figure of any participant is an air figure, 12 s otherwise. | [C 0321] 4.2, 13.2 |
| Aircraft out and back | An air figure of the attacker or the interceptor flies straight from its base to its target. The speed is `MoveRate` x 64 (the Heavy Bomber's 5.4: 345.6 world units per second [D]) and the height is `AttackAltitude` (default 90 [C 4776 M1]; the Atomic Bomb has 110, the Nuclear Missile 160 [D]). It stops within `MoveRadius` of its target (a city or plot: `city_reach`). When nothing is left to strike it flies home and ends there, descending (`FigureMove::air`, `back`, `z0`, `z1`). A flight out that is under way when the needs end is cut where the figure turns. Without positions each leg lasts `air_flight` (1.0 s). No victory pose for an aircraft. | [I] the flight; [L 0456] 12.2: at the limit the bombers vanish (no flight home), which the core does too |
| Air strike code and weapon | Over the ground or the sea the aircraft requests 1180 (bombard), in the air 1100. The first of the pair that the member enables and binds is used. Over a target that is not in the air it drops its `IsDropped` weapon when it has one: it falls `AttackAltitude / (ProjectileSpeed x 64)` s (the Heavy Bomber 1.56 s) and lands below the striker. | [I] the code; [C 0321] 13.5 the drop point; [I] the unit of `ProjectileSpeed` |
| Air opening (13.4) | When the attacker's side is air and the defender's is not, and the attacker's damage in this combat is known: 0 means the defender bombard-defends and the attacker owes no hit (0477's fix sends exactly this); more than 0 means the defender answers whatever the retaliate byte says. Not known (-1): the retaliate byte decides. | [C 0321] 13.4 |
| The answer to an air side | A sea figure requests 1130, a land figure 1180, whatever its `EnableActions`. With `CombatMemberArt::anti_air` 0 (a machine that takes no 1130: the submarines' `1_OMNI`) the answer never plays and the fight holds to its limit, as stock's strike on a submarine does. With -1 (not known), a member that binds no 1130 clip plays its attack clip instead (the ships' machines map 1130 to it); in live mode `playing()` of that clip counts. | [C 0321] 13.5, [L 0477] |
| Interception | Participant 2 (`CombatInput::interceptor`). Its figures strike the attacker; an air interceptor flies out and back as above. The defender owes its hit only when there is no interceptor or the attacker keeps figures standing. [I] An interceptor whose damage is more than 0 takes one owed hit from an attacker without planned deaths. The DLL's aborted interception sends the attacker's final damage as 0 [C DLL `GenerateAirCombatInfo`], so without this rule the interception would show nothing. The attacker strikes the interceptor only once the defender has no open need. | [C 0321] 13.4, [I] |
| Naval | A ship's melee attack approaches as a land figure does (`ships_approach`, default on). Off, ships strike from where they stand. | [I], chosen by 0557 n1-n3 (8.4) |
| Nuclear | The defender may name neither unit nor city: the plot target. The DLL's nuclear record has no defender unless a city intercepts [C DLL `GenerateNuclearCombatInfo`]. The attacker's first hit on the defender (or the plot) is the blast. Every damage member that has figures, and with a nuclear strike the defender too, loses all its planned deaths `AreaDamageDelay` (0.5 s [D]) after it, as `area` hits. A collision attacker (`HasCollisionAttack`, the Nuclear Missile [D]) dies at its own hit. A `WaitForEffectCompletion` weapon holds the fight for its effect: `CombatClips::effectDuration(name)`, else `effect_wait` (10.3 s: the missiles' end minus flash in 0553, 10.11 / 10.43 / 10.43 s). A weapon with no `HitEffect` (the Atomic Bomb's dropped bomb) holds to the 20 s limit with `unnamed_effect_holds` (default on), which is stock's behaviour (0560). | [C 0321] 3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 5.5; [L 0553]; [I] the rule for the bomb |
| Area members (garrison) | The same area rule without a nuke: a garrison (a unit damage member of a city attack) loses its planned deaths at the attacker's first hit on the city, and its figures bombard-defend meanwhile. | [I], compared with 0557 g1-g3 |

## 9. Unit shadows in a fight (4784)

Ticket 4784 (the spike; 4785 builds what it chose). Written 2026-11-20 08:13- EST by w17-0042 (account B, branch
`w17-4784` from `epic-0042-combat-movement`). Static part: this repository's code and knowledge base, and 3907's stock
capture exports read in place (`F:/c5-64bit-work/0301/3907/exports/`, numbers only, D83); the live part (9.6) on a grant.
Marks as in the head of this file; EXE addresses are build 4390913's, as the knowledge base already holds them (D202:
none of build 26577625). Scripts and outputs: `server/evidence/0042/4784/`.

### 9.0 Decision

**(b), with the drop of (a): the server draws its own units' shadow mask, resamples it with the EXE's own resample
program, and adds it into the tapped shadow map before its terrain and water sample it; the compositor drops the EXE's
unit mask draws while a new mode bit says the server casts the units' shadows.** Neither half alone works:

- The breakdown's (b) without a drop (11.1: "the server draws its own unit mask and merges it", no `shell/composite/`)
  doubles every shadow: the EXE's idle figures keep casting into the tapped map while the server's figures cast where
  they stand. 4785's acceptance ("no doubled shadow") cannot pass. So (b) needs the filter change too; the shell files
  are needed by both options (9.4).
- (a) as written ("the server draws its units into the shadow mask it taps") has two readings. Into the tap's copy on
  the server's side, without the EXE's resample, it puts an unblurred mask into a resampled map (already rejected,
  `unit-server-scene.md` 7). Into the EXE's own ShadowRaw before the EXE's resample (the composite drawing a mask the
  server publishes, as `srv_fow_mask_pub` / `fow_models.cpp` do for the fog) it is exact in the resample but costs a new
  insertion inside the EXE's shadow chain and puts every unit shadow one to two frames behind its model (9.3).

Why (b): the units' shadow is drawn in the server's frame with the very ShadowMatrix0 of the triple it binds, from the
same pose as the model, so it cannot lag or misalign; the resample is the EXE's own program (read from the install's
`.shader` section at run time, as the unit programs are), so it equals stock's by construction; the merge rule (add) is
exact wherever a unit's mask does not touch a city block's (9.2); the EXE does less work (its unit mask draws are
dropped) instead of more; and it is what true absence (0328) needs, with no EXE figure left. **Hours for 4785: 10-16 h**
(9.5), against the ticket's 6-12.

### 9.1 The shadow path today (0169) [C, L as cited]

1. **The EXE's pass, every map frame** (`terrain-surface.md` 9, 11 S1): the shadow pass (0x523CA0, both 3D renders)
   returns at once at quality q 0 or without ShadowRaw; else it clears **ShadowRaw** (`[0xDA12B8]`: the back buffer's
   size, R16G16B16A16_FLOAT, 1 mip) and lets each caster system draw into it, gated by its view-mask bit: **Unit 0x40
   first**, then City 0x20, Landmark 0x2 (then DynamicGeometry), Particle 0x1000 (off under D33 as 4302 ran it; the
   product keeps Particle on since D147, so particles may cast too: not looked at here). Then the **resample**
   (0x5580B0, q >= 2 only) draws one quad from ShadowRaw into **ShadowBlur** (`[0xDA12BC]`: 2048 x 2048 R16_UNORM at q 3,
   1024 x 1024 at q 2; at q 1 ShadowBlur is ShadowRaw's own handle, unresampled; at q 0 a 4 x 4 of zeros). q is the ini's
   `ShadowLevel` (11.9). Under D33 no EXE draw reads ShadowBlur.
2. **The units' mask draws** (`unit-draws.md` 1): pass 1 of every unit figure, VS `8cb52b96` / PS `72c27aea` (material
   90), PS `246527ed` (89), VS `59af33ff` / PS `9a5991d7` (87); view-projection = ShadowMatrix0 (byte-equal, 24 of 24
   exports, `unit-server-scene.md` 7 R2); no depth, cull front, **blend off**. The PS writes (1, 1, 1, alpha) with
   alpha = the mesh-instance's palette header row 1 fade (1 for a shown unit) times 0.33 below the water height
   (cb1[8].x) [C, the program's register use; values 0, 0.3298, 1 seen in the captured masks]. The server's unit module
   already has this pass (`c5r::units::PassKind::ShadowMask`, the same programs read from the install): 221 of 228 units
   bit-equal against the captured mask draws, 728,599 of 737,090 pixels (`unit-renderer.md` 13, C) [L, offline].
3. **The tap** (`terrain-surface.md` 11.9, `shell-composite-taps.md` 2): `shell/composite/shadow_tap.cpp` copies
   ShadowBlur at each map frame's Present into one of three NT-shared slots (`Local\VPShellShadowTex.<pid>.<slot>.<epoch>`)
   with the frame's ShadowMatrix0 per view (at most 4), the strength `[0xD90FA8]` (Arg6) and q; the server's
   `ShadowTapReader::acquire` (`server/src/render/srv_shadow_tap.cpp`) takes the newest whole slot once per loop
   iteration; `Scene::draw` (`srv_render_scene.cpp`, the block "issue 4308: the shadow triple of this frame") binds it
   as terrain t3 / Arg6 / ShadowMatrix0 per wrap copy and water t13 / 0x220. The terrain PS samples `saturate(t3.r) *
   Arg6` at p = (world, 1) x ShadowMatrix0.
4. **Under `ServerUnits = 1` today** the compositor drops only the units' pass-0 draws and keeps the mask draws
   (`kVPUnitKeep`, `shell/common/unit_programs.h`; 0375 decision 7 (c)): the shadows on the ground are the EXE's idle
   figures', the "named difference" of `epic-0040-breakdown.md` 1.1 that route S turns into a visible one (figures
   charging, shadows standing).

### 9.2 What the spike established (static) [C, L as marked]

- **M1, the unit mask programs draw only unit figures into ShadowRaw** [C, `mask_premise.py` over 3907's 28 exports,
  `mask_premise_out.txt`]: 628 draws bind a unit mask PS; 0 with another VS than its pair's; all `DrawIndexedInstanced`;
  all into the one ShadowRaw target. Other pairs draw into the same target: city blocks (`88c2b7d4` / `73daa800`, 681),
  landmarks and DynamicGeometry (`e12e9eaf` with three vertex programs, 976), material 3 colour draws (`c4bb25da` /
  `f0e1f0a6`, 33; `city-renderer.md` 5.1) and SimpleShader (`3c39dd7e` / `c8ddf172`, 6). So dropping the three unit mask
  pairs removes the units' shadows and nothing else, as the pass-0 drop does for the models (S1 of
  `unit-draw-filter.md` 1).
- **M2, the composition rule of ShadowRaw** [C, `mask_blend.py` on L01, S01, c_ancient, L10, `mask_blend_out.txt`]: unit
  and city-block mask draws have blend off (last writer wins, alpha 1 for blocks: PS `73daa800` writes (1, 1, 1, 1));
  landmark and DynamicGeometry mask draws (PS `e12e9eaf`: alpha = the texture's alpha, 0 at or below 0.1, halved below a
  height) blend colour SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA and **alpha ONE / ONE (added)**; the material 3 colour draws blend the
  same way. Captured masks hold alpha values 2 and 3 where landmarks overlap (S01, c_ancient). With the pass order
  (Unit, City, Landmark) a ShadowRaw texel's alpha is (block ? 1 : unit) + the sum of the landmarks' alphas.
- **R1, the resample** [C, the program's register use read from the export (`shaders/2047_be955cbb.dxbc`, not
  committed, D83), the draw's state; L, emulated]: one indexed quad (6 indices) over the whole target, VS `c7615a1d`, PS
  `be955cbb` (material 70 `ShadowShader`, pass 0); cb1 = (1/W, 1/H, -1/W, -1/H) for ShadowRaw's W x H (L01: 1/2554,
  1/1411); sampler MIN_MAG_MIP_LINEAR, WRAP; blend off; target ShadowBlur. The output is **the mean of eight bilinear
  samples of ShadowRaw's alpha**, at (+-1, +-1) and (+-0.5, +-0.5) source texels around the target texel's centre,
  written to every channel (R16_UNORM: saturated to [0, 1]). It is linear in the alpha. An emulation on the CPU
  (`resample_check.py`, 8 fractional bits of filter weight) against the captured pairs (frame-start contents of both,
  so the previous frame's mask and blur) of L01, S01, c_ancient and L10: max 163-244 of 65,535 (0.37 %), median 2-7, 97.2-
  98.3 % within 64 over the 28,525-119,146 texels either side shades (`resample_check_out.txt`; full-precision weights on
  L01: max 122). The residual is the emulation's filter arithmetic; the server would run the EXE's own program on a GPU,
  as the EXE does (4785 checks it on the GPU against the same pairs).
- **The merge rule follows from M2 and R1:** with the EXE's unit mask draws dropped, the tapped map is
  min(1, R(blocks + landmarks)); the server adds min(1, R(units)) into it with a saturating ONE / ONE blend. Stock is
  min(1, R((block ? 1 : unit) + landmarks)). Because R is linear, the two are **equal wherever a unit's mask and a city
  block's mask do not meet within R's footprint (about 1.5 ShadowRaw texels)**: a unit over a landmark is added in stock
  too, and inside a block both saturate. They differ on the edge ring of a unit overlapping a block (garrisons): the
  server's is darker there by at most R(unit) [I, to be measured by 4785]. MAX instead of ADD would be wrong under every
  unit standing on an improvement (stock adds). At q 1 (no resample; the terrain reads `saturate(t3.r)`): every caster
  leaves r = 1 where a unit is (units write r = 1 first; a landmark's blend keeps 1; a block writes 1), so adding the
  server's raw unit mask onto the copied float map and the PS's saturate give stock's value exactly [C]. At q 0 nothing is
  drawn (strength 0). (Corrected 2026-11-20 by 4785, 13.4: "a landmark's blend keeps 1" holds only for a landmark colour
  of 1; L10's mask holds landmark r of 0.012-0.041, so under a unit and such a landmark stock's r is below 1 at q 1 [I].)
- **The sizes the server needs:** ShadowRaw's W x H is the composite's back buffer, which the camera block already
  carries (`VPShellCamera::bbW / bbH`, `shell/common/shell_shared.h`), and is the q 1 slot's own size (4302 S2 [L]).
  ShadowBlur's size is the slot's.
- **The program bytes:** VS `c7615a1db4f3731cbeb1ad3067e2427b3037f1e3a3517db71826829abf55302e`, PS
  `be955cbb6b767348a7de81895c3262da5c393546eb5de163169a2ff40303effa` (SHA-256 of the DXBC as the export holds it), found
  in the install EXE's `.shader` section by `c5r::shaders::ShaderSection` as `UnitPrograms::open` finds the unit programs
  (nothing from the EXE is committed: the digests only). The quad's vertex layout: POSITION R32G32B32 at 0, NORMAL
  R32G32B32 at 12, TEXCOORD R32G32 at 24, stride 32; four corners (+-1, +-1, 0) with uv (0.5 x + 0.5, 0.5 - 0.5 y);
  indices (2, 1, 0, 3, 1, 2) [C, the export's buffers].

### 9.3 The two options side by side

| | (a) the server's mask into the EXE's ShadowRaw, the EXE resamples | (b) the server's mask resampled and added on the server (chosen) |
|---|---|---|
| The EXE's unit mask draws | dropped by the filter under a new mode bit | the same |
| Where the units' mask is drawn | server, into a shared texture published to the composite (a new section and slot set, like `shell_fowmask.h`) | server, into its own ShadowRaw-sized target |
| Who resamples | the EXE (its own pass), then the tap copies as today | the server runs the EXE's own resample program (9.2 R1) on its target |
| Merge | the composite draws the server's mask into ShadowRaw after the caster lists and before the resample list executes: a new insertion point in the EXE's frame (the resample list must be recognised at ExecuteCommandList; its render target is ShadowBlur's view, which the shadow tap already resolves) | a saturating ONE / ONE draw of the resampled units onto a server copy of the tapped map; bound as t3 / t13 instead of the tap's srv |
| Timing | the server draws its mask with the newest ShadowMatrix0 it has (EXE frame N-1 or older) into EXE frame N's map, which frame N's matrix maps: **the units' shadows shift by the camera's motion of 1-2 frames while the camera moves**, and show the pose of 2-3 server frames before the model's (mask -> EXE frame -> tap -> server) [I] | the units' mask is drawn in the server's frame with the ShadowMatrix0 of the triple bound in that frame and the pose of the same frame's model: **no lag, no shift by construction**; the blocks' and landmarks' part keeps today's tap latency [I] |
| Exactness | the resample and the composition order exactly stock's (units drawn after the casters: the order differs, the values only on the block edge ring) | the resample stock's program; the merge exact except the block edge ring (9.2) |
| Transitions (the mode bit set or cleared) | the composite knows per frame what it inserted | the server must know per tapped frame whether the EXE dropped its unit mask draws: a slot flag (9.4), else one or two frames doubled or without unit shadows at each switch |
| Cost on the EXE | + one full-target draw per map frame into 2554 x 1411 (28.8 MB written at R16G16B16A16) reading a shared mask, + the shared slots on the EXE's device (2-3 x 3.6 MB at A8_UNORM, 28.8 MB at the float format), + a new hook at the resample list; - the unit mask draws (628 in 28 stock frames: 4-49 per frame) [I] | - the unit mask draws; + one flag write per copy [I] |
| Cost on the server | the mask pass + a copy into the publish slot | the mask pass into 28.8 MB (2554 x 1411 x 8 B, cleared per frame), the resample (2048 x 2048 x 8 taps at q 3), one 8 MB copy of the tapped map and the add: [I] under 0.1 ms on the workstation's RTX 4080, measured by the prototype (9.6); about 37 MB of video memory at q 3 (57.6 MB at q 1) in the 64-bit process |
| True absence (0328) | still works, but keeps the units' shadows inside the EXE's chain | the target state: nothing of the EXE's Unit system is needed |
| Failure (D118, D125) | a new EXE-side install failure (pattern of the insertion) | a server-side failure (program not found, target not made) takes the shadow's existing fatal step (`ShadowFatalStep`); the mode bit is never set without a working mask, so the EXE's shadows stay until then |

### 9.4 The files each option needs (epic 0590's carrier space marked **0590**: read only here)

Both options (the drop and the bit):
- **0590** `shell/common/shell_shared.h`: a mode bit `VPMODE_UNIT_SHADOWS` (0x10; `VPMODE_KNOWN` widened), set by the
  server only with `VPMODE_UNITS` and a working mask path; two counters in `reserved` (mask draws dropped, mask draws
