## 10. The shell's sound executor (4723)

Written 2026-11-20 from 11:00 EST by W19 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w19-4723`, route S (D210; the Architect's
note `research/07-architecture-decisions/architect-2026-11-20-route-s-combat.md` 1.4-1.6; the stream's contract,
section 7; the EXE's audio, `research/02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md`). Marks: `[C]` checked by this worker in code or
tests (each names the check), `[L]` live, `[I]` a design choice or reading.

### 10.1 What it is

- `proxy/src/proxy_sound_exec.{h,cpp}` (new). Three parts, as 4773's hold: the **core** (`Attach`, `Step`, `Detach` on
  an `Audio` of four plain function pointers: script index, play, live, stop) reads the stream (`VPTrigReadNext` until
  NONE at the frame shown, then `VPTrigPublishReader`) and keeps every started sound under its handle with its owner
  (fight = owner / fightSeq; figure; clip instance) in a fixed table of 256 sounds and 64 fights; the **binding**
  (`AudioOfExe`) is the only reader of the build table; the **glue** (`Init`, `FrameHook`, `SetServerFights`, the D118
  report) is the only part that needs the proxy runtime. No STL in the core and the binding; no allocation, file I/O or
  wait on the frame path; no C++ exception can leave the hook (combat-choreography.md 3.5.8 points 1-6).
- **The hook** (MC #8210, one hunk in `proxy/src/proxy_ui_bridge_rt.cpp` `Init`): the plain frame slot is one chain,
  `ProxySoundExec::FrameHook` -> `ProxyCombatHold::FrameHook` -> `ProxyUiDraw::OnFrame` (when on); each part called once
  per drain in that order (3.5.8 point 1). Off (the product today): one test of a word and return.
- **On** only when route S's server fights are on: `ProxySoundExec::SetServerFights(true)` (ticket 4782/4795 calls it
  with the hold's), or the TEST ONLY variable `VP64_TEST_SOUND_EXEC=1` of the EXE's process (read in `Init`). The binding
  is checked at once on the calling thread; the attach (map `<base>.Trig` created-or-opened and `<base>.Frame`, with
  `<base>` = `VPSHELL_SECTION` of the EXE's environment, which the proxy sets for the composite) happens on the main thread
  at the next frame.
- **The frame shown** (R2's G): min(the publish block's frame id, the ring's `latestFrameId`) of `<base>.Frame` (read
  only; seqlock on the publish block): the frame the composite published in this EXE frame once the server has drawn it,
  so every record of it is visible (R1). The drain runs inside the EXE's Lua event of the frame, so a sound starts in the
  frame of its picture or the next (note 1.4) [I: the order of the drain and the insertion within one EXE frame was not
  measured].

### 10.2 The rules as built [C: proxy/tests/sound_exec, 75 checks]

| Rule | As built |
|---|---|
| R2, never queued for later | at frame G every unread record with frameId <= G in seq order, at most 1,024 per frame; a SoundStart more than 3 frames before G (`kStaleFrames`, 0.1 s at the 30-fps cap) is dropped and counted (`droppedStale` in the reader block); a play the EXE refuses (no voice, a script rule, too far) is counted and never retried |
| Owner (R7) | a sound's fight is its owner (the EXE's event id) or, with owner 0, its fightSeq; a start of a fight already ended is refused (`after end`) |
| Fight OwnerEnd | its loops stop at once; its one-shots end by themselves, and one still live `kRingOutMs` (30 s) later is stopped (a guard against a looping script sent as a one-shot) *(4734, 2026-11-21, lead-0042: was "its one-shots stop 3 s later (note 1.5 rule 3)", which cut 19 of 748 played one-shots live, 10.8)*; R8: `ProxyCombatHold::OwnerEnd(owner, played)` once per fight, owner 0 counted and never passed on |
| ClipEnded | the loops of that (player, unit, figure, instance) stop at once, its one-shots end by themselves (the same guard); the fight goes on; never reaches the hold |
| SoundStop | stops its handle |
| Watchdog | a fight with no record for 22 s (`kSilentMs`: the 20-s limit with an air figure plus 2 s, the hold's own) has its sounds stopped (LOUD) and counts as ended |
| R6 | a new generation or a stopped server (magic 0) stops every sound and ends every live fight with Reset (played false to the hold); the first generation after the attach is a join, not a reset |
| R3 | records overwritten unread are counted (`lost`); the watchdogs end what they would have ended |
| Effects | EffectStart / Move / Stop are counted and left to the effect routes (4793) |
| Natural ends | 16 table slots per frame are checked; a sound that has ended by itself frees its slot without a stop (no stop is ever sent to an ended sound: checked) |
| Full | a 257th live sound or a 65th fight is not started (counted, LOUD once) |

### 10.3 The EXE's audio entries and how they are declared

- **Rows** (`exebuild/symbols/proxy.tsv`, lead-0590's names of 0590 #7706, review asked on thread 0590 #8201):
  `audio_play3d` code 0x8DC7F0, `audio_game_obj` data 0x5F54F34, `audio_sound_stop` code 0x90EDE0 (anchors of
  exe-audio.md 8). `audio_sound_fade` is not used: the 3D samples carry no volume ramp, so the fade is an immediate stop
  for them (exe-audio.md 4.1 [L]). **Pattern rows** in `proxy_sound_exec.cpp` (`exebuild/patterns.txt` lists the file):
  the play's first 30 bytes (its first instruction compares `audio_game_obj` with 0, written as `R(audio_game_obj)`, so the
  pattern ties the data row to the code row) and Stop's first 30 (its tests of +0x28 and +0x18 bit 0). **Caller rows**
  (lead-0590 #8203, exe-build-table.md 8's rule for short look-alike functions): `audio_play3d_call` code 0x74C823 (the
  Sound trigger's type-0x15 handler; pattern: the load of `audio_game_obj` and the call of `audio_play3d`, the
  call's rel32 checked by hand on build 4390913 to land on 0x8DC7F0) and `audio_stop_call` code 0x8DB93A (the
  unit-loop record function; pattern: the loop over the record's 64 slots ending in the call of `audio_sound_stop`, rel32 to 0x90EDE0;
  both rows in `exebuild/patterns.txt` through `proxy/src/proxy_sound_exec.cpp`; D83 edit 2026-11-25, 0769: the two
  byte patterns written out were replaced by this description), with stage 2b's `C()` call-target
  token, so on every build the EXE's own calls must lead to the two entries; the product checks all four patterns at run
  time before it arms. Both builds' local tables regenerated with main's gen_table (2b, its ambiguity gate) by the two
  commands of exe-build-table.md 6 (2026-11-20 12:00 EST: 397 of 397 symbols, 253 of 253 patterns OK on both builds,
  exit 0; nothing generated committed). **Carry cross-check, build 26577625 [C]:** the five rows carried with high
  confidence (`audio_play3d`, `audio_sound_stop`, `audio_stop_call` by 16-byte windows, `audio_play3d_call` by 24, 1 vote
  each; `audio_game_obj` by references, 40 of 40), and the two caller patterns' `C()` tokens pass there, i.e. the carried
  caller sites call exactly the carried entries (a swap of look-alikes would fail them). The FSound layout (+0x18, +0x28,
  +0xA4) is not read on that build, so the product still refuses it (below).
- **Declared** in `proxy_sound_exec.h` as `__fastcall` with an unused EDX (proxy_pacing.cpp's form for a thiscall
  method): `VpAudioPlay3dFn` (this, edx, script, context, pos, -1.0, -1, -1.0, -1.0, factor, -1, -1, -1): 11 stack
  words, the callee's `ret 0x2C`; `VpAudioStopFn` (this, edx): no stack word, `ret`. The thiscall reading and the
  `ret N` are 4797's [C, exe-audio.md 2 step 4 and 8]; the play's arguments are those the Sound trigger's handler passed,
  read live from the stack in 4797 (`(index, 0, &pos, -1.0, -1, -1.0, -1.0, 0.0, -1, -1, -1)`, exe-audio.md 2 [L]).
- **How the declaration is tested** (the 4725 defect class): `proxy/tests/sound_exec/sound_exec_abi_test.cpp` calls each
  type on a stand-in callee written in assembly with the EXE function's own return (`ret 0x2C`, `ret`) and compares ESP
  before and after the call (0 for both [C]); the play's stand-in also returns its first stack word plus ECX, so `this`
  in ECX and the script as the first stack argument are checked; a stand-in that pops one word more (`ret 0x30`) is the
  positive control (ESP +4 seen [C]). The STL-setting census of the build (4725's `scl_census.py`): the executor's TU is
  at `_SECURE_SCL=0` with the proxy's other 30 container TUs, and `comdat_overlap.py` finds no std:: function defined
  by both settings (0) [C, proxy 5ddb1dea, 2026-11-20 11:12].
- **Script index**: `ICvEngineUtility1::GetAudioTagIndex(name, AUDIOTAG_3DSCRIPT)` through the proxy's stored engine
  utility (no EXE address), once per name per generation, cached.
- **Liveness** before every stop (the pool reuses `FSound` objects, exe-audio.md 4.3): +0x28 (stopping) 0, +0x18 bit 0
  set, and the script data at +0xA4 naming the same script index at its +4 [C for +0x28 and +0x18 from Stop's own tests;
  I for +0xA4, checked by the live smoke]. These offsets are layout: `kLayoutVerified` lists build 4390913 only; on any
  other build, an unknown build, a symbol not carried or a pattern that does not match, `SetServerFights(true)` answers
  false with one LOUD line and the D118 report (stage `sound-exec`, non-fatal, the helper's popup): ~~the server's fights
  are then silent and the player is told why~~. An access fault in a call or a read (each under `__try`) turns the
  executor off for the proxy load with the same report. *Corrected 2026-11-20 (ticket 4783, MC #8543; was: "the
  server's fights are then silent"): the executor is armed by route S's common state, so its refusal or its fault means
  route S NOT ARMED or DISARMED as one (stock fights, no hold), and its report goes into route S's one report (stage
  `route-s`); section 16.*

### 10.10 Why route S is busier: the tier test, and the extra 1600 / 1280 entries (4737, W39, 2026-11-21)

Written 2026-11-21 from 13:20 EST by w39-0042, branch `w39-4737`, offline (no instance, no build). The EXE's side in
full: `../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md` 13. Marks as there.

**Cause 1 [C stock's rule; C route S's lack of it].** Stock's Sound-trigger handler plays a unit's trigger only when
the trigger's `tier` attribute is -1 or equals the unit's figure tier at that moment (0 for 3 figures or fewer, 1 for
4-8, 2 for 9 or more). The trigger files put every per-figure detail sound at tier 0 and every bed, run loop and run
vox in a T1 / T2 pair (exe-audio.md 13.2), so a whole 12-figure unit plays its T2 beds and its tier -1 cries, falls and
deaths, and none of the detail. Route S applies no tier: `c5r::unitanim::Controller` keeps the trigger's attributes but
`TriggerEvent` carries only `event`, `bone` and `duration` (controller.cpp's trigger walk), and the emitter has no tier
rule (no `tier` anywhere in `render/src/unitanim`, `server/src/effects`, `server/src/units`, grep 2026-11-21). So every
figure sends every tier-0 sound and both beds of every pair. Live pattern [L, W37's Tiny logs]: stock plays one of each
pair, route S both (exe-audio.md 13.3).

**Cause 2 [L observed; mechanism I].** Route S's figures play the combat-ready entry 1600 (and the ranged fight's
target 1280) with its tier -1 `FOOT_ALWAYS` x2 and `FORTIFY_VOX`: 10 fortify vox and 10-20 foot dirt per melee
fight, none on stock. In the melee fights stock's attacking swordsman run-charges (1120 then 1140: no 1600; its run
charge vox in all three stock melee fights) where route S's runs (1400) and enters 1600: the choreography's approach
rule (`combat.cpp`: 1120 only for a member whose `RushAttackFormation` is not empty [C], section 3's `[I 5.5]`; the
swordsman's is empty in VP's database [D], yet stock charges [L]). Stock's rule [C, exe-audio.md 13.3]: an attacking
melee figure farther than its member's `MoveRadius` from its target goes to the charge state 0xC (1120), with no rush test;
then 1140 when the member takes AttackCharge. **Section 3's "Approach" row is corrected by this:** run charge for every
attacking melee figure out of reach whose member enables RunCharge, not only rush members (2026-11-21; replaced "a rush
member with RunCharge charges (1120)" as the reading of 0321 5.5). The ranged fight is not covered by that reading
(exe-audio.md 13.3 (a) / (b)). A rule of the EXE's trigger walk that mutes 1600 / 1280 is unlikely: in the huge pair
stock plays those clips' `FORTIFY_VOX` at ranged and siege fight starts, and route S plays more of them there too
(exe-audio.md 13.3) [L]. So cause 2 is which figures enter 1600 / 1280, a choreography difference.

**Estimate** (W37's per-file counts with the tier-0 classes taken out; foot dirt cannot be split between the tier-0
`FOOT_RUN` and the tier -1 `FOOT_ALWAYS` in the Miles log, so both bounds; `server/evidence/0042/4737/estimate.py` over `perfile.py`'s output; the offline
trigger logs by script and clip: `tlog_sum.py`):

| Fight | Stock one-shots | Route S | Route S, cause 1 fixed (foot dirt kept / removed) | and cause 2 (fortify vox removed too) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| melee | 19 | 80 | 46 / 27 | 36 / 17 |
| kill | 13 | 63 | 37 / 16 | 27 / 6 |
| art_still | 17 | 73 | 47 / 24 | 37 / 14 |
| ranged | 17 | 98 | 44 / 24 | 36 / 16 |
| air | 41 | 79 | 70 / 58 | 66 / 54 |

**Cross-check by time alone** (W38's way, lead-0042 #9319: every 3D start between RunCombatSim and EndCombatSim, any
position; W38's own counts melee 81/21, kill 64/18, art_still 74/19, ranged 98/17, air 74/37 stock-last; here
`server/evidence/0042/4737/window.py <repo> F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w37/tiny2`, 2026-11-21 13:25 EST; stock / route S;
"tier 0" and "FA / FV" (fortify vox and every foot dirt, so FOOT_RUN's tier-0 share is in this column too) by file
stem, "rest" the other one-shots):

(The three AI-turn defence fights follow each other within seconds, so their windows overlap: not used.) Both methods

  two sides enter 1600 / 1280 on stock (the Tiny archer and its warrior target show neither clip's sounds; the huge
  save's riflemen under Gatling fire do): the same read of 0321 5.1-5.3 (state 5's "when the figure is set up for it",

**As built (lead-0042 #9324: P1, then P2 (a), separate commits on `w39-4737`; P2 (b) research only, open).**
- **P1, the tier gate** [C: code and tests]. `c5r::unitanim::TriggerEvent` gains `tier` (the attribute; -1 when the
  file has none: the model reader keeps 0 for an absent `tier`, so the controller looks the attribute up by name) and
  `unit_figures` (the unit's figures held and alive when the frame's steps begin: deaths and removals come with the

### 10.11 The run and surface loops of figures that turn before a ranged, siege or naval fight (4735, W45, 2026-11-21)

Written 2026-11-21 from 22:10 EST by w45-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w45-4735`, offline (no instance, no game).
Marks: `[L]` W37's recorded pairs (10.8, 10.9; logs `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w37/pair` and `.../tiny2`, read only), `[C]`
this branch's code and runs, `[D]` 0327's database copy, `[I]` this section's reading.

**Cause [L counts, C route S, I the EXE's rule].** Every stock loop life of 10.8's gap 1, read again against the fights'
RunCombatSim and EndCombatSim (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w45/scratch/loops.py`, scratch, over `pair_4734.py`'s attribution),
falls in one of two clusters; route S has neither:
- **(A) the start:** 0.11-0.17 s after RunCombatSim the attacker of a ranged, siege or naval fight plays its run and its
  run loops for about 0.2-1.3 s (lives 0.7-1.9 s with the 0.1 s heartbeat and 0.5 s fade): the Gatling's and field gun's
  cannon loop (the field gun with T2 dirt), the archer's T2 run and T2 dirt (Tiny), the ironclad's and cruiser's ironclad
  run and ocean loop, the artillery's run with T1 dirt; the dreadnought's run at +1.37 s; the defender of a city volley
  (a tank) too. Members without `ReformBeforeCombat` run as well (Gatling, ironclad, cruiser `[D]`), so this is 5.1 M3's
  phase 2, both sides turning to face (state 0xF), not only phase 1's reform `[I]`. Under route S such a figure went
  straight to combat ready (`combat.cpp` `look()`: a ranged attacker to `ready()`, a non-answering defender to 1280) and
  `FightMotion` turned its heading at once: no 1400 was requested, so its run loops were never triggered `[C]`.
- **(B) the end:** 0.2-0.8 s before EndCombatSim the survivors of one side run (riflemen, swordsmen with run vox, the
  archer's warrior target, the bomber's infantry target, the melee attackers): the reface and return to formation, in
  ranged, siege, air and melee fights alike `[L]`. Route S's `FightMotion` walks survivors back after the fight's end
  with no clip request, and the emitter sends nothing after the OwnerEnd. Not this ticket: **child 4742** (lead-0042
  #9857), because it changes when every fight's OwnerEnd comes.

**The rule as built (A), `CombatParams::turn_first`, default on** (lead-0042 #9853) `[C: code]`:
- `CombatUnitFigures::has_facing` / `facing_yaw` (additive): `combatPositions` sets them from the placement's yaw.
- At its first look, a placed figure of the attacker or the defender of a fight whose figures stand (a ranged attack,
  both sides; a city's volley, its target; a ship that strikes where it stands) whose unit heading is more than
  `turn_threshold` off the direction to the opponent's centre (its standing figures' centre, or the city's) enters the new
  state `FigState::Turn` (15 = 0xF), requests 1400 and records a `FigureMove` with `turn` set (in place, `yaw0` the unit's
  heading, `yaw1` facing the opponent). After it the figure looks again as it did before 4735 (combat ready and its
  strike, or bombard defend). No turn without the unit's heading, without a Run enable or a 1400 clip (no new hold), for
  an aircraft, or in a melee fight (its attackers run anyway).
- The turn's length: |angle| / (2 pi x rate) with rate = `TurnRateMin` + 0.5 x (`TurnRateMax` - `TurnRateMin`) turns per
  second (M1 / M5 `[C]`; the fraction 0.5 `[I]`: M5's fraction was not read), clamped to `turn_min` 0.3 s .. `turn_max`
  1.2 s `[I]` (a shorter run crosses none of its loop triggers: the Gatling's run clip has its loop trigger 0.43 s in).
  `turn_threshold` 30 degrees `[I]`: half a facing step, so a unit standing in its opponent's hex direction does not turn.
- **The live gate after a turn** (found offline): the first build let the figure strike as soon as the controller's
  machine took the bombard, which from the run state it does at once: the Gatling skipped 1600 and its fight got 0.47 s
  shorter. Now a turned figure's first strike waits for its combat-ready entry (`entry_wait`; 0321 5.3: state 5 requests
  1600 and strikes when its animation is done `[C]`).
- `FightMotion::pose`: during a turn the figure stands and its heading goes the shorter way, evenly; a turn's end faces
  `yaw1`.
- Switch: host key `render_test_units_turn_first` (TEST ONLY; 1 default, 0 no turn; other values refused) ->
  `UnitsOptions::turnFirst` -> `AnimRunner::setTurnFirst` -> `CombatParams::turn_first`; written into every bundle's
  `render_config`; sceneshot replays a bundle without it with 0 (`offline-scene-harness.md` 36).

**Tests [C, runs 2026-11-21 22:30-22:35 EST, head 94514a238 + the live-gate commit 468a2ff0e, workstation].**

### 10.12 Which waiting figures enter combat ready: `CombatParams::ready_after_move` (4746, W57, 2026-11-22)

Written 2026-11-22 from 12:44 EST by w57-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w57-4746` from `origin/lead20-4742`
6e4db11bb (main 33c3fcb44 + 4742's walk home). Offline only (no instance, no game). Marks: `[C]` code or runs here, `[L]`
recorded live (W44's Tiny pair, 15.12), `[I]` this section's reading. The EXE's side: `../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md`
13.3 (the state setter, read 2026-11-21 by W39; behaviour only, D83).

**The cause** `[C code]`. `combat.cpp` `Sim::look()` puts a figure that finds no target (a defender before an attacker is
engaged, an attacker whose target's needs are all reserved, a ranged attacker beyond the strikers its target needs) into
`FigState::Wait` through `ready()`, and `ready()` requested combat ready (1600) for every first entry, Wait or Ready.
The 1600 clips carry tier -1 `FOOT_ALWAYS` (twice) and `FORTIFY_VOX`, so every waiting figure sent three one-shots that
stock's idle figures do not (15.12: battle vox 35 vs 9 and run / move 59 vs 3 over the six Tiny cases `[L]`).

**Stock's rule** `[C exe-audio.md 13.3]`: in state 2 a figure requests 1600 only when its current request, or with none
its last action, is a movement (1400, 1450, 1120), and then only when its member enables Walk (1450; else 1000); a
figure that was not moving gets no new request. State 5 always requests 1600, state 0xE always 1280.

**As built** `[C code]` (`render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h` `CombatParams::ready_after_move`, default true;
`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` `Sim::ready`):
- A figure's first combat-ready entry in `FigState::Wait`: when its last request (`Fig::last`, 1000 at rest) is 1400, 1450
  or 1120 and its member enables Walk, 1600 as before; after a movement without Walk, 1000; otherwise a Wait step with
  no request (the figure stays in its clip) and the figure is not combat ready.
- Unchanged: Ready (5) requests 1600 (a waiting figure that later gets a target enters Ready with 1600 and, self-timed,
  strikes when that entry is done: 0321 5.3; live, when the controller says its machine takes the attack); a figure
  already combat ready after a strike gets no new request and keeps 1600 as its last action (the victory test);
  bombard defend (1280).
- In today's choreography a waiting figure almost never has a movement as its last request (a reform ends with 1000, an
  approach goes to Ready), so with the knob on a waiting figure in practice never requests 1600.
- Off (`ready_after_move = false`): the rule before 4746. Rule A: host key `render_test_units_ready_after_move` (TEST
  ONLY, "1" default, other values than 0 / 1 refused) -> `UnitsOptions::readyAfterMove` -> `AnimRunner::setReadyAfterMove`
  -> `CombatParams::ready_after_move`, written into every bundle's `render_config`; `sceneshot` sets it only on "1"
  (absent: a bundle recorded before 4746, the rule before) and prints `units ready_after_move N`. `trigger_scene
  --no-ready-after-move`.

**Tests** `[C, 2026-11-22, workstation]`:
- `render/tests/unitanim/test_combat.cpp` `a_waiting_figure_enters_combat_ready_only_after_a_move`: 12 against 12
  soldiers without positions, a melee fight and a kill: no Wait step requests 1600 against stock's rule, the defenders
  strike and every striking figure requested 1600 in a Ready step first; members without Walk: no waiting 1600; the
  default is on; off breaks the rule. On lead20-4742 (before the fix) it FAILS (5 checks). The 4733 test
  `a_killed_sides_last_figure_is_spared_while_the_other_side_has_deaths_open` measures timings of the old rule
  (`r.end < 10`; the defenders' first strike now waits 1 s for its 1600 entry) and is pinned to `ready_after_move =
  false`, with a check of the default (no limit, both sides' deaths played, the spared figure strikes twice).
- `server/tests/effects/run_ready_scenes.py` over `trigger_scene.exe` (install art: the pure_vp copy, 0327's database

### 10.14 Why stock's ranged target is silent: phase 2's stance and the machine's path 6 (4750, W61, 2026-11-22)

Written 2026-11-22 from 15:40 EST by w61-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w61-4750` on `w59-4748` 726fae0e6.
Offline, read only: no Ghidra, no game, no build. Sources: this file's 18.14 and 18.15 (W50, W51: headless reads of
the DX11 EXE build 4390913), `combat-choreography.md` 5.2 and 13.4, `../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md` 13.3 (the
state setter); the unit logic files as parsed by 4408's census (`F:/c5-64bit-work/0374/4408/census/census.json`,
built 2026-11-15 from c5h-c's install copy and 0327's database copy; read with `evidence/0374/4408/fsmdump.py` and
`dgean.py --show`, output scratch only); W52's stock sampler file (18.15.1: `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-4745/
w52-run/sim52.jsonl.gz`, sha256 c0200a84...; read with `server/evidence/0042/4750/seq61.py`, summary `seq61.txt`
beside it). Behaviour only (D83). Ticket 4750 asked which state stock puts a ranged attack's non-answering target in;
10.12 left it `[I]`.

**1. Stock's rule: 0xE with 1280, as route S** `[C; L]`. A ranged attack the defender does not answer is stock's fight
type 1: phase 1 (reform), phase 2 (both sides to 0xF, the turn; a land figure goes to 3 when done), then phase 5, its
last, where the attacker looks and strikes and the defender's figures go to 0xE (18.14, 18.15 [C]; the target step
puts a figure of participant 1 or 2 into 0xE when the defender does not retaliate, `combat-choreography.md` 13.4 [C]);
the state setter requests 1280 for 0xE always (exe-audio.md 13.3 [C]). Live [L, W52's 10 AI turns on the huge t350 copy,
stock, 129 type-1 fights]: every defender figure that does not strike goes 0 -> 0xF -> 3 -> 0xE (or 0 -> 0xD -> 3 -> 0xF
-> 3 -> 0xE for a defender that reforms), the 0xE entry at phase 5's first sampled pass in all 401 such figures; none
waits in 2. So route S's `look()` (a defender that does not answer, or a figure that cannot attack: Defend, 1280) is
stock's state rule; 10.12's `[I]` reading "stock may keep the target idle in state 2" was wrong (corrected there).

**2. Why stock's 1280 clip does not sound: what the request finds** `[C from the files and the state setter; I for
the Tiny case]`.
- Phase 2: state 0xF requests 1450 (shuffle) (`combat-choreography.md` 5.2). Stock holds the land figures in 0xF
  about 0.47 s in a ranged fight (18.15.1: phase 2 0.468 [0.098] s reforming attacker, 0.477 [0.087] s not) [L].
- The omni machine (`1_omni_state_01`, and the mounted one the same) takes 1450 from idle into its start-run state
  with the shuffle selected, and after 0.15 s into its run loop (17). In 17, a request of 1600 with the shuffle
  selected goes to the stop-shuffle state 26 and sets path 6 to 1; 26 goes after 0.15 s to the combat-ready loop (12)
  when path 6 is 1, to idle when it is 0. So the figure becomes combat ready **without** the enter-combat-ready state
  8, whose graph plays the 1600 clip (the clip with `FOOT_ALWAYS` x2 and `FORTIFY_VOX`).
- State 3 after the shuffle: the setter requests 1600 when the figure's current request is a movement (1450 is) and
  its member enables Walk, else 1000 (exe-audio.md 13.3 [C]). The warrior, archer, crossbowman, rifleman and lancer
  members enable Walk; 149 of the 366 member rows do; the ship members (ironclad, frigate, dreadnought) do not [D,
  census].
- Phase 5: 0xE requests 1280. The sockets into ENTER_BOMBARD_DEFEND (15) set path 6 to 1 from the combat-ready loop
  (12), the attack (14), the run loop (17) and the two fortify states (16, 22), and to 0 from idle (1); from the fidget
  state (3) they leave it. The stop-shuffle state (26) has no socket to 15: a figure there takes the 1280 after it
  reaches 12.
- The enter-bombard-defend graph's target pose is a selection on path 6: 0 plays the 1280 clip once (its Sound
  triggers: the census counts 389 Sound triggers on 1280 clips over the install, 3 per figure for the warrior), 1 plays
  the 1285 bombard-defend loop, which carries no Sound trigger in any file (census: 1285 Effect triggers only). The
  shuffle clips carry 4 Sound triggers in the whole install.
- So a Walk-enabled stock target shuffles almost silently in phase 2, becomes combat ready without the 1600 clip, and
  enters bombard defend on the silent 1285 branch: none of the 1280 clip's three one-shots per figure. Route S's target
  meets the 1280 request from idle (path 6 = 0, no phase-2 shuffle in the core): the 1280 clip and its three tier -1
  one-shots per figure, the ~32 per ranged fight of 10.12. A member without Walk gets 1000 in state 3, returns to idle
  (path 6 = 0) and plays the 1280 clip on stock too; a ship's machine takes no 1450 from idle at all, so a ship target
  stays idle and plays the 1280 clip on stock as on route S.
- The same chain explains stock's silent archer (10.12's 13 one-shots of the 1600 class per ranged fight on route S):
  stock's strikers too leave phase 2 combat ready via 26 and strike from 12 without the 1600 clip; route S's Ready
  requests 1600 from idle and plays state 8's clip.
- What is still `[I]`: that the Tiny warrior followed this chain (W52's sampler ran on the huge save and read neither
  the figures' request field nor their machine state; the Tiny case has a 12-figure Walk-enabled target, so the chain
  predicts exactly its silence); that the 1600 request of state 3 reaches the machine (phase 5 starts as soon as every
  figure stands in 3, so 1600 may last less than one machine update; then the 1280 meets the run loop, path 6 = 1 all
  the same); type 5's (air) phases. Reading (b) of exe-audio.md 13.3 (the trigger walk) is not needed for this case.
- Settles it live: one Tiny archer fight with the controller oracle (`unit-controller.md` 8) recording the target
  figures' state, request, machine state and path 6 (lead-0042's list for oldpc after the 0.1b2 playtest).

**3. The change agreed** (lead-0042 #10380; built after the 0.1b2 playtest ended, MC #10396).
`CombatParams::defend_from_stance`, default on, with `defend_stance_s` (default 0.45 s: W52's ranged type-1 phase 2;
at least 0.15 s, the machine's start-run time): a defender figure that does not answer or cannot attack, of a land
member that enables Walk and has a 1450 clip in the install, whose last request is not already a movement (a
`turn_first` turn with 1400 leaves its machine in the run loop, already on the silent branch), in a fight whose
attacker is not an aircraft (type 5's phase 2 not read), first requests 1450 (stock's 0xF) and, `defend_stance_s`
later, 1280 (the machine then takes the 1285 branch). No Walk, a ship, or the knob off: 1280 from idle as before
(off byte-identical). The core needs an additive `ActionKind` for 1450 (the controller gets no 1450 today: the
reform's shuffle goes to the motion only): `ActionKind::Walk` ("walk", 1450), appended so that no existing value or
name index moves (lead-0042 #10392). TEST key `render_test_units_defend_from_stance` (the 4746 pattern).
**Known remaining differences** (agreed skips, #10392): (a) a figure whose last request is already a movement gets no
stance (its machine is in the run loop; the 1280 already takes the silent branch, as stock's would); (b) air fights
keep 1280 from idle (stock's air opening sets 0xE directly in its phase 3; whether a phase 2 precedes it was not read);
(c) ships keep 1280 from idle (no Walk enable, and their machines take no 1450 from idle; stock's ship targets play the
1280 clip too, so this is stock's behaviour as far as read). Expected offline: the 1280 class from 32 to about 0 per ranged fight and from 17 to about 0 per
siege fight (land targets); naval_ranged keeps its ship targets' 1280 (the dreadnought-on-lancer case drops, the
ironclad-on-city case has no figures); fight lengths unchanged (a non-answering defender gates nothing).

## 11. The trigger emitter (4722)

Written 2026-11-20 08:21-10:30 EST by W16 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w16-4722`, route S (decision D210; the
Architect's note `research/07-architecture-decisions/architect-2026-11-20-route-s-combat.md` 1.4-1.6 with the MC's
correction of 1.6 from 4799; the EXE's own trigger policy that the server takes over: `../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md`
2 and 4.2). Stage 2 of 4795: the server writes section 7's records. Marks: `[C]` checked by this worker in code or tests
(each names the check), `[L 0557]` / `[L 4797]` recorded live by the ticket named, `[I]` this section's reading or design
choice. Offline only: no game instance, no EXE address, no name from the game's files in git (the logs stay outside).

### 11.1 What it is

- `server/src/effects/srv_trigger_emitter.{h,cpp}`, namespace `srveffects`: `TriggerEmitter` (per frame: `beginFrame(F,
  dt)`, `fightStarted(Fight)`, `triggers(TriggerIn...)`, `ownerEnds(OwnerEnd...)`, `endFrame()`), the ownership table
  (`classOfCode`, `ownerOfCode`), `ScriptTable` (the 3D scripts' loop flags), `substitute` ($(TERRAIN), $(BASETERRAIN),
  $(WEAPON)), the caller's `Substitutions` and `FigurePositions`, and the sinks: `SectionSink` (maps `<base>.Trig` with
  `CreateFileMappingW`, or a caller's buffer; generation = the old one + 1), `TeeSink` (section and log, the name indexes
  kept in step). It depends on `vp_trigger.h` and `srv_units_fights.h` only.
- `srv_trigger_logsink.{h,cpp}`: the offline trigger log (D137) as a sink, through 4721's `TriggerLogWriter`.
- `srv_trigger_controller.h`: the controller's `TriggerEvent` as `TriggerIn` (`triggersOf` keeps the units the emitter
  takes). `controller.h`'s `TriggerEvent` gained `duration` and `file` (additive, lead-0042 #8019: the walk sets both
  from the trigger and its member's trigger file).
- `srv_trigger_tap.{h,cpp}`: what the server's unit scene calls (11.5).
- The API for 4792's projectiles and 4777's figure-less sounds (posted #8010): `startEffect` / `moveEffect` /
  `stopEffect`, `startSound` / `stopSound` with a `StartSpec` (unit, figure, instance, resolved name, pos, orient, scale,
  vel, follows, loop, the trigger's identity, late). The owner is the running fight of the unit; at the owner's end the
  emitter stops every live API effect with EffectStop before the OwnerEnd (note 1.5 item 4: a projectile in flight is
  removed with its trail) and refuses later calls on the handle.
- `FigurePositions::boneTransform` and `figureScale` (additive, for 4793, #8137): a trigger effect takes the bone's world
  point and orientation when the host gives them (else the point or root with identity) and the figure's member scale
  (else 1; <= 0 counted `badScale`); defaults keep the records as before (0557's final series equal record for record).

### 11.2 The rules as built

| Rule | Source | As built |
|---|---|---|
| Which figures | note 1.4 | every figure of a unit in a running fight (from `fightStarted` to its OwnerEnd), on screen or not: the controller steps every fighter (4774's runner); a unit in no fight sends nothing (`noFight`) |
| Frame | note 1.4, R1 | every record of a frame is stamped with F and written at `endFrame`, before the scene marks F's slot READY; within the frame: starts, moves and stops in the order of their time in the frame, then the owners' end stops, then the OwnerEnds |
| Lateness | note 1.5 item 1 | a trigger crossed `offset` s into a frame of `dt` s is `dt - offset` late against F's time; a one-shot (a sound of a non-looping script, a duration-0 effect) more than 0.1 s late is dropped and counted (`droppedLate`, also into the section's `droppedLate`) |
| Lasting effects | note 1.5 item 4 | an Effect trigger with a duration starts late while `late < duration` (counted `startedLate` when over 0.1 s), else not at all (`droppedLateLasting`); the server stops it with EffectStop when its duration has passed; with a bone it carries the follows flag and an EffectMove when its point moved more than 0.01 units |
| Owner end | note 1.5 item 2, R7 | the fight clock's OwnerEnds (the fight's: Natural, Limit, Refused, Gone, Reset; a clip instance's: ClipEnded) are applied after the frame's triggers: the owner's lasting effects get EffectStop first, then the OwnerEnd (`played` by R8); its loops are left to the OwnerEnd (the shell stops them, R7) and their slots freed; a later trigger of that clip instance is dropped (`afterEnd`) |
| Ownership | note 1.6 + lead-0042 #8019 | the combat clips are the server's: attacks 1100, 1130, 1140, 1160, 1180, 1192; charge 1120; combat ready 1600 (with 1620, 1640 `[I]`, 11.6); bombard defend 1280; death 1200; victory 1800; each with its B variant (+1000). Movement 1400-1499 of a fighting figure is the server's too by default (`movementInFight`, #8019: stock's fight sound has the approach's run loops `[L 4797]` and the EXE's figure stands still under route S). Idles and fidgets 1000-1099, fortify, work, capture and every other code: the EXE's, never sent (`exeClass`, per code) |
| Victory tail | lead-0042 #8019 | the fight clock ends a fight when the choreography requests victory, so the 1800 clip plays after the OwnerEnd: for 3 s after a Natural end the unit's victory one-shots are sent owned by the unit (owner 0, fseq 0, player and unit: R7's second form); its loops are not |
| Loops | `exe-audio.md` 4.2 | a looping script (the `ScriptTable`: `bLooping` of the install's `*3DScripts.xml`, then the database's `Audio_3DSounds.Looping`) starts once (SoundStart with the loop flag) and is renewed, not started again, while the same unit triggers it (key: player, unit, script); it ends with SoundStop when its age passes the heartbeat (0.1 s, the fighting value); a Sound trigger's duration keeps it alive over that interval (age = late - duration, 11.3); at most 64 at once (`loopsSlotsFull`); a StopSound trigger stops every loop of its unit (none in the install, `exe-audio.md` 6) |
| Loop owner | note 1.5 item 2, CORRECTED (11.6 item 4) | `loopsByFight` (default on, lead-0042 #8089): a loop's record names the fight (instance 0, its figure kept), so it lives across clip changes as stock's do, renewed by any clip of its unit, and ends by the heartbeat (SoundStop) or the fight's OwnerEnd; off: the note as first written, the clip instance that started it owns it and its ClipEnded ends it |
| Names | note 1.3, R5 | `$(TERRAIN)`, `$(BASETERRAIN)`, `$(WEAPON)` resolved through the caller's `Substitutions` before the name goes into the table; a name with a variable without a value is not sent (`unresolved`); a sound name not in a given `ScriptTable` is not sent (`unknownScript`); a name the section refuses is counted (`namesRefused`); with no table every sound is a one-shot (`loopUnknown`) |
| Positions | note 1.4 | the bone's point from the caller, else the figure's root, else the unit's root; none: not sent (`noPosition`). Orientation identity until the pose source gives bones |

### 11.3 Readings this section adds [I unless marked]

- **A Sound trigger's duration keeps its loop alive.** 0557's fights cross Sound triggers with a `duration` attribute
  (s-w1: 60 of 239, up to 1.0 s; s-r1 and s-s1 up to 1.17 s) `[C: trigger_scene's count, 2026-11-20]`. With the heartbeat
  counted from the trigger alone the emitter's loops lived 0.03-0.27 s (first run, 09:30), against 4797's live lives
  0.19-2.66 s `[L 4797]`; counted from the end of the trigger's interval they live 0.03-1.33 s, median 0.6-1.0 s per
  case (11.6). The EXE's renewal inside a trigger's interval is not read in its code; the reading fits the live lives.
- **`$(WEAPON)`** for a sound is the member's Index-0 weapon's `WeaponTypeSoundOverrideTag`, else its
  `WeaponTypeTag`; for an effect the `WeaponTypeTag` (4797's live log names `..._BAT_AMB_T1_BLUNT` for the warrior,
  whose row has BLUNT / BLUNT `[L 4797]`). For a death clip the dying unit's own weapon (`--death-weapon own`, the
  default) resolves every name of 0557's fights to an existing script; the opponent's (`opponent`) leaves 4 names of
  s-m2 that are no script and 2 + 2 of the city fights (c1, c2) without a value `[C: series deathopp, 11.6]`, so the
  scripts favour own. *Corrected 2026-11-23 (W83, 18.30): live, stock names a fighting unit's Sound `$(WEAPON)` by its
  striker (18.25.2 impacts, 18.30 battle beds); the server's rule is the striker's weapon (5052 for a defender that does
  not strike, 5055 for both sides of a melee) with the own weapon only as the second try when that name is no script,
  which keeps these s-m2 names. Replaced: own as the rule.*
- **`$(TERRAIN)`** is `Features.EffectTypeTag` when the plot has a feature with one, else `Terrains.EffectTypeTag` (DIRT,
  SAND, SNOW, WATER; LEAVES, MUD, SNOW, WATER for features), as `effects-formats.md` 6 reads it for effects; 4797's
  live log names `leavesrunt2` and `dirtt*` files in fights on such plots `[L 4797]`. The offline runs use DIRT for every
  plot (0557's records name no terrain).
- **1620 and 1640** are crossed by fighting figures in 0557's fights (s-a1, s-m2, s-n1, s-n2, s-n3: 62 triggers in the
  first run, then counted as the EXE's); read as the combat-ready loop and its exit by number and given to the server.

### 11.5 The hand-off into the server's unit scene

Built on lead-0042's yes (#8079), each group its own commit:
- `srv_trigger_tap.{h,cpp}` (`AnimTriggerTap`): `fightStarted(Fight)` from 4774's `ControllerFightPlayer::start`, and
  `frame(F, dt, controller, feed.lastFightEnds())` right after the controller's frame in `AnimRunner::apply` (begin, the
  crossed triggers of the units the emitter takes, the frame's fight and clip ends, end). F is `AnimFeed::lastFrameId()`,
  the frame id the feed's `close()` took (`UnitsHost::animFrame`'s `frameId`, the camera block's: [I] that it is the
  vp_frame id whose slot this frame fills; 4723's live smoke checks it).
- `srv_units_anim.{h,cpp}`: the forward declaration, `AnimFeed::lastFrameId()`, `AnimRunner::setTriggerTap` and its
  member, the two calls. A null tap is today's behaviour.
- `srv_trigger_stream.{h,cpp}` (`TriggerStream`): what a host opens: the loop flags (`loadScriptTable`: the install's
  `*3DScripts.xml` under `Assets`, `Assets\Sounds` first, then `Audio_3DSounds`), `$(WEAPON)` (the weapon rows, the
  figure's member from `Controller::combatFigures`, cached per frame), `$(TERRAIN)` from the host or DIRT (counted
  `terrainStandIn`), the units' roots (`useCore`: `UnitsCore::rootOf` in mode exe, else the plot's centre on the frame's
  height grid, z 0), the sinks (`<base>.Trig` and / or the log) and the tap; `close()` clears the section's magic (R6).
- `UnitsHost` (`srv_units_scene.{h,cpp}`): `UnitsOptions::triggerSection` / `triggerLog` (both empty: no stream, the scene
  as before); the stream opened with the controller on each database (a new generation each time) and
  `setTriggerTap`; `setGrid` each frame. Nothing sets `triggerSection` in server.exe yet: the one line in
  `srv_render_host.cpp` (`o.unitsOpt.triggerSection = <base>` beside the other `unitsOpt` lines, armed with route S)
  is outside this ticket's touches (asked of lead-0042).
- `unitfeed --trigger-log FILE`: the same stream on a bundle's replay, its counts printed; `test_unitfeed.py`'s
  `test_aiturn_trigger_log` on 0477's AI turn (the fixture `aiturn`: two barbarian attacks on one unit). Run 2026-11-20
  10:32 EST [C]: 601 frames, 2 fights, SoundStart 267, SoundStop 16, EffectStart 12, EffectStop 7, OwnerEnd 210 (the 2

## 12. The adapter's special inputs (4726)

Written 2026-11-20 10:12- EST by W20 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w20-4726` from `epic-0042-combat-movement`
@1b3ec698d. Closes 8.6's items for `motion.cpp`, 4724's adapter and the feed (6.5 "Open"). Marks: `[C]` checked in this
branch's code or tests (each names the check), `[C DLL]` read in the DLL fork's source (`CvUnitCombat.cpp`,
`CvGameCoreStructs.cpp`, `CustomMods.h`), `[I]` this section's reading.

### 12.1 The feed: the DLL already holds both (no DLL change)

- **The interceptor** is `ICvCombatInfo1::GetUnit(BATTLE_UNIT_INTERCEPTOR)` [C DLL `GenerateAirCombatInfo`:
  `setUnit(BATTLE_UNIT_INTERCEPTOR, pInterceptor)` whenever an interceptor is found, even when the interception fails],
  a getter already on the purity list; `OnCombat` (`server/src/remote/srv_remote_feed.cpp`) never asked for it. Now it
  does, once per combat, and on that unit calls `GetOwner`, `GetID`, `GetDamage`, `GetMaxHitPoints` (all pure; not
  `ReadUnit`, so no table refresh). **Cost per combat:** one more `GetUnit` call for every combat (in-process in the
  server: a virtual call returning NULL, or a wrapper and its `Destroy` when there is an interceptor), four plain getters
  only when there is one, three `GetDamageInflicted` calls while the event is off, one `CustomModOptions` query per load
  (below). Not timed: combats come in tens per turn and every call is a field read [I].
- **Per-combat damage** is `GetDamageInflicted(bt)`, `pure-methods.tsv` `conditional`: it fires the Lua GameEvent
  `BattleDamageDelta` only under `MOD_EVENTS_BATTLES_DAMAGE` = `EVENTS_BATTLES && EVENTS_BATTLES_DAMAGE` [C DLL
  `CustomMods.h` 751, `CvGameCoreStructs.cpp` 345-]; VP ships both 0 (`unit-server-scene.md` 2.3). The feed calls it
  only while the DLL's `CustomModOptions` says the event is off (`SrvDbBattleDamageEvents`, `srv_remote_db.cpp`: a
  SELECT on the DLL's game connection, at the first combat after each load; an option without a row is 0 as in the DLL;
  no table or no connection = not known = not called). Then the getter is a plain read.
- **Deriving the damage is wrong** [C DLL + 0477]: `finalDamage` minus the unit's damage before the combat equals the other
  side's DamageInflicted in the DLL's own record, but 0477's submarine fix (`combat-choreography.md` 13.6) changes only
  `DamageInflicted(BATTLE_UNIT_DEFENDER)` on the engine's copy. A derived value would be > 0 for the fixed strike, 0321
  13.4's opening rule would make the submarine answer, and the strike would hold to 20 s again. So the value is read or
  it is -1.
- **The mapping** [I, from the fix's live effect]: the EXE's attacker record's damage field (0321 13.4: "the attacker's
  damage in this combat") is `GetDamageInflicted(BATTLE_UNIT_DEFENDER)` (the fix zeroes exactly that, and the opening rule
  then sends the defender to bombard defend, [L 0477]); so `CombatSide::damage` = the damage the side takes = the other
  side's DamageInflicted. The interceptor's `damage` is what it deals (`GetDamageInflicted(BATTLE_UNIT_INTERCEPTOR)` =
  `iInterceptionDamage` [C DLL]), as 4777's rule reads it.

### 12.2 The record (no size change; lead-0042 #8117, MC #8153)

| Field | As built |
|---|---|
| `CombatRecord::flags` bit 11 `kCombatDamageKnown` | the per-combat damage was read |
| `CombatRecord::reserved` | with bit 11: low int16 the attacker's damage in this combat (= DamageInflicted(DEFENDER)), high int16 the defender's (= DamageInflicted(ATTACKER)); read with `SrvFeed::CombatDamage(r, side)` (-1 without bit 11); else 0 |
| `CombatRecord::flags` bit 12 `kCombatInterceptorMember` | the members end with the interceptor's |
| member flag `0x8000` `kCombatMemberInterceptor` | the interceptor, not a damage member: player, id, `damage` = what it deals (0 unless bit 11), `finalDamage` = the unit's damage (an interceptor takes none in the DLL's resolve [C DLL]), `maxHP`; x, y, combatType, era -1. The DLL's member flags use bit 0 only [C DLL `CvStructs.h`] |
| `nMembers` | up to 257 (256 damage members and the interceptor; the DLL's cap is 32) |

**Old and new readers (MC #8153 condition 1).** No `format_version` change. A record with neither bit 11 nor bit 12 is
byte for byte a pre-4726 record, so a bundle or unitfeed file recorded before 4726 reads as before (condition 2). New
content always sets a bit above 10, and a decoder built before 4726 (`srvunits::rec`, `kCombatFlagsKnown` 0x07FF) refuses
such a record by name ("COMBATS combat N: flags 0x... above bit 10", BadRecord) instead of reading the interceptor as a
damage member. That meets "a reader built before 4726 can tell old records from new" because every reader of these
records that lives (the server's own feed consumers, unitfeed, the scene bundle replay) is built together with the writer
from one tree: the only way a pre-4726 reader meets a post-4726 record is an old tool on a new file, and it refuses it
(lead-0042 #8169). `srv_units_records.h` now knows bits 0-12,
accepts `reserved` with bit 11 and nMembers up to 257 [C: `test_units_records.cpp`].

**The library (condition 2)** [C: `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w20/scan_combats.py` over feed.bin's record 5, 2026-11-20 10:52
EST]: none of the 16 bundles of `F:/c5-64bit-work/scene-library/bundles` has a combat record (0 combats, 0 members; the
4980 `C7INTERCEPT` bundle is a static scene), so neither the record change nor the adapter's new hold of members and the
interceptor (12.3) changes what any of them replays.

### 12.3 The adapter and the clock

- **The clock** (`srv_units_fights.cpp`): `Fight::interceptor` from the flagged member (only with bit 12); the per-unit
  wait, `unitGone`, `inFight` and the clip-instance OwnerEnd records cover the interceptor too (0321 3.2's three key pairs
  [I]). Damage members are not keys of the clock (as in the EXE).
- **The hold** (`AnimFeed`, `srv_units_anim.cpp`): the interceptor and every damage member that is a unit are named in the
  hold with the two sides (frozen view, 'held in a fight', drawn set, placement inputs kept). Their SetDamage and deaths
  wait for the fight's end, as the EXE's parent-id rule holds a combat's child events (0321 3.2 [C 0321]); before 4726 a
  member's damage and death showed at once, before the blast. A unit that is both the defender and the interceptor (the
  DLL allows it) is named once.
- **`ControllerFightPlayer::start`**: `CombatSide::damage` of both sides from `CombatDamage`; `CombatInput::interceptor`
  from the flagged member; the other participants' figures by (player, id) from the controller (`combatFigures`); one the
  controller does not hold takes part without figures (counted `othersWithout`; the core's "Members:" note names it). An
  interceptor that is also the defender plays as the defender only [I]. `FightPlan::air` looks at the other participants'
  members too (8.6). `CombatRun::start` with `others`.
- **Positions**: each other participant from its placement input of the frame before through `combatPositions`; one not
  placed (culled, fogged) takes part without figures (`othersUnplaced`) so that every participant with figures has
  positions. The nuke's plot target gets the combat plot's centre (`plotCentre`), as a defending city does. **A city
  attacker has no centre**: the feed has no city plot (`ICvCity1::GetX` / `GetY` are not on the purity list); the fight now
  keeps its positions (before: no positions at all for a city attack) and the defender's figures keep their placement's
  heading (`FigurePose::yaw_known`).
- **Motion**: `FightMotion` built with `others`, set on every participant with figures, dropped for all of them on a load
  or a unit gone.

### 12.4 FightMotion: the third participant and aircraft height (`motion.{h,cpp}`)

- `FightMotion::build(r, attacker, defender, others)` (additive; the three-argument form calls it with none): every
  participant of the result in `CombatResult` order; a participant without figures (a city, the plot, a member whose
  figures were not given) is a centre only; a participant that fought with figures that were not given is refused by
  name. A figure with no target faces the defender's centre (the attacker) or the attacker's (everyone else) [I: 0321 4.1,
  the others fight the attacker]; with no known centre it keeps the placement's heading (before 4726 a city side without a
  centre was faced at (0, 0)).
- **Height**: `FigurePose::z` = the figure's height above its ground placement, from `FigureMove::z0` -> `z1` evenly along
  an air move, and the reached `z1` after it (at altitude between the flight out and home). `offsets()` gains a `heights`
  output; `FightPlacement::place` adds each height to the figure's z after `applyFigureOffsets` (which keeps the ZOffset
  over the new ground): no `placement.h` change. An aircraft still in the air at the fight's end (a flight cut by the
  limit, or the adapter's partial result) comes down along its walk back over max(ground distance, height) [I]. The EXE's
  `AltitudeDecelerationDistance` (4776 M1 + 0x60) is not read: the height changes linearly [I].
- The scene tool (`combat_scene`) writes `motion.csv` for every fight now (a column `z`); a refused motion is exit 4.

`Controller::combatFigures` sets `CombatMemberArt::anti_air` = 1 when the member's machine reads 1130 on path 4 (its
`p4` set, the values a CheckPathOption of path 4 compares, 0439), 0 when it does not, -1 without a machine (lead-0042
#8169: `controller.{h,cpp}` added to 4726's touches). By 0321 13.5's census the submarines' `1_omni_state_01` gives 0
(stock's strike on a submarine then holds to 20 s through the adapter, as stock does) and `ships_state_01` / the
modern-ship machines give 1; a member with 1 that binds no 1130 clip answers with its attack clip as with -1 (4777). The
scene tool's `--no-anti-air` stays for the offline runs that do not take members from a controller.

### 12.9 r1's nuke at the 20 s limit and the bomber's 'no pose program' (4729)

Written 2026-11-20 14:30- EST by W27 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w27-4729` (the team branch with `w20-4726`
merged). Offline only, from W20's r1 / r2 records: the server's controller input as written live
(`render_test_units_anim`, `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w20/anim-r1/server.c5anim`, `anim-r2/`; outside git), `render.log` and
`server.log` (`F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w20/live-r1-logs/`), replayed through 0374's driver (`unitanim play`) on the live
game's units database (`units-1.1.db` of the c5h-b run, copied) and the pure_vp install. Marks: `[C]` checked in a replay
or test named here, `[I]` this section's reading.

**Two faults, not one.** The 'no pose program' line names the **bomber** (0, 1053), not the nuke; the nuke's fight held
to its limit for another reason. Neither is a race of a new air unit's first frame (12.7's guess).

**(1) The nuke: three requests in one frame, the last one unread.** [C: the r1 record and its replay]
- The server drew r1's nuke at 0.2-1 frames per second (the loaded workstation; the record's EXE frame ids advance 130-200
  per server frame). The fight started in record frame 142 (dt 4.44 s); its first advance was frame 143 with **dt 6.08 s**,
  then 5.24, 2.81, 0.96 s, then 49 short frames (1.08 s in all), then frame 196 (4.90 s): 54 frames in 21.07 s, the limit
  reached at frame 196 (render.log 12:22:29.041).
- `CombatRun::advance(dt)` steps every 1/30 s step the caller's clock reached, so frame 143's one call ran the missile's
  whole opening on the core's own timers: `run` (1400), `combat_ready` (1600) and `attack` (1100), all three in that
  frame's events (the record: `ev 0 1062 action run`, `... combat_ready`, `... attack` before `frame 143`).
- Path 4 is a level: `Controller::event` writes each request's value over the last, and the machine is updated once per
  frame (at most 0.2 s, `clock.h`), so it read only 1100. The Nuclear Missile's idle state (7, `NuclearMissile_IdleA`)
  takes 1400 (to state 6 `Start_Run_Launch`, then 1 `Run`), not 1100: the replay of r1 keeps the missile in IdleA from
  frame 141 to 196 (t 0.2 -> 2.48 s). The strike's clock starts only when the attack clip plays (4.3), so it never started:
  0 hits, the blast owed, held to the 20 s limit, as the LOUD line says.
- **r2 is the same code on other frames:** `run` came alone in frame 2373 (dt 1.17 s) and `combat_ready` + `attack` 114
  frames later (2487, dt 2.47 s), when the missile was in `Run` (state 1), which reads 1100: the replay of r2 shows IdleA ->
  `Start_Run_Launch` (2374) -> `Run` (2424) -> `AttackA_KABOOM` (2487) -> `DeathA` (2488), and the fight ended by itself at
  about 17 s. **The final-damage clamp (W20's r1 fix) is not why r2's nuke ended:** the nuke's record has no unit side whose
  damage the clamp changes (no defender; the members are not clamped there; the missile's own final damage is not above
  its 100 [I: not read in r1's feed]); r2 differed in its frame clock.
- The same r1 record with the missile's `combat_ready` moved into frame 144 and `attack` into 145 (one request per frame,
  `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w27/spread.py`): the replay gives `Start_Run_Launch` at 144, `Run` at 145 and `AttackA_KABOOM` at
  146 [C].
- **The fix** (`srv_units_anim.cpp`, `ControllerFightPlayer`): the run's events go into a per-unit queue, and `takeEvents`
  gives each frame at most one request-bearing event (Action or Kill) per figure, in the core's order, a unit's later events
  behind its waiting one; at the fight's end what is left goes out in the end frame (a load drops it). The EXE's simulation
  posts its figure requests from one state-machine pass per frame (0321 4.2) [I: the same effect]; CombatRun's live wait
  absorbs the frames of delay. Counted `eventsDeferred()`. Nothing changes when the frame is shorter than one core step
  (1/30 s): at most one request per figure per frame then anyway.
- **Not changed, and why:** the fight's clock stays wall time. Capping the fight's dt at the controller's 0.2 s (one clock
  for both) was weighed and left: on r2's frame clock it slows the run to about half (7.3 s of 0.2-s-capped time in 14.2 s
  of wall time) and the 20 s wall-time limit (the EXE's, and the proxy's watchdog at take + 22 s) would then cut fights that
  end by themselves today [C: the sums over the records' frames] [I: the effect].
- On r1's whole frame clock the fixed nuke still needs more than r1's 21 s: the strike plays (the record replay above) but
  the effect wait follows it; whether it ends by itself or at the limit with its hit paid is the regression's `nuker1` case
  (below). A server drawing 54 frames in 21 s is the loaded workstation's, not a fight fault.

**(2) The bomber: a walk back the controller was not told to draw.** [C: record + log timing; I: the drawn set at that frame]
- render.log's LOUD (12:20:54.104) comes with the drawn frame after `drawn_frames=72`: record frame 72 or 73, the frame
  the bomber's fight ended (frame 73: `1053 action run/idle`, the damage released). `anim_drawn` drops 9 -> 8 in that frame.
- In frame 37, during the fight, the DLL sent the bomber `visibility 0` (the next case's setup ran while r1's slow frames
  still played the strike; a bomber back over its city is hidden). The core's fade takes it at once, so from then on the
  build does not list the bomber; while it is named in the fight the drawn set holds it (`withFighters`) and the view
  relists it.
- At its fight's end the bomber flies home (4724's walk back): no longer named, its view kept (`m_returning`),
  `HoldView::applyTo` relists it after the build, but the drawn set given to `Controller::apply` was built from the build's
  list (plus the named units) only, so `Controller::collect` gave it no program and the drawing asked for one: `UnitRefused
  ... no pose program for unit (0, 1053) figure 0`. In r2 the `visibility 0` came after the fight (line 1104 of the record),
  so the bomber stayed listed and nothing was refused.
- **The fix** (`AnimRunner::apply`): the drawn set holds the units walking back too (`AnimFeed::returningUnits()`).
- **W24's oldpc dev run on TBPP-HUGE_0350** (14.4 on `w24-4778`, kind b only, layout 1c21bea7b which has the walk back):

**Why the numbers moved** `[L]` for the measures, `[I]` for the causes:
- **Server CPU per drawn frame +4.0 ms (+49 %)**: the server's units, their animation and the fights (4756 measured the
  option without fights at +3.43 ms per frame on an idle camera, `unit-draw-filter.md` 4.3); the frame rate falls from
  186 to 134 fps with it. Per turn the server's CPU is lower in b (-2.6 %) only because b's turns are shorter.
- **AI turn wall -17 s (-9 %)**: b is shorter than stock, not longer, because its bursts are cut: the hold's watchdog drops
  the tail of each long burst at 22 s from the take (18-23 of 148 holds per b arm, the SAME event ids in every round, e.g.
  31227, 44415, 44471, 55677, 55698, 62466, 62478, 113690, 113715, 123142: the same fights of the same game), and the EXE
  moves on while the server still plays them. A server-played fight from its take to its drop is 10.5 s mean (queue
  included) against stock's 3.6 s per fight; per fight inside a burst the step is about 4 s against 3.6 s (above). With
  the watchdog fixed, b's turns would be longer than stock's [I]; MC #8748's bar (no watchdog drop, no fight longer than
  stock's per kind) is not met by this head.
- **What the player sees** (MC #8969 asks one line for the owner's A2): the EXE presents 187 fps without server units (a,
  5.335 ms) and 182 fps with them (b, 5.502 ms), -3.1 % [-2.7, -3.6 %], timing launch with no frame cap and
  WaitForVSync 0; the 186 -> 134 above is the SERVER's draw rate of the world picture, not the presented frame rate, so
  with server units some presented frames repeat the world picture (how many: not measured) `[L rates, I the repeat]`.
  No counter counts a repeated picture today: the compositor's `srv_new` / `no_new` count the shared-texture path only
  (0 under `render_handover=ring`), and the ring source counts per present only whether the picture taken matched that
  frame's camera (`ring_exact`) or was an older one (`ring_older`): dev run, a 16,224 / 54,358 (23 % exact), b 603 /
  42,066 (1.4 %). The fresh share is therefore given as an upper bound, server draws over presents: about 1.0 without
  server units, at most 0.74 with them `[I]`; an exact count needs a counter in the shell (a product change).
- **EXE frame time +0.17 ms (+3.1 %), longest frame +48 ms**: the compositor's insertion of the server's units and the
  bridge's position records (4756: +0.13 ms panning without fights); EXE CPU per turn -9.9 % follows the shorter turns.
- **Server memory +173 MB at the end and in growth over the ten turns**: the units' scene, the animation controller and
  the trigger stream (4756 without fights: +72.9 MB); the EXE's memory does not move.
- **The same game in every arm** (a precondition of the per-turn pairing, not the D164 pair): the combats per AI turn
  are identical in all nine arms (51, 52, 60, 63, 57, 41, 37, 29, 35, 28 for turns 350-359). The per-turn regression of b -
  a server CPU on the turn's fights (slope -2.64 +- 1.57 s per fight, n 40) is not a per-fight cost: both arms have the
  same fights and b's turn is cut by the watchdog in the turns with the most fights, so the slope measures the cut, not
  the fights `[I]`.

### 15.6 The flag-model offset, P2, P5 and P6: the methods [I]

- **Flag-model offset.** The flags sit at the EXE's unit position (UnitFlagManager); the server places a unit's root at
  the same position in position mode `exe`, so the offset that matters is the figures' distance from the root during
  walks and fights. From S1's and S4's `--evidence` dumps (`.c5units`, one per changed frame: root and figure lines):
  per frame and unit, the distance between the root and the centroid of its drawn figures, in world units, converted
  to px by the session's scale (the pixel distance of two neighbouring plot centres by the judge's `plot-pixel`, over
  their world distance), median and p95 per kind (walk, approach, strike, reform). The stock reference is the same
  measure on 0557's recorded stock fights (the offline set of 4776's 5.4), so no stock pictures are needed. The
  analysis script is to be written after S1 (its inputs are captured); `render/evidence/0442/fade_dumps.py` and
  `render/evidence/0375/4458/placement_inputs.py` read the dumps today.
- **P2 (effects on the server's figures).** Pictures: per ranged, city, air and nuke case, the frame where the
  projectile leaves and where it hits, against u0's frames of the same case (S3): launch at the launcher's figures, hit
  at the defender's figures, never at an empty plot centre. Judged by eye, two frames per case, written per case.
- **P6 (victory rate).** The controller's timeline of S4 (hundreds of shown fights) gives the server's victory decisions
  per surviving figure; the stock rule is `random(100) > 25` (`combat-choreography.md` 5.3 [C]), so pass is the server's
  rate inside the binomial 95 % interval around 0.75 for its count.
- **P5 (deaths per fight).** The same timeline: deaths per fight against the damage percent by the re-layout rule of
  `unit-formations.md` 7 [C]; the stock pictures of S3's `kill` and `melee` add one picture check each.

### 15.7 D118 negatives: what the player must see when a part refuses

| # | How it is made | Expected (the design) | Today [C] |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | S7's layout with the proxy before 0618's rows, on 26577625 (10 min in the S7 window, lead-0590's word) | the hold, the sound executor and the effect player each refuse with one LOUD line, a D118 report and the helper's popup; the server plays no fight of its own (the EXE shows fights as with Combat off) | the three refusals and popups exist (`Refuse` / `Report` in each module); **the server's question before its first fight is not built**: `SetServerFights` has no product caller (4782 / 4795 name it), so under the TEST switches the server still plays its fights while the EXE ends them in one or two frames (S1 of section 0): damage and flags out of step with the figures, behind a popup |
| N2 | arm nw (S6): the sound executor not armed | every shown fight is held to the proxy's watchdog (20 s + 2 s) and logged LOUD; no crash | follows from rule R8: only the sound executor hands OwnerEnd to the hold (`ProxySoundExec::Init` sets `ProxyCombatHold::OwnerEnd` as its sink; the effect player handles OwnerEnd for its own effects only) |
| N3 | a unit the server refuses (`UnitRefused`: 4726 r1's Bomber, 4778's Artillery, Great War Infantry, Machine Gun; the Destroyer before 0617) | not an invisible fighter (0617's acceptance) | invisible today (`unit-server-scene.md` 10: "that unit not drawn"); S2 and S4 list every `UnitRefused` by type |
| N4 | the server dies during a held fight (`render_test_av` at a frame inside a fight), only on the lead's word | the proxy's server-death report and popup; the hold does not keep the EXE waiting (the watchdog at most) | not run before; a deliberate fault, its cause known (COMMON 30 satisfied by the injection) |
| N5 | a fight the choreography refuses | OwnerEnd `Refused` at its start frame, LOUD, the EXE's fight ends at once | offline only (`fight_refused` in test_scene_units); no live way to cause it without a TEST seam |

**A finding for the owners of 4782 / 4795 and the arming (`[C]`, w26-4727 @ 2026-11-20 15:16 and w19-4723):** the three
proxy parts arm independently (`ProxyCombatHold::SetServerFights`, `ProxySoundExec::SetServerFights`,
`ProxyEffectPlayer::SetServerFights`, each with its own TEST variable). If the sound executor refuses (`sound-exec-bind`,
an unknown build or an access fault) while the hold is armed, the hold loses its only OwnerEnd source and every shown
fight waits the 22 s watchdog: on the huge save's 17 shown fights per AI turn `[L 4778]` that is minutes of stall per
turn, with a popup that says "silent", not "stalled". The product's single arming call should arm the three together
and, when the sound executor (the OwnerEnd carrier) refuses, disarm the hold and tell the server to play no fight, so the
player gets D118's popup and stock-like fights. N2 shows the stall live; the fix is not this ticket's.
