## 16. Route S arms as one and falls back as one (4783)

Written 2026-11-20 17:12-19:00 EST by W30 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w30-4783` (from `lead7-0042` with
`w26-4727` and `w29-4727` merged). The MC's ruling #8543 (thread 0042, 16:41) after W28's finding in section 15.7 of
`w28-4779` (the three parts armed independently; a refusing sound executor left every fight to the 22 s watchdog), with
lead-0042's conditions #8576 and the MC's #8582 (B). Marks: `[C]` checked by this worker in code or tests (each names
the check), `[L]` live, `[I]` a design choice or reading. Offline only: no instance in this pass.

### 16.1 What is built

- **The question and the answer** (`shell/common/vp_trigger.h` rule R9; reserved words only, no size or offset
  change, static_asserts on both blocks): the server block's `routeSAsk` (+72, the generation the server asks route S
  for) and `routeSTaken` (+76, the server's decision: 0 undecided, 1 TAKEN, 2 NO ANSWER, 3 REFUSED); the reader block's
  `routeSGen` (+40, written last), `routeSState` (+44: 0 none, 1 ARMED, 2 NOT ARMED, 3 DISARMED), `routeSParts` (+48:
  bit p = part p armed, bit p + 8 = part p answered; p 0 hold, 1 sound executor, 2 effect player) and `routeSBuild` (+52,
  the EXE's Steam build number, 0 = unknown). Helpers `VPTrigAskRouteS`, `VPTrigRouteSAnswer`, `VPTrigPublishRouteS`.
- **The common state** (`proxy/src/proxy_route_s.{h,cpp}`, new): idle until the server asks. The bridge's frame chain is
  now `ProxyRouteS::FrameHook` -> the effect player -> the sound executor -> the hold -> UI draw (each part's own step
  first, route S last; one hunk in `proxy_ui_bridge_rt.cpp` Init). The glue opens `<base>.Trig` with
  `OpenFileMappingW` (never creates it) every 60 frames until the server has made it. At the first question it arms the
  sound executor and the effect player (`SetServerFights(true)`), waits until both readers are attached (at most
  `kAnswerMs` = 5 s **of step time**, see "The answer window" below; corrected 2026-11-21 by W35, ticket 4730: it was
  5 s of wall time), then arms the hold and clears the Combat bit (16.3): **the hold comes last**, so no hold is ever
  taken while the OwnerEnd carrier is not attached. **Decided once per EXE process**: a later generation (a load) is
  answered with the state already decided.
- **The one line** (the server's log gets its own, 16.4), since 4730 (2026-11-21) for example
  `route S: ARMED on Steam build 4390913 (...) (decided once for this EXE process, 7066 ms after the question, 283 ms of
  step time of the 5000 ms window, longest gap between steps 7033 ms): combat hold armed (answered at 7066 ms, 283 ms of
  step time), sound executor armed (answered at 7066 ms, 283 ms of step time), effect player armed (answered at 7033 ms,
  250 ms of step time); Combat bit cleared at run time (config.ini has it on; set back as found at the disarm and the
  unload)`, or `LOUD: route S: NOT ARMED on <build>: a part did not answer in time; none of the three is armed for this
  EXE process and fights play the EXE's own way (Combat bit: as config.ini has it: nothing written, stock fights): combat
  hold not asked, sound executor NO ANSWER in the 5000 ms window (5016 ms of step time, 5016 ms after the question,
  longest gap between steps 33 ms), effect player armed (answered at 33 ms, 33 ms of step time)`. A refusal ends `REFUSED
  (<its reason>) at N ms`; a NO ANSWER set by the server's decision while arming reads `NO ANSWER before the server's
  decision (...)` with the same three times. (Before 4730 the ARMED line named only "N ms after the question" and a
  missed answer only "NO ANSWER in 5000 ms"; the part texts had no times.)
- **The answer window** (ticket 4730, W35, 2026-11-21) [C: `route_s_test`; L: W24's log for the stall]: the readers
  attach at their own next frame hook, which runs in the same frame chain just before route S's step, so what the window
  must bound is a number of frames, not wall time. W24's pre-merge run (#9046; c5h-b, build 4390913, the huge turn-350
  save, `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w24/live-c5hb/arms/b/vpproxy.log`, read only) shows the case: the question and both
  readers' arm at 77.671 s, then **no frame for 7.7 s** (the UI draw buffers' growth "after 2 frames" logged at 85.392 s),
  both readers attached at 85.393 s and route S ARMED in that same frame, "7718 ms after the question" [L]. It armed only
  because both attached in the first frame after the stall: the old step checked the answers before the 5 s test [C].
  Had a reader needed one more frame there, that step would have seen 7.7 s of wall time and fallen back: a false NOT
  ARMED, a D118 report and stock fights on a game with nothing wrong [C: the test below fails that way on the old rule].
  **Fix chosen: the window counts step time.** Each arming step adds the wall time since the previous step, at most
  `kStepGapMs` = 250 ms (a longer gap is a stall, not a frame), and the fallback comes when the sum reaches `kAnswerMs`
  = 5000 ms. Why this one: (1) while frames run (33 ms apart in the tests, up to 250 ms on a slow huge map) the sum equals
  wall time, so the true NO ANSWER falls back at exactly the old time; (2) a stall of any length costs at most 250 ms;
  (3) the window still ends when every frame is a stall: at least 5000 / 250 = 20 steps, never "never" (restarting the
  window after a long gap would not end at a loading screen's pace of one frame a second); (4) it is one counter in the
  core under the test clock, with no change to the parts. Measuring where the parts answer was not taken: their answer
  is "attached at the next frame hook", which is the same frame count. A longer window costs the player nothing: while
  arming no hold is taken, the Combat bit is not cleared (stock fights) and the server writes no record (16.4); the
  server's own NO ANSWER at its first fight record still ends the arming at once. **Logged times**: each part's answer
  time (wall ms after the question and step time at that moment; a reader's is the first step that saw it attached, the
  hold's the step that armed it, a refusal's the call that refused) in the ARMED line and in every NOT ARMED line, and the
  window's step time and the longest gap between steps. Tests (`route_s_test` 223/223, 2026-11-21 03:05 EST, proxy
  toolchain and ASan): `CaseStallThenAnswered` (W24's shape: 7718 ms stall, both attach at the next frame, ARMED, "250 ms
  of step time"; then a 7 s stall after which the executor needs one more frame: ARMED at 7066 ms wall, 283 ms step, no
  report), `CaseNoAttach` (no stall: NOT ARMED in the frame at 5016 ms, as before), `CaseNoAnswerWithStalls` (one 7 s
  stall: NOT ARMED at 11785 ms wall = 5002 ms step; a step every 1000 ms: NOT ARMED after exactly 20 steps),
  `CaseServerNotTaken` (the server's NO ANSWER while arming: "combat hold NO ANSWER before the server's decision ...",
  the readers attached in that frame named with their times). The negative: the same tests against the old wall-time
  test fail 11 checks (the stall case falls back). Not live: the fix changes nothing in a normal load where the readers
  attach within 5 s of wall time (the ARMED moment is the same frame), so no live run was asked for (brief 4730).
  Builders (2026-11-21 03:08-03:13 EST, head of `w35-4730` with this change, `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w35/allb35.sh`, logs
  beside it): `server/build_server.py --config release` from `keep/pins-0.1b` (server.exe and the proxy) OK, `check stl
  ok: 52 objects`, proxy sha256 `9962d692...`; `test_proxy_rt` 213/213; `test_proxy_session` 165/165.
- **One D118 report per EXE process** (stage `route-s`, non-fatal, the helper's popup; its details name each part's
  reason and carry the four parts' counter lines), only on a supported build (`VpExeBuildProductReady`: 4390913 and
  26577625): a refusal there is a fault. On a build the patch does not support the line is LOUD and ends "(not a
  supported build: no report)". The parts' own reports go into it (`SetReportSink` in the hold, the sound executor and
  the effect player; one small hunk each); a part armed alone by its TEST switch with no question from the server keeps
  its own report (once).
- **Disarmed as one** (state DISARMED, for the rest of the EXE process) on: the hold's watchdog (a new watchdog sink in
  the hold: every hold the watchdog drops is passed with its event id and age), a part that stops answering (the hold
  no longer active, a reader no longer attached: the parts' fault paths turn themselves off), the server's NOT TAKEN or
  REFUSED, the server process ending without an orderly stop (its pid from the section, `WaitForSingleObject` every 30
  frames). Disarm = the hold disarmed, **every held fight released** (`ProxyCombatHold::ReleaseAll`: dropped at the
  hold's next frame, logged "by route S's disarm (released)", counted `released`), the Combat bit back, both readers
  detached at their next frame, the answer DISARMED (the server then sends nothing). One LOUD line names the cause and,
  for the watchdog, the fights' event ids and ages; the report once.
- **The product switch** (MC #8627, lead #8628): `[Renderer] ServerCombat` (options id 28, 0 to 1, **default 1**, in
  effect only with `ServerUnits = 1`). 1: the proxy adds `render_units_triggers=1` to server.cfg after the unit keys
  (`proxy_shell.cpp` `UnitLines`, one `shell: [Renderer] ServerCombat = 1: ...` line), so the server opens its trigger
  stream and asks. 0: the key is not written, the server never asks, route S stays idle and the fights run on the EXE's
  own timing, sounds and particles; one `shell: [Renderer] ServerCombat = 0: route S is off for this session (the
  player's choice, no report) ...` line, no D118 report. It is the troubleshooting switch a tester can be asked to set,
  and the ruling's **live forced refusal** (one session with `ServerCombat = 0` per build: fights stock, no wait).
  `docs/OPTIONS.md`, `research/07-architecture-decisions/options-file.md` 2. The installer's and the helper's
  configuration write it beside `ServerUnits = 1` (W31, after 0616).
- **TEST ONLY, compiled out of every product build** (MC #8639, lead #8635/#8640): only a test proxy built with
  `/DVP64_ROUTE_S_TEST_REFUSE_BUILD` (no builder of the repository defines it) reads `VP64_TEST_ROUTE_S_REFUSE=hold|
  sound|effect` and makes that ONE part's arm answer refused (`ServerCombat = 0` asks nothing, so it cannot make one
  part refuse); a release proxy never reads the variable. The offline tests make each part refuse through their
  stand-ins. The per-part TEST switches (`VP64_TEST_COMBAT_HOLD`,
  `VP64_TEST_SOUND_EXEC`, `VP64_TEST_EFFECT_PLAYER`) stay: without the server's question they arm their part alone as
  before; once the server asks, route S arms all three (an already armed part answers armed) and disarms all three on a
  fallback. So 4779's arm `s` (TEST switches + `render_units_triggers=1`) and the product arm `p` now behave the same,
  and 15.7's N2 (no sound executor) is made with `VP64_TEST_ROUTE_S_REFUSE=sound` (NOT ARMED, stock fights, no wait).

### 16.2 What the player sees [C: route_s_test; I: live not run]

| Case | Route S | Fights | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| all three armed (supported build, the row carried, config.ini as the product writes it) | ARMED, one line | the server's: the hold paces the EXE, sounds and effects from the stream | none |
| a part refuses at the arming, or a reader does not attach within 5 s of frames (step time, 4730; a load stall counts at most 250 ms) | NOT ARMED, one LOUD line | the EXE's own (Combat bit untouched): stock timing, sounds, particles, projectiles; the server's figures still move by its own clock | one, once |
| the hold's watchdog (an OwnerEnd that never came) | DISARMED after that one fight | that fight waited 22 s once; every later one stock | one, once |
| a part's fault, the server's NOT TAKEN, the server died | DISARMED at the next frame | held fights released at once; later ones stock | one, once |
| `ServerCombat = 0` (the player's or a tester's choice), or the server never asks for another reason (no trigger stream) | idle | stock (nothing written) | none; with `ServerCombat = 0` one start-log line |
| config.ini has Combat off (a player's or a test's setting) | ARMED without a write | armed: the server's; not armed: as with Combat off (results at once), named in the line | as above |

### 16.3 The session keys: a run-time bit instead of config.ini keys (4783's scope; lead #8576 (b), MC #8582 (B))

- **Why not the keys.** The EXE reads config.ini's `[DisableSystems]` once, at its start, into the app's mask
  `[g_Civ5App] + 0x940`, and app Startup creates the Combat system only when its bit is set
  (`../02-exe-internals/disable-systems-and-masks.md` 3, gate 0x476AA3) [C]. Route S is decided in game, after the
  server's question; a key set off in config.ini would leave no stock fallback (the system is never created: NOT ARMED
  would mean results at once, not stock fights), and a key set on cannot be turned off later. So config.ini keeps the
  player's values (0368's product: Combat, Particle and Projectile on; **no product default changes**), and the proxy
  writes only the run-time bit.
- **Why the bit works.** The combat simulation tests that bit for every RunCombatSim record it starts
  (`combat-choreography.md` 4.1 step 2, 0x731FF0) [C]: with it clear no simulation object exists, `EndCombatSim`
  follows one frame later (the state 4773's hold and 4771's S1 were built and measured on) and no EXE combat sound,
  particle or projectile of that fight is made (S1, section 0, measured with the key off [L]; the same per-fight test
  [I]). With it set the next fight runs the stock simulation.
- **The guard** (lead #8576 (1), MC #8582 (1)): the write goes only through the build-table row `rts_combat_gate`, the
  simulation's own start test (it loads g_Civ5App, tests the Combat bit 0x800 of +0x940 and branches; build 4390913 at
  0x7321BE, read from the golden copy, bytes only; the row's pattern is in `exebuild/patterns.txt`, used by
  `proxy/src/proxy_route_s.cpp`; D83 edit 2026-11-25, 0769: the byte pattern and its three instructions written out
  were replaced by this description), checked at run time with
  `ProxyExe::CheckPattern` before any write, so cam_app, the +0x940 offset and the 0x800 bit are tied to the code that
  reads them. Counted on both golden copies: exactly one match of that shape in each image, one distinct abs32 operand
  [C, 2026-11-20 18:05, a byte count only, no address of the new build printed]. **The row is lead-0590's** (requested
  #8600, relayed as #8602 on thread 0590): until the build table carries it, the symbol is not found by name, the
  Combat part refuses, and **route S is not armed on either build** (arm as one).
- **Read before write** (MC #8582 (2)): config.ini's mask is read once at the proxy's start
  (`ProxySession::ReadConfigIniMask`, not on the frame path); the value found at the field must equal it in all 24 known
  bits (Combat's included). Anything else (another bit differs, the Combat bit already clear while config.ini has it on,
  config.ini unreadable) is a value the proxy does not recognise: no write, NOT ARMED. Only bit 0x800 is changed, by a
  compare-exchange loop.
- **The restore** (MC #8582 (3)): the bit is set back only when this module cleared it (the value found at the arming had
  it set), at every disarm and fallback, at the proxy's `Shutdown` and `DetachOnUnload` (`ProxyRouteS::OnUnload`, two
  calls in `proxy_rt.cpp`, the 4662 form; lead-0042 #8603: written and tested offline, lead-0590's carrier answer
  pending), and when the server process ends (16.1). While armed the bit is cleared again if something sets it (every 30
  frames; one LOUD line). **At a process exit** (the game closed mid-fight) the memory goes with the process and the EXE
  does not write config.ini then: it writes config.ini only at its start, writing back what it read, and an in-game
  options commit writes `UserSettings.ini` (`../06-tooling-and-workflows/release-driver.md` W3c.2 [L]); `[DisableSystems]`
  has no entry on the options screen. So a cleared bit is never saved (a named limit, accepted #8603).
- **Projectile 0x2000 is not written**: a fight's projectiles are launched by the simulation (`effects-server.md` 1.1,
  0x759110), so with the simulation off there is none to suppress, and in the stock fallback the EXE's projectiles play
  as stock. **Particle stays on** in both states (stage A plays the server's effects on it; stock uses it too). The view
  mask's 0x800 follows the config mask through `proxy_shell.cpp`'s Apply (it clears what the config lacks and sets back
  what it cleared) [I: not read live].

### 16.4 The server's side (`server/src/effects/srv_trigger_emitter.*`, `srv_trigger_stream.*`, `units/srv_units_scene.cpp`)

`SectionSink::setRequireRouteS` (on for TriggerStream's section, `TriggerStreamConfig::requireRouteS` = true; off in
tests and tools that use the sink directly or only a log): the sink asks at each init (a load is a new generation and a
new question) and writes no record of a generation whose answer is not ARMED (counted `routeSDropped`). Decisions, one
line each in the units host's log (`UnitsHost::beginFrame` polls once per frame): TAKEN on ARMED (`units: route S (R9,
generation G, EXE Steam build N: combat hold armed, sound executor armed, effect player armed): TAKEN ...`); REFUSED on
NOT ARMED (LOUD, each part's answer named); NO ANSWER when the first fight record (owner or fightSeq set) comes before any
answer (LOUD; written back, so the shell disarms); a later DISARMED stops every further record (LOUD). The server's own
figure fights are not gated: they play by its clock in both states (only the stream is), so a NOT ARMED session shows
the server's figures fighting with the EXE's sounds and particles at the EXE's (hidden) figures' places [I: not seen
live].

### 16.8 The hold's watchdog from the server's start of each fight (W24 #8726, MC #8731 / #8737) [C: tests; I: live]

- **The fault** (W24's counted series on oldpc, `unit-combat-server.md` 14.4 on `w24-4778`, [L+C] there): the DLL makes
  an AI unit's attacks in a burst (6 takes in 16 ms), the server plays them one after another (4782's barrier), and each
  hold's 22 s watchdog counted from the TAKE: burst positions 1-2 lost 5 of 79 fights, positions 5-9 lost 15 of 27, the
  6th's OwnerEnd 5.7 s after its watchdog. With 16.1's rule each such drop would have disarmed route S for the session.
- **As built** (`proxy_combat_hold.*`, `proxy_sound_exec.*`, `proxy_route_s.*`; lead #8756 design, accepted by the eighth
  lead): (1) the server's START of a fight is its first record in the trigger stream: the sound executor reads every
  record (sounds and effects), and the first one with `owner != 0` that is not an OwnerEnd calls
  `ProxyCombatHold::FightStarted(owner)` once (a 128-entry ring dedupes; cleared at an attach and a new generation; no
  contract change, no new record kind). (2) A started hold's bound is the start + 20 s + 2 s. (3) The OUTER bound, for a
  fight never started: from the take, (20 s + 2 s) x (1 + its queue position), the position being the holds still held
  and not ended at its take (0 = the old 22 s; a burst's 9th = 198 s; bounded by the table of 64). (4) Both fire the
  same way: LOUD with the fight's id, its age and the bound's name (`by the watchdog (started by the server, no OwnerEnd
  within the fight's bound) after N ms (the server started it M ms after the take; queue position k)` or `by the outer
  bound (never started by the server) after N ms (queue position k)`), the watchdog sink passes `started`, route S's
  line names it (`fight event id 609 after 110000 ms (never started, the outer bound)`), every held fight is released
  and route S disarmed as one (16.1). Counters `started by the server N (without a hold N), outer-bound drops N`.
- **Tests** (2026-11-20 20:15 EST): `combat_hold_test` CaseBurst (9 takes in one frame, started and ended one after
  another 4.5 s apart: 9 OwnerEnd drops, 0 watchdog; the 5th never started: dropped by its outer bound at exactly
  5 x 22 s = 110 s, named; a started fight whose OwnerEnd is lost: dropped 22 s after its start, 32 s after its take;
  the existing watchdog and load cases adjusted to the outer bound); `route_s_test` with the three real cores through
  the stand-in stream: a burst of 9 played serially (the 9th OwnerEnd about 41 s after its take: 0 watchdog drops,
  route S stays ARMED, 0 reports), a burst of 9 whose 5th the server never starts (the 8 others end; at 110.0-110.2 s
  its outer bound fires, DISARMED as one, one report, the Combat bit back), a burst across a turn end (5 takes, 2 played,
  4 more takes, the 7 left played: 0 drops), a started fight whose OwnerEnd is lost (DISARMED 21.9-22.2 s after its
  start, the two others released). `route_s_test: 204/204` (proxy toolchain); the ASan and builder pass: 16.9.
- **What a burst costs a player against stock** (W24 #8743, `burst_4778.py` on 10 AI turns of the huge save, Quick
  Combat and Quick Movement off, [L] there, not measured here): one fight alone 4.7 s with route S against 3.8 s stock;

  about 1.2-1.6 times stock's, so with this fix a burst of 9 is about 36-45 s against stock's 25 s [I, W24's estimate].
  Before the fix the watchdog hid part of it by cutting the burst at 22 s. The fix removes the false drops; it does not
  shorten the fights: that is the fight clock's and the choreography's (MC #8748's second bar).

### 16.10 Late combat results: the owner-0 OwnerEnds closed (fix (A); W33 #8801, lead #8802, MC #8807) [C: code and tests; I: live]

Written 2026-11-20 21:36-21:39 EST by W32 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w32-stage5`, commit db1cce5b7. Offline only.

- **The fault** (W33's root cause, #8801, [L] counts on W0-b's s1-mid2 series, [C] code at `w30-4783` @6144b0b79): the
  server's GameplayUnitCombat / GameplayCityCombat override pushes the combat record (`SrvFeed::PushCombat`, returned 0,
  `kCombatReturnedKnown` clear), then forwards the call to the EXE, and stores the EXE's event id after the reply
  (`SetCombatResult`). `SetCombatResult` looked only in the pending batch: when the render thread's `Drain` (once per loop)
  had taken that batch while the call was in flight, the id was dropped and counted `combatResultsLate`. The fight then
  had owner 0: every trigger record and its OwnerEnd said owner 0, the shell's sound executor never passes such an end to
  the hold (`holdOwnerZero`), and since 16.8 `NoteFightRecord` ignores owner 0 too, so the hold ran to its OUTER bound
  (22 s x (1 + queue position), up to 198 s for a burst's 9th) and route S disarmed for the session. W0-b: combats 453,
  results 436 (late 17); 8 of the 17 were shown fights (executor `hold OwnerEnd 140 (owner 0 8)`); hold drops 146 =
  OwnerEnd 122 + watchdog 24, the 24 = 16 burst-class (fixed by 16.8) + these 8. About 5 % of shown fights.
- **As built** (files: `server/src/feed/srv_feed.{h,cpp}`, `server/src/units/srv_units_{fights,anim,core,scene}.*`,
  `server/src/effects/srv_trigger_emitter.*`, `srv_trigger_tap.h`):
  1. `SrvFeed::SetCombatResult`, record no longer pending: still counted `combatResultsLate` and returns false (the record
     was not completed), and the pair (seq, returned) goes into a ring of at most 256 (`kLateCap`; full: the oldest is
     dropped, `Batch::lateResultsLost` counts it) that the next `Drain` publishes as `Batch::lateResults` (the call marks
     the feed dirty, so that Drain returns true). `SetLateResultsKept(false)` turns the ring off: the feed before this fix,
     for the tests' negative only; nothing in the product calls it.
  2. `UnitsCore::onBatch` hands `b.lateResults` to `AnimFeed::lateResults`; `AnimFeed::fightsFrame` applies them before the
     fight clock's frame (`applyLate`): a combat record taken since the last close and not yet added to the clock is
     completed in place (as SetCombatResult would have done), otherwise `FightClock::setOwner(seq, id)` sets owner and
     ownerKnown on the fight of that seq, queued or playing (`Applied`; `Known` when its id was known; `NoFight` when the
     clock holds no such fight: Quick Combat, not visualised, refused or already ended). A started fight's player is told
     (`FightPlayer::ownerKnown` -> `ControllerFightPlayer` -> `AnimTriggerTap::fightOwner` -> `TriggerEmitter::fightOwner`):
     the emitter copies a fight's owner at `fightStarted` into its per-unit fight reference (W33's note said it reads
     `f.owner` per record; it does not), so that reference is updated, and every later record of the fight carries the id.
  3. The fight's OwnerEnd and its clip instances' OwnerEnds read the clock's `f.owner`: they carry the id from then on.
  4. **W30's FightStarted gap (MC #8807 (4))** closes by the same path: the first record after the id arrives has
     `owner != 0`, so the executor's `NoteFightRecord` passes `FightStarted(owner)` to the hold and the watchdog runs from
     there (the start is then the first frame after the reply: milliseconds after the true start, against a 22 s bound).
     No proxy change.
  5. An end still owner 0 (no result, or one later than the end): counted (`FightCounters::ownerZeroEnds`,
     `AnimCounters::ownerZeroEnds`) and LOUD (`fight seq N ends (OwnerEnd why) with no EXE event id ...`); a Reset is not
     reported (the load drops the holds).
  6. **Counts for the series (MC #8807 (3))**: the `units trigger` line (1 s and totals) gains `late=` (late results taken),
     `applied=` (applied through the ring: to a record + to a fight), `late_nofight=`, `oz=` (owner-0 fight ends). With the
     server report's `combats N ... combat results M (late L)` a run can say results == combats or name every difference:
     L = applied + late_nofight, and oz names what still went owner 0.
- **Tests** (2026-11-20 21:20-21:33 EST, this branch before the 0616 merge; the pass of section 19 repeats them on the merged
  head): `run_units_fights_test.py` 5035 passed 0 failed, plain and `--asan` (`testLateOwner`: the id before the start,
  while queued behind a fight of the same unit, while playing (the player told once, the clip instance's and the fight's
  OwnerEnd carry it), never (the negative: owner 0, `ownerZeroEnds` 1), after the end (`NoFight`, the sent end stays owner
  0), an id already known (`Known`, kept), a Quick Combat seq (`NoFight`)); `run_feed_test.py --asan` 304 passed 0 failed
  (the late pair in the next Drain once, not again; the negative with the ring off: counted and lost; 257 late results:
  256 kept, the oldest lost and counted); `run_trigger_emitter_test.py` 4473 passed 0 failed (`testLateOwner`: records
  before the id owner 0, after it and the OwnerEnd owner 1111; a second id ignored; the negative all owner 0);
  `test_scene_units` case `fight_late_result` (the id completing the record before its add; reaching the playing fight;

### 16.11 Late results without a fight, and the 22 s owner-0 lines of the sound executor (4731)

Written 2026-11-21 03:10-03:50 EST by W35 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w35-4730`. Read only: W24's pre-merge run of
stage 5 (#9046; c5h-b, build 4390913, the huge turn-350 save, 2026-11-21 02:33-02:48; `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w24/
live-c5hb/arms/b/` `server.log`, `server-report.txt`, `vpproxy.log`, `proxy-calls.tsv`), and the code at `w35-4730`
(main 7bb97c51c + 4730). Offline: one probe on the sound executor's core (below). No instance.

**(1) What a late result without a fight is.**

- **The late result** [C `srv_feed.cpp` SetCombatResult; 16.10]: every combat the DLL makes (`GameplayUnitCombat` or
  `GameplayCityCombat`) is pushed as a combat record and then forwarded to the EXE; the EXE's event id comes back in the
  reply. When the render thread's `Drain` took the pending batch while the forward was in flight, the id is "late": it
  goes through the late ring into the next batch. Whether a result is late depends only on that race, not on the kind of
  combat [C]. W24's run: 340 combats (213 unit, 127 city: `proxy-calls.tsv` 213 + 127 calls, 0.35 and 0.27 ms mean on the
  proxy's side), 334 results in their batch, 6 late (`server-report.txt` "combats 340 ... combat results 334 (late 6)")
  [L]; 1.8 % of combats.
- **Where a late result goes** (`AnimFeed::applyLate` [C]): (a) the combat record is still waiting in the anim feed (taken
  since the last close, not yet added to the fight clock): completed in place (`lateToRecord`); (b) else the clock's fight
  of that seq takes the id (`FightClock::setOwner` Applied: `lateToFight`); (c) else **NoFight** (`late_nofight`), which
  is any of: the clock never made a fight of that combat, because the EXE plays no simulation for it (the combat's
  visualise flag clear: `GetVisualizeCombat`, the target plot not visible to the active player, or Quick Combat;
  `FightClock::add` counts it `noFight` and adds nothing, 0321 4.1 and 7); the clock refused the record (kind, seq order,
  members); the fight had already ended; or setOwner answered Known. Known cannot happen for a late pair: the ring gets a
  pair only when the record left the pending batch without its id, so the fight's `ownerKnown` is false [C].
- **Why 5 of 6** [L counts, I for the share]: only 100 of the 340 combats were fights (the emitter's `fights=100`; the
  hold's `takes 100`; `combat hold: id ... not visualised: no hold` passed 200 by 533 s), so 240 (71 %) had no fight at
  all. A late result is a draw from all combats, so about 4.2 of 6 are expected without a fight; 5 is within that. The
  other NoFight kinds did not occur in this run: a fight that ended before its id came would end owner 0 and count
  `oz`, which stayed 0 [L]; a refused record would have a hold with no fight, and all 100 holds were dropped by their
  OwnerEnd (`hold OwnerEnd 100 (owner 0 0)` in the executor's line at 663 s, 100 `drop id ... by OwnerEnd` lines, 0
  watchdog or outer-bound drops, no DISARMED or NOT ARMED line) [L]. So the 5 are combats the EXE never visualised. The
  one applied result reached its fight before the fight's first record or while it waited (no `fight 0 (seq N)` line with
  N != 0, which a fight that started without its id and then got it would leave in the executor 22 s later) [C+L].
  The per-seq kind of each late result is not logged; naming it would need a line per late pair (not added: the
  counts already close).
- **Can one leave a hold or a sound open?** [C, L above] Not one of the not-visualised kind: the hold takes only a
  RunCombatSim record whose visualise byte is 1 (`proxy_combat_hold.cpp`: `kNotVisualised` -> "no hold"), and the server
  sends no record of a combat it has no fight for, so the sound executor and the effect player have nothing of it.
  The only NoFight kinds that can leave something open are a fight that ended before its id (its OwnerEnd is owner 0,
  the hold runs to its bound: 16.10 point 5, counted `oz` and LOUD) and a visualised record the clock refused (a hold
  with no fight: the hold's outer bound); both are named by other counters (`oz`, the clock's refusal line), and both
  were 0 in W24's run.

**(2) The `LOUD: sound exec: fight 0 (seq 0) sent nothing for 22000 ms: its sounds are stopped (0) by the watchdog`
lines** (three in W24's run, at 304.2, 488.9 and 645.3 s of `vpproxy.log`) [C code, L log, C probe].

- **Whose they are.** owner 0 with fightSeq 0 is not a fight: it is R7's second owner form, the **victory tail**
  (`srv_trigger_emitter.cpp` `triggers()`: a Victory-class trigger of a unit within `victoryTail` = 3 s after its fight's
  Natural end is sent with a `FightRef` of owner 0 and seq 0, owned by player and unit; 11.2's row "Victory tail",
  lead-0042 #8019). The emitter sends only one-shots in this form (`looping && tail` -> `afterEnd`, never sent). A late
  fight's records are owner 0 with fightSeq != 0, so they would read `fight 0 (seq N)`; none did.
- **Why a watchdog fires.** The executor keys its fight table by (owner, fightSeq) only (`SameFight`: both owners 0 ->
  compare fightSeq), so every unit's tail shares one entry (0, 0), refreshed by each tail record. 22 s (`kSilentMs`)
  after the last tail record the fight watchdog ends that entry; its one-shots ended long before, so it stops nothing
  ("stopped (0)"; `watchdog 0` in every executor counter line) [L]. It never reaches the hold: the watchdog does not call
  `PassOwnerEnd`, and owner 0 is never passed anyway (R8) [C]; route S's state is not touched [C; L: no DISARMED line].
- **Not harmless: a latent fault** [C, offline probe]. After the watchdog the (0, 0) entry is `ended`, and it is
  forgotten only `kSilentMs` after that (`Housekeep`'s last loop). Until then `DoStart` finds it ended and drops every

### 16.12 One dropped hold in S4: the sound executor's false watchdog swallowed the fight's OwnerEnd (4740)

Written 2026-11-21 14:30-14:50 EST by W41 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w41-4740` (from `lead13-0042` 0ba29413c).
Read only: W38's 4779 session S4 (#9432; c5h-c, build 4390913, `C5H-4779-HUGE_0350` turns 350-359, arm p, layout main
5ca0d512e with 4734 and without 4736, Quick Combat off): `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w38/s4779/live-S4-r1/out-p-S4-r1/`
`vpproxy.log`, `server.log`, `server-report.txt`, and `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w38/big/anim-S4-r1/server.c5anim`. Offline
only. Times are `vpproxy.log` seconds unless named `server`. **Corrects the ticket's first reading** ("an OwnerEnd that
came before its take"; "its sounds began about 752 s"): the take came first, and the 752 s figure read the LOUD line's
constant as a measurement.

**(1) The order of events for fight event 122793 (server seq 95112).**

| t (s) | What | Mark |
|---|---|---|
| 765.823 / .831 / .832 | the EXE's takes of 122775 (position 0), **122793 (position 1, outer bound 44 s)**, 122805 (2) | L |
| 765.953 | the server starts 122775 (its first trigger record through the executor) | L |
| 768.886 | 122775's OwnerEnd drops its hold (3062 ms) | L |
| 768.981 | **the server starts 122793**: its first record, `NoteFightRecord` -> `FightStarted`; the hold's bound is now start + 22 s = 790.98 | L |
| 768.981 | the executor's fight entry (122793, 95112) can exist only from here: it is made by a record of that owner, and the first one called `FightStarted` in the same step (the 128-entry ring passes each owner once) | C |
| 774.498 | **the executor's own fight watchdog ends (122793, 95112)**, 5.5 s after the entry was made: `LOUD: sound exec: fight 122793 (seq 95112) sent nothing for 22000 ms: its sounds are stopped (8)`. The line prints the constant `kSilentMs`, not the silence it measured | L line, C text |
| ~774.5-774.8 | the fight ends on the server and its OwnerEnd(122793) reaches the executor: `DoOwnerEnd` -> `TouchFight` finds the entry ended -> `wasEnded` -> **`PassOwnerEnd` not called** | C path, I step |
| 774.794 | the server starts 122805 (its barrier: the next fight after the previous one's end) | L |
| 777.6-789.2 | 122805, 123127, 124876, 124885, 125636, 125681 start and end by OwnerEnd | L |
| 790.978 | the hold's watchdog drops 122793: 21997 ms after its start (25140 after the take) -> route S DISARMED, D118 report | L |

The counts close it [L]: the server's `units trigger` line `fights=158 ... oe=3914 ... oz=0` with every fight ended by
789.65 server s (fights stays 158 through the disarm; the server plays them one after another); the executor `records
10577 ... owner ends 3914 ... hold OwnerEnd 157 (owner 0 0)` at its detach; the hold 158 takes, 157 drops by OwnerEnd, 1
by the watchdog, no `OwnerEnd ... which has no hold` line. So exactly one fight end reached the executor and was not
passed to the hold; `wasEnded` is the only path in `DoOwnerEnd` that does that [C]. The server's and the proxy's clocks
differ by at most a few hundred ms (the server saw the DISARMED answer at 790.727 server s) [L].

**Why the watchdog fired 5.5 s into a fight** [C code; I which record]: `Step` reads the clock once (`now`), then runs
the records; `DoStop` (a SoundStop record) stamped the fight with a **fresh** `Now()` (GetTickCount, 15.6 ms ticks), and
`Housekeep(now)` at the end of the same step computed `(DWORD)(now - lastMs)`. When the tick came between the two reads,
`lastMs = now + 15/16`, the unsigned difference wrapped to about 4.29e9 >= 22000 and the watchdog ended a live fight in
that step. No other path stamps a fight with a clock read later than the step's `now` [C: `DoStart`, `TouchFight`, the
ClipEnded branch and `EndFight` all use `now`]. Beside it [L]: between 765.48 and 783.11 the executor's stop records went
66 -> 74 while `stop record` (sounds stopped by a SoundStop) stayed 54: the stop records of that window found no live
sound by handle, as a stop of an already watchdog-stopped (or refused) sound would. **Which line would have said it**: no
log names the record a step ran; a per-fight `sent nothing` line with the measured silence (`now - lastMs`) would have
shown "4294967280 ms" at once.

**Two faults** [C], both in `proxy/src/proxy_sound_exec.cpp`: (a) the mid-step clock read in `DoStop` (a false executor
watchdog: the fight's loops cut 0.2-0.3 s early, sounds started after it dropped as "after end"); (b) an entry ended by
the executor's watchdog swallowed the server's later fight OwnerEnd, so **any** executor watchdog, false or true, cost the
hold its end and disarmed route S. The hold and route S worked as built: the hold's 22 s bound from the start is the net
that caught (b).

**The 9 `late_nofight` of the session are not this fault** [L counts; I kind]: `late` stayed 14 from 736 to 880 server
s, so 122793 had no late result (its id came in its batch); the 9th `late_nofight` came at 880-884 server s, after the
disarm; `oz=0` all session, so none of the 15 late results left an owner-0 fight end, and the other 157 holds all ended
by OwnerEnd. They are 16.11's kind (combats the EXE never visualised: 518 combats, 168 fights).

**Other logs** [L, 2026-11-21 14:40 EST]: of the 1013 `vpproxy.log` files under `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/` (27 with takes,
3380 takes), two executor fight-watchdog lines on a fight (owner != 0): S4's, and W24's `s1-final/out/arms/R1-b` (the same
file copied as `s1-mid3`): `fight 104583 (seq 986151)` at 1360.85, **6.2 s after its take** at 1354.65 (pre-16.8 code), then
`drop id 104583 by the watchdog after 22000 ms` at 1376.63: the same pair, false watchdog then a lost OwnerEnd [I: the
fight's first record cannot precede its combat call by 22 s]. W38's S1, S2, S3, S5, S7: no executor fight watchdog, no
hold watchdog, no disarm. The effect player's watchdog never fired in any of them.

**The fix** (`proxy_sound_exec.cpp` only; the hold, its watchdog and route S's disarm untouched) [C: tests below]:
- `DoStop(r, now)` stamps the step's `now`; `Elapsed` is signed (`(int32_t)(now - since) >= (int32_t)ms`), so a stamp
  later than `now` reads "not elapsed" (right across GetTickCount's wrap for spans under 24.8 days).
- `Fight::endPassed`: R8's "once per fight" is keyed on what the hold has heard, not on the executor's own `ended`. The
  server's fight OwnerEnd passes to the hold once even when the executor's watchdog ended the entry before it (its sounds
  stay stopped; nothing starts again: `afterEnd` as before). `ResetAll` (a new generation, the stream's stop, a detach)
  passes a Reset end for every entry not yet passed, a watchdog-ended one included.
- **A true executor watchdog** (the server really sent no sound record for 22 s): its sounds stop, the entry is ended,
  and the fight's OwnerEnd, when it comes, still reaches the hold through `DoOwnerEnd` -> `PassOwnerEnd` ->
  `ProxyCombatHold::OwnerEnd` (dropped at the hold's next `OnFrame`, "by OwnerEnd"). If the hold's own bound came first,
  the end finds no hold and is counted (`unknown OwnerEnd`), as for any end after a drop. In practice a true executor
  watchdog comes at or after the hold's bound of a started fight (the hold counts from the first record of any kind, the
  executor from the last sound record), so it matters for a fight whose start the hold missed (records before the take)
  and for the Reset path.

**Sweep of the same two patterns** (lead-0042, MC #9459) [C, read 2026-11-21]: `proxy_effect_player.cpp`: one clock
read per step (`Step`'s `now`; every stamp, `bornMs`, `lastMs`, uses it), so no stamp later than `now`; its `DoOwnerEnd`
ends the fight's effects (`EndOwned`) whatever the entry's state and passes nothing to the hold: neither pattern.
Its `Elapsed` stays unsigned (correct while no stamp passes `now`). `proxy_combat_hold.cpp`: `OnFrame` reads its `now`
once and compares `due` and `testEndAt` signed (`(LONG)(now - h.due) >= 0`), so a `FightStarted` or a take on the other
thread stamped after that read waits for the next frame: no false drop; an OwnerEnd after a drop finds no hold and is
counted, by design (the EXE's record was already released). Cosmetic only: a drop's `after` (`now - h.taken`, unsigned)
would print a wrapped number if a take stamped after `OnFrame`'s read were dropped in that frame, which cannot happen (a
fresh hold is neither ended nor due). `proxy_route_s.cpp`: one read per arming step. Related, not changed: a fight whose
first record comes **before** its take never "starts" for the hold (the ring passes each owner once and that call found
no hold); its hold keeps the outer bound, (1 + position) x 22 s from the take, which a playing fight (20 s limit) does
not reach [I].

**Tests** (2026-11-21 14:38-14:43 EST) [C]: on the old code `sound_exec_test` 118/126 (8 new checks fail:
`CaseWatchdog` now sends the fight's OwnerEnd after the executor's watchdog and expects it at the hold once;
`CaseTickInsideStep` puts a 16 ms tick inside the step that carries a SoundStop 5 s into a fight: no watchdog, the loop
plays on, the OwnerEnd reaches the hold) and `route_s_test` 232/237 (`CaseTickInsideExecutorStep`, S4's shape with the
three real cores: three takes in one frame, the 2nd started after the 1st's end, a mid-step tick at 5.5 s, its
OwnerEnd 0.3 s later: on the old code DISARMED by the hold's watchdog, one report). With the fix: `sound_exec` 12/12
(`sound_exec_test` 126/126 plain and ASan), `route_s` 9/9 (`route_s_test` 237/237 plain and ASan). Builders: the ticket
(4740) names the pass and its head.

**Not verified**: live (the START-REQUEST in 4740's READY: the same save and turns, holds all by OwnerEnd, executor
watchdog 0, disarm 0). Which record ran in the 774.498 step is [I] (no log names it).

### 17.2 What reads the table default instead of the written configuration (MC #8582 (A); #8648, #8650) [C, read only]

1. **A player who deletes `VP64Options.ini`: a gap.** The proxy's boot (`proxy_options.cpp` `OptionsBoot`) re-creates
   the file with every option at its table default, and `docs/OPTIONS.md` told players to delete it to go back to the
   defaults. ServerUnits then falls to 0 (the EXE's own units and fights: complete, no report), and ServerRenderer
   falls to 0 while config.ini keeps D33 (vp64helper's side): no guard was found for that state in `proxy_shell.cpp` or
   `proxy_rt.cpp`, so the player gets a world without terrain, the state the 0030 one-switch rule exists to prevent
   (`research/06-tooling-and-workflows/installer-notes.md` 9). An i2-era gap that i3 inherits. The MC opened ticket
   **0624** (#8659): the proxy writes the release's option set when it re-creates the file in a session with the patch's
   config.ini, a session found with that config.ini and ServerRenderer 0 gets the D118 popup and report, and OPTIONS.md
   is corrected.
2. **The 43-civ variant: no gap.** Both payloads carry the same `release-options.txt` (enforced at the installer build)
   and the same file is written.
3. **The modpack form: no gap.** `install.iss` takes the form from the Community Patch folder and writes the same
   `MyGames\VP64Options.ini`; the proxy reads the EXE's Documents folder in both forms.
4. The name check: 17.1's test.

### 17.3 The soak (4780): set-up, machine, time [I unless marked]

- **Game.** A new Standard game made by `soak_4780.py mksave` in one short launch (front end's new-game start: Continents,
  WORLDSIZE_STANDARD, 7 AI majors and the size's city states, Standard speed, Prince, Ancient era, every victory type on,
  max turns 0 as the front end sets it: whether that means the speed's own limit or none is `[I]`, `--until 500` ends
  the soak at turn 500 either way), saved by name at turn 0 (`C5H-4780-STD_0000`, kept on F: with its SHA-256, the
  instance's copy removed by hash), so any crash can be replayed from the same start, also stock. The map seed is not
  fixed (the front end has no seed key); the save is the reproducible start.
- **Play.** The soak launch loads that save, sets Quick Combat off and Quick Movement on through
  `Network.SendGameOptions` and reads both back (`Game.IsOption` and `PreGame`; PreGame's values decide, because the
  DLL's quick movement is PreGame's keyed option and `Game.IsOption(GAMEOPTION_QUICK_MOVEMENT)` read false while it was
  on, W24 #8726 [C]; 4778's counted series lost Quick Movement that way), then `Game.SetAIAutoPlay(500 - turn, 0)`:
  the human becomes the observer, who sees every plot, so every AI fight is shown and held (the stress case; from player
  0's view only fights on plots player 0 sees are visualised, `[C DLL]` 14.2). Quick Movement stays on because with both
  options off an AI turn is about 11 times longer (162 s per M turn at turn 151 in `turn-time-study.md`
  "screen-quick" `[L 0437]`), which would not fit the window.
- **Arms.** `p`, the product with the full set (needs 4783 and ServerCombat on the layout; the primary soak); `s`, route
  S by 4779's TEST switches, only if 4783 is not on Saturday's layout (the run then says so); `c0`, ServerCombat 0, only as
  a short comparison if the lead asks.
- **Machine.** The workstation, one old-build Goldberg instance on C: (`c5h-a` by default; EXE stamp 0x546CD0A8 checked by
  the chain; F: only under 50 ms read latency). Not oldpc: it is promised to 0615 from Sunday 08:00, and the soak may run
  past it; if the lead moves it there, `--deadline "2026-11-22 07:30"`.
- **Time.** mksave about 8 min; prep and arm 5 min; load 2-3 min; then about 5-15 s per turn for turns 0-80 (few fights),
  30-60 s for 80-250 and 45-90 s for 250-500 with every AI fight shown (the huge save showed about 17 fights per AI turn
  from player 0's view and 51-60 combats in all `[L 4778]`; a Standard map with 8 majors fewer): **about 6-11 h** for 500
  turns. A victory can end the game earlier (0175's huge fixed-seed game ended in a space race at turn 350
  `[L, release-driver.md W5.2]`). Window: Saturday 2026-11-21 about 20:00 to Sunday 10:00 EST; `--deadline
  "2026-11-22 09:30"` cancels autoplay, saves the game by name (`C5H-4780-P-T<turn>`) and stops safely, so a soak that
  is not done can resume from that save (`prep --save-from` it) on any instance.
- **A risk the first samples answer.** With both quick options off under observer autoplay the EXE's memory grew
  21-24 MB per turn over turns 151-155 (`screen-quick`, S2i:quick_off 23.81, S4:quick_off 21.47 MB per turn
  `[L 0437]`, both clients alike). If the soak's EXE grows like that with Quick Combat off alone, the 32-bit EXE
  reaches its address-space ceiling in about 100-150 turns. `check_4780` flags a largest free block under 300 MB and
  the private-bytes slope per turn; a crash for that reason is root-caused against a stock (`u0`) run from the same
  save to the same turn (COMMON 30).
- **A precondition, from 4778's counted series (W24 #8726, 2026-11-20 19:39) [L 4778, I for the soak].** The hold's

(route S as built: stage 4 + 4727/4728/4729 + 4783), for MC #8715 / #8748 and lead-0042's brief. Marks: `[C]` checked in

it from the EXE, `[L x]` recorded live by x, `[I]` this section's reading. No game instance was used. The live numbers are
W24's (14.4, oldpc job `20261120-175348-66a7`, `TBPP-HUGE_0350` turns 350-359, Quick Combat AND Quick Movement off,

### 18.1 In short

- **Why a server-played fight reaches the 12 s limit** `[C]`: nothing the fight waits for is missing. No clip end, sound,
  effect, shell message or owner end is waited for. The server's own choreography does not finish inside 12 s for one
  class of fights. **(L1)** The core kills exactly one figure per landing, so a striker with few figures (artillery 2,
  field gun 3, a battleship or cruiser 1, a WWI tank 2) needs more strike cycles than 12 s hold to kill or heavily damage
  a 14-figure unit. **(L2)** A killed side's owed hit can never be paid by a lone striker once all its figures are dying.
  Stock kills several figures per projectile hit (18.2). Stock arm R1-a: 1 of 151 shown fights at 12 s, all others at
  most 7.6 s `[L]`. Route S W0-b: at least a tenth at 12 s (W24's p90 12.01 s) `[L]`.
- **The 8 holds whose OwnerEnd never came** (lead-0042 #8799) are a feed race, not a fault of the emitter or the adapter:
  the EXE's event id is lost when the render thread drains the combat record before the forwarded call returns (18.3).
  W32 fixes it under 4783 (fix (A), MC #8807). W30's FightStarted rule had the same gap.
- **Every other item costs a few frames** `[C]`: the take to the server's start, the gap between the fights of a burst,
  and the OwnerEnd's way back. The 3 s ring-out and sound ends are not on the fight's path at all (18.4).
- **Cuts** (18.5-18.7), both built under 4783 on `w33-4783-kills` as stock's rules read statically
  (`combat-choreography.md` 5.4, 13.4 [C], 2026-11-20): C2, under which every struck figure pays one owed hit, so a
  killed side's owed hit goes with its first death; and C1, under which a landing strikes as many figures as stock's
  hit does (the weapon's `VisKillStrength`). Offline, after both, no case of 43 x 6 seeds reaches 12 s (before: every
  many-figure kill by a few-figure striker did). The longest is 6.90 s, and the kind means are 2.3-4.7 s against stock
  R1-a's 3.62 s (18.7).

### 18.2 The 12 s limit, offline [C]

**How the core ends a fight** (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`, `Sim::tick`): the run is done when no landing is
pending, every figure is Done / Victory / Removed and no side `need()`s anything. `need()` = planned deaths not yet played
plus owed hits not yet paid. Planned deaths = standing figures x damage % / 100 (`units::livingFigures`, 0321 13.4's
rule). `Sim::land` takes **one** victim per landing (the target figure, else the last doomed one), and it pays an owed
hit only when no planned death is left. Area deaths exist only for damage members and nukes (`Sim::area`). `pickTarget`
skips dying and removed figures. The defender owes one hit whenever there is no interceptor, also when it is killed. At
the core's own 12 s (`Sim::tick`, `t >= r_.limit`), every figure is forced to its end and the run reports done with
`at_limit`. The clock (`FightClock::frame`) then records the end as **Natural**, not Limit, because the player's
`advance` said done first. So in `fights.tsv` and in the OwnerEnd's why, a Natural end at 12.000 s is a limit end; the
adapter's LOUD "ran to its limit" line still names it.

**Runs** (2026-11-20 21:10-21:22 EST, workstation). This branch's builds are in `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w33/`:
`render/build.py --config Release` (176 s) and `build_trigger_scene.py` (57 s), both through quietlock. Install `pure_vp`
(a copy, never Steam); database `F:/c5-64bit-work/0327/db/Civ5DebugDatabase.db`. `trigger_scene.exe` plays one fight
through the server's `FightClock`, with the 4775 core stepped live against the controller (as `ControllerFightPlayer`
does) and the emitter. Drivers: `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w33/fights33.py` (26 kinds x 6 seeds) and `fights33h.py` (17
heavy cases, seed 1). The per-hit detail comes from `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene --live --positions` (`cs33.sh`,
`hits.csv`, `summary.txt`). Sides are `PLAYER:ID:TYPE:X:Y:DAMAGE_BEFORE:FINAL_DAMAGE:100`; ranged fights run with
`--ranged --no-retaliate`, melee fights with retaliation.

| Case | Strikers | Planned deaths | Hits by the limit | Server s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| artillery kills infantry (70 -> 100) | 2, cycle 1.77 s | 14 + owed 1 | 12 deaths (1.58, 3.35, ... 10.41 s, two per cycle) | **12.00** (6 of 6 seeds) |
| field gun kills GWI (40 -> 100) | 3, cycle 2.60 s | 14 + 1 | 12 deaths | **12.00** |
| cruiser kills GWI (40 -> 100) | 1, cycle 2.07 s | 14 + 1 | 6 deaths | **12.00** |
| battleship kills infantry (40 -> 100) | 1, two hits per strike, 1.43 s | 14 + 1 | 14 deaths by 9.48 s, owed 1 never paid | **12.00** (L2) |
| WWI tank kills GWI (50 -> 100), melee | 2 | 14 + 1 | 13 deaths | **12.00** |
| artillery on GWI 0 -> 60 | 2 | 8 + 1 | all | 9.87 |
| field gun on rifleman 0 -> 40 | 3 | 6 + 1 | all | 8.83 |
| tank on infantry 0 -> 50, melee | 3 | 7 + 1 | all | 8.37 |
| battleship on infantry 0 -> 60 | 1 | 8 + 1 | all | 7.87 |
| artillery on GWI 0 -> 35 | 2 | 5 + 1 | all | 6.33 |
| melee kills by many-figure units (cavalry, marine, GWI), MG and Gatling kills, ship on ship, unit on city | - | - | all | 2.1-5.8 |

Every case gives the same result for seeds 1-6 (`fights-s1.csv`, `fights-s2-6.csv`, `fights-heavy.csv`). So the server's
fight length grows with ceil((planned deaths + owed hits) / hits per cycle) x the strike cycle. Kills and heavy damage of
14-figure units (infantry, GWI, riflemen) by artillery, field guns, cannon, cruisers, battleships and WWI tanks reach the
12 s limit, and those are the core of a turn-350 AI war.

**Stock beside it.** Stock's projectile strikes several figures per hit. The figures a projectile will strike are chosen
at its launch from the striker's target and listed on the target participant, and its arrival strikes every listed figure
(`combat-choreography.md` 13.5 [C 0321]). Live, "the submarine's participant counted 4, then 9 hits launched" [L 0477].
The weapon rows carry `VisKillStrengthMin` / `Max` (artillery, battleship, catapult 25-50; the archer's flaming arrow
10-20) and `HitRadius` (machine gun 32 / 16) [D]. Stock's ranged volley of one archer on a warrior, on Tiny: 4.03-4.87 s
(16 fights) [L 4771 P4]. W24's stock arm R1-a over turns 350-359 (all kinds, 151 shown fights): mean 3.62 s, median 3.41,
p90 5.55, one fight at 12.01 s and every other at most 7.6 s [L, R1-a `arm.json`, recomputed 2026-11-20 21:20].

### 18.3 Owner-0 OwnerEnds: the 8 holds that never got an end (lead-0042 #8799) [C code, L counts]

- **Mechanism.** In `srv_remote_objects.cpp` `GameplayUnitCombat` / `GameplayCityCombat`, `SrvRemoteFeed::OnCombat` first
  pushes the combat record (`SrvFeed::PushCombat`: `kCombatReturnedKnown` clear, `returned` 0). The call is then forwarded
  to the EXE, and only after the reply is the EXE's event id stored (`OnCombatResult` -> `SrvFeed::SetCombatResult`).
  `SetCombatResult` looks only in the pending batch. When the render thread's `Drain` (once per loop iteration) took the
  batch while the call was in flight, the id is dropped and counted as `combat results ... (late N)`. The fight then has
  `ownerKnown` false (`FightClock::add`) and owner 0. Every trigger record and its OwnerEnd say owner 0
  (`srv_trigger_emitter.cpp`), and the executor counts the end (`holdOwnerZero`) but never passes it to the hold
  (`PassOwnerEnd`).
- **The counts agree** (W0-b): `server-report.txt` "combats 453 ..., combat results 436 (late 17)"; the executor's "hold
  OwnerEnd 140 (owner 0 8)"; the hold's "drops 146 (OwnerEnd 122, watchdog 24) ... unknown OwnerEnd 16". So the 24
  watchdog drops = 16 late ends (the burst class, 16.8) + 8 owner-0 ends, about 5 % of the shown fights.
- **W30's FightStarted rule (16.8) had the same gap.** `NoteFightRecord` returns at owner 0, so such a fight is never
  "started". Its hold waits for the outer bound, 22 s x (1 + queue position), with the EXE's AI turn stuck behind the held
  record (a barrier); then comes the LOUD line, and route S is disarmed for the session.
- **Fix (A)** (accepted by MC #8807, built by W32 on `w32-stage5`): late results are kept and published with the next
  Drain, and the fight's owner is set from them before its records and its end are written.

| Item | Route S (server, shell) | Stock (the EXE's simulation) | Extra time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Take -> server start | The combat record reaches the server before the EXE's take (it is pushed before the forward). `AnimFeed::fightsFrame` adds it in the frame that drains it, the clock starts it in the next frame, and its first advance comes one frame later: 2-3 server frames (13-25 ms at oldpc's 120-190 fps [I ms]) | the sim starts when the queue dispatches `RunCombatSim`, at the next pump (0321 4.1, 3.2) | 1-2 frames |
| Choreography length (clips) | Melee: the live core is shorter than recorded stock (median 0.64 of 0557's 19, 4.3; 0477's pair 2.50 s against 3.20 / 3.67 s). Ranged fights and kills: 18.2 | P4 4.03-4.87 s (archer volley), R1-a p90 5.55 s | the whole difference: L1, L2 |
| The 12 s limit | 18.2 | rarely (1 of 151) | up to 12 s minus stock's ~4-6 s per such fight |
| Gap between the fights of a burst | the barrier: fight A ends in frame N, B starts in N+1 and first advances in N+2 (`FightClock::frame` order) | median 0.01 s (a frame) [L W24, n 57]; P4 0.033 s on Tiny | ~1 frame |
| Ring-out (3 s) | `kRingOutMs` only stops one-shot sounds 3 s after their owner's end. The OwnerEnd goes to the hold at once (`PassOwnerEnd`, called from the record), and the next fight does not wait for it | no ring-out; every sound ended by End + 0.29 s [L 0599] | 0 |
| Waiting for a sound's end | nothing waits for a sound | nothing | 0 |
| End message's way back | OwnerEnd in server frame F -> the executor reads it at the EXE frame that shows F or later and passes it at once; the hold drops in the frame hook; the EXE's queue moves the waiting records at the next pump. That is a few EXE frames (~5 ms each on oldpc) plus the composite's latency [I ms] | the hold is dropped in the frame the sim ends (0321 4.2) | a few frames; does not gate the server's next fight |
| The hold's watchdog from the take | fixed by W30 (16.8) | - | was 22 s cuts in bursts |
| Owner-0 holds | 18.3, fixed by W32 | - | was a watchdog stall |

**MC point 5 (#8807): is the 1.2-1.6x partly the owner-0 fault?** No. The per-fight steps (W24: mean 3.86 / 4.10 s, p90
7.46 / 12.01 s) leave the watchdog-dropped holds out, so their 12 s steps come from L1 / L2, separate from the owner-0

### 18.6 C2 and C1 as built (`w33-4783-kills`, lead-0042 21:23 / 21:35, MC #8825) [C: these runs]

Both follow stock's rules from `combat-choreography.md` 5.4 and 13.4 (the static read of 2026-11-20, behaviour only).
They are separate commits, each with its own tests, and each has a comparison knob in `CombatParams`, on by default.

- **C2** (`owed_paid_by_any_hit`, `combat.cpp` `Sim::land`): every figure a landing strikes pays one owed hit of its
  side, and so does a death. A killed side's owed hit therefore goes with its first death. Test
  `a_killed_sides_owed_hit_goes_with_its_first_death`: a lone striker kills 6 figures; with the 4775 rule (knob off) the
  run holds to 12.00 s with the owed hit unpaid, and with C2 it ends at the last death plus the 1200 clip. Three
  expectations written for the 4775 rule now count one strike fewer (`one_figure_against_twelve...` 7 -> 6 strikes,
  with the old rule's 7 kept as a knob-off check; `a_strike_waits...` 3 -> 2 spans; the special test's bomber now ends
  at the later of home and the last removal).
- **C1** (`vis_kill`, `CombatWeapon::vis_kill_min` / `max` read by `loadCombatTables` from
  `ArtDefine_UnitMemberCombatWeapons`, `Sim::struckCount`, `Sim::nearestVictim`): a landing strikes max(1, ceil(U(Min,
  Max) % x the target's figures)) figures. The fraction is Min when Max - Min is below 1, the draw comes from the
  fight's seeded generator, and a weapon whose Max is 0 or NULL strikes one figure. The figures struck are the aimed one
  and the nearest others that may die (not the protected survivor; with LastFirst, doomed ones), up to the planned
  deaths still open. The extra figures' hit records carry no effect, sound or trigger: the aimed figure's record has
  them, as an area share's does. Test `a_hit_strikes_as_many_figures_as_its_vis_kill_strength`.
- **The rule in the server's log** (MC #8906, commit 80186e054): once per controller open, `UnitsHost` writes one plain
  line (not LOUD), `units: combat tables: VisKillStrength per landing`, or, when the database has no VisKillStrength
  columns, `units: combat tables: one figure per landing (database has no VisKillStrength columns)`. The line comes
  from `loadCombatTables(..., CombatTablesInfo*)`, `combatStrikeRule()` and `AnimRunner::combatStrikeRule()`. Tests:
  `combat_tables_from_the_database` covers both databases. `test_scene_units fight_controller` covers the hand-made TSV
  database, which logs the fallback line once. The new case `fight_strike_rule` covers the columns, which log the
  VisKillStrength line once.
  Runs on 80186e054 (2026-11-21 00:13-00:45 EST):
  - render `c5r_unitanim|c5r_units`: 41/41 plain and under MSVC ASan, 0 reports;
  - test_scene_units: 72/72 plain and under ASan, 0 reports;
  - `run_units_fights_test --asan`: OK;
  - the unitfeed and trigger_scene builders link.
- **Not ported (named difference):** ~~stock spares a participant's last standing figure while the other side still has

### 18.8 Melee fights at the 12 s limit on the stage 5 head: the killed side's last figure (W36, ticket 4733)

Written 2026-11-21 from 10:51 EST by W36 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w36-4733` from `origin/lead10-0042` (main with
stage 5, 502435e15, plus the tickets). Offline only; no game instance. Marks as in 18.

**The live class** `[L W24]` (#9069, warm-up arm W0-b of the 4778 stage-5 series, oldpc job `20261121-022916-a902`, route S
as the product, `TBPP-HUGE_0350` turns 352-359; `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w24/s5-mid/out/arms/W0-b/render.log`, outside git):
7 fights logged "ran to its limit (12 s)", all melee. W24's counted series (#9152): 7-8 such fights per round, the same
fights each round. The server's AnimFailed line gives the counts per side, not the unit types:

| Event id | Attacker standing, deaths, owed | Defender standing, deaths, owed | Hits | Steps | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 59984 | 14, 0 of 4, 0/0 | 2, 2 of 2, 1/1 | 6 | 42 | killed defender (A) |
| 128427 | 14, 0 of 6, 0/0 | 1, 1 of 1, 1/1 | 4 | 35 | killed defender (A) |
| 64400 | 2, 0 of 0, owed 0 of 1 | 1, 1 of 1, 1/1 | 2 | 12 | killed defender, the attacker's owed hit (A, W33's L2 form) |
| 106600 | 6, 0 of 0, owed 1/1 | 1, 0 of 1, owed 0 of 1 | 1 | 18 | the attacker never lands (B) |
| 114532 | 14, 0 of 4, 0/0 | 2, 0 of 0, 1/1 | 1 | 37 | the defender survives and never lands (C) |
| 120850 | 14, 0 of 2, 0/0 | 8, 3 of 3, 1/1 | 4 | 55 | (C) |
| 135151 | 14, 0 of 6, 0/0 | 1, 0 of 0, 1/1 | 1 | 33 | (C) |

"Standing" is the figures the server's controller still holds at the start: a 14-figure unit that lost figures in
earlier fights stands with fewer (the controller keeps a figure dead after its Kill event; `Controller::combatFigures`).

**(A) Cause** `[C code; C offline replay]`. In a melee fight that kills the defender, the attacker's landings can kill every
defending figure before any defending strike lands: the attacker's strikers (one per open need of the defender: its
planned deaths plus its owed hit) all land within one strike cycle, and with C1 a single landing may strike several
figures. A dying figure's strike is released (`Sim::die`), so no landing on the attacker is left in flight. The attacker's
planned deaths (or its owed hit, 64400: a ranged-capable defender owes the attacker one hit, 13.4) can only be played by
the defender's landings (`targetPart`: the defender strikes at the attacker only), so `need()` stays above 0 and the run
holds to `CombatParams::limit`. Stock's rule (`combat-choreography.md` 13.4 [C]): **the participant's last standing figure
is spared while the other side still has planned deaths unplayed or an owed hit open; the spared figure is only hit.** The
4775 core did not have it (18.6 named it "not ported").

**Fix** (lead-0042 #9134; commit `a059879e2`; `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` `Sim::spares` and three hunks in
`Sim::land`, `combat.h` one knob; 33 lines added, 3 changed, comments included): a landing that would kill the attacker's or the defender's
only figure not dying is turned into a plain hit (it pays an owed hit of its side as C2 has it, else it is Spent; its
`CombatHit` names the spared figure) while the other side's `need()` is above 0; a C1 landing's extra struck figures stop
at that figure too. The spared figure keeps striking; once the other side's needs are paid, the next landing kills it.
Knob `CombatParams::spare_last_figure`, on by default (off = the 4775 rule). `[I]` scope: participants 0 and 1 only; an
area share (a nuke's, a garrison's) and the interceptor or damage members keep the 4775 rule, since an area share is one
landing per death and sparing would drop it for good. A spared side whose figure can never strike (a civilian, a
non-retaliating defender) holds to the limit as before; it did so under the 4775 rule too.

**Regression cases.**
- Unit test `a_killed_sides_last_figure_is_spared_while_the_other_side_has_deaths_open` (`render/tests/unitanim/test_combat.cpp`):
  14 attackers at 15 damage (2 deaths) kill 2 defenders whose strike lands 1.8 s into its clip; knob off: 12.00 s, 0 of 2
  attacker deaths; on: ended below 10 s, both deaths played, the defender's last figure spared at least once and killed
  after the attacker's last death.
- `trigger_scene.exe` (the server's fight clock, the core against the controller, the emitter) on the install's art,
  driver `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w36/fights36.py` (28 cases x seeds 1-6): GWI or Infantry 0 -> 30 / 40 killing a machine
  gun, rocket artillery, a mech, a great bombard, Infantry or Riflemen; and 64400's form (WWI tank, AT gun, tank, XCOM
  squad at 0 damage killing a mech). Stage 5 (W33's build at 80186e054 = the stage 5 core): **144 of 168 runs at 12.00
  s** (every case but GWI killing a 14-figure infantry or rifle unit, whose melee weapon strikes one figure per landing so
  the defender lands first). With the fix (`a059879e2`): **0 of 168**, mean 5.07 s, longest 7.60 s (GWI 0 -> 40 killing a
  machine gun). `combat_scene --live --positions` agrees: 66 of 84 at the limit with `--no-spare`, 0 of 84 with the
  rule, longest 8.73 s (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w36/nofix1.csv`, `fix1.csv`).

**(B) 106600: the attacker never lands** `[I]`. Its 18 steps are the 14 start and end steps plus 4: the defender's
ready, strike and wait (its landing paid the attacker's owed hit), and one more step per attacking striker (2 reserved:
the defender's death and owed hit). Read so, the two attacking strikers reached combat ready or never ended their
approach, and never started (or never played) a strike in 12 s. Not reproduced offline (6-figure XCOM squad, Maori
warrior, Prowler; 2-3 figure tanks and guns against a 1-figure mech, great bombard, gunship or battleship). Candidates for
a diagnostic arm: an approach longer than 12 s (the two sides' figure positions far apart), or a strike request whose
clip the controller never plays (`progress`'s live wait; no LOUD MissingClip note was logged). The 13.4 rule does not
touch it.

**(C) The defender survives and never lands** `[I]`, 114532, 120850, 135151. The step counts say the defender's figures
never left their first state: 135151's 33 steps = 14 + 1 start steps, the attacking striker's ready, strike and wait,
and 15 end steps, so its one defending figure never went to ready (no target found) or bombard-defended throughout. In
the core that happens when the defender does not answer (`def_answers_`: the record's DefenderRetaliates bit; the DLL's
melee path always sets it, `CvUnitCombat::GenerateMeleeCombatInfo`), when its member cannot attack (no attack word in
`EnableActions`: in the offline database only civilians, great people, workers and work boats, `q2.py`), or when no
attacking figure is engaged (a melee defender strikes only at attacking figures that made their approach). Not reproduced
offline on the stage 5 code or with the rule: 14-figure GWI / Infantry / Riflemen / Minutemen at 30-45 damage against
WWI tanks, AT guns, artillery, rocket artillery, Krupp guns, helicopter gunships, great bombards, mechs, and 14-figure
infantry standing with 1, 2 or 8 figures (`combat_scene --defender-alive N`), fortified (`--defender-fortified`), with
and without positions: every run ended in 2.6-8.9 s. The live fights need the unit types and the run's figure steps:
W24's diagnostic arm (route S + the server's TEST timeline + the listener with both units' types) is the next step.

**Ranged and naval kinds shorter than stock** (W24 #9152: ranged 2.73 s against stock 3.91 s, naval 2.53 against 3.32)
`[C code, C offline]`: the 13.4 rule does **not** explain stock's extra time there. A ranged or naval ranged attack has no
retaliation (`DefenderRetaliates` false), so the attacker has no planned deaths and no owed hit, and `Sim::spares` never
fires (the other side's `need()` is 0); the rerun below changes no ranged or naval case. What stock spends beyond the core
there is `[I]`, not read: candidates are the wave counts that limit how many figures strike at once (5.1: +0x2B84,
+0x2B88, +0x2D30, +0x2D48; the core strikes with every figure, `max_in_flight` 0) and stock's choice of struck figures
at the projectile's launch (5.4), which the core makes at the landing. (2026-11-22, W50, 4741: both read and ruled out
as causes, 18.14.)
