### 18.10 Figures given back after a heal: the hole a damaged unit's creation leaves (W36, ticket 4736)

Written 2026-11-21 from 12:05 EST by W36 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w36-4736` from `w36-4733` 4df2ee456. Offline
only. Lead-0042 asked for a fight-end reconcile after impl-0637 saw, once on build 26577625 with route S on, `units:
UnitRefused ... UNIT_GREAT_WAR_INFANTRY: BadInput: no pose program ... figure 6` (MC #9206).

**Cause** `[C code + C offline test]`. The scene's placement draws figures 0..k-1 with k = `units::livingFigures(damage)`
(the 0x4B4B80 rule); the pose source refuses a unit when one of those figures has no program in the controller. The
controller erases figures only on a rise in damage (`ActionBridge`, `remove_fallen`: the range
[livingFigures(new), livingFigures(previous)) of the Damage event's two values) and gives them back on a fall
(`Controller::revive`, 0439). A fight's Kill events do not erase figures: they keep them dead in the controller
(`dies`), still held. And `Controller::create` takes no damage rule (`UnitInput::alive` -1 gives every figure), so a unit
created while damaged (at a load, an embark, or first seen) holds every figure. Its next rise then erases only the
middle range: 14 figures created at 60 damage, then 60 -> 70 erases figures 4 and 5 and keeps 6-13. A later heal
70 -> 40 wants 8 living; the old `revive` counted 12 held figures, gave back none, and the placement's figures 4 and 5
had no program: UnitRefused, "no pose program ... figure 4". impl-0637's figure 6 fits the same form (a 14-figure unit
created damaged, a rise that erased a range starting at 6, a heal) `[I: its event history was not logged]`.

**The fight form** `[C code + C offline test; L the live case]`. W24's stage-5 counted series (oldpc job
`20261121-022916-a902`) has the refusal once in every route S arm (R1-R4 b, 4 of 4), always `unit (6, 13653)
UNIT_GREAT_WAR_INFANTRY: BadInput: no pose program for unit (6, 13653) figure 8`, and in no q1 arm (ServerUnits 1,
Quick Combat on, no fights) `[L]`: a deterministic case of the save that needs a fight. In the code: a unit created
damaged holds all 14 figures; its fight's Kill events kill the last ones (say 8-13), which stay held and dead; the
damage after the fight may erase nothing (40 -> 45: 8 living either way); a later heal (45 -> 30, 10 living) finds 8
and 9 held, so neither the count nor the index rule gives them back, and the placement's figures 8 and 9 are corpses,
or have no program once the death program is gone. That the live unit had exactly this history is `[I]` (the series
does not log a unit's events); a series on a build with the fix shows whether the line is gone.

The fight-end reconcile proposed first (`revive` after a fight's end) would not have helped: the counts were already
enough, and a fight's kills are held figures. W36's server-side test of that idea (`fight_reconcile`, three variants:
the record's final damage above the drawn damage; the attacker's damage set before the combat; a held lower damage
after it) never refused a unit and was dropped.

The fight-end reconcile proposed first (`revive` after a fight's end) would not have helped: the counts were already
enough, and a fight's kills are held figures. W36's server-side test of that idea (`fight_reconcile`, three variants:
the record's final damage above the drawn damage; the attacker's damage set before the combat; a held lower damage
after it) never refused a unit and was dropped.

**Fix** (commit b5703369b, `render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp` `Controller::revive`): give back every missing index below
livingFigures(damage), lowest first, instead of only as many as the count falls short. Figures above the living count
that a creation left are kept (not drawn by the placement). Test
`a_heal_after_a_hole_gives_back_every_figure_below_the_living_count` (`render/tests/unitanim/test_bridge.cpp`): before
the fix figures 4 and 5 stay missing after 60 -> 70 -> 40 on 14 figures (3 failed checks), after it every figure 0-7 has
a program and 2 are revived. The 0439 test `damage_falls_revives_removed_figures` is unchanged and passes.

**Fix for the fight form** (lead-0042 #9278, commit after b5703369b on `w36-4736`): `ControllerOptions::revive_dead`
(default false), set by the server beside `ActionBridge::remove_fallen` (`srv_units_anim.cpp`, `AnimRunner::open`).
With it, `revive` first drops every held dead figure below the living count and then gives it back with the missing ones,
as a new figure in its member's default state: the EXE revives "from the first dead one forward" (`unit-formations.md`
7), and the dead machine itself stays dead (`unit-controller.md` 14.1). Dead figures above the living count stay. Off
(the dies mode, the render tools), dead figures stay as before. Test
`a_heal_after_a_fight_gives_back_the_killed_figures_below_the_living_count`: on, figures 0-9 are in the default state, 10-13
still dead, 2 revived; off, 8 and 9 stay in their death state (before the option, the on case failed 2 checks).

**Not changed** (named): `Controller::create` still holds every figure of a damaged unit (`UnitInput::alive` -1 means
"from damage" in `unit_scene.h`, which the controller does not apply); applying the damage rule at creation would also
close both forms at their source, but (1) it changes what a damaged unit's first fight counts as standing (fewer
strikers and targets, other planned deaths), and (2) stock does not always do it: 0557's w2 showed a unit at 85 damage
standing with every figure (`motion.cpp` `combatPositions`' note), so the rule at creation could draw fewer figures than
stock `[I]`. Not built (lead-0042 #9278).

### 18.11 An embarked unit not drawn: the swap's create refused for facing 7 (W40, ticket 4739)

Written 2026-11-21 from 14:22 EST by W40 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w40-4739` from `lead12-0042` 9489b2207 (main
77e3c0ff6 with 4736). Offline code reading and the kept logs of W38's live sessions; no run of its own.

**Symptom** `[L]`. W38's 4779 session S1' (2026-11-21 13:24, c5h-a, build 4390913, Tiny save, ServerUnits 1, route S)
and again S8 (14:40, c5h-b, server 1894a22b with 4736, ServerCombat 0): a human Swordsman made by the 4779 driver
(`run_4779.py` `embark_case`, `mk` = Lua `InitUnit`) embarks onto a sea plot: render.log `UnitRefused: unit (0, 1075)
UNIT_SWORDSMAN: BadInput: no pose program for unit (0, 1075) figure 0: not drawn`; the refused count rises 30 a second
for the whole stay at sea (S1': 0 -> 181 from 13:24:24.3 to 13:24:31.4) and stops at the disembark. A barbarian Warrior
the same driver made (`city_bombard`, (63, 1060)) is later refused the same way.

**What the controller got** `[C: the server's timeline (render_test_units_anim) and scene dumps (render_test_units_dump)
of those sessions]`. S8, unit (0, 1056), `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w38/big/anim-S8-r1/server.c5anim` and `dump-S8-r1/`:
- dumps 2540-2559: land row, plot 7,22, facing 2, flags 8; the timeline: `remove` at frame 2559's close, no `create`;
- dumps 2560-2743: `ART_DEF_UNIT_GALLEY`, plot 7,23, **facing 7**, flags 9 (visible, embarked) on every frame at sea;
- frame 2743's close: `create UNIT_SWORDSMAN 7 22 ... facing 0 ... flags 8`, `visibility`, `place 7 22 0`; dump 2744:
  land row, plot 7,22, facing 0. This create is the DISEMBARK, 6.13 s after the remove (S1': 6.04 s; the Lua listener's
  two `SerialEventUnitDestroyed` of the unit 6.03 s apart, the EXE's own model swaps), not a re-create from a stale
  record at the embark, as #9411 / #9423 read it.

**Cause** `[C code; L the record's facing in S8's dumps]`.
1. `CvLuaPlayer::lInitUnit` (and `InitUnitWithNameOffset`, `InitNamedUnit`) call `setFacingDirection(luaL_optint(L, 6,
   NO_DIRECTION))`: a unit a Lua `InitUnit` makes without a facing holds 7 (`NO_DIRECTION`, after `NUM_DIRECTION_TYPES`
   in the fork's `CvEnums.h`; `unit-server-scene.md` 2.2 rule (g)'s note) until a move turns it. A unit the DLL makes
   starts at `DIRECTION_SOUTHEAST` (`CvUnit::init`) and only `setXY` (`directionXY`) and the rotations change it: always
   0..5.
2. `CvUnit::move` posts `GameplayUnitEmbark` (`embark(pOldPlot)`) BEFORE `setXY` turns the unit, so kind 21 (a facing
   kind of the feed's table, `srv_feed.cpp` `FacingKind`) puts the getter's 7 into the record. The record stayed 7 at
   sea in S8 `[L]`, so no kind 12 / 30 reached it after the embark `[I: the step onto the sea was a kind 13, which keeps
   the record's facing by rule (g)]`.
3. `UnitsCore::onBatch` hands an embark of a unit the controller holds on as `kUnitCreated` (4469: the EXE's model swap,
   remove + create); `AnimFeed::close` removed the unit and `createOf` refused the create: it took facings 0..5 only.
   `createsNotFormed` counted it, nothing was logged, the unit was no longer held.
4. The scene's build lists the same record (it has no facing test: the module's `facingYaw` gives 6, 7 and -1 the EXE's
   1 rad, 4464) and the pose source finds no program for (0, 1056) figure 0: UnitRefused every frame. Every later op of
   the unit was dropped as not held; the disembark's kind 21 of a unit not held is a creation (`createOf` with the
   record's facing 0 by then): drawn again.

The barbarian (63, 1060) is Lua-made and never moved before the remove that had no create after it: the same refused
create of a remove + create (an embark or another swap) is the reading that fits `[I: no dump of S1' covers its frame
(the dumps stop at frame 4498)]`; it is not a DLL-made unit. **Scope** (lead-0042 / MC #9459): only units a Lua
`InitUnit` made that swap their model (embark, era change, paradrop) before their first move; DLL-made units never hit it.
VP's and mods' Lua, scenario scripts and our test drivers make such units.

**Fix** (`server/src/units/srv_units_anim.{h,cpp}`, `srv_units_scene.cpp`):
- `createOf` accepts the facings the scene lists and the module draws, -1..7 (4464); a create it refuses names the first
  test that refused (no table record; the owner's art; no Units row; the plot; no embarked row; a facing beyond -1..7)
  in a LOUD line `issue 4739: the create of unit (p, id) was not formed: <why>: not drawn until its record changes`
  (through the feed's LOUD channel, `units: AnimFailed`, the first 20 then every 100th).
- At each close the controller follows the table for the units the frame's ops touched and the units whose create was
  refused: a unit the table lists and the controller does not hold is created (`recreated`); a refused one is tried again
  only when its record's seq changes (`retriesWaiting` counts the closes it waited), never every frame; a held unit whose
  embarked bit differs from the table's is removed and created again (`rereads`); a unit whose record is gone is never
  created (its removal stands: no ghost); a unit a fight names or that walks back after its fight is the hold's and is
  not followed. The 1 s line carries `anim_not_formed`, `anim_recreated`, `anim_rereads`.
- The walk's turn rule treats a facing that names no direction (-1, 6, 7) as none: the first step of the walk turns the
  unit (it never turned from 7 before, `WalkOffsetDeg` is 0 there).
- The feed's LOUD lines are cleared at the top of `close` (they were cleared in `fightsFrame`, after the start's creates,
  so a refused create at the controller's start was never said).

**Tests** (`server/tests/units/test_scene_units.cpp`): `anim_embark_facing7` (a facing-7 unit created, embarked with the
canoe row, moved, disembarked: every step held, no create refused; before: the first create already refused),
`anim_record_kept` (MC #9402: create, then {UnitDestroyed, SetDamage} with the record kept: remove + create at the same
close with the record's damage, `recreated` 1; before: removed, not held), `anim_record_gone` (the same with the record
gone: removed, never created again, also when late ops of the key come), `anim_unformed_retry` (a refused create LOUD
once with its reason, not tried while the record is unchanged, created when it changes; the embarked-bit reread; a facing
9 refused with its reason), `anim_facing7_host` (needs the install: a facing-7 warrior through the host is drawn with
the controller's 12 figures, UnitRefused 0; before: refused every frame). Results: the ticket's log and the READY note.

### 18.12 The limit fights' inputs recorded: the diagnostic arm on oldpc (W40, ticket 4738)

Written 2026-11-21 from 15:00 EST by W40 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w40-4738` (= `w36-4738` with form C's fix
+ main 8252c9afc, 4736 in). The run: oldpc job `20261121-150825-9ca1`, 15:08-15:27 EST, rc 0.

**Why not the recorder** `[C offline-scene-harness.md 15]`. The scene recorder writes the feed only until its span ends
(the bundle finishes 600 iterations after the span), and `unitfeed` replays only the span's frames; a span covering 10
huge AI turns would be thousands of frames at 22-30 MB each (200-300 frames were 6-9 GB in 4772 / 0586). So the inputs of
the five fights are recorded as the controller's own input instead.

**Method.** ONE oldpc arm (MC-B's grant 2026-11-21 14:19, lead-0042 #9464): `cost_4778.py` kind d = route S as the product
(`ServerCombat = 1`, no TEST switch) plus the server's TEST timeline `render_test_units_anim` (every frame's controller
input, the fights' events included), TBPP-HUGE_0350, AI turns 350-359, Quick Combat off, no warm-up, no ledger,
functional only (no timing claim). `--check-exe-stamp`: both instances' EXE stamp read in the job, 0x546CD0A8 or no run.
Layout `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w40/rec38` (server.exe c58b54b4, proxy 3ae4e472, x64 DLL b84aa3e9, composite 07573f90).
Driver `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w40/rec38.sh submit`. The arm's `diag.c5anim` and limit lines come back with `tb.py fetch`
into `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w40/rec4738/` (C:, not F:: MC #9266 bars bulk writes on F: while a game runs from it;
nothing committed; `tb.py fetch` leaves `diag.c5anim` on the host unless `--include "arms/R1-d/*"`); the five fights
(106600, 114532, 120850, 135151, 135270) are found by their limit lines and replayed through `unitanim play
--timeline` (the controller as the server opens it) to see which requested strike's clip never plays and why.

**Results** `[L]` (arm R1-d): AI turns 350-359 played; route S armed, 168 holds all dropped by OwnerEnd, 0 watchdog, no
disarm; UnitRefused 0. Limit fights: **4** (120850, form C, is gone with W36's fix): 106600 (attacker 63/17444 Great War
Infantry `approach>strike f0,1`, defender 0/15080 WWI tank `ready>wait`), 114532 and 135151 (attacker 6/13653 GWI
`approach>wait`, defender the machine gun 0/16903 `ready>strike f0,1`), 135270 (attacker 6/18061 Paratrooper, the same
machine gun `ready>strike f0`).

**Cause of all four** `[C: the timeline sliced to the fights' units (W40's tl.py) and played through the controller
(unitanim play), each figure's state per frame; the omni state machine and the enter graph read]`. The frozen side is a
figure that sits in the omni machines' state 15 `ENTER_BOMBARD_DEFEND` from an earlier `bombard_defend` and never leaves
it: the machine gun entered it from its fortify loop at frame 75975 (a ranged strike on it before the fight) and stayed
in it for the rest of the session; the attacking GWI 63/17444 of 106600 the same. State 15 has one socket out, `15 ->
18` on `ECComplete(1280)`. Every socket into 15 from a non-idle state (22 fortify loop, 16 fortify fidget, 12 combat
ready, 14 attack, 17 run) sets path 6 = 1 (from idle 1: path 6 = 0), and `ENTER_BOMBARD_DEFEND_GRAPH`'s To side is a
Selection on path 6: 0 -> the enter clip 1280 (played once), 1 -> the loop 1285 (`Bombard_Defense_Idle`). With path 6 = 1
no source of 1280 is on the selected path, and the controller read `ECComplete` as "a source of the code on the selected
path and every once-played source done" (unit-controller.md 13.1): false forever. The frozen figure plays the 1285 loop
and takes no request but death, so its side's strike (the machine gun's bombard, the GWI's attack) is requested and
never played, and the fight runs to its 12 s limit. W38's S11 third form (106696: attacker standing, its planned deaths
unplayed, the defender losing figures) is the same: its defender 63/17444 is in state 15 at the fight's start `[C, S11's
timeline replayed]`. S11's 84632 (WWI tank on a commando) is another form: the tank's approach run took 8.7 s `[C]`.

**Fix** (lead-0042 #9549, the EXE's rule as W42 read it on build 4390913 [C, W42]): `ECComplete(ec)` holds when the
time in the current state is above the duration of the member's clip for that ec (0 when the member has none); no graph
is looked at, and the condition's value is not used. `render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp` `FigHost::ecComplete` with
`Member::ec_duration` (per member entry, read once when the member is bound, through the additive
`GraphFactory::clipDuration`, which `ClipGraphFactory` answers from its clip-duration cache; a factory that answers
negative, the test doubles, keeps the old walk). State 15 is then left after the 1280 clip's length whatever path 6
selects, strict `>` and per model as W42's reading (its open points, per model against shared and `>` against `>=`,
are W42's). (A first fix, "ECComplete of a code the selection does not reach is complete at once", was built and
withdrawn the same afternoon: the EXE does not walk the graph.) Test `ec_complete_is_the_state_time_against_the_clip_duration`
(`render/tests/unitanim/test_controller.cpp`): a fortified figure asked to bombard-defend enters 15 with path 6 = 1
(its graph plays the loop), is still in 15 at 0.5 s, in 18 at 1.0 s (the enter clip 0.8 s) and takes combat ready; with
the old reading it stays in 15 and never takes it. `ec_complete_shorter_alternative_and_missing_clip`: a death state with
two ECComplete sockets leaves at the shorter clip's length; a code the member has no clip for holds at the first update
with state time above 0 (strict: not at 0). render ctest 106/106 on `w40-4738` f7ba63607 (2026-11-21 16:26).

**The recorded fights replayed with the rule** `[C, 2026-11-21 16:27, unitanim built at f7ba63607; W40's fights38.py over
the play outputs]`: the side that was frozen leaves state 15 after the 1280 clip, takes combat ready and lands its first

sides `2:1041:UNIT_SHOSHONE_PATHFINDER:10:10:28:57:100` and `63:1045:UNIT_BARBARIAN_WARRIOR:11:10:75:100:100`.
- Steady frames (1/30 s), 6 neighbouring plots x seeds 1-8, charge_any on and off: 0 of 96 at the limit (3.9-5.6 s).
- One long frame (`--hitch F:0.7`) at every frame F = 20-110, seed 1: **charge_any on 14 of 91 at 12.000 s** (F = 28,
  29, 34-37, 57-64), **off 0 of 91**; a 0.2 s frame: 0 of 86 on, 0 of 85 off

**The mechanism** `[C: code read, the offline runs above, and unitanim play below]`.
1. The omni machine takes 1140 only from its run loop: `17 -> 14` on `P4==1140` (unit-controller.md 6.2's table); combat
   ready (12) takes 1100, 1160, 1180 and the run requests (1120 to 25 / 27, then 17 after 0.1-0.2 s), idle (1) and
   fortify take the run requests too; the entry into combat ready (8), the post-attack state (20), leaving combat ready
   (11) and the others take neither.
2. The core requests 1140 at its own charge timer's end (`combat.cpp`, `Sim::tick`, the Charge branch -> `startStrike`)
   without asking the controller whether the machine took the 1120. Path 4 is a level and the controller applies a
   frame's events before it steps the machines (`Controller::apply` -> `event` for each, then `step`), so when the charge
   (1120) and its end (1140) fall into one frame only the 1140 reaches the machine; and a 1120 that reaches a figure in a
   state that does not take it (8, 20, 11) is overwritten by the 1140 before the figure gets to a state that would.
3. The figure then sits in combat ready (state 12, the 1620 loop) for good: nothing requests a run again, and 12 has no
   socket for 1140. The core's live wait (`Sim::progress`: the strike's clock starts only when `playing(1140)`) never
   ends, the figure keeps its reservation of the target's last need (the defender's last planned death: `open()` is 0,
   so the attacker's other figures wait), and the fight holds to `CombatParams::limit`. **What would have ended it**: a
   1120 reaching the figure again (none is sent), or a strike code combat ready takes (1100). With charge_any off the
   approach is a run (1400) and the strike 1100, which combat ready (and idle, through 8) takes from any of those states,
   so the same frame does not hold.
4. `unitanim play` on hand-made timelines over the fight's start scene
   (`server/evidence/0042/4743/machine_1140.py`, unitanim of W43's `allb/rb` at ad4e87e85, 2026-11-21 22:55), the
   attacking figure 0's state and played codes per frame:
   - A: combat ready, then 1120 and 1140 in the same frame: `12[1620]` for good, **1140 never played**;
   - B: 1120, then 1140 six frames later: `12 -> 25 -> 17 [1120] -> 14 [1140] -> 20 -> 12`, 1140 played;
   - C: 1600, 1120 one frame later (still entering combat ready), 1140 0.2 s after: `8 [1600]` for about 1 s, then
     `12[1620]` for good, **1140 never played**;
   - D: combat ready, then 1400 and 1100 in the same frame (the charge_any-off path): `12 -> 14 [2100] -> 20 -> 12`.

**The live trigger** `[I]`: the core steps at 1/30 s; a server frame longer than one core step (any frame below 30 fps,
an AI-turn stall) runs two or more core steps before the controller's apply, so a re-charge shorter than that (a figure
just out of reach of its next target) begins and ends in one frame (A); or the 1120 reaches a figure still in 8 or 20
(C). S15's limit line fits A or C: figure 1's first state was a charge and its last a strike, 3 of 3 attacker deaths and
9 of 10 defender deaths played, the defender's last figure in wait (spared while the attacker had deaths open, 18.8,

### 18.14 Stock's strike gate and launch-time choice of struck figures, and what they do to fight length (W50, ticket 4741)

Written 2026-11-22 from 08:55 EST by w50-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w50-4741` from main 4c8d2702a, offline (no
instance, no game). Static read: read-only headless Ghidra 12.1.4 on a scratch copy of project `civ5`
(`reverse-engineering-setup.md` 2), DX11 EXE build 4390913, stamp 0x546CD0A8; behaviour only, no code (D83); the
listings stay in `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w50/out/` (outside git). Builds on `combat-choreography.md` (0321) 5.1, 5.3, 5.4
and 13.4, whose readings of the counts it replaces (corrected there the same day). Marks: `[C]` read in the EXE or run
here, `[I]` this section's reading. **Result: neither rule lengthens a fight; the 4741 gap is elsewhere** (end of the
section).

**The participant's counters** `[C]` (participant slot as in 0321 4.2): + 0x2B84 planned deaths, + 0x2B88 deaths
played, + 0x2D48 owed hits (all 0321 13.4), + 0x34 figures standing at the start (13.4's "whole unit dies" test is
+ 0x34 = + 0x2B84), and **+ 0x2D30 the figures under a projectile in flight**: raised at a projectile's launch by the
number of figures it strikes, lowered at its landing by the same number (floored at 0). It counts struck figures, not
projectiles or strikers. + 0x2CB0 is the participant's list of struck figures (32 entries) with its cursor at + 0x2D34;
the cursor only grows during a fight (0x7A19E0 clears it when the participant is set up), and a launch made when it is
at 32 chooses no figure.

**S1, the strike gate (the "wave counts")** `[C]`: there is no fixed wave size. Each frame, a figure in state 0/1
(looking) or 2/4/0xC with a target, whose member is a ranged one (figure flag 0x100, set by 0x6AE910 for a member with
`HasShortRangedAttack` or `HasLongRangedAttack`, or on an air side) and that is not flagged 0x8000, passes the target
finder 0x5C7100. It goes to the strike (state 10) when its **opponent** (participant 0 <-> 1) still has planned deaths
not covered, **planned > played + under projectiles in flight**, **or owes a hit (owed >= 1)**; otherwise it stands
(state 3 when the fight has a next phase, else 2, flag 0x800000) and is asked again each frame, so it strikes again as
soon as a landing reopens the gate. A weapon whose `ContinuousFire` is set (weapon record + 0x34, read by name in
0x6EDF90; in VP the first weapon of the Gatling gun and of the machine gun) skips the gate and always strikes. A figure
with no target is held by the same test (gate open: it keeps looking). Figures without flag 0x100 take the finder's
other branches (approach, melee) and are not gated this way; their deaths follow 13.4's planned / owed rule. Per kind:
- **ranged, siege, naval** (a ranged attack the defender does not answer): the defender owes one hit from the start
  (13.4), so **every figure of the attacker strikes in the first volley**; after the first landing pays that hit, a
  figure strikes only while the defender's planned deaths exceed the deaths played plus the figures already under
  projectiles. Every naval ranged attacker in VP is one figure (battleship, cruiser, dreadnought, frigate, galleass,
  missile cruiser, submarine), the siege units two or three, the bow units twelve, the Gatling gun, machine gun and
  bazooka three (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w50/py/units.py` on 0327's database copy).
- **a city as target**: a figureless participant (no planned deaths, one owed hit), so every attacking figure strikes
  while the city owes it. A projectile at a city strikes no figure (the chooser finds none; the landing only shows the
  hit effect at the city); where the city's owed hit is paid was not read `[I: open]`. **A city as attacker** has no
  figures, so no gate; its strike (`InitCityRangeStrike`) was not read.

**S2, the struck figures are chosen at the launch** `[C]`: the launch (0x759110, called from the simulation's
animation-event slot 3, 0x41EFC0, at the striker's `Transfer` trigger) counts the figures the shot strikes (0x6AA060,
0321 5.4) and chooses them (0x5E2BB0): the striker's aimed figure (its target, which the per-frame pass 0x5EFC50 keeps
up to date) always, even when it is already marked, plus the nearest others not dead, dying, marked 0x200 or protected.
Each chosen figure is marked 0x200 ("under a projectile") and the list rides with the projectile. At the landing
(0x658890) each listed figure is resolved by 0x5B4D00 (13.4: it dies if its side still has a planned death then, else it
takes the hit and loses 0x200). So **who is struck is fixed at the launch; whether a struck figure dies is decided at
the landing.** Side rules: an attacker's projectile launched when the target already has as many figures under
projectiles as figures standing, or no planned death left, flies to a miss point (its aim offset by the weapon's
`MissTargetSlopRadius` and the target member's `TargetRadius`; in an area fight, 0xC14F4 above 0, none is launched);
and the end test 0x7556C0 never ends a figure marked 0x200 while it waits for its projectile.

**Readings corrected** (in `combat-choreography.md` 5.1 and 5.3, 2026-11-22): 0x7635E0 is not a per-figure "approach or
wait" choice but the phase map (fight type + 0xC14FC, phase + 0xC1500 -> next phase; 5.1 M3 of this file); the victory
test of 0x7556C0 reads the **opponent's** counters: a survivor may play 1800 when the opponent's planned deaths cover all
its standing figures (the opponent's unit dies). Fight types (0x41F5F0) `[C]`: an air attacker 5 (6 with a collision
member); an attacker whose side can answer (+ 0x2D3E: a ranged member, an air side, or the ranged-attack flag) 4 when the
defender retaliates and cannot answer, else 1; every other 2, or 4 when the defender can answer and the attacker's
+ 0x2D45 (a member record's + 0x58, not named) is clear. Type 1, the ranged attack
the defender does not answer, runs **phase 1** (members whose `ReformBeforeCombat` names this side, 1 the attacker and 2
the defender, lay their formation out again facing the opponent and run there: state 0xD, then 3; the others go to 3),
**phase 2** (both sides turn to face, state 0xF; the next phase starts only when every figure of both sides stands in
state 3), then **phase 5** (the attacker looks and strikes through S1; the defender plays 1280), its last.

**What the core does** (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` at main 4c8d2702a) `[C]`: a figure strikes while the target
participant's `open()` = planned - died + owed - paid - reserved is above 0, where `reserved` counts strikes (one per
striking figure, from its decision to its first landing); `max_in_flight` (0, off) caps `reserved` further. The aimed
figure is chosen when the strike is decided (`pickTarget`: the fewest strikers), the extra figures of a VisKillStrength
hit and every death at the landing (`land`, `struckCount`, `nearestVictim`). Against stock: (a) in the first volley the
core lets planned + 1 strikers go where stock lets every figure go; (b) after the owed hit, the core counts strikes where
stock counts struck figures, so the core lets as many strikes go or more; (c) the struck figures differ (who), not the
moment of the deaths (both at the landing).

**Offline estimate** `[C: runs 2026-11-22 08:46-08:52 EST, workstation]`: `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene --positions
--ranged --no-retaliate`, built from 1e3d396e3 (main 4c8d2702a + this ticket's state line; Release, that target only, 31
s), the pure_vp install copy, 0327's database copy, 18 cases x seeds 1-6, `max_in_flight` 0 (the core), 1 and 2 (fixed
wave caps); driver `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w50/py/waves50.py`, rows `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w50/waves.csv` (outside git):

| Kind (cases) | core, cap 0: mean / max s | cap 2 | cap 1 (runs at 12 s) | stock live, 18.9 fe44 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ranged: crossbow x2, archer, composite bow, MG, Gatling, bazooka (7 x 6) | 3.22 / 3.73 | 4.86 / 11.10 | 5.90 / 12.00 (6 of 42) | 3.74 |
| siege: artillery x2, field gun, cannon, catapult, trebuchet (6 x 6) | 3.63 / 5.37 | 3.63 / 5.37 | 4.11 / 7.07 | 4.18 |
| naval: battleship x2, cruiser x2, frigate (5 x 6) | 3.55 / 6.77 | 3.55 / 6.77 | 3.55 / 6.77 | 3.31 |

Reading: a one-figure attacker (every naval case) cannot be wave-limited: identical at every cap. Siege changes only at
cap 1. The twelve-figure bow units are where a fixed cap bites, and it overshoots (the archer's kill of a Warrior at cap
1: 12.00 s in 6 of 6 seeds), because stock's gate is not a fixed count. Stock's own gate (S1) lets **as many or more**
strikes go than the core's at every moment (every figure while the hit is owed; afterwards a count that grows by the
figures each shot strikes), so following it can only keep a fight's length or shorten it, and S2 moves who dies, not
when. **Estimate per kind for stock's two rules in the core: ranged 0 s or shorter, siege 0 s, naval 0 s** `[I: from S1,
S2 and these runs; the rules themselves not built]`. The ranged 0.74x, siege 0.65x and naval 0.78x of 18.9 are not
explained by the wave counts or by the launch-time choice.

**Where the time is, then** `[I: candidates from this read; none measured here]`: (1) phase 1, the reform of
`ReformBeforeCombat` 1 members before they attack: in VP the archer, composite bowman and crossbowman, and the cannon,
field gun and artillery (not the Gatling gun, machine gun, bazooka, catapult, trebuchet or any ship; 0327's database
copy): their figures run to a new formation facing the target. The core has no reform. This fits siege being the
shortest kind (three of its main units reform) and 0557's a1 / k1 gaps (5.4). (2) Phase 2: stock turns both sides and
starts firing only when every figure of both sides has turned; 4735's `turn_first` (main bfb4b66cd, 2026-11-22 08:20,
after every live series of 18.9 and W40's 56eb) turns a figure only beyond 30 degrees and lets each strike on its own.
(3) The end: the survivors' reface and return (child 4742) and the victory clip (only when the opponent dies). A per-kind
rerun of 18.9's series on a build with 4735 is the first measurement to take.

**Two stock behaviours the core does not copy** `[C rule, I effect]`: the first volley of a bow unit shows every figure
firing (the core: planned + 1 fire, the others stand in combat ready), a visible difference with no time effect; and the
32-entry list of struck figures per participant per fight: when a fight's shots strike more than 32 figures in total
(continuous fire at a large unit), later shots strike nothing, so planned deaths can be left for the 12 s limit. Neither
was seen live.

What each phase does `[C]`:
- **Phase 1, reform.** A side whose members' `ReformBeforeCombat` names it lays its formation out again, rotated to
  face the opponent (0x5ACA80 -> 0x4A3560: the unit's formation for its figure count, turned by the direction to the
  opponent plus 90 degrees, living figures matched to the new slots, the slots written to the participant's slot table
  + 0x2B8C), and each figure runs to its slot (state 0xD, then 3); every other figure goes to 3 at once. **The phase
  ends when every living figure of both sides stands in 3.** The layout's centre (a unit-information field filled by
  0x65A900) was not identified: whether the reform turns the formation where it stands or moves it towards the
  opponent is `[I: open]`. In VP 121 member rows have `ReformBeforeCombat` 1 and 15 have 2, exactly the 15 rush (cavalry) members, which
  reform only when they defend; none has 3 (0327's database copy).
- **Phase 2, turn.** Both sides go to state 0xF (1450 shuffle); in type 2 the attacker waits in 3 instead. 0x5BB190
  turns a figure's heading by a quarter turn (to the side its facing is nearer) only when its member has
  `HasLeftRightAttack` (48 rows: every ship and two airship rows): a ship turns broadside. A land figure keeps its
  heading. A figure goes 0xF -> 3 when its turn is done (figure flag 0x2000); the phase ends again when every living
  figure of both sides stands in 3.
- **Phase 3 (type 2 only), the charge.** Every attacking figure goes to the charge state 0xC (run charge 1120 to its
  target, then the strike); the defender stands in 3 and does not strike. With a rush attacker the arriving figures
  stand in 3 instead of striking, and part of the defender is marked and set to 1280 (bombard defend), the rest to
  1600. **The phase ends at the attacker's first landing**: 0x493300 sets a flag (+ 0xC1505 bit 0) and the landing's
  resolver 0x5B4D00 then sets the advance bit (+ 0xC1504 bit 7, 0x44EBE0). It also ends when every attacking figure
  stands in 3.
- **Phase 4.** Every figure standing in 3 is refaced and set to 1 (looking), the attacker's and (when it retaliates)
  the defender's 0xE figures too: from here both sides strike, the defender at once.
- **Phase 5 (types 1 and 4).** The attacker's figures look (1) and the defender's too when it retaliates (else 1280).
  A figure whose member has `HasShortRangedAttack` (figure flag 0x100) takes 18.14's strike gate in the target step
  0x5C7100 and strikes **from where it stands**; there is no approach state in this branch `[C]`. Whether that is
  what a player sees for a Great War Infantry's melee attack depends on the reform's centre above `[I]`. In type 4 the
  first landing moves the fight to phase 4.
- **Phase 6 (defender answers first).** The defender's figures look and strike; the attacker waits in 3. The first
  landing moves the fight on (to 3 or 4).
- **The end** (0x5AD150, state 9 / 0xB): a finished figure that is away from its home slot runs back (the
  simulation's frame keeps the fight running while any figure does), snaps, refaces (state 7, 1000). So stock's
  `EndCombatSim` comes after the survivors' walk home. W45 saw it live as run loops 0.2-0.8 s before `EndCombatSim`
  (ticket 4742) `[L W45, I timing]`. Under route S the walk home came after the fight's OwnerEnd
  (`FightMotion`'s return walk), outside the measured fight (corrected 2026-11-22 by W54: since 4742 it is inside, 18.18).

  the frame loop 0x774FE0 walks it and erases a finished one). Per simulation: + 0x20 its clock (float s), + 0x34 the
  event id the hold is on, + 0x30 a serial (0xFF000000 | counter, 0x5C43E0), + 0xC14FC the fight type, + 0xC1500 the

  state.

  `PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` and reads with `ReadProcessMemory`, as
  `shell/evidence/0167/3701/target_probe.py` and `shell/evidence/0655/farm_pending.py` do, in a loop at 2 ms (about
  4 reads per game frame at 120-190 fps), each pass: the vector, then per simulation the clock, type, phase and the
  two participants' figure states. It writes one line per change (a new simulation, a phase change, a figure's state
  change, the simulation gone) with the wall time and the simulation's own clock, so a torn or missed read costs one
  sample, not a phase. The game never waits on it (an outside read does not stop its threads). At phase 1's start and
  at its end it also writes both sides' figure positions and the slot table: the slot centroid against the unit's own
  centre and the opponent's answers the open question of the reform's centre.

**The rule as built** `[C code]` (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` `Sim::reformFirst`, `combat.h` `CombatParams::
reform_first` / `reform_min_move`, `FigState::Reform` = 13, the EXE's 0xD):
- At the fight's first step, the attacker and the defender (participants 0 and 1; not the interceptor or damage members)
  are checked: a participant reforms when one of its standing figures' members has the side's bit in
  `ReformBeforeCombat` (`CombatMotion::reform`, already read by `loadCombatTables` and carried by
  `Controller::combatFigures` since 4776: **no new data path**; the models reader is not needed): 1 the attacker, 2 the
  defender. In 0327's database the column is 1 on 121 land member rows, 2 on 15 (the rush cavalry), NULL on every Sea,
  Air and Hover row `[C, SQL 2026-11-22]`, so ships and aircraft never reform.
- It needs the figures' positions and the unit's heading (`combatPositions`: `has_facing`); without them, or without the
  opponent's centre, no reform. The new layout is the figures' own start slots turned about the unit's own centre (the
  root, else the figures' centroid) by the angle from its heading to the direction of the opponent's centre (the
  centroid of the opponent's standing figures, a city's centre): stock's reform re-lays in place [L 18.15.1].
  `[I]`: stock lays out "the formation for its figure count"; the core turns the slots the figures stand in (the layout
  for the living count is not re-derived, so a damaged unit does not close ranks).
- Living figures take slots by nearest (greedy: the nearest free figure-slot pair first). A figure farther than
  `reform_min_move` (1.0 world unit) from its slot moves there at the 4776 motion (a run at MoveRate x 64, or the 1450
  shuffle at ShortMoveRate within ShortMoveRadius; the `FigureMove`'s code says which), requesting 1400 (Run) at 0
  (`FigState::Reform`, approach 1); on arrival it requests 1000 (Idle) and stands (`FigState::Look`). The phase ends
  at the last arrival plus that figure's run-stop clip (1440) `[I: the brief's and W51's rule]`; until then **no figure
  of either side looks, approaches or strikes, and a city attacker's volley waits** (stock: the phase ends when every
  living figure of both sides stands, 18.15).
- After it everything is as before (approach, strikes, end). A reformed unit's figures face the opponent: they take no
  `turn_first` turn (4735), which before turned ranged and siege figures in place for 0.3-1.2 s.
- `FightMotion` draws the reform's run (heading along the move), then the figure faces the opponent's centre (the Look
  step's target), unchanged code.

**Rule A** `[C code]`: host key `render_test_units_reform_first` (TEST ONLY, "1" default) -> `UnitsOptions::reformFirst`

### 18.18 The survivors' walk home inside the fight: `CombatParams::walk_home` (W54, ticket 4742)

Written 2026-11-22 from 10:32 EST by w54-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w54-4742` from `origin/w53-reform`
336ae2ed2 (18.17's head), moved at 11:40 to `w54-4742b` from main c781bf309 (reform_first merged; the same code). Offline only (no instance, no game). Proposal #10243, lead-0042's yes #10244 (rank as the
home, the rule A wiring). Marks as in 18: `[C]` read in the code or the EXE, or built and run here; `[L]` recorded live;
`[I]` this section's reading. The EXE reading is behaviour only (D83), taken from W50's and W51's existing read-only
listings of build 4390913 (stamp 0x546CD0A8), outside git under `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w50/out/` and
`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w51/out/`.

**The gap** `[C code]`. Under route S the fight's OwnerEnd is the core's end: `FightClock::frame` ends a fight when
`FightPlayer::advance` returns true, which is `CombatRun`'s end. `Sim::finish` put a surviving figure in Done (0xB) with
1000 at once. The way back to the unit's slots was `FightMotion::offsets` for t past the core's end: a glide with no
clip request, kept running by `AnimRunner::setMotion(ended)`. After the OwnerEnd the trigger emitter sends nothing for
the unit (`noFight`), so the run clip's loops of the way back were never sent. W45 heard stock's run loops 0.2-0.8 s
before `EndCombatSim` (#9852) `[L W45, I timing]`.

**Stock's rule** `[C, behaviour]`:
- A figure the end test finishes either takes victory (0x12, 1800; `combat-choreography.md` 5.3) or goes to 0xB.
  Entering 0xB, the figure is either set to 7 (reface, 1000) at once by a per-participant test, or flagged to return
  and left in 0xB. W52's live transitions 16 -> 7 and 16 -> 0xB -> 7 (18.15.1) are these two branches `[L]`. Which
  property the participant test reads was not read `[I: open]`. The victory branch never enters 0xB: a figure that
  plays 1800 does not walk home inside the simulation `[C]`.
- In 0xB the end handler (0x5AD150) compares the figure's position with **the figure's own stored home position** (not
  the reform's slot table at participant + 0x2B8C). While the figure is farther than a radius taken from its member's
  combat record, it keeps moving. Within the radius, it is snapped home and goes to 7 (reface, 1000). A figure that has
  not moved for a short time is also snapped home. The simulation's frame keeps the fight running while any figure is
  in 0xB.
- The simulation is removed about 0.03 s after the last figure reaches 7 (type 1 melee: 0xB 1.096 s of an end phase of
  1.126 s, 18.15.1) `[L]`. The arrival's run stop (1440) is not waited for.

**The rule as built** `[C code]` (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` `Sim::finish` / `Sim::walkHome` / `Sim::tick`,
`combat.h` `CombatParams::walk_home` (default true) / `walk_home_min_move` (1 world unit)):
- `Sim::finish`, when not at the limit and not a Victory, for a placed participant that is not an aircraft (4777's
  `flyHome` stays as it was), calls `walkHome`. The home is the start slot of the survivor's **rank**: rank i of the
  participant's survivors in figure order (victory figures count; dying or removed ones do not) goes to the start
  position of the standing figure whose index is i. That is the slot the placement after the damage gives it
  (`placeUnit` draws figures 0..m-1 in slots 0..m-1 of the n-member layout), and the slot `FightMotion::offsets`'
  after-end walk already ranks to. If no standing figure has that index (4744's gaps), the figure goes to its own slot.
- `walkHome` first cuts the figure's move still under way where the figure stands, as `flyHome` cuts a flight. Farther
  than `walk_home_min_move` from home, the figure moves there at the 4776 motion: a run at MoveRate x 64, or the 1450
  shuffle at ShortMoveRate inside ShortMoveRadius (the `FigureMove`'s code says which). The figure is put in **Done
  (0xB) with 1400** (Run when the member enables it; approach 1), with `returning` set and its target released.
  Otherwise it is Done with 1000, as before.
- `Sim::tick`: a returning Done figure that has arrived is set to **Reface (7) with 1000** (Idle). The end test counts
  Reface as finished and a returning Done as not. **The fight ends at the later of the last arrival and the last fall**
  (the dying figures still play their 1200 or `death_cap`). At the limit, a walk under way is cut where the figure
  stands, the figure stays in 0xB, and `FightMotion`'s after-end walk finishes it.
- The fight's OwnerEnd, its hold and the emitter need no change: the OwnerEnd comes when the core ends. The run (1400)
  is a Movement clip, which the emitter sends for a fighting figure (`movementInFight`). Its loops belong to the fight
  (`loopsByFight`); the shell stops them at the fight's OwnerEnd, which now comes after the last arrival (D210).
- `FightMotion` (`motion.cpp`): while it walks, a Done figure faces its way (unchanged move code). From its Reface step
  on, `pose` returns `yaw_known = false`, so the placement's heading (the unit's facing) is drawn, as stock's reface
  turns it. The after-end walk is unchanged and is now the fallback.
- `MotionCounters::residualWalks` (`srv_units_anim`): units that a placement still moved after their fight's end.
  Printed as `resid=R/N` (residual walks of N walks back) on the `units trigger totals` line, so a live run shows how
  often the fallback works.

**Known difference from stock** `[I]`. Stock walks each figure to its own home slot inside the fight and closes the gaps
of the dead afterwards, outside the simulation (the unit's own layout). The core walks rank i to slot i, so nothing
glides after the ring-out when the core's survivors equal the placement's living count. The difference shows only in a
unit that lost a figure other than its last: a survivor takes the dead figure's slot inside the fight instead of after
it. What still glides after the OwnerEnd, with no sound, is counted by `residualWalks`:
- a victory figure (stock's victory branch has no walk either);
- a walk cut by the limit;
- a living count after the fight that differs from the core's survivors (4744's undrawn figures, the VisKill sparing);
- a unit whose root or facing changes at the fight's end.
The arrival's run stop (1440) plays after the OwnerEnd, and its sounds are not sent (`noFight`).

**Rule A** `[C code]`: host key `render_test_units_walk_home_in_fight` (TEST ONLY, "1" default) -> `UnitsOptions::
walkHome` -> `AnimRunner::setWalkHome` -> `CombatParams::walk_home`; written into every bundle's render_config; sceneshot
sets it only on "1" (absent = a bundle recorded before 4742: the walk after the end) and prints `units walk_home W`
(`sceneshot_test.cpp`, `test_recorder_host.py`, the refused values in `test_render_host.py`). The library bundles hold no
combat (18.17), so no library frame changes. **Live default frames change**: survivors run home before the fight ends.

**Regression cases** `[C: runs 2026-11-22 10:56-11:03 EST, workstation]`:
- `render/tests/unitanim/test_combat_special.cpp`, 4 tests:
  - H3: melee survivors walk home to their rank's slot, Done 1400 then Reface 1000 at the arrival, the end at the last
    arrival, no strike after the walk's start, the same hits and deaths as off, and nothing left to walk after the end
    (the after-end walk of the rule before 4742 still walks).
  - H1: a reformed ranged attacker walks back from its re-laid slots; the defender does not walk.
  - H2: a gun crew shuffles home (1450 at ShortMoveRate).

### 18.22 When stock ends phase 1: at the last arrival, not after the run stop (W61, 2026-11-22)

Written 2026-11-22 from 16:05 EST by w61-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w61-4750`. Read only (D83): this file's
5.1 M3 and 18.15 [C], and W52's stock sampler file (18.15.1; `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-4745/w52-run/
sim52.jsonl.gz`, sha256 c0200a84...) read again with `server/evidence/0042/4750/ph61.py` (output `ph61.txt` beside it).
Not built. The question (18.17 `[I: open]`): does stock's phase 1 (the reform) wait for the reforming figures' run-stop
clip (1440), end at their arrival, or end on some other position test? Route S's `reform_first` (18.17) ends phase 1 at
the last arrival **plus that figure's 1440 clip** (about 1.0 s for the gun infantry), which makes its reform 1.0-1.5 s
where stock's measured mean is 0.72 s.

**Answer: at the last arrival, by the figures' simulation state, with no wait for any clip** `[C rule; L timing]`.
- The rule [C, 5.1 M3 and 18.15]: a reforming figure runs to its slot in state 0xD and goes to 3 on arrival (the move
  ends when the waypoint is within `MoveRadius`, flag 0x400, 5.1 M2); the phase map moves the fight on when every
  living figure of both sides stands in 3. State 3 is the simulation's figure state; the model's run stop (1440) is the
  machine's own transition and is not tested.
- The timing [L, W52's 10 AI turns on the huge t350 copy, stock, 2 ms passes]: in all 61 simulations with a reforming
  figure (57 of type 1, 4 of type 0), phase 2 begins **in the same sampled pass** as the last figure's exit from 0xD
  (last 0xD exit -> phase 2: mean, min and max 0.0000 s), so within one frame of the last arrival. Stock's reform runs
  (first 0xD entry -> last exit) 0.595 s on average in type 1 (0.881 s in type 0, n = 4); phase 1 lasts 0.620 s (type
  1, reforming fights only; 18.15.1's 0.722 s is the melee subset). Some figures leave 0xD straight into 0xF (the
  arrival and the phase change in one pass).
- So the 1440 stop is not part of stock's phase 1. The machine gets the next request while it is still in its run loop:
  phase 2's 0xF (1450) at once, then state 3's 1600 (with Walk) or 1000, so the run ends in a shuffle and stop-shuffle
  (or, with 1000, the machine's stop) inside phase 2 (10.14's machine chain) `[I for the clips played]`.

**What a change would be** (not built; the lead's and the MC's call): end the core's phase 1 at the last arrival
(`reform_end_` = the last `f.until`, not `f.until + stop`), and let the figures' Look start then. Two consequences:
- Phase 1 per kind would be the reform's last arrival of 18.17's table (reformed runs, K >= 1) instead of arrival + stop:
  melee type 1 about 0.40 s (max 1.02), melee on a city 0.41, ranged 0.51, siege 0.35, against stock's 0.62 (type 1
  reforming, this read), 0.72 (melee type 1, 18.15.1), 0.32 (city), 0.25 (ranged reforming) `[I: 18.17's offline
  arrivals against W52's live means; the core's slot choice and speeds are not stock's (18.17's [I])]`. 18.17's on - off of
  +1.0 to +1.5 s for a reforming fight would fall by the 1440 clip's length, about 1.0 s for gun infantry `[I]`.
- Stock follows phase 1 with phase 2, which the core does not have for land figures: 0xF for 0.43 s on average after a
  reform (this read; 0.41-0.48 s in 18.15.1). The same hold is 10.14's stance (1450 for `defend_stance_s` 0.45 s). A
  core phase 2 for **both** sides (every figure of a fight requests 1450 for about 0.45 s, Walk members, after the reform
  or at the start) would give stock's phase-1 + phase-2 span (about 1.05 s after a reform, 0.45-0.5 s without) and,
  through the machine's path 6, stock's silent combat-ready entry for the attackers too (10.14 section 4, the open
  follow-up). Ending phase 1 at the arrival without such a phase 2 would make a reforming fight about 0.4 s shorter
  than stock's phases 1 + 2 `[I]`.
- Open: the run's last 0.1-0.2 s (stock's figures arrive within `MoveRadius`, the core at the slot), and the turn of a
  land figure in 0xF that 18.15.1 saw take time without `HasLeftRightAttack` (not read).
*Built 2026-11-22 by W65 (ticket 5050) as `CombatParams::reform_ends_at_arrival` (the change above) and
`attack_from_stance` (the attackers' phase 2), both off until the MC decides: 18.23.*

### 18.23 Stock's phases 1 + 2 in the core: `reform_ends_at_arrival` and `attack_from_stance` (W65, ticket 5050)

*Both knobs ON by default since 2026-11-22, ticket 5050 W74, MC #10667 / #10726 (18.23.2). "Off by default" below
is the state W65 built and W70 measured.*

Written 2026-11-22 from 18:53 EST by w65-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w65-5050` from main 044b81d42 (= f2e97eecf,
4750 merged, plus research and tracker commits). Offline only: no instance, no game, no LTO, every build through
quietlock. Marks as in 18: `[C]` built and run here, `[L]` recorded live elsewhere, `[I]` this section's reading, `[D]`
read from the art census. MC #10414 widened 5050 to stock's phases 1 + 2; MC #10501 folded the Gatling and siege early
end of W64's live S20 / S21 (#10495) into (b).

**The rules as built** `[C code: render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp, render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h]`. Two
`CombatParams` knobs, both **off by default** (the rules before 5050) until the MC decides from the table below:
- **(a) `reform_ends_at_arrival`.** `Sim::reformFirst` sets the end of phase 1 (`reform_end_`) to the last reforming
  figure's arrival instead of the arrival plus that figure's run-stop clip (1440). Stock's rule [C 18.15, L 18.22: phase 2
  starts in the sampled pass of the last 0xD exit in all 61 reforming fights]. The figures still request 1000 at their
  arrival (unchanged); every figure of both sides looks from the first step after the last arrival. No reform, no effect.
- **(b) `attack_from_stance`** (with `attack_stance_s` 0.45 s, `attack_ready_s` 0.15 s, `attack_hold_without_walk` on).
  In `ready()`, an attacking figure's first entry into Ready, when its last request is not a movement (1400, 1450,
  1120: an approach, a charge or a `turn_first` turn leaves the machine in its run loop already), of a land member, in a
  fight whose attacker is not an aircraft, first stands in stock's phase-2 state (`FigState::Turn`, the EXE's 0xF) for
  `attack_stance_s` (`Sim::attackStance`), then:
  - a member that enables Walk and has a 1450 clip requests **1450** (`ActionKind::Walk`, 4750's appended kind) for the
    stance, then 1600, and may strike `attack_ready_s` later: the 1600 meets the machine in its run loop with the shuffle
    selected, so the stop-shuffle state takes it to combat ready without the enter-combat-ready clip (10.14 section 2
    [C census]). Live, the strike starts when the controller says the machine takes it, as before;
  - a member **without Walk** (or without a 1450 clip) holds with **no request** for `attack_stance_s`, then requests 1600
    from idle and strikes only after the whole entry clip (`entry_wait`: no live shortcut). In VP's art the Gatling gun,
    cannon, artillery, machine gun, catapult, trebuchet, rocket artillery, mechanized infantry and bazooka members
    enable no Walk; the archer, crossbowman, composite bowman, rifleman and the infantry rows do [D 4408's census,
    `combats` table, 2026-11-22]. Stock's 0xF requests 1450 of such a member too; what its machine does with it was not
    read, so the hold without a request is `[I]`. The entry with its sounds is stock's: W64's S21 heard the stock Gatling
    crew's combat-ready sounds (riflecock, fortifyvoxb, foot) before its first shot at 2.68 s [L #10495].
  Skips (the rule before 5050): a figure that has moved, air attackers, ships (as 4750's skips), defenders (4750's
  `defend_from_stance` is the defender side), and with `attack_hold_without_walk` off a member without Walk.
- Not built: a phase 2 for attackers that approach (route S's melee attackers run to their targets; stock's type 1 melee
  attackers strike from their slots after 0.41 s in 0xF, 18.15.1). Melee lengths therefore do not move with (b).

**Rule A** `[C code]`: host keys `render_test_units_reform_ends_at_arrival` and `render_test_units_attack_from_stance`
(TEST ONLY, "0" default as built; "1" default since W74, 18.23.2; other values than 0 / 1 refused) -> `UnitsOptions::reformEndsAtArrival` / `attackFromStance` ->
`AnimRunner::setReformEndsAtArrival` / `setAttackFromStance` -> the fight's `CombatParams`; written into every bundle's
render_config; sceneshot sets them only on "1" (absent = a bundle recorded before 5050) and prints `units
reform_ends_at_arrival A, attack_from_stance B`. The library bundles hold no combat (W43's scan, 18.16), so no library
frame changes; with the keys at 0 no live frame changes either. `trigger_scene` takes `--[no-]reform-ends-at-arrival`,
`--[no-]attack-from-stance`, `--no-attack-hold-without-walk` and prints a `phases:` line (p1 = the first step that is not
the reform's; p2 = the attacker's first 1600 minus p1; its first strike; `astances` 1450 stances, `aholds` holds without
Walk; its 1600 requests from idle; the end).

### 18.24 5051: sound-start refusals over a session (W67, ticket 5051, 2026-11-22)

Written 2026-11-22 from 18:25 EST by w67-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w67-5051`. Offline: no instance, no
oldpc job, no build. Sources: the logs the sessions left (read only; not committed): S18 (18.20, oldpc job
`20261122-155914-a735`, W60b's local `oldpc-a735/out`), the S13 pair (10.13, `oldpc-6dff`), S20 / S21 (10.15,
`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w64/`), W37's two pairs on c5h-c (10.8, 10.9: `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w37/pair`, `tiny2`); the
executor's code (`proxy/src/proxy_sound_exec.cpp` at main c80eed046); the EXE's audio entries read by hand with
llvm-objdump in the golden copy of build 4390913 (PE stamp 0x546CD0A8), written here as behaviour (D83). Marks: `[L]`
the logs named, `[C]` code read, `[I]` inferred.

**Answer: the surge is the executor's, one cause.** Every sound the executor stops goes to the EXE's `FSound::Stop`
(`audio_sound_stop`), which halts the Miles voice with `AIL_stop_sample` and never gives the voice back: that Miles 3D
handle is not used again for the rest of the process. The 3D voices are 64; after about 64 stops the whole game's 3D
sound (unit sounds and the EXE's own 3D ambience alike) has one voice left. Stock never calls `FSound::Stop` on a unit
sound; it ends its loops through the `FSound` fade, which ends the voice at the manager's next update
(`AIL_end_sample`) and returns it.

**Per case, S18** (`server/evidence/0042/5051/refusals_5051.py`, tables in `server/evidence/0042/5051/tables/`; starts =
the server's `ss` in the case's window; played = the 3D Miles lives started in it, the EXE's own 3D ambience (coast
waves, gulls, whales) apart; lost = 3D handles whose last life ended by `AIL_stop_sample` before the case) `[L]`:

| Case | t from first Run, s | Starts | Played (unit) | Refused | Ambience lives | Peak 3D live at once | Lost before |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| melee | 0 | 45 | 38 | 16 % | 3 | 19 | 0 |
| rf_gwi | 23 | 77 | 55 | 29 % | 8 | 19 | 6 |
| rf_crossbow | 48 | 150 | 126 | 16 % | 10 | 42 | 12 |
| rf_cannon | 72 | 122 | 91 | 25 % | 12 | 40 | 18 |
| rf_lancer | 96 | 102 | 84 | 18 % | 8 | 24 | 24 |
| ranged | 122 | 79 | 33 | 58 % | 11 | 16 | 36 |
| wh_knight | 144 | 143 | 108 | 25 % | 20 | 16 | 42 |
| wh_knight_pike | 174 | 107 | 62 | 42 % | 13 | 12 | 52 |
| wh_warrior | 204 | 64 | 19 | 70 % | 13 | 10 | 54 |
| wh_sword_warrior | 228 | 72 | 3 | 96 % | 12 | 4 | 60 |
| kill | 252 | 36 | 5 | 86 % | 6 | 3 | 61 |
| wh_knight_b | 276 | 115 | 3 | 97 % | 4 | 1 | 63 |
| wh_knight_pike_b | 306 | 112 | 5 | 96 % | 7 | 1 | 63 |

The executor's own 60-s counters (vpproxy.log) agree: refused 26, 37, 39, 40 % in the first four minutes, then 93 % and
97 % (played 8 of 108, 7 of 227). The per-case split is good to a few starts (the server's 1-s lines and the Miles
clock are aligned by the fight starts, about 0.4 s spread); the Miles 3D lives also hold about 60 EXE-own unit sounds
over the session (setup fortify sounds), so "played (unit)" can exceed the executor's plays by a few.

- **It grows with session time, not with case kind** `[L]`: wh_knight 25 % refused (42 handles lost), the same case as
  wh_knight_b 97 % (63 lost); peak 3D voices live at once fall from 42 to 1; the EXE's own ambience starves too (8-20
  lives per case, then 4-7 in the last three).
- **The handles** `[L]`, `refusals_5051.py --fate` over each Miles log (a handle = a Miles 3D sample of the EXE's
  voices; "never again" counts include the lives that were simply the last before the session ended):

| Session (arm) | Machine | 3D handles used | Lives ended by `AIL_stop_sample`: handle used again / never | Loops ended by `AIL_end_sample`: again / never | One-shots ended by EOS: again / never |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S18 (route S) | oldpc | **64** | 0 / 63 | - | 695 / 0 |
| S13 (route S) | oldpc | 51 | 0 / 24 | - | 218 / 25 |
| S20 (route S) | c5h-b | 50 | 0 / 31 | - | 236 / 19 |
| W37 tiny2 b (route S) | c5h-c | **64** | 0 / 52 | - | 803 / 10 |
| W37 huge b (route S) | c5h-c | 54 | 0 / 26 (14 loops, 12 ring-out one-shots) | - | 932 / 27 |
| S13 u0 (stock) | oldpc | 20 | - (none) | 25 / 1 | 206 / 16 |
| S21 (stock) | c5h-b | 41 | - (none) | 21 / 2 | 254 / 39 |
| W37 tiny2 a (stock) | c5h-c | 45 | - (none) | 61 / 1 | 403 / 41 |
| W37 huge a (stock) | c5h-c | 30 | - (none) | 49 / 0 | 1,118 / 30 |

  196 of 196 lives the executor stopped left their handle unused; stock calls `AIL_stop_sample` on no 3D sound. The
  stopped lives equal the executor's stop counters (S18: stopped 63 = owner end 14 + stop record 49; all loops, Miles
  loop count 0, started by `AIL_resume_sample`). Two sessions reached exactly 64 handles and no 65th while refusing
  97 %: **the EXE has 64 3D voices** `[I, strong]`. The `FSound` objects themselves are not the limit: the 3D pool
  (`0x606BB40`, taken by 0x90AC10 from `Do3DSound`'s 0x90B240) is a free list that grows when empty (2n + 1) `[C]`.

**The EXE's two ways to end a sound** `[C, golden copy]`:
- `FSound::Stop` (0x90EDE0): with the sound live and not stopping, logs the name, calls the audio system's stop slot
  (`FAudioSystemMiles` vtable +0x58: for a 3D sample `AIL_stop_sample` `[L]`, a pause in Miles' terms), clears state
  bits 1 and 2 of +0x18, keeps bit 0 (holds a voice) and does not set the end state; then a bookkeeping call
  (0x90E730). Nothing on its path returns the voice or the object: the give-back 0x90AC70 is reached only through an
  `FSound`'s own release method (vtable +0x3C then 0x90AC70, at 0x91A920 and 0x91FDF0), which the manager reaches for a
  sound that has ended `[C for the paths; I that the manager never ends a paused sample; L that its voice never comes
  back]`.
- **The fade** (0x90EB90, thiscall (float seconds, float, int), `ret 0xC`): with seconds equal to 0.0 (the `.rdata` 0.0
  it compares with), or with no volume ramp on the sample (bit 3 of +0x18 clear: every unit 3D sample, exe-audio.md
  9), it only **requests the end**: +0x08 = 4, +0x28 = 1 (stopping), no Miles call; the manager's next update ends it
  with `AIL_end_sample` (exe-audio.md 9: 0.6 ms after the call) and the voice is used again (the stock rows above).
  With a ramp it sets one and lets the sound end at the ramp's end. *This corrects exe-audio.md 4.1's "otherwise it
  stops at once" (the stop is at the next update, through the end request).*
- **Who calls which** `[C]`: the fade is what stock uses for unit sounds: the unit-loop heartbeat's end (call at
  0x8DB6CD in 0x8DB660, with `fUnitLoopHeartbeatFadeLength`, 0.5 s), stop-by-unit (0x8DB600, the StopSound trigger's
  handler) and six other callers in the audio code. `FSound::Stop` is called in stock's unit path only when the 64-slot
  unit-loop table is full (0x8DB93F, the `audio_stop_call` row), so stock leaks a voice only then.

**The executor's paths** `[C, proxy_sound_exec.cpp]`: every stop is `StopNow` -> `ExeStop` -> `FSound::Stop`: a
SoundStop record, a fight's OwnerEnd or a ClipEnded for its loops, the 30-s ring-out guard for a one-shot, the 22-s
watchdog and the R6 reset. Loops are always stopped by the executor (no heartbeat sees them, exe-audio.md 4.3), so every
loop the server starts costs one voice for the rest of the process; one-shots cost one only when the ring-out guard
stops them (W37 huge: 12). The executor's own bookkeeping does not leak `[C + L]`: a slot is freed on every stop and
on every natural end found by the sweep; live now 0 at S18's end, full 0, the fight table under 64.

**Ranked causes of the growth** (the brief's list):
1. **A voice lost per executor stop** (above): `[C path, L]`, the cause. Ours.
2. Rule 9's playing count `[I]`: a stopped `FSound` that never ends may still count as a playing instance of its
   `SoundID`, so a loop script stopped 10 times would be refused for the rest of the process even with voices free. Same
   root and same fix; not separable in these logs.
3. Rule 8's "not again before" `[I]`: set only when the last instance of a define with `iMaxTimeMustNotPlayAgain` ends;
   a define whose instances never end never sets it, so it cannot grow from this. Not a growth cause.
4. Rule 2's manager counter `[I]`: what it counts is not read; nothing in the logs needs it.
5. The cut-off distance `[L]`: the camera is on each fight (18.20's frames), and the first cases refuse less with the
   same camera steps; not a growth cause.

**The part that is not the leak** `[L counts, I rules]`: with voices still free, 16-58 % of starts are refused (S20's
first case, ranged, 59 % with 0 handles lost; S18's ranged 58 % with 28 free). Candidates, from exe-audio.md 12.1 and
the census: rule 6 (161 one-shot unit scripts with `iMaxVolume` 0, always refused), rule 7 (253 with a chance below
100), rule 9's count of 10 per `SoundID` met by many figures at once (13.3: ten `FORTIFY_VOX` in one frame), rule 8.
Route S sends the tier-0 detail stock's tier test drops (13.1), so more of its starts meet these rules; stock's own
refusals leave no Miles line, so the like-for-like per case is not known yet. A separate note, not a defect so far.

**Fix design** (sent to lead-0042 as a QUESTION, #10522; proxy/src is outside 5051's touches until the MC widens them):
the executor ends a sound through the fade with 0.0 s, as stock's heartbeat ends its loops: `ExeStop` calls
`fade(sound, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0)` in place of `FSound::Stop`, which is then not called at all. Files: `exebuild/symbols/proxy.tsv`
(a code row `audio_sound_fade` for 0x90EB90 and a caller row `audio_fade_call` for the heartbeat's call, as the two
existing caller rows; 26577625's rows only in the local tables, D202), `proxy/src/proxy_sound_exec.{h,cpp}` (the
fade's type, a pattern row of its first bytes, the binding's symbol checks, `ExeStop`). No instruction byte is written
(D228): an existing EXE entry called as is, like the play. The executor's slot frees at once (`ExeLive` already reads
+0x28 != 0 as not live). Offline test: the core's tests stay (its `Audio.stop` is unchanged); a binding test that
`ExeStop` calls the fade with (0.0, 0.0, 0) and never the stop entry, with stand-in functions; the pattern rows checked
against the golden copy. The proof that a stopped handle is reused is live (below).

**The live check** (next stage, by its own START-REQUEST through lead-0042): oldpc, W60b's port
(`submit_tb4779.sh`, `tbjob_4779.py --session S18 --arms p,u0`), the 13 cases with the fixed proxy in arm p and stock in
arm u0, Effects raised in game, Miles logger in both. Bars: arm p's Miles log has no `AIL_stop_sample`; every loop ends
by `AIL_end_sample` and its handle is used again (`refusals_5051.py --fate`); distinct 3D handles in the range of the
stock arm (20-45, S18 64); peak 3D voices live per case steady, not falling; refused % of the last five cases within
the first eight's range; ambience lives per case flat. Diagnostic for the second part, with no proxy code: the EXE's
own FireTuner debug Lua (`Debug/Audio Logging.ltp` and `Debug/Audio.ltp` in the install: `BeginAudioLogging()`,

### 18.25 A hit target's sound names: stock's `$(WEAPON)` and `$(TERRAIN)`, route S's, and the fix (W69, ticket 5052)

Written 2026-11-22 from 19:45 EST by w69-0042, branch `w69-5052` (main 3f2add0b7). Offline: no game, no instance.
Marks: `[C]` read in the code named (the EXE: a read-only headless decompile of build 4390913 in a scratch copy of the
project, runbook 3; behaviour only, D83; no address of 26577625), `[L]` W64's live pair (10.15), `[I]` reading.

**Stock's rule** `[C]`. The Sound trigger's listener 0x4C4430 (`../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md` 2 step 1) fills a
name's variables through 0x4981B0 when the trigger belongs to a unit: four variables, in the table at 0xBA32E4,
`$(TERRAIN)`, `$(WEAPON)`, `$(MATERIAL)`, `$(BASETERRAIN)` (the second by its value's source, `[I]` by name), replaced
in one pass (0x54CD40). The values:
- **`$(TERRAIN)` and `$(BASETERRAIN)`** (0x5C59E0): the plot under the trigger's world position; its feature's
  `EffectTypeTag` when the plot has a feature and that tag is not empty, else its terrain's `EffectTypeTag`, else
  `DIRT`. (For a name that is not a sound script, `AS2D_` / `AS3D_`, of an air member, `$(TERRAIN)` takes a fixed value
  instead: effects only, not this ticket.) On VP's database (2026-11-22, the units database of W66's run) the terrain
  tags are DIRT, SAND (desert), SNOW, WATER (coast, ocean); the feature tags SNOW (ice), LEAVES (jungle, forest), MUD
  (marsh), WATER (oasis), none for the rest (flood plains, natural wonders: they fall to the terrain's tag).
- **`$(WEAPON)`** (0x56C4A0, then 0x781790, then 0x70DE60), each giving the weapon's `WeaponTypeSoundOverrideTag` for a
  sound name when not empty, else its `WeaponTypeTag`:
  1. the unit's own entry in its running combat: figure 0's record (the 0x158-byte figure record of
     `combat-choreography.md` 13.3) at +0x60, a weapon entry; who fills +0x60 is not read `[I]`;
  2. when that gives nothing: the **other participant** of the combat (participant 0 <-> 1, 0x665E70): its figure 0's
     current weapon (the member combat record +0x5C, the weapon index +0x64; so a member's second weapon when it is
     the one in use);
  3. else the other participant's city weapon; 4. else empty (the name then fails: "Can't find sound trigger for a
     variation of '%s'").
- The scripts that carry it are per target unit: `AS3D_UNIT_<unit>_IMPACT_<weapon>` (the hit reaction, in the
  install's `*3DScripts.xml`: WARRIOR, RIFLEMAN, TRIREME and the rest have ARROW, BLUNT, BULLET, BULLETHC, SPEAR, SWORD,
  EXPLOSION6POUND, EXPLOSION20POUND, ...), `AS3D_UNIT_<unit>_BODY_FALL_<terrain>`, `..._FOOT[_ALWAYS|_RUN]_<terrain>`.
  So a hit target's impact names the weapon that strikes it, its fall and feet the ground it stands on.

**Route S today** `[C]`: `server/src/effects/srv_trigger_stream.cpp` `TriggerStream::Subs`:
`weapon()` always takes the figure's **own** member's Index-0 row (11.3's `--death-weapon own`); `terrain()` takes the
host's `UnitTerrainFn`, else `DIRT` counted `terrainStandIn`, and **nothing in `server/src` calls
`TriggerStream::setUnitTerrain`**, so server.exe names every plot DIRT. The hit effects take the same `terrain()`
(`srv_fight_geometry.cpp` 419), so their surface is DIRT too.

**Per case** (`server/evidence/0042/5052/table_5052.py` over W64's position splits; the target's group; `[L]` by sample
file name; the stock-rule column from the database's weapon rows and the scripts above):

| Case | Route S (S20) | Stock (S21) | Stock's rule gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| ranged, df_archer (Archer ARROW on Warrior, not forest) | bluntflesh 4, bodyfalldirt 4 | arrowflesh 4, bodyfalldirt 4 | IMPACT_ARROW arrowflesh, BODY_FALL_DIRT |
| df_gatling (Gatling BULLETHC on Rifleman, forest) | smallbulletflesh 3, bodyfalldirt 3, footdirt 1 | bigbulletflesh 3, bodyfallleaves 5 | IMPACT_BULLETHC bigbulletflesh, BODY_FALL_LEAVES, FOOT_LEAVES footforest |
| df_fieldgun (Field Gun, member PARROTT, EXPLOSION6POUND, on Rifleman, not forest) | smallbulletflesh 4, bodyfalldirt 4, explosion6pounddirt 2 | explosion6pound 4, bodyfalldirt 6, explosion6pounddirt 2 | IMPACT_EXPLOSION6POUND explosion6pound |
| df_cannon (Cannon EXPLOSION6POUND on Rifleman, forest) | smallbulletflesh 2, bodyfalldirt 2, explosion6pounddirt 2 | explosion6pound 2, bodyfallleaves 4, explosion6poundforest 2, footforest 1 | IMPACT_EXPLOSION6POUND, BODY_FALL_LEAVES, the hit effect on LEAVES |
| naval_ranged (Frigate EXPLOSION6POUND on Trireme, water) | explosion6pounddirt 2 | explosion6poundwater 2 | the hit effect on WATER |

Every difference is one of the two rules: the target's own weapon where stock uses the striker's, and DIRT where stock
uses the plot's feature or terrain. (The Gatling's pair is the least certain split, 10.15.)

**The fix** (MC #10565 yes to the files, both knobs **default off** until the live pair; lead-0042 owns the touches):
- **(T) `render_test_units_trigger_terrain`** (1: the plot's tag as stock; 0: DIRT, as before): the unit's plot from the
  unit scene's table, the plot's feature and terrain from the fog scene's plot copy handed to the unit scene beside
  `setPlotStates` (no new feed read: recorded bundles replay as before; without a fog table DIRT, counted), the tags
  from `Features` / `Terrains.EffectTypeTag` read when the trigger stream opens. Sounds and hit effects alike. The two
  call sites in `srv_render_scene.cpp` and the accessor in `srv_fow_scene.h` wait for 0674's merge (MC #10565).
- **(W) `render_test_units_trigger_striker_weapon`** (1: a unit that does not strike in its running fight takes the
  opponent unit's figure-0 member weapon, the sound tag for a Sound, the weapon tag for an Effect; a city opponent keeps
  its own, counted; 0: own, as before). "Does not strike": the defender of a combat without `DefenderRetaliates`, and
  not in 4777's air opening (the core's `def_answers` rule). Melee stays own: 11.3 found own names a script for every
  trigger of 0557's melee fights and the opponent's left 4 + 4 without one; the live pair adds a melee case with
  different weapons (Spearman on Warrior: own bluntflesh, opponent swordflesh) to settle which one stock takes there.
  **Settled live 2026-11-22 (18.25.2, W76):** stock takes the opponent's (striker's) weapon in that melee too; (W) as
  written keeps melee own, so melee still differs from stock. **5055 (W83, 18.30):** melee named by the striker too
  (both sides, the battle beds included), the own weapon as the second try.
- Open: who fills a figure's +0x60 (so whether stock's melee impact is the striker's weapon); a figure standing on a
  plot other than its unit's (stock reads the plot under the trigger's point, the fix the unit's plot).

#### 18.25.1 The code: two knobs, default off (W71, ticket 5052, 2026-11-22, offline)

Written 2026-11-22 from 20:25 EST by w71-0042, branch `w71-5052` (from `w69-5052`, main 15bbcccf1 merged). Offline only:
no game, no instance. `[C]` the code named; results `[L]`-offline (trigger_scene on the install's art, no client).

**Where the rules live.** Both rules are header-only in `server/src/effects/srv_trigger_emitter.h` (section "ticket
5052"), so that `trigger_scene` (which does not link the trigger stream) runs the same code as server.exe:
- `DefenderStrikes(retaliates, attackerDamage, attackerAir, defenderAir, defenderFigures)`: the core's `def_answers_` rule
  (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`, 4777): the record's DefenderRetaliates, except in an air strike's opening (the
  attacker's side air, the defender's not, the defender with figures, the attacker's damage in this combat known) where it
  answers when that damage is above 0.
- `FightWeaponRoles`: the running fights by seq (attacker, defender, retaliate flag, attacker's damage). `namer(player,
  unit, isAir, ...)` gives `Own` (an attacker, a defender that strikes back, a unit in no fight), `Opponent` (a defender
  that does not strike: the attacker's player and unit) or `OpponentCity` (its striker is a city: own kept, counted).
- `PlotTags::tagOf(terrainId, featureId)`: the feature's EffectTypeTag when it has one, else the terrain's, else DIRT.

**(W) `render_test_units_trigger_striker_weapon`** (`TriggerStreamConfig::strikerWeapon`, `UnitsOptions::
triggerStrikerWeapon`). `TriggerStream::fightArt` (each fight's start) records the fight's roles from the
`SrvFeed::CombatRecord` (DefenderRetaliates, `CombatDamage(rec, 0)`); the tap's `afterFrame` drops them at the fight's own
OwnerEnd (after that frame's records). `TriggerStream::Subs::weapon`: with the knob on and the namer `Opponent`, the
figure index becomes 0 and the member is the opponent's (`Controller::combatFigures` of the opponent, the frame's cache),
so a Sound takes that member's `WeaponTypeSoundOverrideTag`, else `WeaponTypeTag`, an Effect its `WeaponTypeTag` (the
Index-0 row: stock's "current weapon" of a member with a second weapon in use is not modelled `[I]`). Air: a unit with a
member whose domain is Air (the core's `Part::air`). Melee and every striker keep their own (as before).

**(T) `render_test_units_trigger_terrain`** (`TriggerStreamConfig::plotTerrain`, `UnitsOptions::triggerTerrain`).
`TriggerStream::open` reads `Terrains` and `Features` (ID, EffectTypeTag) into `plotTags()` (`loadPlotTags`; a failed read
is LOUD once and every plot is DIRT). `SceneUnits::setPlotTable(plots, n, width, height, gen)` (new, a default no-op in
the interface) keeps each plot's terrain and feature in the unit host (2 bytes per plot, copied again only on a new
generation or size; nothing kept with the knob off), and the host gives the stream `setUnitTerrain(unitPlotTag)`: the
unit's plot from its record in `UnitsCore`, the tag by `PlotTags::tagOf`. No table (or no record, or another grid's
width): the function says no and the stream takes DIRT as before (counted `terrainStandIn` and `plotNoTable`). The hit
effects take the same `$(TERRAIN)` (`srv_fight_geometry.cpp` through `Subs::terrain`).

**What (T) still needs to work live (after 0674 merges; MC #10565 holds the two files):**
1. `server/src/render/srv_fow_scene.h`: an accessor for the fog scene's last plot table read (`FowScene::m_rec`, which
   `readTable` fills from the table copy and checks against width x height), e.g.
   `const std::vector<SrvFeed::PlotRecord>& records() const { return m_rec; }`.
2. `server/src/render/srv_render_scene.cpp`: at the two places that call `m_units->setPlotStates(...)` before
   `m_units->beginFrame` (the scene's units begin before the terrain, and the unit-shadow path's begin; on main
   15bbcccf1 lines 1195 and 2773), beside each, `m_units->setPlotTable(rec.empty() ? nullptr : rec.data(), rec.size(),
   m_fow.tableWidth(), m_fow.tableHeight(), m_fow.fogGeneration())` with `rec = m_fow.records()` (the same width, height
   and generation as the states; no fog scene: an empty table, so null). `[I]` A feature that changes without a fog
   change (a forest cut) keeps the old copy while the generation stays: the table copy's own snapshot generation

Until then server.exe and sceneshot call nobody: with the knob on every unit is DIRT, as before, with `plotNoTable`
