#### 18.25.3 The plot table reaches the units: (T)'s call sites, offline (W82, ticket 5052 (T), 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 from 03:15 EST by w82-0042, branch `w82-5052t` (from W78's WIP `w78-5052t` @1051943b7, main 18b92ba61
merged = (W) on main). Offline only: no game, no instance. `[C]` the code named; results `[L]`-offline (synthetic bundles
and the WARP device, no client). (T) stays **default off**.

**The call sites** `[C]` (18.25.1's steps 1-2):
- `server/src/render/srv_fow_scene.h` `FowScene::plotTable(size_t& n, uint32_t& key)`: the newest read's records
  (`readTable`'s copy of `SrvFeed::CopyPlots`, `tableWidth() x tableHeight()`), null with n 0 before a table was used or
  while the newest read was refused for its size (new `m_recUsed`, set by `readTable` in `srv_fow_scene.cpp`: before it a
  refused read left `m_rec` holding the refused records). `key` = the fog scene's read count (`rereads`).
- `server/src/render/srv_render_scene.cpp` `HandPlotTable(units, fow)` (anonymous namespace) right after each
  `m_units->setPlotStates(...)` and before `m_units->beginFrame(...)`: in `Scene::draw` (the units' begin after the terrain
  draw, about line 1267 on the merged head) and in `Scene::unitShadowStep` (the unit-shadow path's begin, about line 2862).
  sceneshot's own `setPlotStates` (its unit history replay) hands no table: it opens no trigger stream.
- `server/src/units/srv_units_scene.{h,cpp}` `srvunits::PlotTerrainCopy` (new, beside `FilterByFog`): the copy (2 bytes a
  plot, only when the key, the width or n changed) and the lookup of a unit's plot (its record in `UnitsCore`, refused on
  another grid's width). `UnitsHost::setPlotTable` (still nothing kept with the knob off) and `unitPlotTag` use it, and so
  does unitfeed: one rule for the server and the replay.

**Why the read count is the key** `[C]` `server/src/feed/srv_feed.h`: `SetPlot` after a snapshot "marks it changed"
(`Batch::changedPlots`) and `snapshotGen` moves only with a new snapshot (`EndSnapshot`). `FowScene::onBatch` re-reads the
table on a new snapshot, a sequence gap, an overflow, dropped events and on any changed plot, and `rereads` counts every
copy. A forest cut (a feature change on a plot whose fog does not change) is therefore a new read and a new key, while
`fogGeneration()` (fog states only) and `snapshotGen` both stay. 18.25.1's suggestion of the snapshot generation is
corrected there. A frame without a read keeps the key, so the unit host copies nothing again.

**`render_fow=0`** `[C]` `FowScene::init` returns at once with the fog off (no `m_table`, no read): `plotTable` gives
null, so with (T) on every unit is DIRT, counted `plotNoTable` (`terr=.../<noTable>` in the `units trigger` lines), as
before 5052. The same while the fog scene has not read a table yet, and for the frames after a refused read.

**Which test reaches what.** `trigger_scene` does not: it has its own plot argument and no `SceneUnits`. `test_scene_units`
does reach `UnitsHost::setPlotTable` but has no trigger stream (no real database, no install-backed controller), so it
cannot show a name. So two tests, one per half:
- `server/tests/render/fow/test_fow_scene.cpp` case `units_plot_table_5052`: a real `Scene` with the real `FowScene` and
  a recording `SceneUnits` (`Scene::setUnits`): each drawn frame calls `setPlotStates`, `setPlotTable`, `beginFrame` in
  that order; the records handed are the table's, the grid 4x4, the key the read count; a forest cut on plot 6 (a changed
  plot, the same snapshot and fog generations) is handed with a new key and the new feature; a frame without a read keeps
  the key; a read of 15 records for 4x4 plots hands null, n 0; the next snapshot hands the table again. PASS 2026-11-23
  03:07 (`test_fow_scene.py` 3 passed, every case).
- `server/tools/unitfeed/test_unitfeed.py::test_trigger_terrain_5052`: the product's `TriggerStream` through
  `PlotTerrainCopy` over feed.bin's fog reads (PLOTS of caller `kPlotsFog`: the records `FowScene::readTable` copied and the
  terrain scene hands on), on the fixture's new `aiturnforest` (0477's AI turn with one fog read: every plot plains, the
  defending Spearman's plot 3 FEATURE_FOREST) and `aiturnplains` (no forest). With `--trigger-terrain`: `plot feature 28
  terrain 26 dirt 0 no table 0`; the Spearman's falls are `AS3D_UNIT_SPEARMAN_BODY_FALL_LEAVES` (4 records), no other unit
  has a LEAVES name (the Warriors on plains stay DIRT, their terrain's tag). Knob off: no LEAVES name, and the forest
  bundle's off log equals the plains bundle's off log and its on log (plains is DIRT by its tag). PASS 2026-11-23 03:11
  (21 passed). unitfeed with `--trigger-terrain` now uses the fog reads (before: no table, every unit DIRT); a bundle
  without fog reads (the old `aiturn`) still counts `no table 54`.

**(T) off is byte-identical** `[L]`-offline (`server/evidence/0042/5052/w82/scripts/uf_identity82.py`, result
`uf_identity82.txt`): unitfeed of main 18b92ba61 against the branch's, both with the product's defaults (striker weapon

### 18.26 The Gatling and cannon fights' time after the first shot: stock waits for the dying figures (W72, ticket 5053)

Written 2026-11-22 from 20:31 EST by w72-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w72-5053` from main b3fa2235c. Offline
only: no instance, no game, no LTO, no code change; one `trigger_scene` built from the branch through quietlock. Marks:
`[L]` recorded live (W64's S20 route S / S21 stock Tiny pair, 10.15; W52's stock sampler file, 18.15.1), `[C]` read in
route S's code or run here offline, `[I]` this section's reading. Inputs: the S20 / S21 Miles logs (local,
`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w64/miles-S20/`, `miles-S21/`; listed by sample with `split_w64.py --list`, times from the
fight's `RunCombatSim`), W52's `sim52.jsonl.gz` (stock, huge t350, 2 ms passes; 22 Gatling, 32 siege, 20 machine-gun
fights) read with this section's scripts, and `trigger_scene --dump-core` (the pure_vp copy, 0327's database copy,
seeds 1-3, knobs off and 5050's both on). Evidence: `server/evidence/0042/5053/` (`timeline_S20.txt`,
`timeline_S21.txt`: per case the samples' time, side and file; `rel72.txt`, `dy72.txt`, `st72_gatling.txt`, `est72.txt`,
`ts72_runs.txt`; the scripts `st72.py`, `rel72.py`, `dy72.py`, `est72.py`, `ts72.sh`).

**Answer** `[L]`: the time is not in the volleys or the strikes per death (one volley in both, the deaths landing on the
same bullets); it is after the last death. **Stock holds the target's survivors until every dying figure's death clip
has played, then ends them with a short shuffle (one `runvox` at the target), and only then does the simulation go.
Route S ends the survivors at the last landing and removes each dying figure after the length of its member's first
1200 clip (death A), also when its machine drew the longer death B.**

**(a) The fight after the first shot, by phase** `[L: S21 stock / S20 route S, seconds from the fight's Run; one fight
each]`:

| Phase | Gatling on Rifleman, stock | route S | Cannon on Rifleman, stock | route S |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first shot (fire sample) | 2.681 | 1.472 | 3.080 | 2.772 |
| shots (volley) | 3 GatlingGunFire at once, no second volley | the same | 3 cannon fires 3.08 / 3.18 / 3.58 | 2.77 / 2.91 / 3.11 |
| first shot -> first landing | 0.299 | 0.334 | 0.334 | 0.400 |
| first landing -> last death (death vox) | 0.365 (deaths at 3.047 x2 and 3.345) | 0.034 (3 at 1.840) | 0.066 (2 at 3.480) | 0.035 (2 at 3.207) |
| last death -> survivors released (the target's `runvox`) | 1.534 (4.879) | - (survivors ended at the landing) | 1.801 (5.281) | - |
| death clips (body falls per dying figure) | B, B: +0.93 and +1.43; A: +0.53 | A, A: +0.53; B: +0.93, its +1.43 fall cut by the end | B, B: +0.93, +1.43 | A: +0.53; B: +0.93, its +1.43 fall cut |
| release -> End | 1.087 | - | 0.552 | - |
| last death -> End | 2.621 | 0.993 (the core's 1.0 s death A) | 2.353 | 1.226 (the reformed crews' walk home, 3.94-4.37) |
| **first shot -> End** | **3.285** | **1.361** | **2.753** | **1.661** |
| whole fight | 5.966 | 2.833 | 5.833 | 4.433 |

So of the Gatling's 1.92 s after-first-shot gap, about 0.33 s is the deaths' spread over the burst and 1.6 s the wait
for death B plus the survivors' end; of the cannon's 1.09 s, all of it lies after the deaths. Before the first shot the
Gatling is 1.21 s early and the cannon 0.31 s (5050 (b)'s hold and full entry move them by about +1.43 and +0.36 s
offline, 18.23).

**(b) Stock's rules, from the 2 ms sampler** `[L: W52's file; the EXE's code for R1 not read, D83 description]`:
- **R1, the survivors wait for the dying.** After a ranged fight's last death the target's standing figures stand in
  state 0x10 until the last dying figure (state 8) takes flag 0x10 ("takes no part", `combat-choreography.md` 13.3),
  which marks its death clip played or its 3.0 s cap (`combat-choreography.md` 5.3): they leave 0x10 (to 0xB, then 7) **in the same 2 ms pass in 33 of 33 ranged fights**
  (dying done -> leave 0x10: 0.001 s mean, max 0.013). Last death -> release: Gatling 1.400 [0.165] s (n 13), siege
  1.380 [0.203] (13), all ranged 1.338 [0.109] (33). Melee: 5 fights, 0.195 [0.226] after the dying figure's flag (other
  holds there; not read).
- **R2, a dying figure lasts the death clip its machine drew.** State 8 -> flag 0x10 is bimodal per unit type: about
  1.01 s (death A) or a longer, type-specific time (death B): Rifleman 1.00-1.01 (7) / 1.36-2.19 (7, four at 1.85),
  Great War Infantry 1.01 (26) / 1.34-1.36, Commando 1.01 (9) / 1.84-1.86 (8), Gatling Gun 1.01 / 1.63, Paratrooper
  1.00-1.03 / 1.34-1.36, Mamluk 1.54-1.56 only (`dy72.txt`). The machines draw A (1200) or B (2200) 50/50
  (`unit-controller.md` 6.5, R6). Whether 1.01 s is death A's length for every type or a floor is `[I: open]`; the
  core's Rifleman death A is 1.0 s (offline: dying 1.400 -> removed 2.400).
- **R3, the survivors' end.** A released survivor of the non-answering target goes 0x10 -> 0xB -> 7 in 0.485 [0.070]
  s (n 26) and the simulation goes 0.616 [0.175] s after the release (n 33). Live it plays **one `runvox` at the target
  at the release** in every land case of S21 (archer x2, Gatling, field gun, cannon: 0.32-1.09 s before End) `[L]`,
  read as a 1450 shuffle out of the bombard-defend stance `[I: the clip]`.
- **R4, the volley and the deaths.** Stock's Gatling enters its strike once per figure (2.73 strike entries per fight
  for 3 figures; `st72_gatling.txt`), the deaths land 1.77 [0.24] s after the first strike entry, and its crew finishes
  0.003 s after the last death; the deaths of S21 fall on bullets 0.30 s apart, as the core's three Transfer landings of
  the 1180 clip (1.376 / 1.698 / 1.983 offline). Strikes per death and volleys are not the gap `[L, C]`.

**Correction to 10.15** (2026-11-22, W72): 10.15 read "both arms play one `runvox` at the target in every land case"
as the 1450 of phase 2 in both. The times say otherwise `[L, timeline_S20/S21.txt]`: route S plays it at the start
(4750's `defend_from_stance` shuffle, 0.14-1.74 s), stock at the end (R3, the release); stock's phase-2 0xF at the start
gave no `runvox` at the target in any of the five land cases. Same count, other moment.

**(c) Where route S decides this today** `[C: main b3fa2235c]`:
- `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` `Sim::die`: `f.until = t + min(death_cap, timing(pi, f, 1200).duration)`; the
  timing comes from `Controller::combatClips` (`render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp`), the member's **first** `.fxsxml`
  binding of ec 1200 (death A). Death B (2200) is never asked; the machine draws A or B on its own, so a B figure is
  removed at A's length and the fight's end cuts its clip (S20: the +1.43 falls missing).
- `Sim::tick`'s end test: `needs` is the landings in flight, the city volley, the reform and `Part::need()` (planned
  deaths not played, owed hits); a Dying figure does not count, so every standing figure (Look, Wait, Ready, Defend,
  Approach, Charge, Turn) is finished in the step of the last death's landing.
- `Sim::finish`: victory, `walkHome` (4742, only a figure placed and moved at least `walk_home_min_move`) or `Done`
  with 1000 at once; a defender leaving its 1280 stance gets no end shuffle. The fight ends when every figure is
  Removed / Done / Victory / Reface, i.e. at the later of the last death A and the attacker's own end.
- Offline (`ts72_runs.txt`, `est72.txt`; flat field, attacker facing its target, no reform): Gatling -> Rifleman
  (damage 26): strike 0.033, landings 1.376 / 1.698 / 1.983, 3 deaths at 1.400 and one at 1.700, survivors Done at
  1.700, crew Done 2.500, end 2.700; with 5050's (a)+(b): strike 1.467, end 3.133. Cannon -> Rifleman (19): end 2.700;
  (a)+(b) 3.133. Field gun -> Rifleman (30): 3.667; (a)+(b) 4.100 (5.033 in seed 3).

**(d) The fix design** (not built; the MC decides the defaults; NO code in this stage). Two `CombatParams` knobs, off
by default (the rules before 5053), each a comparison knob as 4746-5050:
- **`death_by_variant`** (R2): a dying figure lasts the death clip its machine plays. With the controller's feedback
  (live and in `trigger_scene`, both use `ControllerFeedback`), the first step the figure plays ec 2200 sets
  `f.until = dying start + min(death_cap, timing(pi, f, 2200).duration)`; on 1200 it stays at A's length. Self-timed
  (no feedback: `choreograph()`, `combat_scene` without `--live`) the core draws A or B 50/50 from its own generator at
  `die()`. Needs an additive feedback query: `CombatFeedback::playingVariant(player, id, figure, code)` returning
  `code`, `code + 1000` or 0 (default body 0, so existing fakes compile), served by `Controller::playingVariant` (the
  same walk as `playing()`, which already tests `code` and `code + 1000`).
- **`end_after_dying`** (R1 + R3): the end test also holds while any figure of the fight is Dying (stock's 0x10: the
  standing figures keep their state and request; a defender stays in 1280), and finishes them in the step the last
  dying figure is Removed. A finished defender figure leaving the 1280 stance, of a land member with Walk and a 1450
  clip (4750's test), then requests 1450 (`ActionKind::Walk`) for `end_stance_s` (0.45 s: R3's 0.485 to 7) and refaces
  (Reface, 1000) before it counts as ended; without Walk it ends at once. The attacker's crew is not held (R4: stock's
  ends at its last landing; siege crews 1.64 s later by their own clips) and its walk home (4742) runs as now.
- Test keys (rule A, as 5050's): `render_test_units_death_by_variant`, `render_test_units_end_after_dying` (TEST
  ONLY, "0" default, other values than 0 / 1 refused) -> `UnitsOptions` -> `AnimRunner` setters -> the fight's
  `CombatParams`; written into every bundle's render_config; sceneshot sets them only on "1"; `trigger_scene`
  `--[no-]death-by-variant`, `--[no-]end-after-dying`; a `phases:`-style `end:` line (last death, release, ends of
  the dying, the end shuffles, the end).
- Regression cases (a new `server/tests/effects/run_end_scenes.py` on `trigger_scene`, or cases added to
  `run_phase_scenes.py`): e1 Gatling -> Rifleman and e2 Cannon -> Rifleman (on: the release no earlier than the last
  Removed, one 1450 per standing target figure, the end at least `end_stance_s` after the release; a figure playing
  2200 removed at B's length, not A's), e3 a melee kill (the killed unit's last death: no standing figure left, the
  end moves only by B), e4 naval ranged (a ship target: no Walk, no shuffle, R1 only); `--expect-fail` with both off;
  `--exe-base` identity with both off; unit cases in `render/tests/unitanim/test_combat_special.cpp`.
- **Files** (5050's set, plus the controller): `render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h`, `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`,
  `render/include/c5r/unitanim/controller.h`, `render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp`,
  `render/tests/unitanim/test_combat_special.cpp`, `server/src/render/srv_render_host.cpp`,
  `server/src/units/srv_units_anim.cpp`, `server/src/units/srv_units_anim.h`, `server/src/units/srv_units_scene.cpp`,

**Open questions of the build stage, answered** `[C]`: the VP Rifleman's 2200 clip is found (B dying 1.867 s, A
1.000 s, e1/e2); the controller's dying machine is read in time for most deaths (e1: B 1, A 3 of 4 deaths; e3: B 1,
A 6 of 8, one death answered neither and kept A's length); e3 (a kill) works as a stand-in for "no standing defender,
no shuffle"; e4 (Dreadnought -> Ironclad) has **no deaths** offline, so it checks only that a ship target takes no
shuffle and the same end, not R1 on a ship.

**What is coded** `[C code]`:
- `CombatParams::death_by_variant` (default **true** since W153, 2026-11-25, the MC's word; was false as coded by W112;
  `render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h`, `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`).
  `Sim::die` records the dying start (`Fig::dying_at`). Self-timed (no feedback) it draws A or B 50/50 from a second
  generator `death_rng_` (seeded from the fight's seed XOR 0x5053, the seq and both units), so the fight's own draws
  (`rng_`: targets, victory) are the same as with the knob off; on B the dying time is min(`death_cap`, the member's
  2200 clip), A's when the member has no 2200 clip. Live (a `CombatFeedback`), the tick's Dying case asks
  `fb_->playingVariant(player, id, figure, 1200)` each step until it answers: 2200 sets `until = dying_at +
  min(death_cap, 2200 clip)`, 1200 keeps A's length; no answer by A's end removes it at A's length (as before).
- `CombatFeedback::playingVariant` (additive, default body 0) and `Controller::playingVariant`
  (`render/include/c5r/unitanim/controller.h`, `render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp`): the walk of `playing()` without its
  alive test (a figure that took its Kill is `alive = false` in the controller but plays its death), answering
  `code + 1000` when a source of ec `code + 1000` plays, else `code` when ec `code` plays, else 0. `ControllerFeedback`
  forwards it.
- `CombatParams::end_after_dying` (default **true** since W153, 2026-11-25; was false) with `end_stance_s` 0.45 s. The end test computes `hold_dying`
  (any figure of the fight in Dying); while it holds, the `!needs` finishing loop skips every participant but the
  attacker (R1; the attacker's crew is not held, R4). `Sim::finish` then calls `Sim::endShuffle` after the victory draw
  and the walk home: a defender figure in Defend whose last request is 1280, of a land member with Walk, BombardDefend
  and a 1450 clip (4750's test), steps to Done with 1450 (`Fig::end_shuffle`, `until = t + end_stance_s`); the tick's
  Done case refaces it (Reface, 1000 when the member has Idle) at `until`, and the fight's end test counts it as running
  meanwhile. Without Walk the figure ends at once (Done, 1000), now at the last removal. At the limit a shuffling figure
  stays in Done.
- Keys (rule A, as 5050's): `render_test_units_death_by_variant`, `render_test_units_end_after_dying` (TEST ONLY, "1"
  default since W153, was "0"; "0" kept for diagnosis; other values than 0 / 1 refuse the start; `srv_render_host.cpp`) -> `UnitsOptions::deathByVariant` /
  `endAfterDying` (`srv_units_scene.*`) -> `AnimRunner::setDeathByVariant` / `setEndAfterDying` (`srv_units_anim.*`) ->
  the fight's `CombatParams`; written into every new bundle's render_config; sceneshot sets them only on "1" and prints
  `sceneshot: render_config: units death_by_variant %d, end_after_dying %d`.
- `trigger_scene`: `--[no-]death-by-variant`, `--[no-]end-after-dying` (default the core's), the feedback wrapped in
  `VariantSeen` (passes every answer through unchanged, keeps the death variants answered), and a line `end:
  deathByVariant= endAfterDying= deaths= lastDeath= lastRemoved= release= shuffles= shuffleReface= dyingMin= dyingMax=
  deathB= deathA= end=` (release: the first Done or Victory step of a figure that is not the attacker's).
- `server/tests/effects/run_end_scenes.py`: e1 Gatling -> Rifleman and e2 Cannon -> Rifleman (deaths, release no earlier
  than the last removal, at least one shuffle, end at least 0.45 s after the release, the variant read, a B longer than
  an A), e3 Swordsman kills a Warrior at 50 -> 100 (no shuffle, the variant read), e4 Dreadnought -> Ironclad (no shuffle,
  the same end as off; not counted by `--expect-fail`); `--expect-fail` (both off), `--exe-base` (the off arm's
  `trigger_scene:` line and triggers.log byte-identical to a main build's), `--table` (gatling, cannon, field_gun,
  melee, melee_kill x arms off / v / e / ve x seeds: end, first strike, time after it, release after the last death,
  shuffles, B deaths).
- Unit cases (`render/tests/unitanim/test_combat_special.cpp`): `d1_a_dying_figure_lasts_the_death_clip_its_machine_drew`
  (off: every dying time A's 1.0 s; on, seeds 1-8: each 1.0 or 1.8, both drawn, hits identical to off; B capped at
  `death_cap`; no 2200 clip: the same fight as off; live with a fake feedback: even figures 1.8, odd 1.0, off never asks)
  and `e1_the_standing_figures_wait_for_the_dying_then_a_defender_shuffles_out_of_1280` (off: a standing defender ends
  before the last removal; on: none before it, one 1450 and one 1000 reface per standing figure, end = last removal +
  0.45 s within two steps, attacker's Done unchanged; without Walk no shuffle; a melee kill the same fight as off). They
  cannot compile on main (the knobs do not exist); the failing-before evidence is `run_end_scenes.py --expect-fail`.
- Builders: `server/evidence/0042/5053/w109/scripts/allb112.sh` (W85's allb85.sh, phases b q t r 1 2 3 lw sh a; the r
  phase runs every other scene runner's default arm against main's with `cmp_logs.py`, since both knobs are off by
  default). No other runner needed a `--no-5053` flag: the defaults are the rules before 5053. (Corrected 2026-11-25 by
  W153: with both knobs on by default, `trigger_scene` reads `C5_TRIGGER_SCENE_NO_5053=1` to start both off, and the r
  phase runs each runner's default arm (its own expectations), lists its cases that differ from main's, and requires

#### 18.26.4 The Gatling's crew entry: a turned crew without Walk stops, then plays its whole 1600 entry (W162, ticket 5074, 2026-11-25)

Written 2026-11-25 from 14:30 EST by w162-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w162-5074` from main aead3569e. Marks:
`[L]` read in recorded live data (W52's stock sampler file, 18.15.1; W158's same-dice Tiny pair, 18.26.2), `[C]` read in
route S's code or run here offline, `[D]` read from the art census (4408's `census.json`, outside git, D83: only the
values described here), `[I]` this section's reading. Numbered after 5075's 18.26.3 (lead-0042).

**Answer.** Route S's Gatling crew fires about 1.2 s before stock's because, after its turn, it asks for combat ready
straight from its run, so its machine skips the 1600 entry clip, and the crew strikes 1.0 s after the turn. Stock's crew
ends its phase 2 with a stop (state 3's 1000: the run stop, then idle) and its strike from idle plays the whole entry
clip, with the rifle cock and fortify vox, before the attack.

**Correction to 18.26.2 and 18.23.1** (2026-11-25, W162): the route S Gatling's "run" at the fight's start in S22 and
S5053p is 4735's `turn_first` turn (the crew stands 2 facings away and turns in place with 1400 for `turn_min` 0.3 s;
the controller timeline's `run` 0.000 -> `combat_ready` 0.299 for all three figures at once), not a reform: the Gatling
member does not reform (no stock Gatling attacker reformed in W52's 22 fights, `reform_a` False in every row of
`phases52.csv`) and a reform would have ended in 1000 at each arrival and taken 5050 (b)'s hold. The skip is the same:
`attackStance` returns at `f.last == 1400`.

**(a) Stock's Gatling crew before its first shot** `[L]`:
- **States** (W52's sampler, 22 stock Gatling attacks, huge t350, 2 ms passes; `server/evidence/0042/5074/gat162.py`,
  output `gat162_stock.txt`): every crew figure goes 0 -> 0xF (phase 2) -> 3 -> 1 -> 10 and never enters state 5; the
  strike state (10) follows phase 2's end within 0.006-0.010 s; phase 2 lasts 0.559-0.828 s in 12 of the 16 fights whose
  phase 1 ended at once (0.559, 0.586-0.592 x4, 0.708-0.716 x3, 0.826-0.828 x4; the other four 0.014, 0.319, 0.328 and one
  0.173 after 0.2 s), 0.173-0.178 s in the five whose phase 1 lasted 0.78-0.98 s (a reforming Mamluk defender) and 0.478 s
  after 1.275 s; the first state 10 comes 0.030-1.762 s after the simulation's start
  (mean 0.787). The strike state then lasts about 2.0 s per entry (its clips, below).
- **Sounds** (W158's df_gatling a-d stock arm, `seq162.py` over `tables/timeline_u.txt`, output `seq162_u.txt`; seconds
  from the fight's Run): a run 0.17-0.58 s (the foot, foley and wheel squeak samples, the Gatling's 1400 clip triggers at
  0.081 / 0.094 / 0.100 and 0.434 / 0.450 s into it [D]), silence, then from 1.707-1.742 s one clip shared by the three
  figures (every group x3 in the same millisecond) whose samples fall on the Gatling's **1600 Combat_Ready clip
  triggers** [D: foot 0.157, rifle cock 0.463, fortify vox 0.494, foot 0.580, foley 0.635, foot 0.839 s] to 0.005 s:
  heard at +0, +0.301, +0.333, +0.433, +0.500, +0.700 s after the first foot. So **the entry clip starts at 1.551,
  1.550, 1.585, 1.583 s** (fights a-d), and the attack clip (1180 Attack_City: foley at 0, fire at 0.035 s [D]) at
  2.608-2.640, 1.057 s after the entry's start; the first shot 2.642-2.675 s.
- **Reading** `[I, from the rules of 5.2, 5.3, 6.2 and 4746]`: 0xF requests 1450 (the Gatling binds a Shuffle clip but
  enables no Walk [D]); 0xF -> 3 requests 1000 for a member without Walk after a movement (4746's state-2 rule, exe-audio
  13.3); the omni machine leaves its run loop for the run stop (9, `EC(1440)` or `EC(2440)`) and idles; the strike's 1180
  from idle enters combat ready through state 8 (the whole 1600 clip) and attacks from 12. Stock's run lasts from about
  0.1 s to about 0.6-0.7 s, its stop to 1.55 s.

**(b) Route S before 5074** `[C: render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp, main aead3569e]`: `Sim::turnFirst` sends the
crew into `FigState::Turn` with 1400 for the turn (0.3 s here); the tick's Turn case then sets `entry_wait` and calls
`look()` -> `Sim::ready()`; `attackStance` (5050 (b)) returns false at `f.last == 1400` (a figure that moved), so
`ready()` requests 1600 at once with `ready_at` = now + the 1600 clip (1.0 s). The 1600 meets the machine in its run
loop, which goes to the combat-ready loop without state 8 (W70's clip chain `Gatling_Gun_Run > Combat_Ready_Idle >
Attack_City`, 18.23.1), so the entry's sounds never play; the strike comes at 1.30 s (timeline), the first shot at
1.48-1.51 s [L 18.26.2].

**(c) The rule as built** `[C code: render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h, render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp]`:
`CombatParams::attack_entry_after_turn` (on by default, a parity fix: D255, no player key; `attack_turn_stop_s` 0.0).
`Sim::entryAfterTurn`, called from the tick's Turn case at a `turn_first` turn's end: an attacking figure (not
figureless, not a flyer, no air side) whose last request is the turn's 1400, of a land member without Walk or without a
1450 clip (5050's `attack_hold_without_walk` class), with CombatReady, Idle and a 1440 clip, first keeps its run in
place until `attack_turn_stance_s` (0.40 s) after the turn's start when its turn was shorter (stock's 0xF, below), then
requests 1000 (`Look`) and stands until `turn_stop_until` = that moment + max(its 1440 clip, `attack_turn_stop_s`,
0.0 by default); it is then marked
`astanced` (no Walk) and `entry_wait`, so its next look's `ready()` requests 1600 from idle and the strike waits for the
whole entry clip (no live shortcut). Off: 1600 at the turn's end (the rule before 5074), byte for byte. No host key:
the server's `CombatParams` takes the default (`srv_units_anim.cpp` sets only the keyed knobs), and the library bundles

### 18.27 The 11 s render-loop stall in S22 p+ is a C: file-system stall, not combat (W73, ticket 5054)

Written 2026-11-22 from 21:00 EST by w73-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w73-5054` from main 5150259a0. Offline
only: no instance, no build, no code change. Marks: `[L]` read in the live logs and files named below, `[C]` read in the
code of main 5150259a0 (the run's build was main 8a2f0874e), `[I]` this section's reading. **The cause is not combat's:
it is the server's render host and its logging (0417's finding in
[terrain-bake-slow-first-use.md](terrain-bake-slow-first-use.md) 5.2: the render thread writes its log lines itself).
The fix stays ticket 5054's (MC #10726, lead-0042 #10737: "no blocking file I/O on the render thread").**

Inputs: W70's S22 arm p+ (c5h-c, 4390913, main 8a2f0874e, server.exe 4cc76f6d..., route S with
`render_test_units_reform_ends_at_arrival=1` and `render_test_units_attack_from_stance=1`, TEST keys
`render_test_units_dump` and `render_test_units_anim`; launch 20:23:17, the stall 20:25:02.07-13.07 wall = server
+104.9..+115.9 s) and its arm p0 (20:31-20:37, same keys without 5050's), under
`F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-lead25/w70/s4779-c5h-c/live-S22-w70on|w70off/` and `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-lead25/w70/big/`
(moved from C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w70/ on 2026-11-23); every server
render.log on C: written since 2026-11-20 (366 files). Evidence: `server/evidence/0042/5054/` (`timeline_w73.txt` from
`timeline_w73.py`: the three stalls' lines and the lockstep rows; `census.txt` from `stall_census.py`: every render-loop
stall of 2 s or more and every render.log write of 1 s or more since 2026-11-20; `dump_times.txt` from `dump_times.py`:
the units dump's file creation and write times in both arms; `scan_window.py`: files created or written on C: in a
window).

**(a) What the render loop waited for.**

- `[L]` **One frame's submission took the 10975 ms, with the render thread blocked, not computing.** The `host 1s` line
  at 20:25:13.083 (covering 20:25:01.513-13.083): `submit_n=18 submit_ms=612.978 submit_max_ms=10975.047
  rt_cpu_ms=109.4`. `submit` is `Scene::draw` plus `RingSink::end` for one frame (`srv_render_host.cpp` 1131-1161
  `[C]`); 109 ms of thread CPU over 11.6 s is the other 17 frames' normal cost.
- `[L]` **The frame is camera 1978.** The lockstep csv: the server's last drawn frame before the gap is 1977 (submitted
  qpc 20524.877 s); the EXE kept presenting every 33 ms and took 1977 for its frames 1977-2306 (kind 1 "older", age up
  to 330), then 2307 (server wake 20535.891 s). The units controller's file (`server.c5anim`) has frame 1363 = render
  frame 1978 at 20524.907 s and frame 1364 = 2307 at +10.985 s.
- `[L]` **Not the units and not the controller.** The `units 1s` line that covers frame 1978: `frame_ms_max=1.5`
  (`beginFrame`: build, fog filter, route S poll, the controller's apply, prepare; plus the scene pass),
  `anim_ms_max=0.4`, `slow_frames=0` (a units frame over 250 ms is logged). `units trigger 1s` shows `fights=2` from
  +95.2 s to +118.96 s: no fight started or ran in the runner (the Gatling's had ended at +98, the field gun's starts at
  +122).
- `[L]` **The generation-5 lines are consequences.** `set_gen=5 keys=5539 acked=1` was already in force at 20:24:58;
  during the stall the EXE's filter saw the server stale (shell_composite.log 20:25:04: `modelfilter set_gen=0`,
  `unitfilter latched=0x0 ignored_stale=30`: the EXE drew its own units and models again) and re-applied the set when
  the server came back (`the compositor applied identity set generation 5` at 13.132). The decals' generation 5 was
  published by the EXE at qpc 20537.606 s, 1.7 s after the stall ended.
- `[L]` **Another server process on C: was released in the same millisecond.** The c5h-new-a server (main dde0d762e, no
  5050 key, no units dump, idle: `submit_n=0`) wrote its render.log line of 20:25:08.617 and logged `render log: the
  line before took 4455.6 ms to write (... render.log 4455.6 ms ...)` at **20:25:13.072**, its own render-loop stall of
  4457 ms ending at 20:25:13.073. W70's stall ended at 20:25:13.073 (`models mode` line). Two processes released at
  once by nothing they share but the machine: a file-system stall on C:.
- `[L]` **In W70's frame the blocked call was a file-system call, most likely the TEST dump's file create** `[I]`. The
  units dump (`render_test_units_dump`, `UnitsHost::dump`, `srv_units_scene.cpp` 892-924 `[C]`) creates one
  `frame_<id>.c5units` per drawn frame on the render thread with `_wfopen` / `fwrite` / `fclose`, after the units scene
  pass. `frame_1977.c5units` was created at 20:25:02.069; `frame_1978.c5units` was created at **20:25:13.059** and
  written at 13.072 (13.5 ms; the arm's median is 0.5 ms), `frame_2307` at 13.089. No render.log or server.log line
  carries a time inside 02.1-13.0 (a log write blocked in the frame would show its line with an early stamp), so the
  blocked call was not a log write; the dump's create is the only file-system call in that part of the frame in this
  configuration `[C]`. Not proven: a D3D11 call in the untimed parts of the frame (water, forest, models' scene pass,
  the sink's `CopyResource` / `Signal` / `Flush`) waiting on the GPU for 11 s would fit the thread CPU too, but not the
  common release with the other process.
- `[L]` **C: was not frozen for every writer.** The EXE's shell_composite.log on C: got its lines every second through
  02-13, and the c5h-new-a server's lines of 07.611 and 08.617 were written in time; its write from 08.617 blocked.
  What C: was doing (the volume at 98 % full, 43 GB free at 21:00; MC-B's note of the 0630 take writing until 00:30) is
  not read: `scan_window.py` over the work folders, the repo's worktrees and the instances, 20:24:50-20:25:16, was still
  running at this section's write.
- `[L]` **The class is common on the workstation tonight and is on the product path.** `census.txt` (render.logs since
  2026-11-20): render.log writes that blocked the render thread for **29.9 s** (c5h-new-a, 13:17:00, in a load), **11.0 s**
  (c5h-new-a, 14:39:59), **17.9 s** (c5h-new-a, 20:04:23), **4.5 s** (c5h-new-a, 20:25:13, above), **7.4 s** (0674's
  c5h-new-b, 21:00:27), and 1.0-1.5 s writes on 11-20 and 11-21 (0618, 0619, 0643). The 21:00:20-27 one fell inside
  this worker's own `worktree add` (18,453 files written on C: 21:00:11-21:01:32): heavy small-file writing on this C:
  blocks a server's render.log writes for seconds. None of these runs had a 5050 key; only W70's had the dump.
  Arm p0 (same keys but 5050's, 20:31-20:37): no stall of 2 s or more after the load; its dump's largest gap 101 ms.

**(b) The knobs.** **5050's knobs cannot matter outside a fight, and did not matter here** `[C + L]`.
`CombatParams::reform_ends_at_arrival` and `attack_from_stance` are read only inside the fight simulation
(`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp` 960, 991, 1109: arithmetic on a fight's figures; no lock, no file, no device call),
copied into the runner's parameters once (`srv_units_anim.cpp` 1349-1350, `srv_units_scene.cpp` 754-755). The frame
that stalled had its whole units frame, controller included, in at most 1.5 ms, with no fight in the runner (above). A
fight leaves nothing behind on the stalled path: the controller's record (`render_test_units_anim`) is written in the
1 s line, outside the submission, and only with that TEST key. Answer posted to lead-0042 at 21:14 (#10705), before this
write-up; 5050's default switch does not wait on 5054.

**(c) Fix design** `[I: not built]`. The MC said yes to the fix and its files (#10740; main 820635717 widens 5054's
touches, priority 9, for the next beta). Today's code `[C]`: `EmitBody` (`server/src/render/srv_render_common.cpp`
28-59) does `fprintf` + `fflush` to render.log under `s_logLock` on the calling thread, then for a note calls the host's
function, `SrvLog` (`server/src/srv_main.cpp` 213-266), which does `fprintf` + `fflush` to server.log (and stdout when it
is a pipe or a visible console) under the critical section `s_csLog`, held across the disk write. So the render thread
waits for its own render.log write, for its own server.log write, and for any other thread's server.log write that
holds `s_csLog`.

1. **One log writer thread; producers never wait on a disk** (`srv_render_common.cpp`, `srv_main.cpp`).
   - `EmitBody` and `SrvLog` take the time stamp and format the line on the calling thread as now, then push
     `{target render.log | server.log | both, text}` into one bounded FIFO under a lock held only for the push (no I/O
     under it). Capacity **4096 lines or 4 MiB**, whichever comes first: the steady rate is about 10 lines/s, so the
     longest stall seen (29.9 s) needs about 300 lines; a load's bursts (hundreds of lines) fit too.
   - The writer thread pops in batches and does the `fprintf`s, one `fflush` per batch per file, and the stdout copy.
   - **Full queue: the line is dropped and counted, the producer goes on.** When the writer next gets through, it writes
     ONE line per episode to both logs, LOUD: `log writer: N lines dropped (render.log R, server.log S) while a write
     waited M ms; queue peak P lines`. The current slow-write lines (`render log: the line before took` /
     `log: the line before took`) move to the writer: one per write of 50 ms or more, worded as the disk's wait
     ("the render thread did not wait").
   - **Drain at exit**: `LogShutdown()` before `fclose(s_pLog)` (`srv_main.cpp` 1236) and in the render host's stop:
     stop the writer after it has written everything queued, at most 5 s, then close the files; a line pushed after the
     shutdown is written directly (synchronous, the process is ending).
   - **Drain on the crash path**: the crash filter (`srv_crashdump.cpp` `Filter`), `LogException` and the D119 report's
     path (the `dll-fatal` vectored handler, `server/src/remote/srv_dll_fatal.cpp`) call `LogFlushForCrash()` first: it takes the queue under its lock (bounded
     try, the lock is never held across I/O), switches the logs to synchronous mode, and writes the queued lines itself
     with `WriteFile` on the files' handles (not the CRT `FILE*`, whose lock the writer may hold while stuck on the disk).
     The writer's one in-flight batch can be lost or written twice in that case (said in the crash report's line). The
     crash path itself may block on the disk: the process is ending.
2. **TEST keys that write files per frame write from a worker** (`UnitsHost::dump`, `writeTable`, the c5anim write in
   `secondLine`; `server/src/units/srv_units_scene.cpp`): a bounded queue of 64 pending files; when full the frame's
   file is skipped and counted, one LOUD line per episode (`units: TEST dump: N frames not written, the writer was
   behind`). W70's stall would not have happened with it (the create would have waited on the worker).
3. **A slow submission names its part** in `srv_render_host.cpp` only (`srv_render_scene.cpp` is 0674's): time
   `scene.draw` and `sink->end` apart, and when a submission passes 1 s write one line `host: frame F's submission took
   N ms: scene draw D ms, sink end E ms, thread CPU C ms`. A finer split inside the scene waits for 0674's file.

**Which of tonight's stalls fix 1 would have prevented** `[I from census.txt]`: all five product-path ones (13:17 29.9 s,
14:39 11.0 s, 20:04 17.9 s, 20:25 4.5 s on c5h-new-a; 21:00 7.4 s on c5h-new-b): each log line says the whole wait was
in the render.log part with 0.0 ms on the lock (`render.log N ms`), so the render thread would have queued the line and
drawn on, and the writer would have waited instead. W70's 11 s is fix 2's (the TEST dump). Not covered: a file read the
render thread still does itself (the residency's first use of an install file: `pipeline: first use ... files 2, read
1.0 ms`) could still wait on such a disk; none was seen in these stalls.

**Tests** (the MC's conditions, #10740): (a) a writer blocked on purpose (a test hook: the writer waits on an event the
test holds) while a producer thread pushes 10,000 lines: every push returns in under 1 ms, the dropped count equals the
lines past capacity, after release the file holds the kept lines in order and exactly one drop line; (b) exit drain: lines
pushed then `LogShutdown()` are all in the file; (c) crash path: with the writer blocked, a forced crash (a test key that
raises an access violation after N lines, as `render_test_av`) writes the queued lines and the D119 / crash line to
server.log; (d) every builder that compiles `srv_render_common.cpp` links (server.exe, and the test builders
`server/tests/render/{cities/build_models_tests.py, cut_tap/build_cut_tap_tests.py, decal/build_decal_tests.py,
ice/build_ice_tests.py, overlay/test_reader_build.py, shadow/build_shadow_tests.py, shadow/build_unit_shadow.py,
water/build_water_tests.py}`, `server/tests/extras/run_extras_test.py`, `render/tools/bakecompare/CMakeLists.txt`), and an
ASan run of (a)-(c). Rule A: no picture change is expected (only the logs' timing and the new drop / slow-submission
lines). Merge main LAST before READY: 4940 and lead-0673 also change `srv_render_host.cpp`.

#### 18.27.1 The fix as built: the log writer, the TEST files' worker, the slow-submission line (W75, ticket 5054, 2026-11-22, offline)

Written 2026-11-22 from 22:30 EST by w75-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w75-5054` (from `w73-5054` @8949376e7
and main). Offline: no instance, no LTO link. Marks: `[C]` the code as built, `[T]` the tests named below (run on the
workstation, 2026-11-22). The design is (c) above; where the build differs, it says so.

**What was built** `[C]`:

1. **The log writer** (`server/src/render/srv_render_common.{h,cpp}`; every builder links it, so it lives there and not in
   `srv_main.cpp`). `LogWriterStart()` starts one thread; from then on `RLog`, `RNote` and `SrvLog` format and stamp their
   line on the calling thread and `LogQueue` it under `s_qLock`, a lock held only for the push (a `std::vector` of
   `{targets, text}`; the string copy is made before the lock). The writer takes the whole queue at once, writes each line
   to render.log / server.log / stdout with `fwrite`, one `fflush` per file per batch. Bounds `kLogQueueLines` 4096 and
   `kLogQueueBytes` 4 MiB: a line past either is dropped and counted (per target), and the writer, when it next takes the
   queue, writes ONE line per episode to both logs: `LOUD: log writer: N lines dropped (render.log R, server.log S) over
   M ms while the writer was held up (its last write took W ms); queue peak P lines; no thread waited for the log, the
   render thread included (ticket 5054)`. A batch write of 50 ms or more gives `log writer: a write of N lines took M ms
   (the disk's wait: no producer waited, the render thread included; slow write K; ticket 5054)` (the first 64, then one
   "more slow writes are not logged"). The two old slow-write lines (`render log: the line before took`, issue 0417's
   `log: the line before took` in server.log) are written only when no writer runs (test programs, before the start,
   after the stop). Test programs that never call `LogWriterStart` write synchronously as before.
   - **Who starts it:** `srv_main.cpp` right after server.log opens and the window guard's check (both modes):
     `LogSetServerSink(s_pLog, &NowS)`, `LogWriterStart()`, and the line `server: log writer started: ...` (or LOUD
     when it cannot start). `srv_main.cpp` and `srv_remote_main.cpp` declare the writer's functions themselves (their
     include path has no `shell/common`, which `srv_render_common.h` needs).
   - **Exit drain:** `LogShutdown(5000)` queues the exit line (`log writer: stopping at exit: N lines written, ...
     dropped in E episodes, queue peak ..., the slowest W ms`), lets the writer write everything and stop, at most 5 s;
     later lines are written synchronously. Called in `srv_main.cpp` before server.log closes (standalone mode; the file
     stays open when the writer did not finish) and in `srv_remote_main.cpp` after the last line of `ReportAndExit` and
     of the `kRt_Shutdown` end ("remote: shutdown complete, exiting"). A writer that does not finish in 5 s is left and
     the crash path writes the queue. The render host's `HostStop` does not drain (design (c) named it): the process
     goes on after it, and every end of the process drains. Not covered: a server ended from outside (the proxy's kill of a hung server): the
     lines still queued then (normally under 100 ms of lines) are lost; before, each was on disk when its call returned.
   - **Crash path:** `LogFlushForCrash(why)` (first line of `LogException` in `srv_main.cpp`: the remote mode's unhandled
     filter and the standalone phases' filter) switches to crash mode, takes the queue (`TryAcquireSRWLockExclusive`, at
     most about 200 ms), writes its lines with `WriteFile` at the end of each file (OVERLAPPED offset 0xFFFFFFFF, the
     handles taken from the `FILE*`s at open: not the CRT's lock, which a writer stuck on the disk may hold), then the
     line `LOUD: log writer: the crash path (<where>): N queued lines written by thread T; D lines had been dropped ...;
     the writer's batch in flight, if any, can be missing or written twice`. From then on every line is written that way
     on its own thread. `srv_crashdump.cpp` is unchanged: its filter writes the dump, the exception line comes from
     `LogException`.
   - **The reports:** `srv_exe_crash.cpp` `WriteReport` (the D119 report of an EXE crash, dll-fatal, the render-init
     fatal and the non-fatal server-failure reports of 0573 / live terrain) calls `SrvExeCrash::LogSync(2000)` before
     it reads server.log and render.log: a hook (`SetLogSync`, set by `srv_main.cpp` to `srvrender::LogSync`, null in
     the two unit builders) that waits until every line queued before the call is written, at most 2 s (a LOUD line when
     not). `srv_dll_fatal.cpp`'s handler syncs once more after its report, because the DLL's own filter then ends the
     process and nothing else drains.
2. **The TEST files' worker** (`server/src/units/srv_units_scene.cpp`, class `TestFiles`): `render_test_units_dump`'s
   per-frame `.c5units` file, `render_test_units_table`'s table file and `render_test_units_anim`'s `.c5anim` are
   formatted on the render thread (as before: the scene text, the table text, a copy of the `AnimRecord`) and written by
   one worker thread (started at the first file; joined at most 5 s when the units host closes). At most 64 files wait;
   past that a file is skipped and counted, and the next accepted file says the episode once: `LOUD: units: TEST files: N
   files not written, the writer was behind (64 pending; T in all; ticket 5054)`. A worker's failure comes back to the
   render thread at the next second line and is said as before (the dump's each time, the table's and the anim's once).
   Differences from before: the table's state key and the anim record's frame count are taken when the file is queued,
   not when it is written (a failed write is not retried until the table or the record changes); the anim file is
   written when the record has new frames.
3. **A slow submission names its part** (`srv_render_host.cpp`, the frame's submission only, about 20 lines): a
   submission of 1 s or more writes `host: frame F's submission took N ms: scene draw D ms, between B ms, sink end E ms;
   thread CPU C ms (ticket 5054)` (`between`: the recorder's work after the draw and the report's fill). Inside the scene
   it does not split further (`srv_render_scene.cpp` is 0674's).

**Tests** `[T]`:

- `server/tests/render/logwriter/` (new; `build_logwriter_test.py --out DIR [--asan] --run`; logwriter_test.cpp's

`lead25-0042`. Offline only (no instance). Inputs: W79's live sessions on c5h-c (18.28; build 4390913, Tiny save
C5H-3000-TINY-T0018, Miles logger, Effects raised at run time, Quick Combat off; layout from main 60af959b7): S28 stock
(u0) and S30 route S at main's defaults with `--evidence`, the same cases in the same order as S27, so the same dice
(after-states identical; S30's Run -> End 11.13 / 10.53 s against S27's 11.07 / 10.50 s). Raw logs stay in
`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w79/` (Miles `miles-S2x-w79/mss_log.named.tsv`, `big/anim-S30-w79/server.c5anim`). Scripts and
tables: `server/evidence/0042/5057/` (`sndline_5057.py`: every one-shot of a case with its time from Run and its 3D
position, from the Miles log, for either arm; `figline_5057.py`: the route S controller timeline of one fight;
`sounds-S28.txt`, `sounds-S30.txt`, `timeline-S30.txt`, `offline-kn-s1.txt`, `offline-seeds.txt`). Marks: `[L]` from
these live logs, `[C]` read in the install's files (on a scratch extract outside git, D83) or run offline here, `[I]`
this section's reading. Times below are seconds after the knights' run-charge vox (`runchrgvoxt2`, the 1120 clip's
first sound), which stock plays 0.84 s and route S 0.15 s after `RunCombatSim`.

**Result.** Stock's knights kill their first targets while still in the run charge: each Spearman figure dies as a
rider reaches it, 0.2 s apart, and the riders ride on; no knight plays its run stop (1440) or its combat-ready entry
(1600) in either fight. Route S stops every rider at its target (1440), enters combat ready (1600), then strikes
(1100): its first deaths come 2.8-3.0 s later than stock's. A rider whose target is gone re-charges (1120) and asks
1100 at once; the controller's machine plays that 1100 only after the same run stop and entry, so its hit lands
3.4-3.5 s after the request (3.46-3.53 live, 3.43 offline): that is the "last death 2.8-3.5 s after the last strike request" of W79's S29 / S30. The
two together are the whole extra time; route S's earlier start (-0.69 s) and shorter tail after the last death
(-0.95 / -1.41 s) pay a part of it back.

**Side by side** (`sounds-S28.txt`, `sounds-S30.txt`; deaths are each side's death vox at the dying figure's position;
route S's requests from `timeline-S30.txt`, whose zero is the 1120 request, within 0.05 s of the vox) `[L]`:

**What stock's riders do** `[L, Miles 3D positions of S28's kn_kill]`: the four riders' `HORSE_RUN` / `ARMOUR_MOVE`
(the 1120 clip's sounds at 0.030 / 0.096 s of each loop) repeat every 0.53-0.55 s per rider from the vox to +2.0; the
riders cover about 66 units from +0.33 (they stand the first 0.3 s) at 30-50 units/s. The rider at x -1070, z 321
at 2.24 s (from Run) passes the Spearman figure at -1065, 316, which dies at 2.27 s; the rider at -1052, 343 (2.54 s)
passes the figures at -1054, 320 and -1046, 325 (deaths 2.47, 2.67 s); the riders end beyond the Spearmen's line
(-1037 to -1050 at 3.40 s, the line at -1065 to -1046). No knight sound of the combat-ready entry (`SWORD_SHEATH` at
0.089 s and `FORTIFY_VOX_H` at 0.398 s of the knight's 1600 clip, both tier -1) and none of the run stop
(`HORSE_FOOT_DPMT` of 1440) occurs before the walk home in either stock fight (S28: 0 `swordsheath`, 0 `fortifyvoxh`;
`horsefootdirt` only at 7.04 / 7.94 s, after End); the same riders' other tier -1 sounds (horse run, armour move,
sword swing, attack vox) do play, so the tier gate does not hide them `[L]`. Route S plays 20 such entry sounds in the
two fights (S30) `[L]`.

**The knight's clips** `[C: fx_triggers_knight.ftsxml and knight.fxsxml read from the pure_vp copy's UnitModels.fpk
with fpkscan, outside git]`: 1120 (`Knight_Charge_Run.gr2`) has Sound, Effect and no Action trigger; 1100
(`Knight_AttackA.gr2`) Action at 0.304 s; 1140 (`Knight_Charge_Attack.gr2`) Action at 0.370 s, with horse-run sounds
at 0.030 and 0.511 s (a strike at the gallop). The member's `EnableActions` has no `AttackCharge` (0327's database), so
the core never asks 1140 of a knight (`strikeCode`) and the controller's bridge refuses it (unit-controller.md 17.7).
Whether stock's ride-through hit is a 1140 played from the run or a landing at the arrival with the 1120 still looping
is open: the sounds fit the second better (each loop's horse-run / armour-move pair stays 0.066 s apart through the
deaths, the 1120 spacing, not 1140's 0.015 s) `[I]`. Either way the hit lands at the rider's arrival at its target
figure, with no stop and no entry `[L]`. 18.15's reading "with a rush attacker the arriving figures stand in 3 instead
of striking" (phase 3) does not match these fights `[L against C]`: the EXE's arrival branch for a rush member
(0x5C7100's start, `HasStationaryMelee` at + 0x4B, set on every cavalry member) was not read.

**Why route S's riders stop and enter** `[C, render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp]`: in `Sim::tick` a `Charge` that ends
calls `ready()` for a member without `AttackCharge`, which requests 1600 and sets `ready_at` = arrival + the 1440 clip
+ the 1600 clip (about 2.0 s for the knight); the strike (`startStrike`, 1100) starts at `ready_at` and, live, holds
(`live_wait`) until the controller plays the 1100 (hit 0.30 s in). After a kill, `look()` finds the next target out
of `MoveRadius` reach and sends the rider to `Charge` again (1120; a move shorter than `ShortMoveRadius` 24 is recorded
as 1450). That rider is already `combat_ready`, so `ready()` asks nothing and the 1100 goes out at the re-charge's end,
while its machine is in the 1120 loop: the machine takes 1100 only from combat ready (18.16; 0557 h1 / m1), so it plays
1440 and 1600 first. Hence 3.43-3.54 s from that request to the hit, live and offline.

**Offline, the same shapes** `[C: trigger_scene built from this branch's main, pure_vp copy, 0327's database, steady,
seeds 1-3; offline-seeds.txt]`: kn_kill's shape (Knight 20 -> 46 on Spearman 60 -> 93) ends at 10.63-10.73 s, kn_kill_b's
(-> killed) at 9.60-10.73 s, against 11.13 / 10.53 s live; 4 combat-ready entries by the riders in every run. Seed 1
(`offline-kn-s1.txt`): arrivals 0.79-1.28 s, strike requests 2.83-2.97, hits 4.24-4.37, a re-charge at 4.93 (a
17-unit move, 1450, to 5.71), its 1100 asked at 5.77, its hit 9.20 (3.43 s), end 10.73. So the offline core holds the
whole difference and a fix can be measured there.

**A second ordering difference** `[C 18.15 phase 3; L]`: stock's type 2 fight (a rush attacker, a defender without
`HasShortRangedAttack`) lets the defender strike only after the attacker's first landing; stock's Spearman kills its
Knight at +2.80, after three or four ride-through deaths. Route S's Spearman strikes at once and kills a rider at
+1.96 / +2.13, one before its first hit (kn_kill_b: a 1100 asked at +1.61 and lost), so fewer riders strike and more
re-charges follow (18.16 saw the same offline: "the defender's first hit lands before the riders strike").

**Not verified:** stock's own requests (stock has no controller timeline: its sequence is read from sounds and their
positions); the ride-through rule beyond these two fights (one knight pair on one save; other rush members, a horseman
or a lancer, not looked at); the EXE branch that makes it.

**Fix design** (posted to lead-0042 for the MC; nothing built; 18.29.1 when built):
- `CombatParams::rush_ride_through` (default on proposed; off = today's rule). A rush member's charge (1120 to its
  target figure) lands its hit at the arrival (a `Landing` at the move's end, no attack clip, the 1120 left playing);
  the rider then takes its next target: in reach of the line it is on, it rides on to it in the same 1120 and lands
  again on arrival; else it stops (1440) and stands without a 1600 request. A later strike of a standing rider asks
  1100 only when the controller says its machine takes it (`accepts`), else 1600 first as today. A re-charge lands on
  its arrival too, so it costs the run, not run + 2.0 s + 0.3 s.
- `CombatParams::defender_waits_first_landing` (default on proposed): in stock's type 2 (an attacker without a
  `HasShortRangedAttack` member against a defender without one), the defender's figures do not strike before the
  attacker's first landing (18.15 phase 3 `[C]`).
- Host keys `render_units_rush_ride_through`, `render_units_defender_waits_first_landing` (0 or 1, default 1) in every
  bundle's `render_config`, a bundle recorded without them replayed with 0; `trigger_scene` and `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene`
  take `--no-rush-ride-through` / `--no-defender-waits`.
- Regression: `run_charge_scenes.py` cases `kn-kill-s1..s3` and `knb-kill-s1..s3` (the shapes above, steady): end
  <= 8.0 s and no 1600 request by a rider before its first hit; today 0/6 pass (9.60-10.73 s, 4 entries each).

#### 18.29.1 The ride-through and the type 2 wait as built, both on by default (W85, ticket 5057, 2026-11-23, offline)

Written 2026-11-23 from 10:43 EST by w85-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w85-5057` from main 49fb92508 (which carries
4743's charge_any default at 067b25613). Offline only: no instance, no LTO, every build through `quietlock.py run`. The
design is W80's (18.29, thread 0042 #11160), approved by the MC with both knobs on by default (#11162). Inputs read only:
`C:/c5-64bit-work/keep/pins-0.1b`, the pure_vp game copy (build 4390913, Vibrant Textures as every install here), 0327's
database `F:/c5-64bit-work/0327/db/Civ5DebugDatabase.db`. Marks: `[C]` code read or run offline here, `[L]` W79's live
sessions as 18.29 reads them, `[I]` this section's reading.

**What was built** `[C code]`:
- `CombatParams::rush_ride_through` (default true; `render/include/c5r/unitanim/combat.h`, `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`).
  A rush member (`RushAttackFormation`) without `AttackCharge` whose charge (its last request 1120) ends at a target
  figure of a unit lands its hit at the arrival: `Sim::rideLand` makes a landing at the step of the arrival, code 1120,
  no trigger, no attack clip; the 1120 keeps playing. The rider then takes its next target (`reserveTarget`, the same
  choice `look()` makes). When that figure lies ahead of the rider and within its `ShortMoveRadius` of the line of its
  last move (`Sim::inLine` `[I]`, 24 world units for every VP rush member) and a move is needed, it rides on: a `Charge`
  step with no request (no new 1120 reaches the controller) and a 1120 move at the full `MoveRate` (no shuffle,
  `moveTo(..., no_shuffle)`), and lands again on arrival. Otherwise it stops: a `Wait` step with 1000 (from the run loop
  the omni machine goes to its stop-run state 9, plays 1440 and goes to idle, unit-controller.md section 2 `[C]`), no
  1600, and it looks again only when its 1440 clip is over (`Fig::ride_stop_until`). A figure that the landing spared
  (4733, the last standing figure) is never landed on twice without a move: the rider stops. A re-charge of a standing
  rider (`look()`: target out of reach, 1120) also ends in `rideLand`. A standing rider (`Fig::rode`) whose target is in
  reach strikes 1100 at once only when the controller says its machine takes it (`CombatFeedback::accepts`, live); else
  `ready()` as before (1600 entry, then 1100). Rush members WITH `AttackCharge` keep 1140 from the charge (none in VP:
  all 15 rush members of 0327's database, Horseman, Knight, Lancer and twelve unique ones, enable `Idle Attack RunCharge
  AttackCity Bombard Death BombardDefend Run Fortify CombatReady Walk`; VP's Cavalry and Cuirassier are not rush members,
  so (A) does not reach them).
- `CombatParams::defender_waits_first_landing` (default true). `Sim::setup` sets `type2_` when neither side is figureless,
  air or sea, neither has `Part::can_answer` (a projectile weapon that is not Vs_City: the stand-in for
  `HasShortRangedAttack`, 13.3 `[I]`) and the attack is not ranged. In such a fight a defender figure that would look for a
  target waits (`ready(Wait)`, as a defender without a target does: no request after no movement) until the attacker's
  first landing (`land()` sets `att_landed_` for any landing by a figure of participant 0), or until no attacking figure
  is in Look, Approach, Charge, Ready, Strike, Turn or Reform (so the wait cannot hold a fight). 18.15 phase 3 `[C]`.
- Plumbing as 4743's: `AnimRunner::setRushRideThrough` / `setDefenderWaitsFirstLanding` (`srv_units_anim.*`),
  `UnitsOptions::rushRideThrough` / `defenderWaitsFirstLanding` (`srv_units_scene.*`), host globals and keys
  `render_units_rush_ride_through` and `render_units_defender_waits_first_landing` in `server.cfg` (absent = 1, "0" / "1",
  anything else refuses the start) and in every new bundle's `render_config` (`srv_render_host.cpp`); `sceneshot` replays
  a bundle without the keys (every bundle recorded before 5057) and one with "0" with 0, and turns each on only on "1",
  with one line `sceneshot: render_config: units rush_ride_through %d, defender_waits_first_landing %d`.
- `trigger_scene` and `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene`: `--no-rush-ride-through`, `--no-defender-waits` (both default to the
  core's). `trigger_scene` prints a line `ride: rushRideThrough= defenderWaits= rideLandings= rideOns= rideStops= att1600=
  readyBeforeHit= defFirstLanding= attFirstLanding= end=` (readyBeforeHit: attacking figures whose first 1600 request came
  before their first hit).
- Runners: `run_charge_scenes.py` gains the ride cases (`kn-kill-s1..s3` Knight 20 -> 46 on Spearman 60 -> 93,
  `knb-kill-s1..s3` Knight 20 -> 31 on Spearman 60 -> killed, `ln-kill-s1..s3` Lancer on Pikeman and `hmsp-kill-s1..s3`
  Horseman on Spearman, both 20 -> 46 on 60 -> 93; steady), their bar (exit 0, end <= 8.0 s, readyBeforeHit 0; the old bar
  with `--no-rush-ride-through`), `--no-rush-ride-through`, `--no-defender-waits` and `--no-ride-cases` (main's 39 cases).
  The nine other scene runners (trigger, phase, ready, defend, walk_home, reform, city, turn, names) gain `--no-5057`
  (both knobs off; on EXE only where the runner has `--exe-base`), as W81's `--no-4743` (lead-0042 #11498).
- Tests: `test_combat.cpp` `a_rush_rider_lands_at_its_arrival_and_rides_through` (on, seeds 1-8: every 1120 hit lands at
  the end of one of the rider's moves, no 1600 before a rider's first hit, ride-ons happen and each lands at its move's
  end; off: no 1120 hit, no ride-on, every strike 1100 after a 1600; an `AttackCharge` rush member keeps 1140) and
  `a_type_2_defender_waits_for_the_first_landing` (ride-through off so the riders stand in 1440 + 1600: on, the
  defender's first strike is never before the attacker's first landing; off, the defender lands first in some seeds; an

  arms name the new knob off, as written before 5057: `a_killed_sides_last_figure_is_spared...` (its spare-off arm needs
  the defender to strike before it dies) and `h3_melee_survivors_walk_home_inside_the_fight` (its walk on / off margin);

**The gap by part** (18.29.2's phase split, kn_kill: route S 3.73 s, stock 6.90 s): start 0.14 / 0.85, arrival 0.80 /
1.43, strikes 1.23 / 1.43, tail 1.56 / 3.19. The tail is the largest part in all four cavalry cases (-1.53 to -1.85 s),
then the start (-0.70 s in every case, the infantry control too), then the arrival (-0.37 to -0.92 s).

**(1) The tail: stock ends no survivor of either side until the last dying figure has played its death** `[L]`.
- Stock kn_kill (S34): the last death is a knight's (`deathvoxh` + `horsedievox` at -1045, 332, 3.65 s from Run); its

  death vox; a Spearman figure moves at the same 5.18; the riders are still on their way at 6.45-6.58 (-1090, -1103, -1085,
  about 30 units per second on average), End 6.90, the run stop (`horsefootdirt`) at 7.05. wh_knight (S34): the knight's
  death vox 3.44, its weapon drops at 4.01 (+0.57: the shorter of the two death clips), the four riders start home at 4.51
  (+1.07), End 6.40. So the release follows the dying knight's clip (about 1.1 or 1.6 s by the variant drawn, 18.26 R2),
  then the walk home takes 1.7-1.9 s.
- The sampler's one type 2 simulation (Lancer 5 figures kills a Field Gun's 2 planned figures; `t2sim122.py`, the per-figure
  dump stays local) `[L]`: the last death enters state 8 at 5.158 s (simulation clock); the four riders leave the charge
  (0xC) for state 0x10 at 5.163 and stand; the last dying figure takes flag 0x10 (its death played) at 6.165 (1.002 s:
  death A); **the riders go to 0xB (walk home) at 6.172, 0.006 s later**; the simulation is removed at 6.984 (longest 0xB
  walk 0.71 s). This is 18.26 R1 (ranged targets, 33 of 33) for the attacker of a type 2 fight. **W91's 24 type 2 fights
  confirm it** `[L]`: the attacker's first release (0xB or 7) comes 0.020 s [0.000-0.034] after the last dying figure's
  done in all 12 Knight fights and 0.017 s [0.000-0.034] in all 12 foot fights, the defender's 0.000-0.003 s; last death
  start -> last dying done 1.382 s mounted [0.833-1.633], 1.224 s foot; the removal comes 1.720 s [0.900-2.366] after the
  attacker's release in the Knight fights (the riders' 0xB walk, longest per fight 0.27-2.00 s) but only 0.686 s
  [0.633-0.767] in the foot fights, whose attacker is still forward at the removal (18.33 (b): stock draws the rest of
  its way back after the simulation). kn_kill_b's first launch keeps one rider in 0x10 with other flags until 8.398 s,
  2.0 s after the other riders' walk ended (not read). Over all 134 sampled
  simulations with a death (`tail122.txt`): type 2 attacker release - last dying done +0.006 s (n 1); type 1 -0.284 s

  (`reform_end_`, so the first step when nobody reforms) in a fight with `type2_` (5057 (B)'s test); `Sim::type2Phase2`

  1450 clip, whose last request is not a movement, into `FigState::Turn` with 1450 (`Fig::p2stance`). The tick's Look / Wait
  case does not look before `phase2_end_` (so the riders stand with no request, stock's 3); the Turn case lets a stance
  figure look at `phase2_end_`; the end test counts the phase as a need. A defender that took the stance has 1450 as its
  last request, so 4750's `defendStance` gives it no second stance. Off: `phase2_end_` stays 0 and no line runs.

### 18.30 Both sides of a melee named by the striker's weapon: impacts and battle beds (W83, ticket 5055)

Written 2026-11-23 from 05:35 EST by w83-0042, branch `w83-5055` (from main 2efd32ab5, 5052 (T) included). Offline only:
no game, no instance; written under the 0630 take 6 HOLD (reading, design and code only; builds after HOLD OFF). Marks:
`[L]` a live Miles log named, `[C]` the code or the install's sound scripts named (read from the pure_vp game copy at run
time, nothing committed from them), `[I]` reading.

**Stock's rule for a melee hit's `$(WEAPON)`** `[L]`. In a melee where both sides strike, stock names every Sound
`$(WEAPON)` of a fighting unit by its opponent's weapon, not only the hit reaction:
- impacts (18.25.2, W76's S25): the Warrior's hits swordflesh (`AS3D_UNIT_WARRIOR_IMPACT_SPEAR`), the Spearman's bluntflesh
  (`..._SPEARMAN_IMPACT_BLUNT`), each with that unit's death vox at the same Miles position;
- battle beds (new, the same logs): stock S25 started `spearvsclubt2.mp3` at the Spearman's side and `clubvsspeart2.mp3`
  at the Warrior's; route S S24 (5052 on) started `spearvsspeart2.mp3` and `clubvsclubt2.mp3`. `[C]` the scripts:
  `AS3D_UNIT_SPEARMAN_BAT_AMB_T2_BLUNT` plays `SND_UNIT_T2_SPEAR_VS_CLUB` (`AudioDefines.xml`: file `SpearVsClubT2`),
  `AS3D_UNIT_WARRIOR_BAT_AMB_T2_SPEAR` plays `SND_UNIT_T2_CLUB_VS_SPEAR` (`ClubVsSpearT2`), `..._SPEARMAN_..._T2_SPEAR`
  `SPEAR_VS_SPEAR`, `..._WARRIOR_..._T2_BLUNT` `CLUB_VS_CLUB`. So a bed `AS3D_UNIT_<unit>_BAT_AMB_<tier>_$(WEAPON)` is
  "<own weapon> vs <$(WEAPON)>", and stock fills `$(WEAPON)` with the opponent's weapon there too. Evidence
  `server/evidence/0042/5055/w83/melee_w76_S24_S25.txt`.
- The Swordsman pair (`melee`) has one weapon on both sides (`swordvsswordt2` both runs): no test of the rule.
This fits 18.25's decompile reading of stock's chain with the figure's own entry (+0x60) empty in a fight, so that step
2, "the other participant's figure-0 weapon", gives every `$(WEAPON)` of the unit `[I]`. The attacker of a ranged fight
without retaliation has no `$(WEAPON)` name in the cases seen (the Archer's and the Gatling Gun's trigger names carry
none; W81's names logs, 2026-11-23), so what stock gives it is not observed.

**A city's strike** `[L]` W38's Tiny pair of 2026-11-21 (build 4390913; S3 stock u0, S1 / S2 route S arm p on main
a7b809601, before 5052; named offline by crc from W76's named logs, `city_naval_w38.txt`):

- `[C]` the scripts: 82 of the 96 `*3DScripts.xml` files have `AS3D_UNIT_<unit>_IMPACT_CITY_EARLY` / `_MID` / `_LATE`
  (Warrior and Swordsman: `SND_UNIT_ARROW_FLESH` / `_BOULDER_FLESH` / `_EXPLOSION20_POUND`); `Eras.CityBombardEffectTag` is

**Air and naval melee.** Naval `[L]` S3 stock only, `naval` (a Destroyer attacks a barbarian Frigate, which fires back:
`frigatefusillade` at the Frigate): the Frigate's hit is `explosion200pound` (`AS3D_UNIT_FRIGATE_IMPACT_EXPLOSION200POUND`
by `[C]`; the Destroyer's sound tag is `EXPLOSION200POUND`), so the struck defender of a naval melee is named by its
striker; no impact sample at the Destroyer (only `explosion6poundwater`, the Frigate shot's surface sound), so the

says so, the air opening included).

**Where 5052's namer kept Own for a striking defender** `[C]` main 2efd32ab5, `server/src/effects/srv_trigger_emitter.h`
`FightWeaponRoles::namer`: the loop skipped every fight where the unit is not the defender (`if(f.defUnit < 0 ||
f.defPlayer != player || f.defUnit != unit) continue;`, so an attacker always fell to the final `return Namer::Own`), and a
matched defender returned `Namer::Own` when `DefenderStrikes(f.retaliates, f.attackerDamage, attAir, isAir(player, unit),
true)` held (melee). The callers: `TriggerStream::Subs::weapon` (`srv_trigger_stream.cpp`, about line 184) and
`trigger_scene.cpp`'s `SceneSubs::weapon` (about line 272).

**The fix (5055)** `[C]`, under its own default-ON key since 2026-11-23 (MC #11607; the switch below):
- `FightWeaponRoles::namer(..., bool struck = false)`: with `struck` every unit struck in its running fight is named by
  its striker: the defender by its attacker whether it strikes back or not; the attacker by its defender when
  `DefenderStrikes` holds (melee, the air opening when the bomber took damage); an attacker nobody strikes back keeps its
  own; a city striker (either side) gives `OpponentCity` (own kept, counted). `struck` false is 5052's rule line for line.
- Only for a Sound: `TriggerStream::Subs::weapon` passes `strikerMelee && type == Sound`. Effects (the hit effects'
  `$(WEAPON)`) keep 5052's rule: no live data on them, and an effect name has no script table to fall back on.
- The fallback: `Substitutions::weaponFallback` (new virtual, default false); `TriggerEmitter::sound` gives a Sound name
  with `$(WEAPON)` that is no script a second try with it (`substituteFallback`, a wrapper that forwards `$(TERRAIN)`); the
  stream's `weaponFallback` gives the figure's own weapon when the namer said `Opponent` (counted
  `NameCounters::strikerFallback`). A name with both variables resolves `$(TERRAIN)` twice on that second try, so the
  (T) counters count it twice `[C]`. This keeps 11.3's 0557 cases named: there the opponent's weapon left 4 names of s-m2
  that are no script.
- The switch (corrected 2026-11-23 by W93, MC #11607; replaced: "no server.cfg key of its own, it widens
  render_test_units_trigger_striker_weapon"): `TriggerStreamConfig::strikerMelee` has its own host key
  **`render_units_trigger_striker_melee`, default 1**, so each stock-faithful sound change stays switchable on its own
  for a beta report, and `render_test_units_trigger_striker_weapon` keeps its meaning. **The melee naming is in effect
  only when both keys are 1** (it refines the striker-weapon naming; lead-0042's rule): striker_weapon 0 is the rule
  before 5052 whatever the melee key says; striker_melee 0 with striker_weapon 1 is main before 5055, byte for byte.
  With both on (the product default) melee impact names and the battle beds (BAT_AMB) of both sides change, as stock
  (the MC accepted the behaviour, #11607). Plumbed as 5052 (T) and 5057: the host global `g_unitsTriggerStrikerMelee`
  with its per-start reset and 0/1 check (`srv_render_host.cpp`), `UnitsOptions::triggerStrikerMelee`
  (`srv_units_scene.h`) into `TriggerStreamConfig::strikerMelee` (`srv_units_scene.cpp`), every bundle's
  `render_config` (rule A: sceneshot reads it absent as 0, line `sceneshot: render_config: units trigger_striker_melee

- Tests: `test_trigger_emitter.cpp` `testStrikerMelee5055` (melee both ways, ranged, a city striker on each side, the air

### 18.32 The flag-model offset, measured offline: route S against stock per fight class and phase (W90, ticket 4779, 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 10:06-10:40 EST by w90-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w90-4779flag` from main 975fc28f7.
Offline only: no game, no instance. Marks: `[C]` this run's numbers, `[L]` from a live recording, `[I]` a reading.

**The question** (15.6, 15.9's open row): how far a unit's drawn figures stand from the unit's root, where the EXE's
flag sits (route S places the root at the EXE's unit position in position mode `exe`), per phase kind, and how that
compares with stock.

**Why the 4779 dumps could not answer it, and what was used instead** `[C]`:
- The `--evidence` dumps (`.c5units`) and the timelines (`server.c5anim`) of S1, S4, S8, S10, S11, S12
  (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w38/big/`, read only) carry each figure's clip and time but no figure position (15.9). 0557's
  recorded stock fights carry fight times but no figure track either (5.5). So the brief's stock reference "0557's
  recorded fights" does not exist as positions. Running 4776's 5.4 set through the core gives route S on 0557's cases,
  not stock's figures.
- **Route S:** in a fight the server places the figures by the core's `FightMotion` (5.2; its adapter builds it from
  the `CombatRun` result with `combatPositions` on the frame's grid). The same core with positions,
  `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene --positions --live`, writes every figure's world position each 1/30 s (`motion.csv`) and
  the moves (`moves.csv`: 1120 charge, 1400 / 1450 run or shuffle). It was built from main 975fc28f7 (Release, target
  only, through quietlock, about 1 min, no LTO), so these are main's defaults: `charge_any`, `reform_first`,
  `walk_home`, `attack_from_stance`, `city_in_place` all on. The fights: (a) every unit-on-unit fight rebuilt from the
  six timelines, 83 of them (S1 14, S4 31, S8 4, S10 1, S11 29, S12 4; 45 ranged). Left out: segments with no partner
  (city attacks, unseen attackers: 274), pairs longer than 13 s (13), two partners (6), no attack action (5).
  (b) 0557's 19 cases (4776's 5.4 set). Seed 1, the pure_vp install copy, 0327's database copy, a flat stand-in field,
  each unit facing the other (nearest of six). 102 runs, all exit 0, 1 min. The root is the plot centre, computed as
  `units::plotCentre` does on that tool's grid.
- **Stock:** W52's sampler lines (18.15.1, `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-4745/w52-run/sim52.jsonl.gz`, read only;
  stock, build 4390913, Huge t350-359, 174 shown fights) hold every figure's world x, y at the fight's creation, at each
  phase change and at each of the figure's state or flag changes `[L]`. The root is the plot centre: the hex-lattice
  point nearest the side's median figure at creation (rows 64 x 0.866 apart, odd rows at x = 64 n, even rows at
  64 n + 32, fitted on these lines). Figure samples farther than 100 world units from the root are stale records of
  the participant, seen 140-570 units away at creation and never drawn there `[I]`. 5,435 of 214,016 samples (2.5 %)
  were dropped as stale. Figures are resampled at 30 Hz on the fight's own clock, each at its last read position.
- **The measure** (both sides alike): per frame and unit, the distance between the root and the centroid of the
  unit's figures (all figures standing at the start; dying figures stay where they fell). The kinds:
  - `rest`: the first frame, i.e. the standing layout.
  - `approach`: a charge under way (route S 1120; stock phase 3).
  - `strike`: standing and striking (route S: no move under way; stock: phases 4-6 before the first finished figure).
  - `reform`: the re-lay before the fight and the walk home from its start to the end (route S: a run or shuffle
    before the first hit, and from the first run after it; stock: phases 1-2, then from the first finished figure,
    state 7 / 9 / 0xB, to the removal).
  Fight classes are stock's (18.15): type 2 = a melee attacker with no `HasShortRangedAttack` member (stock charges);
  type 1 = a gun attacker (stock strikes from where it stands); ranged; melee on a city. Route S's class comes from the
  database.
- **px scale** `[L: S1's own picture, measured 2026-11-23]`: in S1's pictures (2554 x 1411, the driver's two wheel ticks
  in) the EXE's unit flags of neighbouring plots stand 546.7 px apart at row y 495 (8.54 px per world unit). Two plots
  are 1080.2 px apart there (8.44) and 975.5 px apart at y 213 (7.62). The ground scale is linear in the screen row, so
  the screen centre is about 9.1. Here **8.5 px per world unit** is used (range 7.6-9.1 over the middle of the screen).
  The pictures stay outside git (DIAGNOSTIC, D112).

**The table** `[C: these runs]` (median / p95 in world units, px at 8.5; n = fights, f = frames; attacker side unless
named; the defender columns are in `server/evidence/0042/4779/w90/table_w90.md`):

| Class | Kind | Route S | Stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| melee type 2 (charge) | rest | 0.9 / 4.4 (8 / 38 px), n35 | 5.9 (50 px), n1 |
| melee type 2 | approach | 12.7 / 42.8 (108 / 364 px), n35 f1444 | 15.9 / 53.6 (135 / 455 px), n1 f79 |
