**Walk** (a unit moving between plots): route S's walk keeps the standing layout on the root (the inner placement
stands on the root, mode `exe`, 5.2 "The 4981 seam") `[I]`. So its offset is the `rest` row: median 0.9-1.3, p95 at
most 4.4 world units (38 px). **Stock's walk has no figure recording anywhere** (W52's sampler reads fights only), so
it is not compared.

**Verdict** `[C]` for route S's numbers, `[L]` for stock's samples, `[I]` for the comparison:
- **Within stock:** ranged (strike p95 1.9 against 10.5), melee on a city (2.0 against 13.5), every defender (p95 at
  most 2.6 against 13.5-25.5), and the standing layout or walk (p95 at most 4.4 against 8.5-13.3). Route S keeps its
  figures closer to the flag than stock does in all of these. Stock's figures stand off their plot centre even at rest:
  defenders at p95 24, the EXE's figures not returned to their slots between fights.
- **Outside stock: melee type 1 (gun attackers), strike and approach.** Route S's attacker strikes at its target:
  strike p95 60.7 against stock's 14.1, so 46.6 world units, about 396 px at 8.5 (330-420 px over 7.6-9.1). The
  median is 3.7 against 1.7 (+2.0 units, 17 px). Route S also has an approach of p95 43.2 (367 px) that stock does not
  have. The cause is known: stock's type 1 attacker strikes from its slots (18.15.1), and route S still charges in
  type 1. 18.17 named this as "the next item if the lengths are to match per phase". `attack_from_stance` (5050)
  does not change it. Per case on 0557's set, the attacker's strike offset in world units: d2 Tank 60.7, d3 Mechanized
  Infantry 43.0, d1 Infantry 18.0, i3 Rifleman 8.6. The reform rows agree (p95 30.0 against 27.9).
- **Melee type 2 (charge): no adequate stock reference.** W52's ten turns hold one stock type 2 fight: a Lancer
  killing a Field Gun, with phases 1, 2, 6, 3. Against it, route S's approach (p95 42.8 against 53.6) and walk home
  (68.3 against 67.1) are within that fight's range. Its strike frames are not comparable, because stock's phase 6
  comes before its charge. Route S's charging figures stand at the target while they strike (p95 69.6, 592 px: the
  whole unit on the defender's plot), as stock's phase 3 sends them to the target's position (5.1 M3). Whether stock's
  type 2 strike sits as far needs a stock sampler run on an earlier-era save (an ancient or medieval melee series) `[I]`.
  *Measured 2026-11-23 by W91 (18.33): stock's type 2 runs up in 24 of 24 fights (foot attackers meet the defender part
  way, strike p95 35.6; Knights strike on the defender's plot, p95 63.8); route S's strict type 2 is inside stock at the
  approach and up to 7-12 units beyond its strike p95.*
- **Naval melee: not compared.** Route S's ships approach (`ships_approach`, strike p95 69.4). W52's sea class is
  ranged naval and air (strike p95 1.3), not melee.

**Limits** `[I]`:
- Stock positions are seen only at state changes. A figure running between two changes is seen at its next change, so
  stock's in-motion offsets (approach, walk home) are undersampled and its p95 there is a lower bound.
- Route S runs on a flat field with facings rounded to the six, seed 1. The live fights' own dice and terrain are not
  reproduced.
- The S-session fights were drawn live by W38's build of 2026-11-21 (before `reform_first`, `walk_home`, 4743's
  default). This replay measures today's main core on those fights' units, not the 2026-11-21 pictures.
- The px scale is S1's camera. The huge sessions' camera was not measured.

### 18.34 A unit struck by a city: stock names its hit by the city owner's era index (W92, ticket 5058, 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 from 11:40 EST by w92-0042, branch `w92-5058` (from `w83-5055` abb19b1cb). Marks: `[C]` a read of
the EXE (build 4390913, headless Ghidra on a copy of the project, runbook 3 "A headless Ghidra read"; no decompiler
output kept in git, D83) or of the DLL source (the fork checkout of 2026-11-10, `CvGameCoreDLL_Expansion2`), `[L]` a live
log named, `[I]` reading.

**Where stock's `CITY_<EARLY|MID|LATE>` comes from** `[C]`:
- The EXE holds the three names as its own strings (`.rdata` 0x9EE004 `CITY_EARLY`, 0xA00780 `CITY_MID`, 0xA059E4
  `CITY_LATE`); the database has no such value (`Eras.CityBombardEffectTag` is `CITY_BOMBARD_*`, the projectile's
  VisEffect, a different path: effects-formats.md 15.1).
- The combat simulation system (`cvCombatSimSystem.cpp`) makes, once at its set-up (0x4C7AD0), three city weapon
  objects, slot 0, 1, 2, and names them through 0x6E4630: slot 0 `CITY_EARLY`, slot 1 `CITY_MID`, slot 2 `CITY_LATE`
  (each also sets two values at +0x74 / +0x78, not read). The name lands where a weapon entry keeps its weapon tag, and
  the sound-override field is left empty, so a Sound's `$(WEAPON)` gets the tag itself (18.25's chain, step 3 through
  0x70DE60 -> 0x589380: the city participant's figure-0 weapon entry, tag at entry +0x38, override +0x3C empty).
- The slot is chosen by 0x4739C0: **the slot equal to the given index when the index (unsigned) is below 3, else slot 0**.
- A city participant (0x4024F0: the attacker when a city strikes, the defender when a unit attacks a city, a city damage
  member from participant 3 on) passes the 32-bit word at +0x18 of its 0x24-byte participant entry, the entry copied from
  the 0x59 payload (`combat-choreography.md` 4.1). The entry has the layout of the DLL's `CvCombatMemberEntry`
  (`CvStructs.h`: player, id, flags, damage, final damage, max HP, x and y as int16 at +0x10 / +0x12, combat type +0x14,
  **era +0x18**, weapon type, weapon option); the x / y at +0x10 / +0x12 and the hit-point words at +0xC / +0xE are read
  as such by 0x731FF0, which fits. A plot target with no city (0x6BD1A0) always takes slot 0.
- The DLL fills a member's era with `GET_PLAYER(owner).GetCurrentEra()` (`CvUnitCombat.cpp` `AddCombatMember`, the
  damage members); `CvPlayer::GetCurrentEra` is the team's current era (`CvPlayer.cpp` 34741). What the EXE writes into
  the era word of participants 0 and 1 (built by `GameplayUnitCombat` 0x67DD90 from the combat info's getters) is
  **not read** `[I: the owner's current era, as the damage members carry it]`.

So stock `[C, with the participant-word reading I]`: a unit struck by a city of an owner in era 0 (ancient) is named
`IMPACT_CITY_EARLY`, era 1 (classical) `IMPACT_CITY_MID`, era 2 (medieval) `IMPACT_CITY_LATE`, **era 3 (renaissance) and
every later era `IMPACT_CITY_EARLY` again**. 18.30's `[I]` reading by the `Eras.CityBombardEffectTag` buckets (EARLY
ancient-classical, MID medieval-industrial, LATE modern on) agrees only in the ancient era; it is corrected there. W38's
S3 (`city_bombard`, `city_attack`, ancient) gave `arrowflesh` = `IMPACT_CITY_EARLY` both ways. The live check of 5058 (c)
(W94, below) confirmed the selector in era 1 and era 3 `[L]`: the `[I]` on the participant word now stands confirmed for
the city attacker.

**Where the server knows the era** `[C]`: `SrvFeed::PlayerRecord::era` (record 6 PLAYERS, `GetCurrentEra`, updated by
`kEraChanged` between reads), already in every live feed, recorded feed and scene bundle; the trigger stream reads it at a
fight's start from `UnitsCore::players()` (the city side's owner, `FightSide::owner`). No format change: no record gains
a field. The combat record (record 5) carries no era for the attacker and defender; its damage members carry
`CvCombatMemberEntry::m_eEra`, not used here.

**The design (lead-0042 #11591)**: `FightWeaponRoles::Fight` keeps each city side's owner era (-1 when not known); a
Sound whose `$(WEAPON)` the namer gives to a city striker (`OpponentCity`) takes `CITY_EARLY` / `_MID` / `_LATE` by the
selector above, the unit's own weapon as 5055's second try when that name is no script of the unit (14 of the 96 unit
script files have no `IMPACT_CITY_*`, 18.30); era not known, or the switch off: the unit's own, exactly as before.
Effects are unchanged (no `CITY_*` effect names). The switch is its own host key `render_units_trigger_city_era`
(default 1; rule A: absent in a bundle's `render_config` = 0), not a ride on the striker-weapon key.

**Merged state and offline proof (W94, 2026-11-23 12:21-14:40)** `[L]`: the branch merged 5055 with its own key
(`render_units_trigger_striker_melee`, W93) and main; the three keys sit side by side, each with its off arm, and the units
host's trigger-names line names `city_era 1 (5058)` only when it is in effect (as 5055 does). One builder pass
(`server/evidence/0042/5058/w94/allb_summary94.txt`, 0 failed steps; base = the 5055 head ad2203187): names 15/15,
expect-fail 13/13, exe-base 15/15 (ce0-ce3 differ from the base, cu equals it); every trigger_scene runner's default arm,
its `--no-city-era` arm and the base's equal byte for byte; units 80/80, unit extras 13/13, test_unitfeed 23 passed,
unitfeed with 5058 off byte-identical to the base on all five fixtures (`uf_identity94.txt`), emitter plain and ASan OK,
server.exe, scene bundle 4 programs, sceneshot smoke, R13's other builders. run_all on the pure_vp copy: render-host
195 passed, scenebundle-py 27 passed (`test_bundle_carries_trigger_city_era_off` included), offline-equals-live 17 passed.

**Live same-dice pair (5058 (c), W94, 2026-11-23 14:24-14:48)** `[L]`: c5h-a (EXE build 4390913, mods548, Goldberg),
run_4779's Tiny T18 save copy, layout from w92-5058 a1fc94c01 (server 340348b1...), Miles log (4797's `mss_log.dll`)
named by `map_samples.py`; driver `server/evidence/0042/5058/w94/run_5058.py` over run_4779 (cases `city_era1`,
`city_era3`: Lua grants the human's team every tech below the era and one of it, `GetCurrentEra` read back 1 and 3, then
run_4779's `city_bombard`: the capital strikes a barbarian Warrior). Arms u0 (stock) and p (route S, the key at its
default 1). Same dice: the defender ends at 28 damage on every arm and case. The struck Warrior's three impacts:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 classical | `boulderflesh` x3 | `boulderflesh` x3 | CITY_MID | EARLY |
| 3 renaissance | `arrowflesh` x3 | `arrowflesh` x3 | CITY_EARLY | MID |

Death voices (`deathvoxb`) and falls (`bodyfallleaves`) also match, 3 each. So route S names a city's hits as stock does

### 18.36 Victory vox where stock is silent: stock never takes victory in VP (W96, ticket 5059, 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 from 12:50 EST by w96-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w96-5059` from `origin/w85-5057` cab97a1d6.
Part (a), analysis only: no build, no instance, no EXE read beyond the knowledge base (D83). Marks: `[C]` code or data
read here, `[L]` from live logs already on disk, `[I]` this section's reading. Inputs read only: W85's offline
`triggers.log` files of cab97a1d6, W52's and W91's live stock samplers (`F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/evidence-4745/w52-run/
sim52.jsonl.gz`, 18.15.1; `F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w91/sim-w91-1.jsonl`, `sim-w91-2.jsonl`, 18.33), the Miles logs of
seventeen stored arms on F:, 0327's database.

**Result.** Stock plays no victory clip at all in VP: not a silent pose, no 1800. Route S draws victory for survivors that
stock ends in 0xB / 7. The rule that separates them is 5.3's "it has 1800 enabled" `[C 0321]`: route S reads it as the
member's machine taking 1800, which every machine does; the EXE's enable mask has a word Victory, and no VP member row
carries it `[C data, I that 5.3's test reads that bit]`.

**Route S's rule** `[C code, render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp]`: `Sim::victoryEligible` takes a survivor whose `Fig::last`
is 1600 or 1000, whose member has `CombatMemberArt::victory`, not air, of a side whose opponent is killed; `finish()`
then draws `random(100) > 25`. `CombatMemberArt::victory` is set in `Controller::combatMember`
(`render/src/unitanim/controller.cpp`) as "the member's machine takes 1800 on path 4" (`[I]` in combat.h). `Fig::last`
starts at 1000 ("a unit at rest"), so an attacker that never gets a request is eligible. Which figures take it
(offline, W85's logs of cab97a1d6, `scripts/vict_logs.py`, `victory-offline-w85logs.txt`):
- the infantry kills (0557's s-w2, a Warrior on a barbarian Warrior at 15 hp; s-k1, a Swordsman on a Catapult): 8 and 5
  victory figures per run, in the default, the 5057-off and the main arm alike: the attackers beyond the chargers never
  move or strike and keep `last` 1000. Live, S33's kill (W86, 18.28.2): `3.63:avictory/7` after 4 chargers;
- the knight kill knb-kill (Knight on a Spearman killed): main 2-3 victory figures per seed (riders that entered 1600
  before their 1100 and keep 1600 as `last`), 5057's default 1-2 (riders that stop with the ride stop's 1000);
- hm-kill (Horseman kills a Warrior): main 2-3, 5057 0-2; kn-kill, ln-kill, hmsp-kill: 0 (no kill).
- Per figure `[C: trigger_scene --dump-core, W85's build of cab97a1d6, seed 1, steady, 2026-11-23 13:41 EST;
  victory-dumpcore.txt, scripts/dump_vict.py]`: s-w2's victory figures are 8 of the 10 attackers with no request at all
  (`wait` with code 0 at 0.0, then `victory` 1800 at 1.167 s; the other 2 lost the draw); its 2 chargers end on 1140 and
  walk home. s-k1: 5 of 8 such waiting attackers. knb-kill-s1: riders 0 and 2, each after a ride stop's `wait` 1000.

**Stock** `[L]` (`scripts/vict_sampler.py`, `victory-stock-samplers.txt`; `victory-miles-logs.txt`):
- W52's sampler (174 stock simulations on the huge t350 copy, 25 kills, 100 surviving killer figures): no figure enters
  state 0x12 and none is in it in any removal's last snapshot. *(Trace, 2026-11-23: W96's first post (#11695) carried
  the caveat that 96 of these 100 struck, so the last-action test alone might explain stock's silence; W91's sampler
  below settles it the other way and replaces that caveat.)*
- W91's sampler on the same Tiny cases as W86's live row (two launches, 12 simulations each): in each kill every
  surviving attacker charges (0xC); only 1-2 strike; the others go 0xC -> 1 -> 2 and end 0x10 -> 0xB -> 7. By the state
  setter (`../02-exe-internals/exe-audio.md` 13.3 `[C]`) a figure in state 2 whose last action is the 1120 run charge
  requests 1600 when its member enables 1450 (the Swordsman and the Knight have `Walk`), so these figures pass the
  last-action test, their opponent is killed, they are not air, and still none takes 0x12: 26 such figures over the six
  kill fights of the two launches, 0 victories, where a 74 % draw gives about 19 (P(0) about 0.26^26). **So the
  last-action test does not explain stock's silence; the enable condition does** `[L, I]`.
- Miles: 0 victory vox in every stock arm stored (W37's huge pair arm a, tiny2 a, W39 tiny3 a, S28, S34, S13 u0, S18 u0
  twice; about 52,000 lines), 3-15 in every route S arm with a kill.

**Why** `[C data, I rule]`: the EXE parses `EnableActions` into a per-member bit mask whose word table has `Victory` as
bit 13 (`unit-controller.md`, 0439 [C]); 0 of the 364 `ArtDefine_UnitMemberCombats` rows of VP's database (0327's copy)
carry the word Victory (`DisableActions` is empty everywhere). Reading 5.3's "1800 enabled" as that bit explains every
observation above; the routine's test of the bit was not read (D83: description only), so the reading stays `[I]`, now
backed by `[L]`. Answers 18.28.2's open point "whether stock plays a silent victory pose is not read" and replaces 10.12's
reading "stock has no idle attackers to take victory" (stock's idle chargers qualify by last action and still do not
take it).

**The fix (part (b), designed; built after 5057 is on main; lead-0042 GO #11696):** `CombatParams::victory_needs_word`,
default on: `victoryEligible` also needs the member's `EnableActions` word `Victory` (`CombatMemberArt::enable`); off =
today byte for byte. Host key `render_units_victory_word` (server.cfg absent = 1; render_config absent = 0, rule A),
`trigger_scene` / `c5r_unitanim_combat_scene` `--no-victory-word`. Regression: a `test_combat.cpp` kill with and without
the word; runner cases s-w2, s-k1, knb-kill-s1..s3, hm-kill: 0 victory records (today 8, 5, 1-2, 0-2). The victory
tail (11.2) stays for a mod whose member carries the word. Part (c): the live same-dice pair, victory vox 0 as stock.

Evidence `server/evidence/0042/5059/w96/` (the two scripts and their three outputs; counts only, no names from the install).

#### 18.36.1 The fix as built; the pre-merge offline check (W100, ticket 5059 (b), 2026-11-23, offline; all-builders pass NOT run)

Written 2026-11-23 from 20:45 EST by w100-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w96-5059` after merging main 00e662fd5
(5057 in), head b6e2f2b60. Marks: `[C]` code or offline run here, `[I]` reading.

**Built** `[C code]`: `CombatParams::victory_needs_word` (default true; `combat.h`); `Sim::victoryEligible` (`combat.cpp`)

### 18.37 A city's own shot and miss sounds: stock's chain, and why route S plays none (W98, ticket 5062, 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 from 15:00 EST by w98-0042, branch `w98-5062` (from main 941609179, 5058 in). Offline only so far.
Marks: `[C]` a read of the definitions (the install's `Civ5ArtDefines_VisEffects.xml` through 4786's extract, the
install's `Assets/Sounds/XML/*3DScripts.xml`, the debug database `Eras` table), of the DLL source (the fork checkout) or of
the server's code on main; `[L]` a named live log; `[I]` reading. No EXE code was read for this section (D83).

**Stock's chain** `[C]`:
- The DLL's `CvCity::GetCityBombardEffectTag` (`CvCity.cpp` 34199) returns `Eras.CityBombardEffectTag` of
  `GET_TEAM(getTeam()).GetCurrentEra()`, the owner team's current era (the same value as `SrvFeed::PlayerRecord::era`,
  18.34). The VP database (debug database of 0327): eras 0-1 `CITY_BOMBARD_EARLY`, eras 2-4 `CITY_BOMBARD_MID`, eras 5-7
  `CITY_BOMBARD_LATE`. This bucket is **not** 18.34's impact selector (index 0 / 1 / 2, 3+ back to 0): the projectile
  and the struck unit's hit name come from two different era rules.
- The tag is the VisEffect's own name. Each of the three carries one `<SoundEffect>` and one `ProjectileEnd` child, and
  the child carries the landing's sound:

| Tag (eras) | Shot script (the VisEffect's SoundEffect) | Stock sample | Child at the landing | Its script | Stock sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CITY_BOMBARD_EARLY` (0-1) | `AS3D_UNIT_ARCHER_FLAMING_ARROW_T2` (DontPlayMoreThan 1, DontTriggerDuplicates) | `flamingarrowt2` | `ART_DEF_VEFFECT_PROJ_ARROW_IMPACT` (no surface variant) | `AS3D_IMPACT_ARROW_MISS` (DontPlayMoreThan 2) | `arrowmiss` |
| `CITY_BOMBARD_MID` (2-4) | `AS3D_UNIT_CATAPULT_CATAPULT_STRIKE` (DontPlayMoreThan 2) | `catapultstrike` | `ART_DEF_VEFFECT_CATAPULT_ROCK_IMPACT_$(TERRAIN)` | `AS3D_IMPACT_BOULDER_<surface>` (DontPlayMoreThan 2; LEAVES = `SND_UNIT_BOULDER_FOREST`) | `boulderforest` on a forest plot |
| `CITY_BOMBARD_LATE` (5-7) | `AS3D_UNIT_ROCKET_ARTILLERY_MBL_SAM_FIRE_ROCKET` | not measured | `ART_DEF_VEFFECT_TANK_IMPACT_$(TERRAIN)` | `AS3D_IMPACT_EXPLOSION6_POUND_<surface>` (CITY: `..._EXPLOSION20_POUND_CITY`) | not measured |

- Only these three VisEffects in the base file have both a sound and a child: no unit projectile carries its own sound
  (a unit's shot sound is its clip's Sound trigger). `ARROW_MISS` is named nowhere in the trigger files: in stock and
  on route S it plays only as `PROJ_ARROW_IMPACT`'s SoundEffect. The "miss" sound plays at **every** landing, hit or miss.
- **The counts are the scripts' caps, not the volley's size** `[C for the caps, I for the reading]`: stock plays one
  `flamingarrowt2` and two `arrowmiss` (era 1, W94; ancient, W38's S3 `city_bombard` and `city_attack`) and two
  `catapultstrike` and two `boulderforest` (era 3, W94) while three figures die; the caps are 1 / 2 / 2 / 2. The volley
  may hold more projectiles than the sounds show.
- **Timing in stock** `[L]` (seconds from the case MARK; W94's `live_w94.txt`, W38's `city_naval_w38.txt` on 5055's
  evidence): era 1 shot 1.038, landings 1.469 / 1.534, the struck figures' impacts 1.672-1.734; era 3 shots 1.002 / 1.034
  (the second 32 ms later about 18 units along the line to the target `[I: the second projectile, or its sound placed
  where it is when it starts]`), landings 1.403 / 1.467, impacts 1.669-1.735; ancient (S3) shot 1.137, landings 1.537 /
  1.601, impacts 1.885. So **shot to landing 0.40-0.50 s, landing to the figures' impacts about 0.2 s**; the shot plays
  at the city's centre about 10 units above the ground (z 22 against the plot's 12), the landing sounds about 10-12
  units up near the target figures.
- **A unit attacking a city gets the same volley** `[L, W38's S3 city_attack]`: the city answers a melee attack with
  `flamingarrowt2` at the city and two `arrowmiss` at the attackers (1.001, 1.535 / 1.567), then the attackers'
  `arrowflesh` and deaths. Route S (S2, same case) plays none of it.

**Why route S plays nothing** `[C, main 941609179]`:
- The core makes a city's strike as `CombatHit`s with `city` true and `effect` / `sound` from `CombatParams::city_effect`
  / `city_sound` (`render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`, `Sim::cityVolley` and the landings, and the city's answer in a melee).
- **The server never sets either**: `AnimRunner`'s fight start (`server/src/units/srv_units_anim.cpp`, the
  `ca::CombatParams params` block) fills only the rule-A switches; the two names stay empty. Only
  `render/tests/unitanim/test_combat_special.cpp` sets them (test names).
- So `planHitEffect` (`render/src/effects/effect_routes.cpp`) returns "the hit names no effect" with route `None`;
  `EffectRoutes::hits` counts it `hitNone` and keeps nothing pending, so no `CITY_BOMBARD_*` flight is added, no
  `ProjectileEnd` child starts at the landing, and the hit's sound branch in `applyHit` is never reached. The city's
  answer in a melee goes to route `CityDefence` ("nothing [I]") whatever its names. Route S therefore draws **no city
  projectile either** (a visual gap beside the audible one) `[C; not looked at live]`.
- The server's effect library (4786's reader) does not read `<SoundEffects>`: the server knows no VisEffect's sound.

**How a server-started VisEffect sounds** `[L, inferred]`: route S's ranged fights play `arrowmiss` at the target (S24,
5052 W76: 2 per case) although no trigger file names `ARROW_MISS`, so the EXE plays a VisEffect's SoundEffect when the
server's player starts it as a one-shot (record 0x28, the flight's `ProjectileEnd` child). Whether a **lasting** start
(0x29, a flight with `FOLLOWS`) plays its SoundEffect is **not known**: no unit projectile has one to show it, and 4727's
r5 flew `CITY_BOMBARD_EARLY` without a Miles log.

**Not known, and what closes it:** (1) the 0x29 start's sound (one live arm, 5062's live pair); (2) stock's flight scale
for a city volley (15.7.8 open item 5: the server flies it at 1.0, about tree-sized with the definition's 1.3; stock's not
read); (3) the volley's projectile count in stock (the caps hide it); (4) the `LATE` row live.

#### 18.37.3 The attacking city's centre from the DLL thread, and its offline proof (W107, 2026-11-23)

Written 2026-11-23 from 17:21 EST by w107-0042 on branch `w98-5062` (head 552a88da0 + this work; main 55808b00c, not yet
merged again). Source decision: lead-0042 GO #12015 on W107's question #12012. Marks: `[C]` source read or offline run
named here; nothing live yet.

**Where a city's plot can come from on the server** `[C]`:
- `UnitsCore` holds no city record (players, units, minor civilizations only). 5058's owner era is
  `SrvFeed::PlayerRecord::era` (`ICvPlayer1::GetCurrentEra` on the DLL thread), not a city record.
- The feed carries no city plot: kinds 4-6 and 26-28 have `plot = -1`, `PlotRecord.flags` bit 4 is never set, and the
  combat record (64 bytes, full) has only the target's plot.
- The DLL adds **no damage member** for an attacking city: `CvUnitCombat::GenerateRangedCombatInfo(CvCity&, ...)` (fork
  `CvUnitCombat.cpp` 751-823) calls `setCity`, `setUnit`, `setPlot` and no `AddCombatMember`, so the members carry no
  city x, y either.
- The render thread may not call into the DLL (`srv_feed.h`, bug 0103), and `AnimRunner` runs there.
- So the only source is the DLL thread, in `srv_remote_feed.cpp OnCombat`, on the city pointer it already reads with
  `GetOwner` / `GetID`.

**Purity audit of `ICvCity1::GetX` / `GetY`** `[C, the fork at the D30 audit's commit 1b87dd185]`: `CvDllCity.cpp`
143-146 / 148-151 return `m_pCity->getX()` / `getY()`, and `CvCity.h` 549-552 / 554-557 are inline `return m_iX;` /
`return m_iY;`. They are plain member reads with no side effect. The audit is the server's own: it is cited in
`srv_remote_feed.cpp`'s header and in renderer-in-server-design.md 2 (correction note), and **`proxy/model/pure-methods.tsv`
is not changed**.

**The code** `[C]`:
- `OnCombat` reads `GetX` / `GetY` only for a `kCityCombat` whose ATTACKER is a city. It makes the plot index on the
  feed's own grid (`SrvFeed::GetSize`, as `OnFowChanged` does) and writes it as **kind 28's `a[3]` = plot + 1**. `a[3]`
  was always 0 before, so 0 = not known: no attacking city, a position outside the grid (counted `s_nCityPlotsOutside`),
  or a recording made before 5062. Recordings and fixtures therefore replay unchanged.
- `AnimFeed::take` copies `a[3] - 1` into `CombatIn::cityPlot`. `FightClock::add` takes it through a new last parameter
  (default -1) into `Fight::attackerCityPlot`.
- `ControllerFightPlayer::positions` (the attacker side, a city): with `render_units_trigger_city_shot` on, the city side
  gets `has_centre` at `cu::plotCentre` of that plot (`AnimRunner::cityCentres`). When no plot is known or the centre is
  refused, the side gets no centre: the rule before, counted `cityNoCentre`, with a plain (not LOUD) line
  `units: city shot (5062): fight seq N: city O/ID (plot P) has no centre: ...` (the first ten, said by UnitsHost each
  frame). With the key off, no centre is ever set, so the rule before 5062 holds byte for byte. The positions stay all or
  nothing: a defender that was not placed in the frame before still leaves the fight without positions and without a
  flight.
- The core's `cityVolley` then sets `has_origin` from the placed city part, and `planHitEffect` flies each landing as a
  `CityVolley` from the centre (18.37.1).

**Offline proof** `[C, 2026-11-23, pure_vp copy, 0327's debug database, Release, no LTO, W102's c5render of b6ceba385;
evidence `server/evidence/0042/5062/w107/offline_w107.txt`]`:
- New units case `fight_city_flight`. It runs the product's path: UnitsHost -> AnimFeed (`a3`) -> FightClock ->
  AnimRunner positions -> the core's volley -> the TriggerStream's EffectRoutes (`planHitEffect`), with the routes open
  (`TestEnvCombat(..., geometry)` adds the weapon and member columns that `FightGeometry::open` reads). It counts the
  routes' hits, not only `city_effect`. Results:
  - plot known: named 1, centres 1; routes hits 5, **city volleys 5, flights 5**, none 0.
  - `a[3]` = 0: centres 0, no centre 1 (one line); hits 5, city volleys 0, none 5, **flights 0**.
  - key off: named 0, flights 0.
- **The same case fails on the rule before W107.** A units build with `positions()` given no plot (the code before this
  fix, build only, reverted at once) gives `plot: ... city volleys 0, none 5, flights 0`, and the case FAILs (81 of 82).
  With the fix the units tests pass 82 of 82.
- unitfeed: new fixtures `cityshot` (`a[3]` = 1) and `cityshotnoplot` (`a[3]` = 0), and `test_city_shot_replay_5062`.
  unitfeed gives `AnimRunner` **no height field and no fight placement** (it never calls `setGrid` / `fightPlacement`),
  so no fight is positioned there. The city is never placed (`centres 0, no centre 0`), its 5 hits route None, no flight
  is added, and the trigger logs of the two bundles are byte-identical on both arms. This also holds for unitfeed built
  from the code before W107 (`flights 0`). This limit applies to every unitfeed replay, not only to cities, and it is
  why the proof is in the units test. test_unitfeed passes 24 of 24.
- server.exe built (release, `keep/pins-0.1b` x64 1b87dd185 source; build only, not run).

**Still open (W107, 18:08; see 18.37.4 for what W108 closed):** the merge of main (5057, 0707, 0704), the full builders,
rule A, and the live pair. The pair answers whether the 0x29 lasting start plays its SoundEffect, and gives the first
look at the city projectile's size.

#### 18.37.5 Live: the plot was lost in `SrvFeed::PushCombat`; with that fixed route S plays the city shot (W108, 2026-11-23/24)

`[L]` c5h-b (EXE build 4390913, mods548), W94's `run_5058.py` unchanged, a copy of the Tiny T18 save, one case per prep,
Miles log named by `map_samples.py` on the pure_vp copy. Table: `server/evidence/0042/5062/w108/live_w108.txt`.

- **Era 1, layout eb1d5f3cd (server fac1fc74), 23:42-23:54.** Route S still played no `flamingarrowt2` or `arrowmiss`.
  The DLL-thread read worked (`server-report.txt`: `feed combats (5062): attacking city plots read 1, outside the grid 0`),
  but the server log said `units: city shot (5062): fight seq 302: city 0/1021 (plot -1) has no centre: NotFound: the
  feed gave no plot`.
- **Cause** `[C]`: `SrvFeed::PushCombat` (`server/src/feed/srv_feed.cpp`) set `e.a[3] = 0` on every combat event it
  kept, so kind 28 lost the plot between `OnCombat` and `AnimFeed::take`. W107's offline proofs built the events by hand
  (units test and unitfeed fixtures) and never went through `PushCombat`. The feed test even checked that a kind 28
  event's `a[3]` came out as 0. This is lesson 4 again: an offline case must enter by the product's own input path.
- **Fix** (5ad5aefae): `PushCombat` keeps the caller's `a[3]` for kind 28 and still zeroes it for kind 25, so kind 25 is
  unchanged. `test_feed.cpp` now expects the caller's value on kind 28 (77) and 0 on kind 25. `test_remote_feed.cpp`
  runs `OnCombat` with a positioned city stand-in through `PushCombat` and `Drain`: a[3] is 0 with no grid, and
  `y * w + x + 1` after a snapshot of 8 x 6. The City stand-in now models `GetX` / `GetY`. Before this, the suite had
  failed since W107 on an unmodelled call `ICvCity1::GetX`; W107 had not run it.

### 18.39 Projectiles drawn huge and pointing the wrong way: the held start's scale and orientation (W110, ticket 5064, 2026-11-23)

The owner's beta 3 report (2026-11-23 evening, beta 3 = main d56fbd94f, route S): projectiles such as an archer's arrow
or a city's thrown stone [reworded for privacy] intermittently come out massive and backwards, also when a defender shoots back in a melee fight.
Marks: `[C]` this worker's read of this repository's code on main 8de4539d1 (the same lines in d56fbd94f, checked with
`git grep`) or a count over recorded offline logs; `[L]` a live result of an earlier ticket, named; `[I]` reading.

**How a unit's projectile reaches the EXE** `[C]`. A clip's Effect trigger that a Transfer row names by `refid` (the
arrow in the hand) is not sent as an ordinary trigger: `EffectRoutes::startHeld` (`server/src/effects/srv_effect_routes.cpp`)
starts it through the emitter's API as a lasting effect. At the Transfer, `EffectRoutes::transfer` asks the planner
(`FightGeometry::plan`) for the flight and `addFlight` hands the held handle to the flight (`ProjectileSpec::start_effect`
false). From then on the flight sends only `EffectMove` records on that handle. A Transfer with no held effect waiting
plans no flight at all (`transfersNoHeld`), so **every unit projectile route S draws is a held start moved by its flight**.
The proxy's effect player keeps the start's scale for every later move (`proxy_effect_player.cpp` `DoMove` rebuilds only
the matrix; `PostPose` posts `e->scale` of the start), and `TriggerEmitter::moveEffect` carries no scale.

**The causes** (posted to lead-0042 #12202, 21:04):
- **C1, the scale** `[C]`. `startHeld` filled a `StartSpec` without a scale, so the start went out at `StartSpec::scale`'s
  default 1. The planner's `ProjectileSpec::scale` (the firing member's `Scale`, `effects-server.md` 2.4 `[L]`: 0.14 archer
  and swordsman, 0.12 catapult) is only used by a flight that starts its own effect, which a held flight never does. The
  emitter's ordinary trigger path takes `figureScale` (`srv_trigger_emitter.cpp`, the trigger effect start); `startHeld`
  bypassed it. So every unit projectile flew at 1.0: about 7x (arrow, 0.14) to 8x (rock, 0.12) stock's size.
  `effects-formats.md` 15.7.8 r5/r6 `[L]` had already shown the look: the arrow model at 1.0 "the length of a forest plot",
  at 0.12 "small, as stock's". Offline count `[C]` over the recorded `--effects` logs of W36 (2026-11-21, code of
  `startHeld` unchanged since 2026-11-20): all 16 moved projectile handles in five of 0557's fights (archer arrows, the
  catapult's rock, crossbow bolts, the thrown torch, boat arrows) start at scale 1 with the identity orientation
  (`server/evidence/0042/5064/flight_scales.py`).
- **C2, the orientation in the hand** `[C]`. `startHeld` asked `FigurePositions::bone` (a point) instead of `boneTransform`,
  so the held start carried the identity orientation. Between the Effect trigger and the Transfer (and for the whole held
  interval when no Transfer takes it: the trigger's duration, else `heldGrace` 0.5 s) the arrow hangs along the
  definition's own axis in a fixed world direction (15.7.8 r5 `[L]`: "it hangs along the identity orientation (the
  definition's -90 degrees about z only), not along the flight"), so for about half the facings it points away from the
  target, at scale 1. The flight's moves then carry the path frame (`pathFrame`, +y along the tangent).
- **C3, a launcher without a heading** `[C code; rate not counted yet]`. `FightGeometry::frameOf` took `FigurePose::yaw`
  without `yaw_known`; when the motion gives no heading (no target, no move and no opponent centre, or a 4742 reface) the
  yaw is 0, while the figure is drawn at its placement's heading. The planner then turns the Transfer's tangent by yaw 0
  (a fixed world direction) and the bone is posed at yaw 0: the launch direction and point from the wrong side.
- **C4, a city's volley** `[C code; stock value not read]`. `planHitEffect`'s `CityVolley` flies the era's `CITY_BOMBARD_*`
  and its children at scale 1.0 (15.7.8 open item 5). In beta 3 and on main no city volley is drawn at all (an attacking
  city has no centre, the route is None; 18.37.2 `[L]`), so the city projectile [reworded for privacy] the owner reported was a unit's flight [I]: a
  catapult's or trebuchet's `CATAPULT_ROCK_PROJECTILE` at a unit or a city, which is C1. C4 becomes live with 5062's city
  centre (18.37.3) and needs stock's value first.
- **C5** `[I]`: `ProjectileChildEffectScale` NULL is taken as 1.0 for the `ProjectileEnd` children (`projectile.h`); the
  EXE's NULL value was not read. **C6** `[I]`: the flight frame leaves out the EXE's stored local transform (+ 0xB0,
  `effects-server.md` 1.5 item 2): a constant turn of every flight, not an intermittent one.
- Why "intermittently" `[I]`: C1 applies to every drawn unit projectile; a held start refused as too late
  (`heldRefused`) gives no projectile at all; C2's backwards hang depends on the shooter's facing; arrows fly 0.1-1 s.

**The fix as built** (branch `w110-5064`, one product key `render_units_projectile_pose`, default 1; off = the rule before
5064 byte for byte): `RouteParams::projectilePose` (`srv_effect_routes.h`), carried by `TriggerStreamConfig::routes`,
`UnitsOptions::triggerProjectilePose`, the host key in `srv_render_host.cpp` (into every bundle's render_config;
sceneshot replays a bundle without it as 0: the projectiles are the EXE's effects, never a server pixel), unitfeed's and
trigger_scene's `--no-projectile-pose`, `run_trigger_scenes.py --no-projectile-pose`. With the key on:
- `startHeld` asks `boneTransform` (position and orientation, as `TriggerEmitter::transform` does for any trigger effect);
  a refused or non-finite transform falls back to the bone's point with the identity, as before; the start takes
  `figureScale` (the member's `Scale`; 1 when no member is known, counted).
- `FightGeometry::plan`: a launcher whose motion gives no heading faces its target (`yawFacing` of the launch-to-target
  direction), as a standing figure with a target does in `FightMotion::pose`; the bone pose itself is unchanged.
- Counters: `RouteCounters::heldBoneTransform / heldNoBoneTransform / heldScaleMember / heldScaleUnknown`,
  `GeometryCounters::figureYawUnknown / planYawUnknown / planYawToTarget`; in server.log's `units trigger 1s` line as
  ` pp=bone/nobone/member/one yaw=unknown/toTarget` (only with the key on), in trigger_scene as a `pose5064:` line.
- Test: `test_effect_routes.cpp` `testHeldPose5064` (on, off, a refused transform, a NaN orientation, no member scale, a
  member at 1; each checks the start's scale and orientation, that the flight moves the same handle and starts nothing
  else, and that off never asks for the transform).
- Offline count driver `server/evidence/0042/5064/run_5064_scenes.py` (trigger_scene `--geometry`: archers turned 0, 2
  and 3 facings away, composite bowman, crossbow, catapult, archer and catapult on a city, three melee fights where the
  defender shoots back; arms on / off / base; off must equal base byte for byte); builder pass
  `server/evidence/0042/5064/scripts/allb110.sh`; unitfeed identity `uf_identity110.py`.

**Built and counted offline** (W113, 2026-11-23 23:01-23:4x, branch `w110-5064` @b913a9493 against its merge base main
8de4539d1, Release through quietlock, no LTO; game files of the pure_vp copy, 0327's debug database) `[C]`:
- Everything compiled first time with the builders' own flags; `test_effect_routes` 394 of 394 (with `testHeldPose5064`), also under
  ASan (0 reports, peak 63 MB); `test_scene_units` 80/80, units fights, units extras 13/13, unitfeed pytest 23/23,
  emitter test OK; server.exe built (Release, the 0.1b pins).
- `run_5064_scenes.py`, 12 cases x 3 seeds x 3 arms (`server/evidence/0042/5064/w113/s5064_g1.log`, `.csv`): **RESULT

### 18.42 A move and its attack in one order: the fight starts before the walk arrives, the walk home goes to the plot left (W117, ticket 5066, 2026-11-24)

Written 2026-11-24 from 01:21 EST by w117-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w117-5066` from main 15bf0cb94. The owner's
beta 3 report (2026-11-23, build main d56fbd94f): once, after a route S fight, a mounted unit walked back to a plot two tiles
away from where it attacked from, then snapped to its own plot. Offline only so far (no instance). Marks: `[C]` code read
or run here, `[I]` reading. (The section number may be renumbered at the merge; 18.35-18.41 are on other branches.)

**Cause** `[C code; C offline run; I live]`:
- The core has one home. `Sim::walkHome` (4742, 18.18) walks each survivor to its start slot (`Fig::hx`, `hy`), set once
  from the start positions; the ride-through (5057, 18.29.1) and the reform never move it. A wrong home therefore means
  start positions taken on a plot other than the one the unit stands on after the fight.
- The start positions are `AnimRunner::m_placeIn`, the placement input of the frame before the fight, which for a unit a
  fight names is its frozen `HoldView` (6.1, 6.5).
- The DLL sends a move and its attack together: `CvUnit::UnitAttackWithMove` calls `PublishQueuedVisualizationMoves` and
  then `CvUnitCombat::Attack` (read in the DLL source, `CvUnit.cpp`); the mission timer between a move step and the attack
  step is 0 for the AI and 1-2 updates for a human (`CvUnitMission::CalculateMissionTimer`). So the kind 12 and the combat
  come in one drain, or a frame or two apart, while the EXE's walk of the move takes seconds.
- In mode exe (the product: `render_units_positions=exe`) a kind 12 does not move the view (6.1), the hold freezes the
  attacker where it was last drawn (the plot it left, or mid-walk), the EXE's arrival is held (kind `kHoldArrive`), and
  `FightClock` starts the fight in the next frame without waiting for the walk (6.4 left this open as a start rule;
  `merge_walk_held_fight` tests the freeze as intended). The whole fight is drawn from the plot left, the survivors walk
  home to it inside the fight, and at the OwnerEnd the view goes and the unit is drawn at the EXE's newest position, its
  real plot: the snap. Stock keeps `RunCombatSim` behind the unit's move records in its queue, so it fights from the
  arrival plot (0321 3.2).
- Mounted units have the moves for a two-plot move-and-attack, which fits the distance of two plots [reworded for privacy] the owner reported `[I]`.

**Before, on main** `[C: test_scene_units walkopen_*, 2026-11-24 01:37-01:39 EST, workstation, the pure_vp copy read
only; evidence server/evidence/0042/5066/w117/walkopen_before_main.txt]`. The cases (new
`server/tests/units/test_scene_units_walkopen.inc`) feed SrvFeed batches as the bridge sends them (kind 12 with its path,
the combat record, the damage, kind 6 positions and the arrival behind a frame mark) into `UnitsCore` in mode exe and run
the host's frame through `MotionRig` (the feed's close, the controller, the 4775 core, `FightPlacement`). `TestEnvCombat`'s
new `rush` option gives the warrior rows VP's mounted shape (RushAttackFormation 1, ShortMoveRadius 24, RunCharge without
AttackCharge): the test database has warrior art only. Distances are of the attacker's figure centroid, in world units
(plot spacing 64):

| case | start: from the plot left / after | home: from the plot left / after | settled on the plot after | largest step in one frame after the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| move 21->22->23 and attack in one drain, rush | 0.7 / 127.3 | 2.2 / 126.7 | 2.2 | **128.0** (two plots) |
| the same, foot row | 0.7 / 127.3 | 2.2 / 126.7 | 2.2 | **128.0** |
| the attack 2 frames after the move, rush | 0.7 / 127.3 | 2.2 / 126.7 | 2.2 | **128.0** |
| control: the walk arrives first, then the attack | 128.7 / 0.7 | 129.3 / 2.2 | 2.2 | 0.0 |
| fight B (move 23->34 and attack) queued behind fight A | 2.8 / 108.1 | 2.8 / 108.5 | 2.8 | **110.9** |
| kill and advance 23->24 (one drain) | 1.5 / 62.5 | 43.2 / 21.0 | 2.8 | **64.0** (one plot) |

- Fight B behind fight A is the same cause: the move between them comes back at A's end, the EXE walks only after A's
  OwnerEnd, and B starts in the next frame frozen on A's plot.
- **Kill and advance** (a second defect of the family, one plot): the victory figures (1800) do not walk home (as stock,
  18.18) and stand 43 units forward at the end; the view kept for the return holds the root on the attack plot while the
  after-end return glides them back there for about 1.5 s; the EXE's advance walk is hidden meanwhile, and when the return
  ends the view goes and the unit snaps 64 units onto the defender's plot (trace:
  `walkopen_trace_kill_advance_before.txt`). Cause `[C code]`: in `AnimFeed::fightsFrame` a mode-exe kind 12 that passes
  while the unit returns ends the return, one the hold gives back at the end does not. In stock the winner walks from where
  it stands onto the plot `[I]`.

**Fix direction** (lead-0042 #12565, decided): one mechanism as in stock. Ticket 5065 (W118) holds a unit's later ops
behind its open walk at the point where all of its ops pass; 5066 adds the mover's combat records to that held set under
its own knob (default on, off byte for byte, rule A host key), with the walkopen_* rows as the regression test. No
`FightClock` gate unless a row still fails. Not 5067's cause: its kn_kill cases (run_4779 `land_case(..., 1)`) start
adjacent, with no move.

**Part (b) as built** (lead-0042 #12574: the kill-advance snap folded into 5066) `[C: code; test_scene_units 2026-11-24
02:0x EST, 87 of 87 cases]`: `AnimFeed::fightsFrame`, after the ends of the frame: in mode exe, a kind 12 the hold gave back
at a fight's end (the winner's advance, a withdrawal) frees the unit's view kept for its walk back (`m_returning`), and the
runner's after-end walk goes on. The placement then follows the core's root (the plot left until the EXE's first
position, `UnitsCore`'s `fromPlot` rule, then the positions), so the figures walk from where they stand into the slots
of the EXE's walk. Counter `AnimCounters::returnsFreed`. Knob `AnimFeed::setFightAfterWalk` <- `UnitsOptions::
fightAfterWalk` <- host key `render_units_fight_after_walk` (default 1; written into every bundle's render_config;
sceneshot: absent = 0 and prints `units fight_after_walk N`; refused values in `test_render_host.py`, the default in
`test_recorder_host.py`, absent and "1" in `sceneshot_test.cpp`). Part (a) will sit behind the same key. Off: no state
changes (the rule before 5066). After, `walkopen_kill_advance` (on) against `walkopen_kill_advance_off`: largest step in
one frame **2.4** against 64.0 units, settled 2.8 on the plot after in both, `returnsFreed` 1 and 0; every other walkopen
row unchanged (evidence `walkopen_after_b.txt`).

**Part (a) as built** (W120 at the address w117-0042, 2026-11-24 from 01:53 EST; branch `w117-5066` with `w118-5065`
@453b6bf74 merged in) `[C: code; test_scene_units 2026-11-24 02:17 EST, 98 of 98 cases, plain, workstation, the pure_vp copy
read only; evidence server/evidence/0042/5066/w117/walkopen_after_a.txt]`. In ticket 5065's hold point
(`AnimFeed::holdBehindWalks`, unit-controller.md 20), under the same knob `render_units_fight_after_walk` (which also puts
kinds 25 and 28 in the hold's table; off: the table without them, no state touched, the rule before 5066 byte for byte):
- **What waits.** A combat record (kind 25 or 28; the unit is the record's attacker unit, never the op's `a[0]`/`a[1]`, which
  name a city for kind 28) waits in the queue of its attacker's walk when that walk is open (a kind 12 earlier in the batch
  or `m_walks`), or when a fight names the attacker and holds a kind 12 of it (`m_fightHeldMoves`, filled where the fights'
  hold answers Held for a kind 12, emptied when the hold gives it back or overflows): fight B behind fight A then waits for
  the walk that A's end opens, as in the EXE's queue (A, the move, B). A combat one of whose units already waits behind
  another combat goes into that combat's queue (feed order); given back, it is decided again.
- **The trap W117 found** (Op.combat indexes `m_combats`, which every close clears): the waiting op keeps its record in
  `m_afterWalkCombats` by seq (`combat = -2`); `giveBackAfterWalk` (the close's end, where 5065 puts given-back ops first)
  re-attaches it to `m_combats`, which fightsFrame has just emptied. A late combat result (4783) for a waiting record goes into
  the kept record (`applyLate`).
- **Feed order.** While a combat waits, every later op naming one of its units (attacker, defender, the unit members) waits
  behind it in the same queue (`m_fightTaint`), whatever its kind, so the defender's damage, death, removal or move come
  after the fight (`walkopen_feed` (a): the defender's move sent before the arrival comes out as `damage:2001,move:2001`
  at the fight's end). The attacker's own walk ends pass (the arrival, a teleport, a rebase, its removal, its creation);
  each ends the walk, which gives the queue back at the next close (5065's `endWalk`); F9's rule ends it by an arrive; a
  queue whose unit has no open walk and no fight naming it comes back at the close's end (5065's no-walk rule); a load
  drops waiting combats and the ops behind them (`fightWalkDropped`), as the fights' hold drops its own.
- **A unit behind two walks** (W125, 2026-11-24 04:55 EST, `[C: code; test_scene_units 99 of 99, plain, workstation]`).
  `m_fightTaint` keeps, per unit, every walk whose queue holds a waiting combat naming it (a set; before 04:55 one walk,
  the newest, replaced the older). An op of the unit, or a combat naming it, waits while any of those queues still waits
  (`AnimFeed::taintedQueue`: the first such walk); given back by one walk, it is decided again and waits behind the next.
  The own-walk-end rule passes when the unit's own walk is among them and still has a queue. Row `walkopen_two_walks`:
  A walks and attacks D (c1), B walks and attacks E (c2), then D attacks E (c3), one drain; A arrives first, B walks 20
  frames more. Before the fix c3 went into A's queue and took E's wait from B's: begun while B walked `[c1,c3]`, c3 ahead
  of c2 (stock keeps E's records in feed order). After: `[c1]` while B walks, then c1, c2, c3. Every other walkopen row
  gives the same numbers to the digit as the table below.
- **What is drawn meanwhile.** The attacker walks on the EXE's positions (not frozen). Every other unit of the waiting
  combat that does not walk keeps the view of the frame before (`HoldView::freeze` right after `beginFrame`, as a fight's
  begin), is relisted when the table drops it and is stepped by the runner (`AnimFeed::waitingFightUnits`, added to the
  units `fillFigures` steps beside the named and returning ones): without the stepping a defender killed in the same drain
  had no figures for the 47 frames of the walk (first run, 02:15). The view goes when no waiting combat names the unit and
  no fight owns it (`preFrozenFrame`; Quick Combat or a refused fight), and step (3) of fightsFrame keeps it meanwhile.
- **Timing.** The combat comes back at the close after the arrival's, the fight is added there and starts at the next
  close (the clock's frame-after start, section 4): 2 frames after the arrival (stock: `RunCombatSim` right after the move
  record `[I]`, not measured).
- Counters `AnimCounters::fightWalkHeld / fightWalkBehind / fightWalkDropped`, printed as ` fight_walk=H/B/D` after the
  5065 ` after_walk=` field of the units 1 s line while the table holds kind 25. unitfeed reads the key from scene.json
  (absent = 0, prints `unitfeed: fight after walk N`); `SceneUnits` sets the knob beside 5065's, outside the anim branch.

After, against the before table above (the `_off` rows give the before numbers again, equal to the digit):

| the same, foot row | 130.2 / 2.8 | 129.3 / 2.2 | 2.2 | **0.0** |
| the attack 2 frames after the move | 130.2 / 2.8 | 129.3 / 2.2 | 2.2 | **0.0** |

### 18.43 A city's ranged attack: no projectile, or a huge one (W136, ticket 0742, 2026-11-25)

The owner's beta 4 report (cut dc259f0b1, server 6c75d7fa..., proxy 48524398..., combat animations on): when New York
shoots, sometimes no projectile shows, sometimes drastically oversized ones. Written 2026-11-25 from 01:05 EST by
w136-0042, branch `w136-0742` from main 1821f5456. Marks: `[C]` this worker's read of this repository's code on main or a
headless Ghidra read of build 4390913 (runbook 3, no output kept, D83); `[L]` a live log named; `[I]` reading. This is a
fault of 5062's design (18.37.1-18.37.5), not a regression of 5064: 5064 changed held unit starts only.

**Fault 1, no projectile: the volley's flight is planned at its LANDING, with its start in the past** `[C, code; agrees
with 18.37.5's L timing]`:
- The core makes a city shot as a `Landing` at `Sim::cityVolley` (launch `t + k * city_stagger`, landing `launch +
  city_flight`, 0.6 s), but its `CombatHit` is pushed into `CombatResult::hits` only by `Sim::land`, at the landing.
  `AnimTriggerTap::fightHits` hands the hits over as the result grows, so the routes first see a city shot when it lands.
- `planHitEffect`'s `CityVolley` then sets the flight's `t0 = hit.launch` and `duration = hit.time - hit.launch` (0.6 s):
  the flight starts 0.6 s in the past. `EffectRoutes::hits` puts it pending at `t0`, `endFrame` applies it at once, and
  `ProjectileSet::frame` finds `el = now - t0 >= duration` on its first frame: it posts the lasting `EffectStart` at the
  path's start (the city's centre, `late` about 0.6 s) and in the same frame the landing's `ProjectileEnd` children. No
  `EffectMove` is ever sent: the projectile never travels. Whether one frame of it shows depends on the frame's
  alignment with the landing (el just under or over the duration) [I]: hence "sometimes".
- 18.37.5's live times show it: route S's shot sound at 1.536 s and its first landing at 1.539 s (3 ms), against stock's
  0.40 s flight; its era-3 shots and landings 0-9 ms apart.

**Fault 2, oversized: the city volley flies at scale 1.0** `[C, code]`: `planHitEffect` sets the flight's `scale` and
`child_scale` to 1.0 (a city has no member; 18.39's C4, 15.7.8 open item 5). `CITY_BOMBARD_EARLY` is the archer's arrow
model, which stock draws at the archer member's 0.14 (effects-server.md 2.4 `[L]`): at 1.0 about seven times stock's
length (15.7.8 r5 `[L]`: "tree-sized"). The never-moved lasting start of fault 1 also stays at the city's centre at 1.0 until
the fight's end stops it [I: not looked at live yet].

**Stock's city-volley scale, what the EXE read gave** `[C partial, build 4390913; addresses by name only, lead-0042
#13673]`: only two code sites post the EXE's projectile flight record (type 0x33, effects-server.md 1.1 step 7) and its
t = 0 start: the unit launcher of effects-server.md 1.1, and one event handler that the EXE's event system registers by
a function pointer (two registration functions name it). That handler copies the caller's start record whole (matrix,
owner key, name hash, **scale**) into the flight and sets its time field to a constant (likely 1.0 [I]); so if it is the
city's path, stock's scale is whatever the event's poster put in the start record, not read. The two `InitCityRangeStrike`
strings have no code reference. Not read further (time box): stock's value is open; the fix takes 0.14 (the archer
member's arrow scale, and the EXE's default `ProjectileChildEffectScale` 0.14, effects-server.md 1.1 item 1) [I] until
the live strip measures it. (Corrected 2026-11-25 by W145: measured live, the fixed arrow is stock's size within about
20 % at the same camera, 18.43.4 `[L]`; was "[I]" only.)

**The fix as built** (branch `w136-0742`, one product key `render_units_city_volley`, default 1; off = the rule before
0742 byte for byte) `[C, code; not yet compiled or run at 01:29]`:
- Core (additive): `CombatResult::launches`, one `CombatHit` per city shot made at `Sim::cityVolley` (time = its planned
  landing, launch, the city's origin, `pos` = the aimed figure where it stands at the launch, `shot` = its index);
  `CombatHit::shot` (-1 default) carries the same index on the landing's hit.
- `AnimTriggerTap::fightRun` hands new launches to `EffectRoutes::launches` before the hits. With the key on each launch
  is planned by the same `planHitEffect` (now with `HitPlanParams::city_scale` / `city_child_scale` from
  `RouteParams::cityVolleyScale` / `cityVolleyChildScale`, 0.14 / 0.14) and applied at its launch, so the flight travels
  its 0.6 s and lands with the core's landing; the landing's hit with a flown `shot` adds nothing (`hitCityVolleyFlown`).
  A launch that cannot be planned (no centre, no name) is counted (`cityLaunchNotFlown`) and the landing routes as before.
- Counters in server.log's `units trigger 1s` line as ` cv=launches/flown/notFlown/landingsFlown`, only once a city has
  shot. Host key in `srv_render_host.cpp` (into every bundle's render_config; sceneshot reads absent as 0, the
  projectiles are the EXE's effects, no server pixel), `UnitsOptions::triggerCityVolley`, unitfeed and trigger_scene
  `--no-city-volley`; trigger_scene hands the core's launches to the routes as the tap does.
- Test: units case `fight_city_flight` gains a `pre0742` arm (key off) and counts the routes' start, move and child
  records: on, every launch is flown once and moves at least 10 times (0.6 s at 30 frames a second: about 18); off, the
  same flights each start and land with at most one move.

#### 18.43.1 Fault 3: route S disarmed by the fight clock's seq rule after a walk-held combat (W138, 2026-11-25)

**Branches** (2026-11-25 02:10): the beta 4 hotfix branch `w138-0742-hotfix` (from main) carries only this fault 3 fix
and its tests; the fix of faults 1 and 2 above (the city volley key) stays on `w138-0742` until its build and live check.

The owner's real game (Steam build 26577625, beta 4 cut dc259f0b1, the owner's options; run folder
20261124-235235-46664-1, a copy read only) wrote a D119 report at 01:22:00: `route-s-watchdog`, the hold dropped fight
event id 437649 by its outer bound (never started by the server) after 22000 ms, and route S disarmed for the rest of
the process. From then on every fight, New York's shots included, plays the EXE's own way, and the EXE's projectiles are
not seen [I: the composite hides the EXE's unit layer while the server draws the units]: the other half of "no
projectile". Written 2026-11-25 from 01:52 EST by w138-0042, branch `w138-0742`.

- **What the logs show** `[L, the owner's logs]`: vpproxy.log at 5343.21 s (01:21:38) takes ids 437649 (queue position
  0, bound 22000 ms) and 437664 (position 1) on the same thread in the same millisecond; neither is ever started. The
  server's log, 1.2 s later (01:21:40.642 / .666 in render.log): `the fight clock refused a combat record: combat seq
  505501 not above the last one added (505613): fights start in the DLL's call order`, and the same for seq 505507. No
  other refusal of this kind in the session; `fights=30` stays unchanged from 01:21:34 to the end. At 5365.21 the
  outer bound drops 437649 and route S disarms; 437664 is released by the disarm. The units totals give
  `fight_walk=21/166/0` (21 combats held behind a walk, 166 ops behind them, none dropped) for the session.
- **Cause** `[C, code read of main 1821f5456; consistent with the logs]`: ticket 5066 (a) (`AnimFeed::holdBehindWalks`)
  keeps a combat whose attacker's walk is open in `m_afterWalkCombats` and lets every op that names none of its units
  pass on, a later combat of other units included; that one is added to the fight clock at once.
  `FightClock::add` refused any record with `seq <= lastSeq_` (a rule of 4782, from before 5066, "fights start in the
  DLL's call order"). When the walk ended, `giveBackAfterWalk` gave the waiting record back below the last seq and
  `add` refused it: no fight, nothing held, and no OwnerEnd (only a fight the clock holds ends with one). The shell's
  hold for its event id waited for the outer bound. Here seq 505613 was a later combat that the clock took as a record
  without a fight (not visualised: `fights` did not grow), while 505501 and 505507 (two visualised combats of the same
  drain, held behind a walk) came back after it.
- **Load is not the cause** `[L, the owner's logs]`: the render log has its 1 s lines every second through 01:21:38-01:22:00
  (`pass 1s`: 70-130 passes a second, `long` 0 except one second with 1 after 01:21:40), so the server's render thread was not starved; the 20 s gap in server.log is the
  units trigger line being printed only when it changes. The log writer's "slowest write 21997.2 ms" (ticket 5054) is an
  asynchronous writer's figure and stopped no thread [I: when it happened is not logged]. B's scene-bundle programs of
  01:10-01:27 on the workstation therefore did not starve the hold.
- **Fix** (`w138-0742`): `CombatIn::resumed` marks a record that `giveBackAfterWalk` gives back; `FightClock::add(...,
  resumed)` takes such a record below the last seq (counted `resumedBelow`; the last seq stays), and still refuses it when
  it equals the last seq or a fight of its seq is held. A record that is not resumed is refused as before, so with
  `render_units_fight_after_walk` 0 (nothing waits) the clock is the rule before 0742. No new key: the change is part of
  5066's after-walk wait. Tests: `test_units_fights.cpp` testRefusals (resumed 7 below 11 taken once, a repeat and a held
  seq refused, the last seq unchanged); units cases `walkopen_later_combat_first` (c1 behind A's walk, c2 of other units
  added at once; after A's arrive both fights start, c2 first, `combatsRefused` 0, `resumedBelow` 1; before the fix c1 is
  refused) and `_off` (no wait, both in feed order).
- **Still open:** a refused record of any other kind still leaves its hold to the watchdog (no OwnerEnd for a record
  without a fight); not met in the logs, so not changed here [I].
- **Did the city volley's hand-over (faults 1, 2) leave a hold that never starts?** (MC-B's question, #13737) No
  `[L, the owner's logs]`: every other take of the session ends by OwnerEnd (30 of 32), the two LOUD ones as "the
  server could not play this fight" (server.log: refused by the choreography, BadEvent, the attacker not held); the only outer-bound drop is 437649 above.

### 18.44 Melee attackers ran much further forward than stock: stock's reach and target, `CombatParams::melee_reach` (W137, ticket 0743, 2026-11-25)

Written 2026-11-25 01:15-02:30 EST by w137-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w137-0743` from main 2ffd65fc4. The
owner's beta 4 report (cand6, combat animations on) [reworded for privacy]: melee attackers moving forward go much further
than in the stock game. Marks: `[C]` a read-only headless Ghidra pass on a scratch copy of the analysis project
(old build 4390913 only, runbook 3's Ghidra line; addresses and behaviour only, no decompiler text in git, D83, D202) or
this repository's code and offline runs; `[L]` W91's live stock sampler lines (18.33) re-read; `[I]` a reading.

**Stock's rule** `[C]`:
- **The reach.** The target step (0x5C7100) sends a melee figure (figure flag 0x100, `HasShortRangedAttack`, clear)
  whose target is a figure to strike (state 10) when its distance to that figure is at most the sum of its member's
  `AttackRadius` (combat record + 0x0C, 5.1 M1) and the target member's `AttackRadius`: **8 + 8 = 16 world units** with
  VP's defaults (no melee row sets `AttackRadius`). Farther away it charges (0xC, 1120). A figure whose target is a
  slot of the target participant (participant word flag 0x100: the rush formation's slots, the riders) is instead
  stopped by the charge pass (0x6902C0 case 0xC) within its `MoveRadius` (in phase 3 with figure flag 0x8000: its
  `AttackRadius`) of the slot, or when it has passed the slot's line along the participant's direction (+ 0x2B78),
  which is 5.1 M2's "target line".
- **The target.** A melee figure's target comes from the chooser dispatch 0x70D630, kind 2 (no flag 0x100) =
  0x6F8DC0: over the opponent's living figures (not flagged 0x4000214), first those not yet claimed (a bit per figure
  the per-frame pass 0x5EFC50 sets when it gives a figure as a target), then the claimed ones, it keeps the **nearest**
  (squared distance, with the projection on the opponent's direction as a second test); a figure beyond its
  `AttackRadius` whose straight path is blocked (0x421A90) is kept only as a fallback. 0x5EFC50 asks again when the
  path test fails. So a stock melee figure runs at the figure in front of it and stops 16 units short.
- **Route S before this ticket** `[C code]`: `Sim::pickTarget` drew the target at random among the least-struck
  candidates, and with `DeathPick::LastFirst` (the default) the candidates are the doomed figures, the last by index =
  the rear ranks of the defender's formation; `Sim::moveTo` ran each figure to `MoveRadius` (3.5) of that figure. Its
  runners crossed the defender's whole formation.

**The numbers** (foot type 2 attacks, per attacking figure, its first charge; world units; Swordsman, Spearman,
Warrior, Longswordsman attackers on Swordsman, Warrior, Lancer defenders; `[L]` stock = W91's 12 foot fights on c5h-b,
build 4390913, 144 figures; route S = the offline core with positions, `--live`, seed 1, the 6 foot cases of
`cases_w137.sh`, the server's `type2_phase2` on, 28 runners):

| Arm | first charge median / p90 / max | its time median / p90 | where it ends | foot fight length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock `[L]` | 20.1 / 34.5 / 43.1 | 0.518 / 0.800 s | strikes at 12-16 from the nearest defender figure (p10 7.0, median 13.6, p90 15.7; 76 strike entries) | 4.785 s (18.33) |
| route S main (`melee_reach` off) `[C]` | **62.4 / 67.6 / 77.8** | 1.247 / 1.353 s | 3.5 from its target, inside the defender's formation | 4.611 s (mean of 6) |
| route S fix (`melee_reach` on) `[C]` | **22.3 / 31.2 / 38.3** | 0.446 / 0.623 s | 16.0 from the nearest standing defender figure | 3.261 s |

So the difference the owner saw is **+42 units at the median** (about 360 px at 18.32's 8.5 px per unit) and +34 at the
max: route S's foot attackers ran three times as far as stock's, and twice as long. Mounted (Knights, rush members):
route S 61.3 median against stock 60.8 `[L]`, unchanged by the fix. A melee on a city: no move in either (stock 18.21,
route S `city_in_place`).

**The fix** (`CombatParams::melee_reach`, on by default; off = the rule before byte for byte; server key
`render_units_melee_reach`, default 1, written into every bundle's render_config, sceneshot reads absent as 0, rule A):
an attacking land figure of a member without `RushAttackFormation`, in a melee attack, (a) takes the nearest of its
candidates as its target instead of a random one, and (b) stops where its straight run first comes within the two
`AttackRadius` values (`CombatMotion::attack_radius`, read from `ArtDefine_UnitMemberCombats`, default 8.0) of any
standing opponent figure; a figure already within that reach does not move. Riders, ships, aircraft, ranged attacks and
city targets are unchanged. **Named difference** `[I]`: under `LastFirst` the struck figure is still a doomed one, which
may stand behind the figure the attacker stopped at; stock kills the figure it struck. Changing that needs the death
rule `Targeted` and the server's figure identity after the fight (5.2), not this ticket.

**What it costs** `[C offline]`: route S's foot fights get **1.35 s shorter** (4.61 -> 3.26 s) and now end about 1.5 s
before stock's 4.79 s. The long run had hidden that route S lacks stock's phase 4: after the first landing stock's
defender figures step forward to meet the attackers (18.33 (a): mean 14, up to 37 units in the `melee` fight) and the
attackers charge again (25 charge entries for 12 figures). That is ticket 5061's ground (backlog). Also not here: stock
starts all 12 attacking figures in phase 3 and stops those its gate does not need (state 1); route S moves only the
figures holding a strike (5 of 12 in `melee`).

**Tests** `[C]`: `render/tests/units/test_fight_motion.cpp`: `melee_reach_stops_at_the_two_attack_radii_of_the_nearest_figure`
(on: every first run ends 16.0 from the nearest standing defender figure, at least 12.5 shorter than off; off: 3.5 from
its target; `AttackRadius` 4 + 6 gives 10), `melee_reach_targets_the_nearest_candidate` (a kill: the first runner heads
at the nearest defender figure), `melee_reach_leaves_riders_and_ships_alone` (a rush member and a ship: on equals off).
The older approach tests that measure MoveRadius set `melee_reach = false`. Server: `test_render_host.py` (bad values),
`test_recorder_host.py` (the key in render_config, its "0" arm), `sceneshot_test.cpp` (absent = 0, "1", "0").

**Files and commands:** `server/evidence/0042/0743/w137/`: `stock_charge_w137.py` (W91's raw lines, outside git, per
figure charge start, end, time, end distance), `cases_w137.sh` (the offline cases, both arms; `EXTRA=--type2-phase2`),
`route_charge_w137.py` (per case), `route_first_w137.py` (pooled first moves and fight ends). Offline runs:
`python -I perf/quietlock/quietlock.py run --who <t> --what combat_scene -- python render/build.py --config Release
--target c5r_unitanim_combat_scene --build-dir <rb>`, then `DB=<db copy> GAME=<4390913 install copy> EXTRA=--type2-phase2
bash server/evidence/0042/0743/w137/cases_w137.sh <rb>/tests/unitanim/c5r_unitanim_combat_scene.exe <out>` (20 runs,
seconds) and `route_first_w137.py <out>`. `combat_scene` gained `--no-melee-reach` and `--type2-phase2`.

### 18.45 Type 2 after the first landing: stock's defender steps in, both sides walk home inside the simulation; the design of `CombatParams::defender_step` (W139, ticket 5061, 2026-11-25)

Written 2026-11-25 from 01:57 EST by w139-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w139-5061` from main 39e736026. Offline only
so far (a full hold on the workstation: no build, no instance). Builds on 18.44 (0743, `melee_reach`, branch `w137-0743`,
not merged when this was written). Marks: `[L]` W91's live stock sampler lines (18.33: c5h-b, EXE build 4390913, stamp
0x546CD0A8, Tiny turn 18, 24 type 2 fights, both launches; raw lines outside git, MC #10264:
`F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w91/sim-w91-1.jsonl` sha256 8bee6ed8..., `sim-w91-2.jsonl` b6d75e41...) re-read here with new
readers; `[C]` this repository's code; `[I]` a reading. No EXE code was read for this section (D83): the behaviour is
the sampler's states and positions and 18.15 / 18.44's existing reads. Readers (`server/evidence/0042/5061/w139/`):
`defstep_w139.py` (phase 4 per figure: each defender figure's forward step along the line between the two sides' start
centroids, its 0xC spans and where each ended against the nearest attacker figure; the attackers' 0xC spans after the
first), `endwalk_w139.py` (each survivor's release, its 0xB walk, its distance from its own start at 7 and at the
removal), `centroid_w139.py` (each side's survivor centroid at the removal against its start; each survivor's distance to
the nearest start position of its side); outputs `defstep_w139.txt`, `endwalk_w139.txt`, `centroid_w139.txt`; the
per-figure dumps stay local, as W122's did. Commands: `bash server/evidence/0042/5061/w139/run_offline_w139.sh` (seconds). "Foot" = the 12 fights
of Swordsman, Spearman, Warrior and Longswordsman attackers (the two `kill` cases named apart where they differ);
"mounted" = the 12 Knight fights.

**(1) Phase 4: where the two sides meet** `[L]`. Phase 4 starts at the attacker's first landing (18.15; foot 1.23-1.57 s,
rf_lancer 2.93 s, mounted 2.77-3.03 s on the simulation's clock).
- **The defender steps in at once.** A foot defender figure goes 1 -> 0xC (run charge) 0.067 s after phase 4 starts
  (median; p90 0.133; 86 figures, two 33 ms position samples), 77 of 130 foot defender figures move more than 2 units
  towards the attacker (8 or 9 of 12 per full-strength fight; in `kill`, whose defender is all but dead, 1 of 24). Each
  figure's furthest forward step: median 7.3 / p90 27.2 / p95 30.1 / max 40.5 units (all foot fights). **109 defender 0xC
  spans** in the 12 foot fights (two per moving figure is common: a charge, a stop in 1 or a strike in 10, a second
  charge), run median 10.0 / max 42.4 units, at about 50 units per second (34.4 units in 0.70 s), ending **16.8 units**
  (median; p10 9.7, p90 27.0) from the nearest attacker figure. That is 18.44's reach, the two `AttackRadius` values
  (8 + 8), applied to the defender: stock's target step treats both sides alike once both strike. Figures already within
  reach strike where they stand (`melee` run 1: figures 7 and 9 go 1 -> 10 with no move).
- **Mounted:** the defender's 0xC spans run median 0.4 units (100 spans): the riders strike on the defender's plot, so
  nearly every defender figure is already within reach; a few figures step up to 27.6 units (p95 21.8).
- **A rush defender does not step:** rf_lancer (Longswordsmen on a Lancer): 0 defender 0xC spans in phase 4 (its figures
  moved only in its reform before, `ReformBeforeCombat` 2).
- **The attacker re-charges:** 170 attacker 0xC spans after each figure's first in the 12 foot fights (about 14 per
  fight), run median 8.3 / max 41.4 units, ending median 22.4 from the nearest defender figure (the defender moves too).
  Mounted: 1 in 12 fights.

**(2) The end: both sides walk home inside the simulation** `[L]`; *this corrects 18.33 (b)'s reading*. Every survivor of
both sides, foot and mounted, enters 0xB (none goes straight to 7). Foot attacker (91 survivors, kills apart): at its
release median 33.0 units from its own start (p90 45.4); 0xB lasts median 0.533 s (max 0.733) and it runs median 25.9
units (max 39.7); at 7 it stands 15.8 units from its own start (p90 27.3) but only **5.1 units** (p90 9.3) from the
nearest start position of its side: it runs back **into its unit's formation**, not to its own start slot. The side's
survivor centroid stands **7.9 units** forward of its start at the removal (max 14.8); the foot defender's 11.6 (max
16.8), its survivors 5.6 from the nearest start position. Release -> removal: foot **0.667 s** (median; 0.633-0.768 in
the 12 fights), mounted 1.966 s (riders' 0xB median 1.77 s over 61 units). Kills: the attacker advances (`kill` centroid
66.6 units forward, the plots are 64 apart; `kn_kill` 53.9), the defender has no survivor. So in stock's foot type 2 the
attacker is **not** kept forward until the removal: it is home within about 5 units per figure. What 18.33 (b) read as
"kept forward" is its 0xB run under way inside the short walk window (W90's walk kind is the frames from the first
finished figure to the removal; foot 0.67 s, so its median catches the run in mid-way) plus that residual. What stock
draws after the removal (the last 5 units per figure, the centroid's 8-12 units) is not in any record: the sampler stops
at the removal `[I: the clip and the time are open]`.

**Route S before 5061** `[C code, w137-0743 bd36ca595]`: only an attacker approaches (`Sim::look`'s approach block is for
`Role::Attacker`); a type 2 defender waits until the first landing (5057 (B) `defenderHeld`) and then strikes **from where
it stands** with no move, whatever the distance (its hit lands on its target anyway); only figures holding a strike
(`pickTarget` under the side's need and `max_in_flight`) look, the rest stand in combat ready; 4742's `walk_home` walks
each survivor of a placed participant to its rank's start slot inside the fight, which ends at the last arrival.
18.33's route S defender strike p95 is 2.6 units against stock's 15.3.

**What is missing from stock's record, and why no new stock run is planned for the design** `[I]`:
- What stock draws after the removal (above). It is small (about 5 units per figure, under 0.1 s of a run) and only
  the pose sampler of `unit-formations.md` 12.2 (a game, the D3D palettes) could see it; not proposed.
- A stock sampler on build 26577625 does not exist (D202: no address of that build in anything committed; 0743's note).
  W91's `[L]` on 4390913 stays the reference: what is measured is the simulation's per-figure rule (phases, reach,
  target), which an EXE build changes only if the combat code changed; 0743's stock strip on the new build (MC #13779)
  is the visual check on 26577625 for both tickets.

**The design** (posted to lead-0042 for an OK before code):
- **D1 `CombatParams::defender_step`** (on by default, stock's; off = the rule before byte for byte): in a type 2 fight
  (`type2_`), from the attacker's first landing (`att_landed_`), a defender figure that answers, of a land member
  without `RushAttackFormation`, not a ship or a flyer, with both sides placed, (a) takes the nearest candidate as its
  target (18.44's nearest rule: `Sim::reaches` widened to it), (b) runs to it as an attacker does under `melee_reach`:
  `moveTo` with the two `AttackRadius` values, cut at the first standing opponent figure within that reach, the
  attacker's clip rule (1120 with `RunCharge` and its charge art, else 1400; the 1450 shuffle inside `ShortMoveRadius`),
  then combat ready and the strike as an arriving attacker; a figure within reach strikes where it stands, as now;
  (c) a defender figure without a strike to hold steps to that reach of the nearest standing attacker figure that is not
  walking home and waits there in combat ready, again whenever that figure is out of reach (stock moves 8-9 of 12; with
  (a)-(b) only, route S would move the 4-5 figures holding a strike and the side's centroid would stay short of 15.3).
- **D2, the walk home: no new rule first.** With D1 the stepped defender figures walk home by 4742's `walk_home` too
  (stock's defenders do: 0xB median 0.40 s). Target: release -> end foot 0.667 s [0.633-0.768], the side's centroid
  near its start. Only if route S's walk then lasts more than 0.1 s longer than stock's: a knob
  `walk_home_stop_radius` that ends the in-fight walk within stock's residual (5 units) and leaves the rest to
  `FightMotion`'s after-end walk (counted by `residualWalks`).
- **Not in 5061** (named; lead-0042 #13806: stays out, a child ticket if the MC wants it): stock starts all 12
  attacking figures in phase 3 (18.44, "Also not here"), route S only those holding a strike; D1 (c)'s rule would carry
  over to the attacker's figures without a strike as a separate knob. A kill's advance is unchanged (the DLL's move
  after the combat).
- **Approved** by lead-0042 #13806 (2026-11-25 02:09): D1 (a)-(c) as written, key default 1, off byte for byte, D255 no
  options-file key; D2 as written.
- **As coded** `[C code, w139-5061b 23f9f5f20; not built yet: the workstation's full hold]`: `CombatParams::defender_step`
  (true) and `defender_step_slack` (1.0 world unit: (c) moves only when the nearest attacker figure is beyond the reach
  by more than it, so a figure stopped at its reach's edge does not shuffle); `Sim::steps` (the rule's test:
  `type2_`, `att_landed_`, the defender's land non-rush figure, both sides placed); `Sim::reaches` returns true for
  such a figure too, so `pickTarget`'s nearest rule and `moveTo`'s reach and cut (18.44) apply; `Sim::look`'s approach
  block takes the stepping defender beside the attacker; `Sim::stepIn` is (c): after a failed pick, the nearest attacker
  figure that has made its approach (`engaged`; route S's attackers without a strike stay home, and stock's defenders
  run at a figure in front of them, so a defender never runs into the attacker's home ranks), standing and not
  returning, is the move's destination through `moveTo` with no target kept (no strike, no claim); its arrival looks
