### 18.46 Route S knights play almost no attack vox since 5057: the riders never strike after the ride (W150, W151, ticket 5071, 2026-11-25)

Written 2026-11-25 from 07:43 EST by w150-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w150-5071` from main 9de049b0c. Offline
only so far (no instance). Inputs read only: W101's 5057 (c) sound tables with 3D positions (`origin/w101-5057c`,
`server/evidence/0042/5057/w101/S33|S34/sounds_S3x.txt`: S33 route S with 5057, S34 stock, the same dice), W79's S28 stock
table (`server/evidence/0042/5057/sounds-S28.txt`), W147's vox table (18.36.4), and **W91's stock sampler records**
(`F:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w91/sim-w91-1.jsonl`, outside git; 18.29.3 and 18.33 describe it: per figure its state and
flags each 2 ms pass). Marks: `[C]` route S's code on main 9de049b0c or run offline here, `[L]` those live records, `[I]`
this section's reading. **Status: cause found (W150); fixed by W151, offline and live results below; rule A and phases 2 / x of the builders pending at the time of writing.**

**Cause** `[C code, L]`. (1) `Sim::rideLand` (5057 (A), `render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp`) lands each rider's hit at its
arrival with code 1120 and no attack clip, so no swing and no vox. That matches stock's ride deaths: in S28 and S34 every
death during the ride is the victim's `swordflesh` + `deathvoxa` with no swing and no attack vox at the rider `[L]`.
(2) After the ride a stopped rider (`Fig::rode`, Wait with 1000) looks again only through `Sim::look` -> `Sim::targetPart`,
which gives a target only while the defender's `open()` (planned - died + owed - paid - reserved) is above 0. The ride
landings pay every planned death of the defender within 0.8-1.6 s offline (kn-kill seed 1: four landings, four deaths),
so no rider strikes again; the fight is then held only for the attacker's own planned death (the knight the Spearman's
answer kills) and ends at it. Hence 0 rider attack clips and 0 rider attack vox in wh_knight and wh_knight_pike, and in
kn_kill / kn_kill_b only the Spearman's one (`attackvoxa`, the defender's single 1100 in the controller timeline) `[C, L
S33]`. No rider attack is lost to the tier gate or the emitter.

**Stock** `[L]`. Every knight attack vox (`attackvoxh`) comes AFTER the ride, with a `swordswing` at the same moment at a
rider's position (then `swordrattle` +0.06 s, `armourmove` +0.1 s, a second swing up to +0.17 s), 0.3-1.8 s after the
first ride death and before the fight's last death; no `horsefootdirt` (1440) and no 1600 entry sound comes before the
walk home. Rider `attackvoxh` per case: W101 S34 wh_knight 4, wh_knight_pike 5, kn_kill 1, kn_kill_b 4; W79 S28 kn_kill
1, kn_kill_b 4; the rest of stock's attack vox class is the Spearman's `attackvoxa` (kn_kill 2, kn_kill_b 2). The
spread between stock launches on the same dice is wide (W147's S34 kn_kill_b: 1 attack vox in all, W101's S34: 6).
W91's sampler (same Tiny cases, stock, `seq91.py` in the work folder) shows the order per rider: all riders stay in the
charge state 0xC through the ride while the defender's deaths are played (wh_knight: 6 of 7 planned by 2.77 s; kn_kill
4 of 5, wh_knight_pike 4 of 5, kn_kill_b 4 of 5), some go to 3 (standing) on arrival; at phase 4 (2.77-2.97 s) every
rider goes to 1 (looking) and riders in reach go to 0xA (state 10, the strike) while the defender still has a planned
death open (kn_kill f1 at 3.60 s, kn_kill_b f1 and f2 at 3.00 s), then 0x10 / 0xB at the end. So **stock pays only part
of the defender's deaths in the ride and the rest by strikes after phase 4; route S pays all of them in the ride**. By
0321 5.2 state 10 a strike asked right after the charge (last action 1120) is a 1140, which the mounted machine takes
from its run loop with no stop (unit-controller.md 2: 17 -> 14 on 1140), which fits the missing 1440 / 1600 sounds `[I]`.

**Why 1100 from the run cannot work, and why 1140 does** `[C: the mounted machine 1_omni_mounted_state_01.fsmxml and
fx_triggers_knight.ftsxml as copied by 4402's logicfiles.py, outside git; W151, 2026-11-25]`. In the mounted machine the
run loop (17) tests 1100 only on its socket to 9 STOP_RUNNING, and that socket sets path 6 = 0 for every code it takes
(1000, 1500, 1160, 1180, 1100, 1600); 9 leaves to 1 (idle) on the 1440 clip's end with path 6 = 0, and 1 goes to 8
ENTER_COMBAT_READY on 1100. So a 1100 asked of a rider in its run plays the whole 1440 stop, then the 1600 entry, then
the attack: exactly W150's variant (b) (3.3-3.9 s late, `HORSE_FOOT_DPMT`, `SWORD_SHEATH`, `FORTIFY_VOX_H`). The run
loop's only attack socket is 17 -> 14 ATTACKS on 1140 (path 1 = 2, the request consumed), with no stop and no entry. The
knight's 1140 clip carries `ATTACK_VOX_H` at 0.315 s and `SWORD_SWING` at 0.326 s (Action at 0.370 s; horse run at
0.030 and 0.511 s); its 1100 clip `ATTACK_VOX_H` at 0.298 s and `SWORD_SWING` at 0.370 s. Stock's state 10 asks 1140
"when the last action was 1120 run charge and 1120 is enabled" (combat-choreography.md 5.2 [C]): the test names
RunCharge, not AttackCharge, so the EXE asks 1140 of a knight right after its charge. Stock's S34 swings lean that way: of
kn_kill_b's four rider `attackvoxh` (W101 S34), two have their `swordswing` in the same 1/30 s, one 0.10 s later and one
none (1140: 0.011 s apart; 1100: 0.072 s) `[L, I]`. After 14 the machine goes back to combat ready by itself (14 -> 20 -> 12), where 1100 is taken directly (12 -> 14).
The server's bridge refused 1140 for a member whose EnableActions lack `AttackCharge` (`BadEvent`, unit-controller.md
14.1; VP's knight row has RunCharge without AttackCharge); what the EXE's word mask does with 1140 is not read [I], the
state-10 rule and the sounds say it is taken.

**The fix** `[C: render/src/unitanim/combat.cpp, bridge.cpp, branch w150-5071 from 959edda2d]`, in
`CombatParams::ride_strikes_while_held` (default on; off = 5057's rule byte for byte; no player key, a parity fix), for
a rush rider of the attacker without AttackCharge, with RunCharge and a 1140 clip, at a figure unit (`Sim::runStrikes`):
1. a ride landing never pays the defender's last planned death, nor do the extra struck figures of a VisKillStrength
   landing (`Landing::keep_last`): the rider whose arrival would pay it strikes its reserved target with 1140 from its
   run instead (`Sim::keepsLast`, `Sim::runStrike`; stock's 4 of 5 and 6 of 7 in the ride);
2. a rider standing after its ride while the defender still has a planned death or an owed hit open (`need() > 0`)
   strikes the nearest standing defender figure with no reservation (`Sim::heldStrike`): 1140 when still in its run
   (riding on in its 1120 when out of reach, the strike at the arrival), 1100 from combat ready after its own strike
   (`combat_ready` is set by the run strike: no 1600 request); in combat ready and out of reach it stands. A landing
   kills only a planned death (0321 13.4), so each side's deaths are those of 5057;
3. `strikeCode` returns 1140 for such a run strike (`Fig::run_strike` after a 1120);
4. the bridge takes 1140 from a member whose EnableActions carry RunCharge (`ActionBridge::requestsFor`);
5. live, a run strike is asked only when the controller says the figure's machine takes it (`Sim::takes`, the
   controller's `accepts`): a rider at its arrival holds `charge_wait` (0.5 s) at most and then lands as 5057's rider;
   a held strike in reach that the machine does not take is not started (the rider stops). Found on the first offline
   run (W151, 08:29): in knb-kill a rider back in combat ready after its 1140 made a short 1120 move (0.03 s) to the last
   Spearman and asked 1140 while its machine was still in START_RUNNING (4): the request never played, the strike's
   clock waited for the clip (`live_wait`) and the fight held to the 12 s limit in all three seeds.
W150's variants (a) a81ba26d1 and (b) c6e05cc35 are replaced (not merged). Tests: `test_combat`

### 18.47 A fight span replayed offline unlike live: sceneshot ignored the unit position source (W157, ticket 5070, 2026-11-25)

Written 2026-11-25 from 10:18 EST by w157-0042 (team-0042, account B), branch `w157-5070` from main 2b4c93846. The case:
18.43.3's overtaking bundle `C5H-0742-OVERTAKE_0009_20261125-041228_workstation` fails sceneshot's offline-equals-live
(exit 10) from frame 1525 (1.7 s after the orders) to 1875 on the two fighting pairs only, the same figures in another
idle pose after both fights.
- **Cause [C]** (code read offline; both replay logs of W142's arms): the bundle's `scene.json` records
  `render_units_positions = exe`. server.exe takes it through `ParseHostConfig` (`srv_render_host.cpp`, `g_unitsPositions`);
  `MakeLive` (`server/src/units/srv_units_scene.cpp`) sets `UnitsOptions::positionsExe` from it, and `SceneOpts` copies it
  into `SceneOptions::unitsPositions` for the mode writer. sceneshot's `OptionsFromBundle`
  (`server/tools/sceneshot/sceneshot.cpp`, a port of `SceneOpts`) copied every units key but this one and
  `render_units_ready_hold_ms`, and builds its unit scene with `MakeSceneUnitsWith` directly (not `MakeLive`), so the
  offline scene ran in **mode own**: its log says `units mode: the unit scene is ready but the position source is own
  (render_units_positions=own)`, while unitfeed on the same bundle (which reads the key since 4755) says `position source
  exe (scene.json)`. In mode own the server roots and times every walk itself (0375's rule) instead of following the
  EXE's kind-6 position and arrival records, and the 0042 rules that need mode exe (`AnimFeed`'s `m_posExe`: the hold
  after a walk, 5065's orders after a walk, 5066's fight after a walk) stay off. So A's walk onto M, the fight held behind
  it and C's fight beside it start and end at other times offline, and every clip after them runs at another phase. Idle
  units do not walk, so frame 1475 (before the orders) is byte-equal, as every library bundle without a walk is.
- **Not the clocks**: the unit scene's two clocks are recorded and replayed as live: `beginFrame`'s `m_bodyT` is the
  frame's `nowMs` (live: the recorder's `beforeDraw` value, `srv_render_host.cpp` DrawFrame; offline: frames.bin's), and
  `onBatch`'s drain time is feed.bin's `drainMs` (live: the recorder's `lastDrainMs`). `AnimFeed::close` steps the fight
  clock by the difference of those frame times; sceneshot draws every recorded frame, not only the dumped ones.
- **Fix** (sceneshot only; live is right, no key, no D255 line): `OptionsFromBundle` takes both keys as `ParseHostConfig`
  read them (`RenderUnitsPositionsOption`, `RenderUnitsReadyHoldMsOption`) into `SceneOptions::unitsPositions` /
  `unitsReadyHoldMs` and `UnitsOptions::positionsExe`, and says `sceneshot: render_config: units positions exe|own,
  ready_hold_ms N`. Test: `sceneshot_test.cpp`'s units gap case (absent: own and 30000; `--set` exe and 5000; own; a bad
  value refused by the server's parser), which fails before the fix (no such line).
- **Other bundles affected** [C, F: master scene.json files read 2026-11-25 10:2x]: of the 16 library bundles with
  `render_units = 1`, the nine `C5H-4980-*` record `exe` (the seven `C5H-0301-*` record `own`); they pass today because
  no unit walks in their spans; after the fix they replay in mode exe, as they were drawn live. Rule A covers them.
- **Results** `[L]` (2026-11-25 10:56-11:36, workstation, every step through quietlock, builds on F:, head 6b599ce7a with
  main 2b4c93846; driver `server/evidence/0042/5070/allb157.sh` phases b, s, r): `sceneshot_test` `RESULT: 316 passed, 0
  failed, 0 skipped` (warp and hardware; its first run had 2 fails of the case order inside the test, not of the fix);
  `build_sceneshot --smoke` rc 0; the bundle (a copy on F:) `sceneshot --dumped --compare --tolerance 1:1 --asset-root
  mods548-vt`: **OK, exit 0, 9 of 9 dumped frames 1475..1875 byte-equal** (0 colour pixels, 0 depth values; the log says
  `units positions exe, ready_hold_ms 30000`). Negative arm, the same build with `--set render_units_positions=own`:
  exit 10 with W142's numbers exactly (87,788 px at 1525, 33,388-37,342 at 1575..1875), so the key alone makes the
  difference. Main 7d239081c (0742 B) and 0beaa24f7 (5053) merged, b, s, r and the own arm again on each head: the same
  (316 passed; 9 of 9 byte-equal; own exit 10; the bundle replays with `death_by_variant 0, end_after_dying 0`, 5053's
  keys absent in it). **Rule A** `[L]` (MC-B's turn 13:41-14:02, head 69d7e948a with main 0beaa24f7; `allb157.sh` l, a, d):
  on a private library (the 16 bundles of the C: copy as NTFS hard links, all read-only, plus a copy of the 0742 bundle;
  no `scenelib-manifest.json`, so no `scenelib.py check`; deleted after, `scenelib.py check` of the C: copy OK):
  `run_all.py --only offline-equals-live --only scenebundle-py` OK: scenebundle-py 34 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (155 s),
  offline-equals-live 18 passed (17 bundles and the missing-bundle case; 740 s), none hit 0xC0000142. **The first fight
  bundle passes offline-equals-live.** It enters the F: master only after the merge of 5070 (MC-B #14814: with it in the
  master every branch without the fix fails rule A); main fed21d8bb (0685, `srv_units_*`, `combat.h`) merged after rule A.
  Relink `[L]` (W160, 2026-11-25 15:34-16:11, head 2a55a3a7a with main 3f2534191: 0685 and 0755's options row): b, s, r

in the step of the last landing. This is 18.29.3's **T1**, proposed for 5067 and not built until now.

## 20. Server cost per frame and memory, offline itemisation (W34)

Written 2026-11-21 from 01:10 EST by W34 of team-0042 (account B), branch `w34-perfitem` from `origin/w32-stage5`
61cb50b6d (MC #8876 (4), MC #8932 (3), lead-0042's brief). The question: where W24's +4.02 ms of server CPU per drawn
frame (14.4, oldpc, route S, Quick Combat and Quick Movement off) goes, the +3.43 ms of it that 4756 measured for units
WITHOUT fights (`unit-draw-filter.md` 4.3), what the fights add, and where the +173 MB of server memory goes. Offline
only: no game instance. Marks: `[C]` read in this repository's code or computed exactly from recorded data, `[L x]`
recorded live by ticket x, `[I]` this section's reading. **Every number this section measured on the workstation is
DIAGNOSTIC**: the workstation ran W32's rule A run and 0626's release chain at the same time; arms were interleaved on one
build and are compared only with each other, never with oldpc's series.

### 20.1 Method and inputs

- **Recorded live data, re-read** (no new run): 4756's grade A series (oldpc job `20261117-122621-ef38`, 18 counted arms,
  `F:/c5-64bit-work/0040/4756/oldpc-20261117-122621-ef38/out/arms/*/render.log` and `arm.json`): the render thread's
  per-second lines (`terrain 1s`, `forest 1s`, `fog 1s`, `units 1s`, `host 1s`, `mem periodic`) over each arm's 45 s idle
  window, by `server/evidence/0042/w34/split_4756.py` (standard library; output `C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w34/split_4756.txt`).
  W24's arms (`C:/c5-64bit-work/0042/w24/s1-mid3/out/arms/`) carry `arm.json`, `server.log` and `vpproxy.log` only: their
  `render.log` was not fetched, so W24's series cannot be split this way (20.6).
- **Offline replays** of the scene library's huge bundle `C5H-0301-HUGE_0350_20261119-214920_workstation` (Huge, turn
  350, 853 units in the table, `render_units=1`, controller on, `render_units_passes=0`, `render_units_positions=own`)

### 20.2 The +3.43 ms is mostly a longer render-thread frame, not more CPU (4756 re-read) [C from L 4756]

The series' metric is server CPU seconds over the window divided by the frames the server drew. Read per second, with
the host loop's own counters, the six repetitions give (mean [95 % half-width], paired by repetition):

| Over the 45 s idle window | a (ServerUnits 0) | b (ServerUnits 1) | b - a |
|---|---|---|---|
| server CPU per drawn frame, ms (the series' metric) | 7.864 [0.087] | 11.293 [0.173] | **+3.430** [0.218] |
| server CPU per second, ms (= cores x 1000) | 1545.2 [12.3] | 1467.5 [10.3] | **-77.7** [9.2] (-5.0 %) |
| frames drawn per s | 196.5 [1.2] | 130.0 [1.7] | -66.5 [2.8] |
| frame period, ms (1000 / fps) | 5.089 [0.032] | 7.696 [0.101] | **+2.607** [0.127] |
| the host loop's camera waits per s (`waits_event`) | 195.5 | 128.4 | -67.2 |
| EXE cameras the loop skipped per s (`skipped_cams`) | 0.44 | 67.3 | +66.8 |
| terrain CPU ms per frame (`terrain 1s cpu_ms`) | 0.847 | 0.871 | +0.024 [0.011] |
| forest CPU ms per frame | 0.844 | 0.855 | +0.011 [0.010] |
| fog CPU ms per frame | 0.290 | 0.285 | -0.005 [0.006] |
| units: the controller's per-second maximum, ms (`anim_ms_max`) | - | 1.701 [0.024] | |
| units: beginFrame + scene pass, per-second maximum, ms (`frame_ms_max`) | - | 5.404 [0.055] | |

What this says:
- **The server does not spend more CPU with its units on: it spends 5 % less per second and draws a third fewer
  frames.** The render loop draws one frame per EXE camera it waits for (`waits_event` = frames drawn in both arms). In a
  it keeps pace with the EXE (195 of 195 cameras, 0.4 skipped per s): the loop waits on the EXE, so its frame's work is
  less than the 5.09 ms period. In b it cannot: it skips 67 cameras per second, i.e. the render thread's frame is the
  bottleneck at 7.70 ms [C from the counters].
- **The per-frame metric's +3.43 ms is therefore two things**: the render thread's frame got longer (period +2.61 ms;
  the work it added is at least that, more if a's render thread had slack), and the CPU of every other thread, which
  runs per second, not per frame (the feed and remote engine, the residency's bake workers, the pre-check), is divided by
  130 frames instead of 196 (at a's 545 ms per second of other-thread CPU, the same work per second costs 2.78 ms per
  frame at 196 fps and 4.19 at 130 fps) [C arithmetic; I that the render thread is busy all the time in b]. With R = the
  frame period (the render thread busy all the time) the split is: render thread +2.61 ms, other threads +0.82 ms per
  frame although they used 78 ms per second LESS (the bake starved, 4.3's video-memory reading) [I: the R = period
  bound; a per-thread measurement settles it, 20.6].
- **The terrain, forest and fog passes do not move** (+0.02, +0.01, -0.01 ms per frame): the added frame time is the
  units' own work on the render thread, plus what the GPU makes it wait for (the units' GPU work, +0.07 ms on the terrain
  timer's mean, not resolved).
- **The units' frame is up to 5.4 ms** (beginFrame + the scene pass, the per-second maximum; the controller up to 1.7 ms
  of it), on oldpc with 32 drawn and 821 held units at camera 1, position mode exe, the reflection pass on
  (`render_units_passes=1`) whose draw is not inside `frame_ms` [C `srv_units_scene.cpp` 1130-1160]. The mean is not
  logged (only the maxima: `m_beginMs` holds each part per frame, 20.5).

### 20.6 Where the +173 MB goes (item 3) [C from L 4778; C offline; DIAGNOSTIC where offline]

**Live, W24's stage-4 arms** (`server/evidence/0042/w34/mem_w24.py`, `mem_owners_w24.py`; render.log's `mem periodic`
every 10 s and the residency's own sizes in the `terrain 1s` and `near 1s` lines):
- The residency (tile cache + arrays + the near pool) ends at **997 MB in both arms** (410 + 416 + 171), but b reaches it
  about 6 minutes later than a (its bake runs at 134 frames per second, 20.4) [C from L].
- **Private bytes minus the residency at the end: a 1055 / 1065 / 1067 / 1082 MB, b 1229 / 1245 / 1233 / 1256 MB: b - a
  = +174, +180, +166, +174 MB per round.** That difference is already there when the residency has caught up (R1-b 19:16:
  1209 against R1-a 18:44: 1045) and grows by about 2 MB per turn more than a's afterwards (b +30 MB over its last 20
  minutes, a +10) [C from L].
- So **the +173 MB is a one-off of the unit scene and route S, not a growth with the turns.** The "growth over 10 turns

### 20.8 Not verified, and what would close it

- The per-pass times on oldpc: `UnitsHost` keeps each part of every frame (`m_beginMs[0..3]`, the scene pass's
  `drawMs`) but logs only the per-second maxima; a mean beside each maximum in the `units 1s` line (and the reflection and
  mask passes timed the same way) would itemise the live +3.07 ms directly [C `srv_units_scene.cpp` 924-973, 1138-1147].
- The reflection pass, the mask pass and mode exe's position intake are not in the offline history replay (20.3);
  their sizes in 20.5 are estimates.
- The cycles-to-ms factor (3.187 GHz, the rated MHz of `cputime.py topology`) is assumed to be the reference clock of
  `QueryThreadCycleTime` on this machine; the steady passes by cycles (1.23-1.33 ms) and by the polls (1.42 ms) agree
  within 10-15 %.
- About 120 MB of the offline U - Z and the parsed `.gr2` share of the pre-check's 359 MB are not attributed.
- Every workstation number is DIAGNOSTIC (W32's rule A run and 0626's chain ran beside them); the oldpc numbers of 20.2
  and 20.4 are re-reads of recorded grade A / B series.
